### B-41 · `_classify_provider_exception` misroutes AuthenticationError to TRANSIENT_RETRY *(surfaced at B-38 grounding, 2026-07-15, advisor()-flagged)*
- **What it is.** `_classify_provider_exception` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:265-286`) returned `ValidatorRetryExitClass.TRANSIENT_RETRY` for any exception other than `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError`/`LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` — including an SDK `AuthenticationError` (`anthropic`/`openai` `.status_code` 401/403) — running the full retry staircase before eventually exhausting, contradicting the function's own docstring's claim that "AUTH ... are fail-fast."
- **Close-out.** Verified against `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` v1.99 (canonical HEAD) directly, not from memory: §14.5's C-RT-15 fail-class table states `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-AUTH` (the raw SDK auth error, 401/403 — NOT a harness wrapper type) is "Raise unmodified"; §14.6 D2's fork-resolution text and its own narrative both independently say AUTH is fail-fast. Three independent spec statements plus the function's own docstring all agreed — this was a straightforward conformance fix, not an open design decision, so no fork was needed. Added a `status_code in (401, 403)` duck-typed guard to `_classify_provider_exception`, placed after the wrapper-type check and before the `TRANSIENT_RETRY` catch-all — deliberately NOT reusing `_classify_breaker_cause` so the two classifiers' control-flow contracts stay independent. This also closes `B-38`'s noted divergence as a side effect (both classifiers now agree on AUTH).
- **Test-witness gap closed.** Added a fail-fast witness test — the naive assertion "exactly 2 total dispatch calls" does NOT discriminate fail-fast (candidate 0 abandoned after 1 call, candidate 1 gets the 2nd) from a buggy retry-then-succeed on candidate 0 (also totals 2 calls); the real witness checks WHICH candidate the 2nd call actually reached. Added a regression-guard test proving 429/5xx still retry (guards against an overly-broad `status_code is not None` mutation, which would wrongly fail-fast rate-limits and server errors). Both mutation-probed against real production-code reversions — the fail-fast test genuinely fails when the guard is reverted, and the regression-guard test genuinely fails when the guard is broadened past 401/403.

### B-42 · `breaker.cause`'s `FIVE_XX_STREAK` is tagged by the terminal exception only, not a verified streak *(surfaced at B-38's own PR, out-of-family Codex round 1, 2026-07-15)*
- **What it is.** `_classify_breaker_cause` tags `FIVE_XX_STREAK` from a single last-attempt exception's `.status_code >= 500` — but `BreakerStateMachine` (`retry_breaker.py`) tracks only an aggregate `fail_count`, not a per-cause failure history. A breaker with `fail_threshold > 1` that trips after a mixed sequence (e.g. a rate-limit failure, then an auth failure, then a terminal 5xx) still reports `FIVE_XX_STREAK` — the name implies N *consecutive* 5xx responses, but only the terminal exception is ever inspected.
- **Close-out.** CLOSED 2026-07-15. Grounded directly against `Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md` §7.1 (only requires "the classified trip-cause, when known" — no streak-verification mandate) and `BreakerStateMachine`'s own source (only an aggregate `fail_count`, no per-cause history); confirmed no live consumer reads `harness.breaker.cause` today. Chose option (b) from this row's own close-out options: a documentation-only clarification, not new per-cause tracking infrastructure (which would be speculative ahead of any consumer — the same discipline the B-19 redundancy analysis already established). Added a clarifying paragraph to `BreakerCause`'s docstring in `harness_breaker_schema.py` stating `FIVE_XX_STREAK` is tagged from a single terminal 5xx exception, not a verified N-consecutive streak — mirroring the equivalent clarification `_classify_breaker_cause`'s own docstring in `retry_breaker_fallback.py` already carried since `B-38`'s original landing. The spec-committed enum value (`5xx_streak`) is UNCHANGED; only the docstring's description of its derivation is now precise. No behavior/test change; ruff clean; OD breaker test suite (30 tests) still green.
- **Adjacent finding split out, not folded in.** OD spec v1.32 §7.1's own prose still describes `harness.breaker.cause` as "vacuous-today ... absent from every emitted event," which is now stale since `B-38` populated it for 3 of 4 values. Fixing spec prose is a design-substrate edit requiring design-phase posture, not a Phase-7 code fix — registered separately as `B-43` rather than bundled into this row's code-only PR.

### B-66 · B-60 fence-consult order at admission discrimination has no single-site witness *(registered at the B-60 close, merge-gate test-witness lens, 2026-07-21)*

### B-67 · Protected result store's TTL GC sweep has no shutdown-time hook — bootstrap half only *(registered at the B-65-A impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 1 [P1], 2026-07-22; CLOSED at round 4 correction, same date)*

- **What it is.** CORRECTED at out-of-family Codex round 4: this row's own premise ("this runtime has no graceful-teardown chain to hook") was FALSE. `shutdown(ctx)` at `harness_runtime/shutdown.py` IS that chain — it is invoked unconditionally in `run()`'s/`resume()`'s `finally` block regardless of workflow outcome (verified by direct read of `api.py` lines ~671/941). The row's earlier reasoning conflated this with the SEPARATE signal-handler drain path (`admin/shutdown_cli.py`, which only sets `drained_flag`) — that path is real but immaterial here: `shutdown()`'s own step 1 sets `drained_flag` too, so whether a signal pre-emptively flips it or not, `shutdown()` still runs once `run()`/`resume()` unwinds.
- **Fix landed.** A new step 5b in `shutdown()`: a bounded, best-effort `ctx.protected_result_store.gc_sweep()` off the default executor via `asyncio.to_thread` — safe here specifically because `shutdown()` only runs AFTER `execute_workflow` has already returned, so no sync driver can be occupying the default pool concurrently (unlike the request-path raise sites this same round also fixed to avoid that exact deadlock class). The `stage_4_od.py` comment carrying the false premise was corrected in the same commit. Both halves are now wired: bootstrap reaps a PRIOR process's abandoned entries; shutdown reaps THIS process's own before exit. Residual: only a hard kill (SIGKILL/segfault) that bypasses Python's `finally` entirely still relies on the next process's bootstrap sweep — the same case the bootstrap half was always designed for.
- **Council: no** — corrective wiring fix once the false premise was caught by review, not a design fork.

### B-68 · Protected result store's opportunistic GC can race a concurrent in-flight publication under a short TTL *(registered at the B-65-A impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 11 [P2], 2026-07-22; CLOSED 2026-07-25 -- in-process synchronization scope; cross-process residual split to B-73)*

- **What it is.** `write_once()` captures `_StoredEnvelope.written_at` via `time.time()` BEFORE serialization/encryption/`_publish_atomic`'s fsync+`os.link` commit — a real, non-instantaneous gap. A CONCURRENT sweep (a different in-process opportunistic call from another request, or the bootstrap/shutdown-half sweep from a co-resident process sharing the same store directory) that runs during that gap decrypts the envelope, computes `current_time - written_at`, and — if the deployment-configured `ttl_seconds` (operator-settable, `gt=0.0`, no floor) is shorter than the write's own encrypt+fsync latency — can judge the just-published entry already expired and unlink it before `write_once()` even returns. The caller then holds a "live-looking" `composite_key` whose first `read()` raises an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` instead of the typed `ProtectedStoreCrossTenantError`/`ProtectedStoreTamperError` refusals the store otherwise guarantees.
- **Fix landed (2026-07-25, branch `b68-protected-result-store-gc-race-mtime-authority`, 5 rounds of out-of-family Codex review).** (1) `gc_sweep()`'s age authority switched from the pre-publish `_StoredEnvelope.written_at` field to the committed entry file's own filesystem mtime, explicitly refreshed via `os.utime` + its own fsync AFTER the durable `os.link` commit — closing the original timing gap. (2) A process-wide `threading.Lock` registry keyed by the store root's RESOLVED path (`_root_locks`, module-level, not per-instance) now serializes `_publish_atomic`'s entire publish critical section against `gc_sweep`'s entire scan — closing same-process races, including a co-resident concurrent-INSTANCE race (e.g. across bootstrap/resume cycles) the original registration did not anticipate; the lock key uses the root's filesystem identity (`(st_dev, st_ino)`, falling back to the resolved path only before the directory exists) so filesystem-equivalent path aliases (e.g. a `..`-containing spelling, or a case-folded spelling on a case-insensitive volume) share the same lock, and the temp-file's full lifetime (creation through the post-commit mtime-refresh fsync) is inside the lock so a sweep cannot reclaim an in-flight temp file mid-publish. (3) `read()` degrades a missing entry to a typed `ProtectedStoreEntryNotFoundError(FileNotFoundError)` — the optional interim hardening this row's close_out named — instead of a raw `FileNotFoundError`. Each fix is witnessed by a deterministic (non-flaky, mechanism-level) mutation-probed test: reverting the fix makes the corresponding test fail; restoring it passes. 10 new tests added across all rounds; full `harness-runtime` + `harness-cp` suites green.
- **Frequency correction (merge-gate round-1 concurrency lens, PR #1078, 2026-07-22).** Independently confirmed the race is real and reachable via genuine multi-threading, and sharpened this writeup's own framing: `shutdown()` step 5b fires `gc_sweep()` UNCONDITIONALLY once per `run()`/`resume()` call, with no interval throttle — unlike the in-write opportunistic trigger's `_OPPORTUNISTIC_GC_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 300.0` gate. On a daemon serving many concurrent short-lived workflow runs against the SAME shared store instance, concurrent-sweep frequency is materially higher than a reading based only on the 300s opportunistic throttle would suggest — the fix above closes the race regardless of frequency for the same-process case.
- **Residual split out (round 5 convergence check).** Out-of-family Codex round 5 confirmed the in-process fix is sound but restated the SAME cross-PROCESS gap this row's fix comments always disclosed ("a genuinely separate OS process sharing the store directory remains an open residual, registered, not silently assumed closed") — two co-resident daemon PROCESSES each hold their own independent `_root_locks` registry, so a `threading.Lock` alone cannot exclude them. Not a defect introduced by this fix; split to **B-73** as its own registered row rather than expanding this arc's scope, per the terminal register discipline (B-64/B-67 precedents).
- **Council: no** — narrow TTL-dependent race with a documented reachability precondition; the in-process fix was a known primitive (a resolved-path-keyed lock), not a judgment call.

- **Close-out steps** *(historical, pre-2026-07-30 — DISCHARGED by the spec leg; the live close-out is the X-AL-2 conjunctive criterion in the STATUS bullet above)*. Design a durable-pause-state read accessor (Runtime-owned, since it reads `JournalWorkflowPauseStore`, §14.14.8) that a `resume_handle` caller can invoke BEFORE constructing `resume_context`, to learn the currently-paused children's `run_id`s (and, ideally, enough context per child — e.g. the gate description/workflow position — to compose a sensible operator response) for the SAME `workflow_id` the caller intends to resume. ### B-70 · `effect_fence_resolution_for`'s uniform-fallback semantics share B-39's cross-branch-misapplication hazard, unfixed in the already-shipped mechanism *(registered at the B-39 spec-leg PR #1092, out-of-family Codex round 3 (branch-vs-main), 2026-07-23; GROUNDED + fork filed 2026-07-24; SPEC LEG LANDED 2026-07-24 — CP spec v1.107 + plan v2.43; IMPL LEG LANDED 2026-07-25 — PR #1101, CLOSED)*

- **What it is.** `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_106.md` §1.2 property 4 (round-3 correction) closes a safety gap in the NEW `ResumeContext.hitl_responses`/`hitl_response_for` mechanism: when 2+ children are concurrently paused, an operator supplying only the uniform `hitl_response` field (no keyed map) must NOT have that response silently applied to every unaddressed child — the resolver must instead leave unaddressed children paused/INERT. The SHIPPED, ALREADY-CLEARED sibling mechanism this pattern was modeled on, `ResumeContext.effect_fence_resolutions`/`effect_fence_resolution_for` (§26.8.1, unamended by the B-39 arc), has the IDENTICAL uniform-fallback shape and the IDENTICAL gap: with 2+ children concurrently effect-fence-paused, a uniform `effect_fence_resolution` (no keyed map) resolves EVERY unaddressed child to the SAME SKIP_AS_FIRED/RE_FIRE/ABORT judgment, which can be wrong for some of them (e.g. one child's non-idempotent effect genuinely fired and needs SKIP_AS_FIRED while a sibling's did not and needs RE_FIRE).
- **Current state.** GROUNDED 2026-07-24 (autonomous-loop grounding pass, `.harness/class_2_fork_b70_effect_fence_resolution_uniform_fallback.md`) — direct read of `workflow_driver.py` confirms the mechanism (the singular `resume_context.effect_fence_resolution` is consulted independently at every `execute_workflow` recursion depth whose own `resume_snapshot.effect_fence_resume` is set, with no cross-depth uniqueness check) and resolves the two open grounding questions the register originally deferred: (1) NO container/gate-owning split is needed (unlike HITL) — `EffectFencePausedBranchResumeState`'s own docstring + `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_106.md` §2 (REMOVED) both confirm effect-fence carriers never cross a recursion boundary the way HITL child-pause delivery does (a nested descendant's own effect-fence pause propagates via the generic `PausedChildBranchResumeState`/`SubAgentChildPausedError` path, never via `EffectFencePausedBranchResumeState`, so every captured fence-pause entry is inherently gate-owning and already `idempotency_key`-unique across depth); (2) the fix DOES need its own CP spec property (a §26.8.1 companion mirroring §1.2 property 4's safety+liveness shape, simpler — no property-5 equivalent) before code, since restricting the auto-fallback is an observable CONTRACT change to a cleared mechanism, not pure impl-to-spec. **SPEC LEG LANDED 2026-07-24** (operator ratified "open the spec-leg now" via `AskUserQuestion`) — `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_107.md` NEW §1 (the safety+liveness invariant, sharpened across 5 out-of-family review rounds from the fork's §3 draft — round 1 added the previously-omitted ORCHESTRATOR carrier; round 2 fixed a gap where the LINEAR consume site never calls `effect_fence_resolution_for` at all, but its own fix over-corrected; round 3 found round 2's fix would permanently livelock any 2+-simultaneous-LINEAR-pause resume, corrected to genuine map-addressability via the LINEAR carrier's already-existing `idempotency_key` field; round 4 added a `resume_handle` scope-limit note mirroring `B-69`; no property-5 equivalent still holds per the grounding above) + `Implementation_Plan_Control_Plane_v2_43.md` (ONE deferred coverage-matrix row, zero unit amendment — mirrors how v2.42 §5 deferred the parallel `hitl_responses` property 4/5 invariants) + 2 clearance markers. Status flipped `registered_finding` → `design_substrate_gated` → `open` (spec-leg gate cleared; impl leg — the resolver's tree-walk enumeration of the unaddressed effect-fence-pause set, wired at the LINEAR + ORCHESTRATOR + two fan-out consume sites — is the next buildable slice, NOT yet opened, per the B-33/B-39/B-59 precedent). `council: no` unchanged (mechanical parity, no cross-domain tension). **IMPL LEG LANDED 2026-07-25** (PR #1101) — `compute_effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key`/`_collect_effect_fence_idempotency_keys` (a tree-walk across all three carriers) + `_resolve_effect_fence_gated` (a genuine caller of the existing `effect_fence_resolution_for`, per a merge-gate spec-conformance BLOCK caught pre-merge — an earlier draft reimplemented its logic inline) wired at the LINEAR site (round-3-corrected to become map-addressable), the ORCHESTRATOR's own dispatch, and both fan-out consume sites; `effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key` threaded end-to-end `mcp_server.py` → `execute_workflow` → `StepExecutionContext` → `sub_agent_dispatch.py` → `child_workflow_runner.py`, mirroring the existing `hitl_uniform_fallback_eligible_run_id` wiring. 2 merge-gate rounds (round 1 BLOCK on spec-conformance + test-witness, both fixed; round 2 all-approve); 1767 harness-cp + 3046 harness-runtime tests green. **Status flipped `open` → `closed`.**
- **Close-out steps (round-7-corrected — do NOT copy the round-3-vintage phrasing below verbatim; see the correction note).** Extend `effect_fence_resolution_for`'s CONSUMPTION contract (not necessarily the field/method signature itself) with the SAME KIND of multi-branch fallback-safety invariant B-39's `hitl_response_for` now carries at its FINAL, round-7-corrected shape (`Spec_Control_Plane_v1_106.md` §1.2 property 4) — a deterministic SAFETY rule (uniform fallback resolves a branch only when it is the sole unaddressed member of the relevant set this cycle) stated as an invariant on the OUTCOME, not a prescribed counting mechanism. **Correction note:** an earlier draft of this row said "the resolver must count concurrently-effect-fence-paused children first and apply the uniform fallback only when exactly one is paused" without B-39's own gate-owning-vs-transitively-paused-container distinction (property 5) — B-39 itself REJECTED an unscoped version of that exact count-based framing at its own round 4 (it strands container branches). Before implementing this row's fix: FIRST determine whether effect-fence pauses have an analogous transitively-paused-container concept under `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` recursion (unresolved as of this registration — `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_106.md` §2's REMOVED-section text claims "the effect-fence mechanism does not cross a recursion boundary the way HITL child-pause delivery does," but this claim was never re-verified against the ACTUAL `EffectFencePausedBranchResumeState`/`effect_fence_paused_branches` carrier code — grep `harness-cp/src/harness_cp/pause_resume_protocol_types.py` before assuming either way). If containers exist for effect-fence too, mirror B-39's gate-owning/property-5 split exactly; if not, the plain count-based rule (no container exclusion needed) is safe as originally drafted. Requires a small design-substrate amendment to CP spec §26.8.1 (a Class 2/3 fork, likely — mechanical parity fix once the container question is resolved) plus updating the callers of `effect_fence_resolution_for` (the SAME `workflow_driver.py` peek-reader sites B-39's own `resume_context_holder` retirement touches — see the B-39 impl leg's own scope-discovery pass) to enforce the gate. **Council: no** — parity fix mirroring an already-ratified pattern (B-39's own property 4), not a fresh open design question.

### B-72 · A `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` step's own `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY` HITL gate can re-fire on every resume-forward of an already-dispatched, deeper-paused child, discarding the child's `paused_child_branches` cursor *(registered at the B-39 impl-leg Slice B branch `b39-impl-leg-slice-b-hitl-delivery-mechanism`, out-of-family Codex round 4 (branch-vs-main), 2026-07-24)*

- **What it is.** `RuntimeHITLGateComposer.dispatch()`'s Step 0 one-shot short-circuit (`hitl_gate_composer.py` ~1652-1730) only bypasses the gate when `step_context.hitl_delivery_holder.consume_and_clear()` is non-`None`. This session's B-39 Slice B delivery mechanism populates `hitl_delivery_holder` ONLY at the linear `resume_at` reconstruction site in `workflow_driver.py` — it is never threaded to fan-out branch composition (`_execute_parallelization` / `_execute_orchestrator_workers`, which build each branch's `StepExecutionContext` via `compose_branch_child_context` and only pass `resume_context`/`child_resume_snapshot` through, never `hitl_delivery_holder`). So when a fan-out branch's own `step_kind` is `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` AND that step carries its own `HITLPlacement(position=SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY)` declaration, EVERY re-dispatch of that branch (including a pure resume-forward whose sole purpose is carrying `child_resume_snapshot` down to an already-paused descendant) runs Step 0 → finds `hitl_delivery_holder is None` → falls through to full gate re-evaluation. `HITLPlacementTrigger` for `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY` (`hitl_placement.py:128-138`) states applicability as "All cells; sub-agent interrupt stranding mitigated via cascade-timeout per C-CP-21 §21.3" — confirming `DURABLE_ASYNC` synchrony is spec-reachable for this placement, and that the spec's own anticipated mitigation for this exact stranding class is a cascade-timeout, not cursor-preservation. If the ancestor's OWN gate re-raises `HITLPauseRequestedSignal` on this re-evaluation (never reaching `inner.dispatch()`, so `child_resume_snapshot` is never forwarded to `RuntimeSubAgentDispatcher`), the fan-out branch-failure capture logic builds a FRESH `PausedChildBranchResumeState` for this cycle representing "paused at its own gate" — with no evident mechanism to nest or preserve the PRIOR round's already-known deeper `child_snapshot` (the descendant that was already dispatched and is already paused further down), because a fresh signal carries no reference to the previous cycle's branch disposition. This is PRE-EXISTING and orthogonal to B-39's own delivery-cell mechanism, not introduced by it: under the OLD, now-retired ctx-level global `ResumeContextHolder`, the SAME ancestor gate re-fire would ALSO occur on every resume-forward (the composer's Step 0 had no first-dispatch-vs-resume-forward distinction then either) — but the OLD holder was tree-wide-shared, so ANY non-`None` operator-supplied value (even one addressed to a different, deeper branch) would satisfy the ancestor's Step 0 and let it proceed to `inner.dispatch()`, accidentally forwarding the child cursor correctly (while risking the OLD mechanism's own already-documented misapplication hazard). ### B-73 · Protected result store's GC/publish synchronization is in-process only -- two co-resident OS processes sharing one store root are not mutually excluded *(split from B-68 at its close, out-of-family Codex round 5, 2026-07-25; CLOSED 2026-07-26 -- PR #1120)*

- **What it is.** Split out of B-68 at its close (2026-07-25). B-68's fix serializes `gc_sweep()` against `_publish_atomic()` via a `threading.Lock` keyed by the store root's resolved path, held in a module-level `_root_locks` registry — this closes every same-process race, including multiple `ProtectedResultStore` instances constructed against the same root within one process (e.g. across bootstrap/resume cycles). Out-of-family Codex round 5 (the B-68 fix's convergence check) confirmed the registry does NOT extend across a process boundary: two separate daemon PROCESSES sharing one store directory each hold their own independent `_root_locks` dict, so one process's bootstrap/shutdown sweep can still unlink another process's just-published entry between its `os.link()` commit and mtime refresh, if the deployment-configured TTL is shorter than that window.
- **Current state.** Registered, not built. This is the SAME reachability precondition B-68's original registration already named (TTL shorter than single-digit-ms publish latency — roughly seven orders of magnitude below the factory 86400s default) and the same residual B-68's own code comments and commit history disclosed throughout its 5 review rounds ("a genuinely separate OS process sharing the store directory remains an open residual, registered, not silently assumed closed"). Not a defect introduced by B-68's fix — an inherent limitation of an in-process primitive.
- **Close-out steps.** Add an OS-level advisory lock (`fcntl.flock` on a dedicated lockfile under the store root, or equivalent) wrapping the same `_publish_atomic`/`gc_sweep` critical sections the in-process `threading.Lock` already wraps, acquired/released around the existing lock so both layers compose without a nested-lock ordering hazard. Witness with a genuine multi-PROCESS test (e.g. `multiprocessing` workers, not threads) pinning a TTL shorter than an injected publication delay in one process while a second process sweeps concurrently, asserting the entry survives.
- **Council: no** — narrow TTL-dependent cross-process race with a documented, unchanged reachability precondition; the fix is a known primitive (`fcntl.flock`), not a judgment call.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-26 (PR #1120).** `_cross_process_lock()` (an `fcntl.flock` on a dedicated `.cross_process.lock` file, disjoint from both `gc_sweep` glob patterns) is now composed INSIDE the existing in-process `self._publish_lock` at both `_publish_atomic` and `gc_sweep`'s candidate-selection phase — a single, fixed nesting order everywhere, no lock-ordering hazard. Guarded on Windows (`_IS_WINDOWS = sys.platform == "win32"`) per C-STK-10, mirroring the same carve-out already shipped at `harness_is.cross_process_ledger_lock`; `fcntl` is imported lazily inside the lock method, never at module scope. **4 rounds of out-of-family `just codex-review main` to clean convergence:** round 1 caught a [P1] (the unguarded top-level `import fcntl` would have broken `import harness_runtime` entirely on Windows, since `harness_runtime.types` imports `ProtectedResultStore` unconditionally) plus a [P2] (a fresh child store's opportunistic pre-write GC sweep already acquires the same lock, so the write-once regression test passed even with `_publish_atomic`'s own lock removed alone — fixed by suppressing the opportunistic sweep in the test's child process); round 2 caught 2 further [P2]s (the new tests would spuriously fail on Windows, where the lock intentionally no-ops — added `skipif`; the readiness marker was written before `flock` was ever attempted, leaving a scheduling window); round 3 found the same underlying concern persisted (writing the marker "right before" the contending call still is not proof of being AT the `flock` attempt, since real serialization + Fernet encryption happen first) — fixed by wrapping `fcntl.flock` itself in each child script so the marker fires at the actual syscall attempt; round 4 clean. Each fix mutation-probe-verified (revert, confirm the regression test fails; restore, confirm green) before landing. Witnessed with two genuine-subprocess regression tests (`subprocess`, not `multiprocessing` — avoids both the fork-after-lock-held deadlock hazard and spawn's pickle-by-module-name ambiguity in this monorepo's several same-named `tests` packages) asserting cross-process blocking via `store._cross_process_lock()` held directly in the parent — a deliberate, reasoned deviation from the originally-envisioned TTL-race-survival recipe (lock-identity blocking is the more deterministic, non-flaky witness shape for this claim). `merge-gate` 3-lens review: concurrency + test-witness APPROVE at round 1; spec-conformance BLOCKED once (this register row was not updated in the same PR, diverging from the B-68 precedent) — fixed by this same update.

### B-74 · Protected result store's mtime-based GC age authority can under-report publish time below a filesystem's timestamp granularity *(surfaced at the B-68 impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 7 [P2], 2026-07-25)* *(**CLOSED 2026-08-05 at the B-96 impl leg** -- residue DISSOLVED under ceiling form C-2, not narrowed)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-05 at the `B-96` impl leg (`U-RT-150`).** The residue is **DISSOLVED, not narrowed**: reclaim no longer rests on the filesystem timestamp ALONE, so a granularity error can no longer reach the decision by itself, and the inter-sweep gap ceases to be a term in it at all. No TTL floor, no volume probe and no knowledge of the filesystem's real resolution were required — exactly this row's SECOND stated option, delivered structurally. The witness disposition this row prescribes was applied literally: `test_coarse_filesystem_mtime_granularity_does_not_lose_a_live_entry_on_sight` is **re-pinned as a POSITIVE witness that the live entry SURVIVES BOTH SWEEPS**, kept rather than deleted.
- **2026-08-05 ratification-leg disposition (`B-96` Reading C / ceiling C-2): under the ratified C-2 form THIS ROW CLOSES**, and closes in the shape its own `close_out` asks for (`.harness/council-b96-grace-ceiling-2026-08-01.md` §8, reached independently by all three voices and re-derived by that record's adversarial pass against the live test). C-2 delivers this row's **second** stated option — *an age authority that cannot predate publication by more than the TTL* — **structurally**, with no volume probe, no floor and no knowledge of the filesystem granularity `G`, because the age authority stops being mtime-alone. **The residue as scoped is DISSOLVED, not narrowed:** the inter-sweep gap ceases to be a term in the reclaim decision at all. **Witness disposition at the `B-96` impl leg:** `:1982` flips `== [entry_path.stem]` → `== []` and is **re-pinned as a positive witness**, exactly as its own comment at `:1978`–`:1981` instructs; `:1975` and `:1976` are **untouched**. **Two corrections the impl leg must not inherit as fact:** (1) the Δ figure — neither *Δ ≈ 1.0s* nor *Δ ∈ [0.3, 0.9) guaranteed* is right; Δ is the fractional part of wall-clock at the patched `os.utime` call, phase-guarded only at loop exit, so `[0.3, 0.9)` is **overwhelmingly likely, not guaranteed**; (2) the stale §14.8.11 anchor lived in **this** row — **refreshed** at this leg by direct read at HEAD `4815ebef` to **`:4926` at Runtime v1.110** (heading `:4915`); the council record's own *`:4909` at v1.109* prescription was already stale. **Status unchanged (`registered_finding`)** — this row flips to `closed` only when the `B-96` impl leg merges. **No separate `B-74`-residue filing is owed**: the question it would have carried is answered by the `B-96` ratification.
- **What it is.** `_publish_atomic`'s `os.utime(entry_path, None)` refresh sets the entry's mtime to the current system time, but the underlying filesystem is what actually STORES that value, at whatever timestamp resolution it supports — on a coarse-granularity filesystem (e.g. legacy FAT32, or certain network filesystem configurations; NOT the modern POSIX filesystems — ext4/APFS/NTFS — this workspace's committed local-development/self-hosted-server/managed-cloud deployment surfaces default to, which offer sub-millisecond resolution), the stored mtime can round DOWN by up to the filesystem's own granularity (e.g. up to ~1 second on a 1-second-resolution filesystem). If the deployment-configured `ttl_seconds` is SHORTER than that rounding error, `gc_sweep()` can classify a just-published, genuinely-live entry as already expired and reclaim it — even though the B-68 mtime-authority fix (round 1) is working exactly as designed; the filesystem itself cannot represent the precision the fix relies on.
- **Current state.** NARROWED (not closed) 2026-07-26 (PR #1123): the "likely ONE finding" framing below was directionally right but not literal — `B-77` and `B-74` share raw mtime as an untrustworthy age authority, but `B-77`'s reorder fix only removes the DATA write+fsync duration from its OWN crash window, not the whole window (see `B-77`'s row — a residual metadata-fsync+commit tail remains, reproduced by out-of-family Codex round 9). This row's own concern (filesystem storage-resolution rounding) is UNTOUCHED by that reorder either way — it was never about ordering, only about what a coarse filesystem stores once a value is fsync'd, so it stays fully in scope, not reduced. Two same-arc attempts to dispose of this row were both wrong and reverted: PR #1123 round 1 tried "no realistic operator would configure a below-floor TTL" (rejected by Codex — `protected_result_store_ttl_seconds` enforces only `gt=0.0`, no floor, and the env loader + factory pass an override through unchanged, so this is a SUPPORTED configuration, not an unreachable one); a later round considered adding that same TTL floor as a mechanical fix and advisor() rejected it too — it is this row's own close_out option ("reject TTLs below a guaranteed timestamp resolution"), already flagged as a genuine design decision, and the field is a spec'd deployment-configurable surface (Runtime §14.8.11's bounded-retention bullet, `:4883` at v1.108 — **cite corrected 2026-07-31**: §14.8.11 carries no AC numbering, so the prior "AC 7" resolved to nothing) Phase-7 impl discretion should not narrow unilaterally. Remains open, not dormant, not built this arc.

  **NARROWED AGAIN 2026-07-30 (dated re-check against the landed `B-77` fix, PR `#1163`).** `B-77`'s first-observation grace covers this row's reachable loss case but does NOT subsume it. **Now covered:** a granularity error up to ONE sweep interval — the sweep that FIRST observes a coarse-stamped, genuinely-live entry can no longer reclaim it, which is the bootstrap-sweep-immediately-after-publication path (witnessed at `test_coarse_filesystem_mtime_granularity_does_not_lose_a_live_entry_on_sight`, whose first assertion passes only because of the grace). **Surviving residue — this row's whole remaining scope:** a rounding error EXCEEDING the gap between two consecutive sweeps. That gap is not TTL-bound — a bootstrap sweep (`stage_4_od.py`) and an explicit or shutdown-step-5b sweep (`shutdown.py`) can land milliseconds apart, well inside a 1-second filesystem granularity — so a live entry can still be lost on such a volume. That exact residue is PINNED as an executable assertion in the same witness (its second `gc_sweep` reclaims the live entry, labelled REGISTERED RESIDUAL in the test body), so a future fix must come back and update it rather than silently diverge. Not closed as subsumed-by-`B-77`; the close-out below is unchanged and still the fix.

  **Cross-reference (advisor(), B-76 arc, 2026-07-26):** likely ONE finding with `B-77` — both concern raw mtime as an untrustworthy age authority (this row: filesystem timestamp-granularity rounding; `B-77`: crash-window non-atomicity). A fix that moves the age authority off raw mtime would likely close both; ground as a single "does the age authority stay mtime?" question before building either in isolation.
- **2026-08-05 grounding re-check at HEAD `43d4dda5` — premise INTACT on every limb; disposition FORK-SHAPED.** `_publish_atomic`'s `os.utime(entry_path, None)` refresh is at `protected_result_store.py:581`; the mtime-derived age comparisons at `:756`, `:777`, `:787`, `:794`; the B-77 first-observation grace at `:796` with the previous-sweep set at `:877-879`. Critically, **the TTL still has no floor**: `protected_result_store_ttl_seconds: float = Field(default=86400.0, gt=0.0, allow_inf_nan=False)` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/types.py:1879`), so a below-granularity TTL remains a **supported** configuration — the exact ground on which the "no realistic operator" dismissal was rejected. The narrowed residue is still pinned as an executable assertion labelled `REGISTERED RESIDUAL (B-74)` at `harness-runtime/tests/test_lifecycle_protected_result_store.py:1943`/`:1978`, inside `test_coarse_filesystem_mtime_granularity_does_not_lose_a_live_entry_on_sight` (`:1924`). **Decision required:** pick a concrete resolution floor, or move the age authority off raw mtime entirely.
- **⚠️ Linkage correction (2026-08-05).** This row is **not** deferred pending `B-96`'s ratification, and no row surface has ever said it was. This row's own cross-reference names **`B-77`** (now closed), and its close-out is stated as *"unchanged and still the fix"* — not gated on `B-96`. The relation appears only from **`B-96`'s** side, which names this row as *"open — the filesystem-granularity dimension of the same mtime-as-age-authority question"* and adds *"All three re-check together."* The two are **siblings sharing one root question** (does the age authority stay mtime?), not a dependency. **B-74 was independently actionable at that pass — and the shared root question is now ANSWERED.** *(2026-08-05: `B-96` ratified as Reading C with ceiling **C-2**, so the age authority does **not** stay mtime. Per the council record §8 this row's residue is **dissolved, not narrowed**, and it closes at the `B-96` impl leg — see the ratification-leg bullet at the top of this block. The sibling-not-dependency reading above stays correct as history: the two rows were never in a formal blocking relation; they shared a question, and that question now has an answer.)*
- **Close-out steps.** Design a TTL-floor validation or a probe-based age-authority selection that accounts for the deployment filesystem's actual timestamp resolution — e.g. probe the store root's filesystem granularity at construction/first-write time (write a marker file, read back its mtime precision) and either refuse a TTL below that floor with a typed error, or fall back to a higher-resolution age signal (e.g. a companion sidecar file recording a monotonic sequence number or a separate high-resolution timestamp store) when the TTL is below the floor. Witness with a test that simulates a coarse-mtime filesystem (e.g. via a monkeypatched `os.stat`/`os.utime` rounding to whole seconds) and a TTL below that resolution, asserting the store either refuses the TTL or does not lose the live entry.
- **Council: no** — narrow, filesystem-dependent TTL-precondition gap; the fix requires picking a concrete resolution floor which is a design decision, not an immediate judgment call.

### B-75 · Protected result store's gc_sweep candidate-selection scan can itself stall inside the publish lock under a pathological backlog or a hanging filesystem *(surfaced at the B-68 impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 8 [P1], 2026-07-25; FIXED 2026-07-26 -- PR #1122, CLOSED)*

- **What it is.** Surfaced at round 8 — a finding directly about round 7's OWN fix, the third consecutive round to surface an issue in the immediately-prior round's change (round 6→7→8). Round 7 narrowed `gc_sweep`'s lock to a fast, `stat()`-only candidate-selection phase specifically to bound lock-hold time against a slow DECRYPT phase (see B-68's closed row). Codex round 8 observes that even this narrowed phase — `glob()` + `stat()` over every `*.entry`/`.tmp-*` file, still inside the lock — is itself unbounded in a MORE EXTREME scenario: a pathologically large backlog (far larger than what makes decrypt slow, since `stat()` is orders of magnitude cheaper per file), or a filesystem mount that hangs/stalls on `stat()` itself (e.g. a dead network mount). Under `run_off_loop_detach_on_cancel`'s detach semantics, a shutdown sweep stuck in THIS phase would ALSO get detached while still holding the lock, reopening the same class of liveness hazard round 7 closed for the decrypt phase specifically.
- **Current state.** CLOSED. Registered, not built — was the state through round 8's own registration — per `advisor()`'s explicit round-8 guidance: three consecutive rounds each surfacing a defect the PRIOR round's own fix introduced is the non-convergent-adversarial-hardening-arms-race signature (this workspace's own standing discipline) — stop patching, register, and ship rather than open a round 9. Reachability is genuinely narrower than round 7's finding (needs either an extreme file count or a hanging/failing filesystem mount, not merely a large-but-normal backlog), and a failing filesystem mount would likely be causing failures well beyond this store already. **Escalation (advisor(), B-76 arc, 2026-07-26):** `B-73`'s cross-process `flock` is now ALSO held across this candidate-selection phase, so a stalled `glob()`/`stat()` scan blocks other OS PROCESSES sharing the store root, not just other threads in this process — worse than this row's original P1 framing. Own arc, not a continuation of B-76's.
- **Close-out steps.** Bound the candidate-selection phase itself — e.g. batch the `glob()`/`stat()` scan with a periodic lock release/re-acquire (yielding between batches so a stalled scan cannot monopolize the lock indefinitely), or move the scan itself off-lock using a snapshot-then-verify pattern (enumerate + stat unlocked, then re-verify each candidate's mtime under a BRIEF lock hold immediately before acting on it — mirroring how phase 2's unlink already trusts a monotonic once-confirmed-expired fact, but applied one level earlier). Witness with a test that stalls `glob()`/`stat()` itself (not decrypt) and asserts a concurrent write still completes within a short bounded window.
- **Council: no** — narrow liveness-hardening follow-on to an already-shipped fix; the fix shape (batch/yield or snapshot-then-verify) is a known pattern, not an open design question.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-26 (PR #1122).** Selected via `advisor()` over the still-open `B-74`/`B-77` pair — its close_out already named a known fix shape (no open design question), it's the P1, and `B-73` escalated it to cross-process blast radius. Candidate ENUMERATION (`glob()`/`stat()` over `*.entry`/`.tmp-*`) now runs fully unlocked, producing PROVISIONAL candidates; each is re-verified in a single brief COMBINED lock acquisition before being trusted — never one acquisition per candidate (would turn `_cross_process_lock`'s per-call `fcntl.flock` into N kernel round-trips). Resolved advisor()'s flagged asymmetry (does the fix cover `.tmp-*`, or scope to `*.entry` only?) by hand: a `.tmp-*` file's mtime is not a trustworthy "definitely done" signal unlocked (it could be mid-write) the way an entry's is (monotonic expiry + fresh uuid4 keys) — but since `tempfile.mkstemp` itself only ever runs INSIDE the lock, a temp-file candidate that survives to be re-observed once the sweep holds the lock can only be a genuine crash orphan (its creator either already finished and already unlinked it, or crashed while holding a now-free lock). Same unlocked-scan-then-brief-relock-reverify pattern is correct and safe for both file types — not scoped to `*.entry` only. Two new regression tests: a structural witness recording whether `_publish_lock.locked()` is true at each `glob()` call (asserts unheld, not a wall-clock check per `[[verification-shape-sharpened-grep-vs-e2e]]`), and a stalled-enumeration concurrent-write test mirroring the existing stalled-decrypt pattern. Both mutation-probe-verified. Hand-traced the fix against the two most load-bearing pre-existing lock tests before writing code to confirm neither would regress — both pass unchanged. Full `harness-runtime` suite: 3087 passed, 10 skipped; ruff + pyright strict clean.

### B-76 · Protected result store's lock-key registry can fail open on a transient stat() failure during root-identity resolution *(surfaced at the B-68 impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 8 [P2], 2026-07-25; FIXED 2026-07-26 -- PR #1121, CLOSED)*

- **What it is.** `_lock_for_root` keys the process-wide lock registry on `(st_dev, st_ino)` when `resolved.stat()` succeeds, falling back to the resolved-path STRING when it raises `OSError` (a defensive branch added at round 6 for the not-yet-created-directory case, now effectively unreachable in normal operation since round 6's own fix made `_lock_for_root` unconditionally `mkdir` the directory before stat'ing). Codex observes the fallback is still live for a TRANSIENT `stat()` failure (not "doesn't exist yet", but a genuine intermittent I/O error) — if one concurrent caller's `stat()` transiently fails while another's (near-simultaneous) call succeeds, the two callers key DIFFERENT locks for the SAME logical root (one string-keyed, one inode-keyed), silently reopening the exact aliasing race the identity-based key exists to close.
- **Current state.** CLOSED. Registered, not built — was the state through the B-68 arc's round 8. Narrow: requires a genuinely intermittent filesystem error at the precise moment of a concurrent lock-key computation, not a sustained failure (a sustained failure would surface elsewhere — e.g. the `mkdir` immediately preceding this stat would itself already be failing loudly).
- **Close-out steps.** Do not silently fall back to a different key namespace on a `stat()` failure after a successful `mkdir` — propagate the `OSError` (or retry with a bounded backoff before propagating) so a transient failure surfaces as a typed refusal rather than a silent identity-namespace split. Witness with a test that monkeypatches `Path.stat` to fail once then succeed, asserting the lock registry does not admit two distinct lock objects for the same resolved root across that transient failure.
- **Council: no** — narrow transient-I/O-error handling gap; propagate-vs-fallback is a correctness fix, not an open design question.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-26 (PR #1121).** Selected via `advisor()` as the cleanest of the 4 findings surfaced at the same round (`B-74`/`B-75`/`B-76`/`B-77`, all in this file) — a genuinely mechanical propagate-vs-fallback fix with no interaction with `B-73`'s new cross-process flock and no reopening of the phase-1/phase-2 GC-sweep safety argument. Removed the `except OSError: key = str(resolved)` fallback; `resolved.stat()`'s `OSError` now propagates. Verified all 3 direct/indirect callers of `_publish_lock`/`_lock_for_root` already tolerate the raised error by direct grep (not just the docstring's own claim): `write_once` folds it to `UnresolvableResultRef`; the bootstrap (`stage_4_od.py`) and shutdown-step-5b (`shutdown.py`) `gc_sweep()` callers each wrap it in `except Exception`; `_maybe_opportunistic_gc_sweep` does too. Witnessed with a frame-targeted `Path.stat` monkeypatch (checks the immediate caller is `_lock_for_root` specifically) rather than a blind global intercept — `Path.resolve()`/`Path.mkdir()` both call `.stat()` internally in this pathlib version and each already swallows its own `OSError`, so a naive intercept gets absorbed there instead of ever reaching the line under test. Mutation-probe-verified: reverting the fix makes the new test fail (`DID NOT RAISE`); restoring it passes. `advisor()` additionally flagged that `B-74`/`B-77` are likely ONE finding (both concern raw mtime as an untrustworthy age authority — worth a combined grounding pass, not two separate builds) and that `B-73` made `B-75` WORSE (candidate selection now also holds the cross-process flock, so a stalled scan blocks other PROCESSES, not just threads) — both recorded at their own rows, not built here. Full `harness-runtime` suite: 3085 passed, 10 skipped; ruff + pyright strict clean.

### B-77 · Protected result store's mtime refresh is not durable atomically with the publish commit, leaving a crash window where a recovered entry looks pre-aged *(surfaced at the B-68 impl arc, out-of-family Codex round 8 [P2], 2026-07-25; CLOSED 2026-07-30 -- first-observation grace)*

- **THE `B-77` RESIDUAL IS NOW CLOSED (2026-08-05, `B-96` impl leg / `U-RT-150`).** The sweep-COUNT grace this row landed is replaced by a DURABLE ELAPSED-TIME one, so the residual practical-duration gap — a short or immediately-failing run whose own shutdown sweep fires milliseconds after its bootstrap sweep — no longer exists, and the persisted-sidecar reversal recorded below is now BUILT rather than merely ratified. **This row's own status was already `closed` and does not move.**
- **2026-08-05 — the *no persisted sidecar* judgment is REVERSED, and the reversal is recorded here so it is never later read as unratified drift.** The ratified `B-96` Reading C / ceiling **C-2** form publishes a **dedicated candidate-filename + timestamp sidecar** (carrier **(C-i)**, keyed over **both** sweep classes per council condition #5) by temp-write + `fsync` + `os.replace` + directory `fsync`. The reversal is **ratified** — operator `AskUserQuestion` 2026-08-05 on the `B-96` fork, with the C-1/C-2 sub-decision resolved by the convening at `.harness/council-b96-grace-ceiling-2026-08-01.md` (PR #1183). **The `B-77` residual flips to `closed` when the `B-96` impl leg merges**; this row's own status is already `closed` and does not move.
- **What it is.** `_publish_atomic` makes the entry durable in two separate steps: the `os.link` commit + its directory fsync (durability step 1), THEN a separate `os.utime` mtime refresh + its own fsync (durability step 2). If the process crashes BETWEEN these two steps (after the entry is durably linked and visible, but before its mtime is refreshed), the entry that survives the crash retains the TEMP FILE's original, pre-fsync-latency mtime — the exact stale timestamp the B-68 round-1 fix exists to move away from. The NEXT process's bootstrap sweep, reading this crash-recovered entry, would then see the OLD (potentially already-TTL-exceeded) mtime and could immediately reclaim an entry that in fact just barely finished publishing before the crash.
- **Current state.** NARROWED TWICE, not closed, 2026-07-26 (PR #1123). This PR went through THREE wrong claims before landing here, all caught by out-of-family Codex: round 1 tried to classify B-77 as dormant via a "sub-millisecond `os.link`-to-`os.utime` window" argument (wrong — the real pre-fix window was the FULL pre-link write+fsync duration, unbounded). Round 2 moved the SOLE mtime refresh from post-commit to pre-commit and claimed this "closes the window structurally" (wrong — Codex round 9 [P1] reproduced a DIFFERENT, normal-path regression against `main`: with the stamp now before the metadata-fsync+`os.link`+directory-fsync tail instead of after, a successful uninterrupted write could return a reference an IMMEDIATE sweep reclaims — `ttl_seconds=0.02` + a 100ms-delayed directory fsync — something that could never happen on `main`, where the stamp already ran after that tail). Round 3 (current): `_publish_atomic` now stamps TWICE — once pre-commit (on the temp file, for crash recovery) AND once post-commit (on the entry, restoring `main`'s exact original normal-path behavior) — rather than moving the single stamp. Strict improvement over `main` on both axes, no reopened ground. The residual crash window is now `os.link` → the post-commit refresh completing — the SAME shape B-77 originally named, starting from the fresher pre-commit baseline rather than write-time. Restoring the post-commit block also reintroduces a pre-existing, out-of-scope inconsistency the round-2 reorder had incidentally fixed: if the post-commit refresh's own fsync fails, `write_once` reports `UnresolvableResultRef` even though `entry_path` is already durably linked and readable — matches `main`'s original semantics, intentionally not fixed here. Mutation-probe-verified regression tests added for BOTH the crash-recovery path (pre-commit stamp) and the normal-path regression Codex round 9 found (post-commit stamp); the residual is registered, not tested — no fix for it has landed. `merge-gate`'s 3-lens review approved the round-2 diff; only the concurrency lens was re-run for round 3 (the durability-step change is inside the same lock its reasoning already covered) per advisor()-directed scope.
- **Close-out steps.** advisor()-directed: do NOT add a TTL floor — that is `B-74`'s own already-declined close_out option ("reject TTLs below a guaranteed timestamp resolution... a genuine design decision"), and the field is a spec'd deployment-configurable surface (Runtime §14.8.11's bounded-retention bullet, `:4883` at v1.108 — **cite corrected 2026-07-31**: §14.8.11 carries no AC numbering, so the prior "AC 7" resolved to nothing) Phase-7 impl discretion should not narrow. The actual fix is an age authority that cannot predate publication by construction, not a further reordering of a two-stamp pipeline: `gc_sweep` should not reclaim an entry it has not observed in a PRIOR sweep (a grace period) — bounded to one sweep interval, immune to arbitrary I/O latency in the publish path, implementable entirely inside `gc_sweep`/`_publish_atomic` without touching the config contract. Witness with a test that simulates a crash strictly BETWEEN `os.link` and the post-commit refresh completing (e.g. a monkeypatched post-commit `os.utime` that raises once) and asserts a subsequent bootstrap-style sweep does not reclaim the crash-recovered entry immediately.
- **Council: no** — the grace-period fix shape is a known pattern (first-observation gating), not an open design question; narrow implementation-discretion follow-on once picked up.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-30 (PR `#1163`, branch `b77-gc-first-observation-grace-20260730`).** The close_out above landed verbatim as a FIRST-OBSERVATION GRACE inside `gc_sweep` — no fourth reordering of the two-stamp pipeline, no TTL floor, no change to the `ttl_seconds` config contract. `gc_sweep` now records the filenames it verified past TTL under its own lock (`_observe_expired`) and reclaims only those a PRIOR sweep of the same root already recorded. **Persistence judgment (the central design call):** the record is module-wide, keyed by the root's filesystem identity (`_root_identity_key`, extracted from `_lock_for_root` so both key identically) — NOT per-instance. Grounded against the real call graph rather than the abstract pattern: the composition root builds a FRESH `ProtectedResultStore` per `run()`/`resume()` bootstrap (`bootstrap/factories/protected_result_store_factory.py:78` ← `bootstrap/stage_4_od.py:123`, which sweeps immediately), so a per-instance record would hand EVERY bootstrap sweep a fresh grace and defer reclaim to shutdown indefinitely, weakening the spec's own bounded-retention term. A fresh PROCESS legitimately starts with an empty registry — it cannot tell a genuine age from a crash-window artifact, so granting the grace is the safe direction, and that IS precisely the crash-recovery case this row names. Four mutation-probed witnesses: `test_crash_between_link_and_post_commit_refresh_survives_a_fresh_bootstrap_sweep` (the close_out's own recipe), `test_uninterrupted_write_survives_an_immediate_sweep_past_the_grace` (the PR #1123 round-2 normal-path regression class, swept twice so the grace cannot mask it), `test_genuinely_expired_entry_is_reclaimed_at_the_second_sweep_not_the_first` (liveness — one interval, not immortality), and `test_coarse_filesystem_mtime_granularity_does_not_lose_a_live_entry_on_sight` (the `B-74` re-assessment). Pre-existing single-sweep witnesses were updated to sweep twice at one pinned `now` (`_sweep_past_grace`) so their original TTL-classification discrimination is preserved rather than masked. Spec check before building: Runtime v1.106 §14.8.11's bounded-retention term requires GC sweeps at bootstrap/shutdown plus a periodic-or-opportunistic runtime sweep and a typed expiry report line — it states no reclaim-on-first-observation timing, so the grace violates no AC. The out-of-scope inconsistency this row also recorded (a failing post-commit refresh fsync reporting `UnresolvableResultRef` for an already-durably-linked entry) is UNCHANGED and still not fixed.

### B-78 · A `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` step's own `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY` gate under `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER`/`DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF` can exhibit the same pre-dispatch re-fire livelock `B-72` property 6 closes for the fan-out topologies, ungrounded by any reproduction *(split from B-72's spec leg, out-of-family Codex round 5+7, 2026-07-25; GROUNDED + IMPL LEG LANDED 2026-07-26 — PR #1117, CLOSED)*

- **What it is.** `B-72`'s CP spec v1.108 §1.2b scopes property 6 to ONLY the `PARALLELIZATION`/`ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS`/`HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` topologies — the ones whose gate-owning-branch pause state is captured via the `PeerFanOutResumeState`/`FanOutResumeState` carrier family (`HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` included on carrier-identity grounds per round 6, since it recursively reuses `_execute_orchestrator_workers` per U-CP-88/89, not a separate implementation). A `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` step carrying its own `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY` placement under `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` or `DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF` is captured into a DIFFERENT carrier family instead (`EvaluatorOptimizerResumeState`/`HandoffResumeState`) and can plausibly exhibit the SAME re-fire-on-resume symptom `B-72`'s round-3 reproduction pins for the fan-out case.
- **Current state.** CLOSED. Registered, not built, not even reproduced — was the state through round 7. This has never been directly grounded against those carriers' own code paths — round 5 first flagged it as an explicit exclusion in `B-72`'s spec leg; round 7 (out-of-family Codex, [P2]) flagged that the exclusion needed its own durably-tracked register row, not just correction-history prose buried inside `B-72`.
- **Close-out steps.** A future arc's own reproduction-first grounding pass (mirroring how `B-72`'s round-3 repro preceded its own spec leg): construct a real `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` or `DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF` workflow whose `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` step carries `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY`, confirm (or falsify) that its own pre-dispatch gate re-fires identically on resume, and only then determine whether a property-6-shaped fix (or a materially different one, given the different carrier shape) is warranted — not yet designed, not yet specified.
- **Council: no** — narrow topology-specific livelock candidate with a clear grounding-first next step (reproduce before designing), mirroring `B-72`'s own precedent; not a judgment call yet.

### B-79 · A resumed branch's `HITLDeliveryCell` is constructed from `step_id` identity alone, so a HITL placement/gate-configuration change between pause and resume is not detected as a material diff *(surfaced at the B-72 impl leg, out-of-family Codex round 3 (branch-vs-main), 2026-07-25; SPEC LEG + IMPL LEG SLICE 1 LANDED 2026-07-27 — PR #1132; IMPL LEG SLICE 2 LANDED 2026-07-27 — PR #1133, CLOSED)*

- **What it is.** Out-of-family Codex round 3 (branch-vs-main, B-72 impl leg PR #1116, 2026-07-25). The B-72 impl leg's `_resume_body_mismatch` guard (mirroring the pre-existing `effect_fence_paused_branches`/`paused_child_branches` precedent) validates a pre-dispatch gate-owning branch's `step_id` identity before delivering the operator's resolved response, but does not validate whether the branch's HITL placement (e.g. `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY`) or `step_kind` still applies to the resumed step. If a workflow is edited between pause and resume while preserving the branch's `step_id` — removing its `SUB_AGENT_BOUNDARY` placement, for instance — the guard still accepts the resume and `RuntimeHITLGateComposer`'s Step 0 unconditionally consumes and applies the stored `HITLDeliveryCell` (e.g. a REJECT) to the now-ungated branch, before any current-placement evaluation runs. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by the B-72 impl leg — the identical unconditional construction (no placement-identity check at all) already exists at the already-shipped LINEAR `resume_at` delivery-cell site (`workflow_driver.py` ~4748-4777, landed at the B-39 impl leg), which B-72's fan-out wiring mirrors verbatim — confirmed by direct grep/read of that site before registering this row, per this workspace's own `[[codex-finding-scope-verify-sibling-pattern]]` discipline.
- **Current state.** Registered, not built.
- **Close-out steps.** Design a HITL placement/gate-configuration identity check (e.g. persisting the resolved set of applicable HITL placements, or a content hash of the step's HITL-relevant fields, alongside `step_id` at pause-capture time) and validate it at BOTH the LINEAR `resume_at` site and the fan-out `_resume_body_mismatch` closures (`_execute_parallelization`/`_execute_orchestrator_workers`) before a `HITLDeliveryCell` is constructed — reject the resume as a material diff if the check fails, mirroring the existing step_id/step_kind precedent. This is a genuine design task (what identity to persist, and whether the composer's own persona/engine-class placement-resolution logic — which `harness-cp` does not have visibility into, that logic being Runtime-owned — needs a new cross-axis seam to expose it), not a mechanical patch. Witness with a test that edits a paused step's HITL placement (or step_kind) between pause and resume while preserving `step_id`, and asserts the resume is rejected as a material diff rather than silently delivering the stale response.
- **Council: likely.** A dyadic pass (a design task touching a Runtime-owned cross-axis seam, not mechanical) — C10 (blast-radius/gate-integrity, mirroring the B-72 spec-leg's own prior falsified-draft caution) paired with whichever voice owns the CP↔Runtime HITL-placement-resolution boundary. Not urgent — the reachability precondition (an operator edits a workflow's HITL placements between an in-flight pause and its resume) is narrow, and this gap is symmetric with an already-shipped LINEAR mechanism that has not surfaced in production.
- **CONVENED 2026-07-27 (roadmap-continue, dyadic `council-orchestrator` pass, C10 + C1 co-primary; C11 considered and recused — the register's "HITL" phrasing invited it by association, but C1's own SKILL.md draws the boundary explicitly: "C1 owns *where* HITL plugs in; C11 owns the *primitive*," and this question is squarely placement, not primitive).** The convened agent ran the orchestrator's mandatory probe-first discipline BEFORE any deliberation, and the probe **falsified this row's own premise**: "the composer's own persona/engine-class placement-resolution logic... is Runtime-owned, and `harness-cp` does not have visibility into it" is false for the scenario in scope. Direct read confirmed `step_context.hitl_placements` (via `fold_step_hitl_placements`, computed at every dispatch/resume site e.g. `workflow_driver.py` lines 5107-5114, 7885-7890, 8051-8060, 11832-11840) and `StepEffectiveBinding.removed_placements` (`per_step_override_evaluator.py:259-362`) are BOTH CP-native, deterministic folds already available at pause-capture time — `hitl_gate_composer.py:1752-1762`'s own inline comment confirms the Runtime composer only *consumes* `step_context.hitl_placements`, which is "surfaced onto the per-step `StepExecutionContext` at workflow-binding time by the CP driver." Only the gate-*level* computation (persona_tier × blast_radius × mcp_trust_tier) is genuinely Runtime-resolved, and that's a function of deployment configuration, not the workflow-body edit this row's reachability precondition names — **so no new cross-axis seam is needed**, contrary to the close-out steps' own framing above. One TENSION surfaced and probe-resolved: C1 initially proposed hashing only `HITLPlacement.position` (narrower, cheaper); C10 wanted the full applicability surface covered (a `tool_filter`/`cascade_policy`/`timeout` edit on the same placement kind would otherwise slip through). Re-checking the evidence found `HITLPlacement` (`hitl_placement.py:176-197`) is itself a frozen 4-field Pydantic model already inside the SAME tuple C1 proposed hashing — hashing all 4 fields costs nothing extra over the narrow framing, so both voices converged on the broader hash with zero additional plumbing cost. **Recommendation:** persist a SHA-256 content hash over `(ordered HITLPlacement tuple, sorted removed_placements)` on the existing pause-capture carriers (`PausedChildBranchResumeState`/`PreDispatchGateOwningBranchResumeState`, drop-when-`None` byte-compat mirroring the B-31 `child_workflow_id`/B-72 `step_kind` precedent exactly) plus a new analogous carrier for the LINEAR `resume_at` site — the probe found that site has NO per-step identity check at all today, not even `step_id`, a slightly larger gap than the fan-out sites this row originally scoped; a companion fix is also owed at `hitl_gate_composer.py`'s Step 0 short-circuit (~1684-1750), which never gates delivery on placement drift today. **Fix size:** mechanical-with-a-thin-design-decision, not a genuine architectural task. **Classification: Class 1** — every prior material-diff-identity addition to these same carriers (`step_kind`; `child_workflow_id` at B-31/v1.99; the B-72 pre-dispatch-gate-owning identity itself at v1.107→v1.108) went through a CP spec-leg amendment before impl per `C-CP-26` PauseResumeProtocol authority; this is architecturally identical in kind, not a bug-fix-shaped impl-discretion call. **Next action:** open a CP spec-leg (fork doc, or a B-72-lineage follow-on) proposing the additive field(s) + a new §1.x invariant mirroring property 6's shape, before any impl. Not yet opened this pass — this update is doc-only.
- **SPEC LEG LANDED 2026-07-27 — `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_110.md` §1 (property 7) + `Implementation_Plan_Control_Plane_v2_46.md`, co-designed with `B-80`.** Before drafting, every load-bearing call-graph claim from the convening above was independently re-verified against current HEAD (per this same session's own `B-71` arc lesson about a spec delta built on an unverified premise): `PreDispatchGateOwningBranchResumeState`'s exact field shape (`branch_index`/`step_id`/`step_kind`/`child_workflow_id`, `pause_resume_protocol_types.py:208-252`); `HITLPlacement`'s exact 4-field, frozen, hashable shape (`hitl_placement.py`); `fold_step_hitl_placements`'s CP-native fold (`workflow_driver_types.py`); `removed_placements`' CP-native origin (`per_step_override_evaluator.py`, `hitl_placement.py`, `workflow_manifest_entry.py`); and the Runtime composer's Step 0 unconditional-delivery shape (`hitl_gate_composer.py:1684-1750`, confirming `resumed_placements`/`resumed_matching` are computed ONLY for the audit entry, never gating delivery) — all confirmed exactly as the convening found. Property 7 requires the gate-configuration identity be validated unchanged at the fan-out closure's pre-dispatch-gate-owning delivery site, the LINEAR `resume_at` site, the `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` site, and the `DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF` site (all 3 sequential sites carry no per-step identity check of any kind today; a net-new carrier, shared or per-site, is authorized); a Runtime-side defense-in-depth check at Step 0 is left to impl discretion, not required, since a rejected CP-side resume never constructs a `HITLDeliveryCell` for the paths this property covers. **4 out-of-family codex findings caught before merge across 2 rounds, all fixed:** (1) [P1] round 1: an initial draft ALSO authorized this field on `PausedChildBranchResumeState` — WRONG, confirmed by direct read (`workflow_driver.py:8016-8058`) that carrier only forwards `child_resume_snapshot` to a recursively-dispatched child's own, separate `execute_workflow()` call and never itself constructs a `HITLDeliveryCell` (that only happens for `branch_index in _recovered_pre_dispatch_gate_owning`, `workflow_driver.py:8036-8045`) — a hash there would neither close a real gap NOR be neutral, it would incorrectly reject a valid resume whenever the PARENT's own unrelated placement config changed; corrected to scope §1.3a's carrier authorization to `PreDispatchGateOwningBranchResumeState` only (the child's own gate identity is covered recursively at its own `execute_workflow()` invocation); (2) [P2] round 1: §1.1(c) falsely claimed the rejection emits a C-CP-20 audit-ledger entry — confirmed by direct read that `_resume_body_mismatch`'s actual existing behavior is `RunResult(status=FAILED, fail_class=...)` only, no audit-ledger write; corrected to match; (3) [P2] round 1: the plan's "entirely CP-native, zero cross-axis cascade" claim was wrong for property 8 (see B-80's own update below); (4) [P1] round 2: property 7's scope entirely OMITTED the `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` (`workflow_driver.py:10789-10806`) and `DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF` (`workflow_driver.py:14803-14820`) delivery-cell construction sites — both landed later by the `B-78` impl leg (PR #1117) and confirmed by their own inline comments to mirror the LINEAR mechanism EXACTLY, sharing the identical no-per-step-identity-check gap; ### B-80 · The `_any_fence_abort` HITL-delivery suppression guard is scoped to the current fan-out level, not the true root of a nested resume tree *(surfaced at the B-72 impl leg, out-of-family Codex round 6 (branch-vs-main), 2026-07-25)*

- **What it is.** Out-of-family Codex round 6 (branch-vs-main, B-72 impl leg PR #1116, 2026-07-25). The round-4 fix suppresses a pre-dispatch gate-owning peer's `HITLDeliveryCell` construction when `_any_fence_abort` is true, but that value is computed from `_recovered_effect_fence_paused`, which is scoped to the CURRENT fan-out level's own recovered branches only. When an effect-fence ABORT targets a DIFFERENT, nested pause subtree (e.g. a deeper `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` level, or a sibling peer's recursively paused child), a shallower level's own `_any_fence_abort` stays false and its pre-dispatch gate-owning peer can still receive a delivery cell and dispatch before the run-level abort is honored — resumed branches are processed sequentially, so an earlier pre-dispatch branch can consume its HITL response and execute ahead of a later subtree processing the abort. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by the B-72 impl leg — `_any_fence_abort` itself was computed fan-out-locally by the B-70 impl leg (CP spec v1.107), and the pre-existing effect-fence-directive peer suppression already consumes that same narrow value; B-72's round-4 guard mirrors the established pattern verbatim. Affects BOTH the pre-existing effect-fence directive suppression and the new B-72 HITL delivery gate, at all four fan-out dispatch sites (`_execute_parallelization` and `_execute_orchestrator_workers`, including `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION`'s recursive reuse).
- **Current state.** Registered, not built.
- **Close-out steps.** Compute the abort guard from the true root of the resume tree (or thread a run-level abort signal down through the recursive `_execute_orchestrator_workers`/`HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` calls) rather than from the current level's own `_recovered_effect_fence_paused`, and consume it uniformly at both the pre-existing effect-fence-directive suppression site and the B-72 pre-dispatch HITL delivery-cell gate. This is a genuine design task (what "true root" means for a peer fan-out vs. a recursively nested `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION` tree, and how to thread it without a new cross-axis seam), not a mechanical patch. Witness with a test where a nested/deeper subtree's effect-fence ABORT races a shallower sibling subtree's pre-dispatch HITL delivery in the same resume round, and assert the shallower delivery is suppressed.
- **Council: likely.** A dyadic pass (a design task touching cross-recursion-boundary abort propagation, not mechanical) — C1 (orchestration/topology, owns `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION`'s recursive reuse) paired with C10 (blast-radius/gate-integrity, mirroring B-79's own reasoning). Not urgent — the reachability precondition (a nested subtree ABORT racing a shallower pre-dispatch HITL delivery in the SAME resume round) is narrow, and the suppression gap is symmetric with an already-shipped effect-fence-directive mechanism that has not surfaced in production.
- **CONVENED 2026-07-27 (roadmap-continue, dyadic `council-orchestrator` pass, C1 + C10 co-primary).** The convened agent's probe-first check confirmed `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION`'s "recursion" is NOT same-stack-frame Python recursion — each nesting level re-enters via a FRESH `execute_workflow()` call across the CP→Runtime→CP boundary (`RuntimeSubAgentDispatcher` → `ChildWorkflowRunner` → `execute_workflow`), and TWO existing sibling values — `hitl_uniform_fallback_eligible_run_id` (B-39) and `effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key` (B-70, `workflow_driver.py:2873-2908`) — are ALREADY computed once at the true depth-0 root and threaded VERBATIM through this exact crossing (`execute_workflow()`'s signature → `_execute_orchestrator_workers()`/`_execute_parallelization()` → `child_workflow_runner.py`'s `ChildWorkflowRunner` Protocol), which is precisely B-70's own already-solved instance of this problem shape. **Recommendation:** a THIRD sibling value, `effect_fence_tree_wide_abort_present: bool`, computed once at depth-0 via a ~5-line helper reusing the EXISTING `_collect_effect_fence_idempotency_keys` tree walk + `_resolve_effect_fence_gated` resolver, threaded through the IDENTICAL channel as the two siblings, **OR**ed (not replacing) into the level-local `_any_fence_abort` at both consume sites — no new cross-axis seam, no new carrier field, satisfies this row's own registered constraint exactly. **TENSION probe-resolved** (blanket tree-wide boolean vs. a precise `cascade_policy`-chain walk, in favor of the blanket reading): (a) the already-shipped local-level rule this arc extends is itself `cascade_policy`-blind ("tier-agnostic FAILED" per CP spec v1.107 §1.1) — a `cascade_policy`-aware tree-wide extension would be MORE discriminating than the shipped convention it extends, out of family; (b) `PauseSnapshot` carries ZERO `cascade_policy` field anywhere in its schema (verified directly) — the precise reading would need a NEW durable carrier field, a strictly bigger, separately-scoped task. C1's precision concern is registered as a named, deliberately-declined refinement, not silently dropped — revisit only if a real production case demonstrates non-negligible over-suppression cost under `cascade_policy=proceed` nesting. **A genuine new finding, not resolvable as pure impl discretion:** the fix surfaces an undocumented interaction between TWO existing CP-spec invariants — §1.1's abort-suppression rule and §1.2 property 6's MANDATORY delivery for the sole-unaddressed pre-dispatch gate-owning branch (v1.108) — since widening `_any_fence_abort` tree-wide widens the circumstances under which that mandatory delivery is skipped. Traced empirically: this does NOT reintroduce a livelock (suppression only delays a peer by one resume round; the run either terminates `FAILED` via the abort's own path regardless, or a later round recovers the peer if the run turns out not doomed) — but the spec text as written does not currently reconcile §1.1 against §1.2 property 6 for the tree-wide case. **Fix size:** mechanical (one new pure function reusing two existing utilities + a parameter threaded through an existing channel + a 2-line `OR` at each of 2 consume sites + the already-specified witness test). **Classification: Class 1, not Class 3** — mirrors the B-70/B-72 precedent exactly (both routed through a CP spec delta + clearance marker + plan coverage-row before impl), and additionally owes the §1.1/§1.2-property-6 reconciliation as new spec prose (likely a new §1.1(c) or similar, noting the tree-wide suppression rule takes precedence over property 6's mandatory-delivery obligation, with the delayed-not-lost liveness rationale this convening worked out). **Next action:** route to a CP spec leg before any impl, co-designable with B-79 (both touch the same `_resume_body_mismatch`/pre-dispatch-carrier family). Not yet opened this pass — this update is doc-only.
- **SPEC LEG LANDED 2026-07-27 — `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_110.md` §2 (property 8) + `Implementation_Plan_Control_Plane_v2_46.md`, co-designed with `B-79`.** Before drafting, every load-bearing call-graph claim from the convening above was independently re-verified against current HEAD (per this same session's own `B-71` arc lesson): `execute_workflow()`'s own signature threading `effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key` through `_execute_orchestrator_workers`/`_execute_parallelization` and `child_workflow_runner.py`'s `ChildWorkflowRunner` Protocol at lines 88-89/185-186/258-259; `_any_fence_abort`'s exact consume sites at `workflow_driver.py:7999`/`8037` and `12257`/`12281`; and — the single most load-bearing check — that `compute_effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key` (`workflow_driver.py:2873-2908`) is a PURE COMPUTED VALUE derived fresh from the already-persisted `root_snapshot` at each resume call, never itself stored in `PauseSnapshot` — confirming property 8 needs NO new durable carrier, unlike property 6/7. §2.3 states the genuine new spec-prose reconciliation: property 8's tree-wide signal, once true, TAKES PRECEDENCE over property 6's §1.1(b) mandatory-delivery outcome — property 6's TEXT is unamended, only the circumstances under which it fires are now conditioned. **Out-of-family codex [P2] caught before merge:** an initial draft's plan text claimed "zero cross-axis cascade" for this property — WRONG, the new parameter's threading DOES touch the Runtime-owned `ChildWorkflowRunner` Protocol (`child_workflow_runner.py`) exactly like its two sibling parameters already do; corrected to state accurately: no NEW crossing point is introduced (the SAME established CP→Runtime→CP boundary the two siblings already use), but the touch itself is real, not absent — confirmed at this correction that neither sibling parameter is documented anywhere in `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` today, a pre-existing Runtime-spec coverage gap this delta does not attempt to backfill. Clearance at `.harness/clearance/spec-control-plane-v1-110-cleared-2026-07-27.md` + `.harness/clearance/implementation-plan-control-plane-v2-46-cleared-2026-07-27.md`. Register status flips `registered_finding` → `open` (the design-extension blocker is cleared; the impl leg — the new function, the parameter thread, the two `OR`-sites, the §1.1(b) precedence wiring, the witness test — is a separate follow-on arc, not yet built).
