### B-82 · Ollama dispatch branch never serializes the standard memory tools its selected access mode promises *(surfaced at the gate-(d) R-300 live re-confirmation, 2026-07-27; CLOSED 2026-07-27 — PR #1140)*

- **What it is.** `reflect_memory_provider_capabilities` reports `supports_standard_memory_tools=True` for `ollama` (verified empirically 2026-07-27), so `select_memory_access_mode` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/memory_access_mode.py:190-200`) returns `MemoryAccessMode.STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` for an ollama binding under a permissive policy. But the ollama arm of `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.dispatch` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`, the `elif provider_name == "ollama":` branch) has no standard-memory-tools counterpart to the openai arm's `_dispatch_openai_with_standard_memory_tools` — it calls the bare `_dispatch_ollama` unconditionally. The five C-MEM-14 tools the selected access mode promises are therefore never serialized into the ollama request, and no continuation loop exists to execute a returned tool call: **the selected mode silently degrades to no memory access at all.**
- **Why it is coupled to the OpenAI wire-name fix.** This is NOT itself a wire-name defect (`ollama.chat` was never handed a dotted `function.name` because it was never handed a memory tool at all). But fixing it *independently* of the wire-name map would **extend the OpenAI HTTP-400 failure class** — a dotted `tools[].function.name` rejected by `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$` — to any name-validating ollama build or downstream OpenAI-compatible shim. Any ollama injection must route through an adapter-owned wire encoding from the start.
- **Current state.** CLOSED. Discovered 2026-07-27 during the gate-(d) R-300 live re-confirmation, while diagnosing the OpenAI 400 that the wire-name map closes; deliberately left out of that fix's scope to keep the surgical diff surgical.
- **Class 3 doc-clarity observation (same discovery).** C-MEM-14's tool-name table (`Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` lines 485-497) reads as **identity-normative**, and the per-provider **wire encoding** of those identities is **adapter-owned** — not a spec-level rename. The `MemoryToolName` enum stays dotted and provider-neutral (`memory.search` ...); only the OpenAI adapter boundary re-spells it (`memory_search` ...). Recorded here so a future reader does not mistake the wire map for a C-MEM-14 divergence.
- **Close-out steps.** (1) Decide the ollama shape: `ollama.chat` accepts an OpenAI-compatible `tools=` array, so the most likely fix is an `_dispatch_ollama_with_standard_memory_tools` sibling reusing the same tool-schema builder + continuation loop, with the wire-name map (or an ollama-specific equivalent) applied at serialization AND at inbound resolve. Ground the actual ollama tool-call response shape against a real local daemon before writing the loop — do not assume it is byte-identical to OpenAI's `choices[].message.tool_calls[]`. (2) Alternatively, if standard memory tools are deliberately out of scope for ollama, the FIX IS IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: `reflect_memory_provider_capabilities` must stop reporting `supports_standard_memory_tools=True` for ollama so the selection degrades explicitly to `PROMPT_EXTENSION_PACKET` rather than silently to nothing. Either way the current state — a selected mode the dispatch branch does not serve — is a fail-silent gap. (3) Witness with a deterministic test that captures the kwargs handed to a fake `client.chat` and asserts either the tools are present under provider-safe names, or that the selected access mode is not `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` for an ollama binding.
- **Council: mixed.** No for the mechanical half (mirroring an existing, already-reviewed openai dispatch arm). YES if grounding shows option (2) is the right answer — narrowing a declared provider capability changes which memory access mode an entire provider family receives, which is a C-MEM-13 selection-semantics decision, not impl discretion.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-27 (PR #1140) — direction (1) built; the wire-name coupling DISSOLVED by grounding, so the council gate this row raised never fired.** A live probe against the local ollama daemon (`llama3.2:3b`, client `ollama==0.6.2`) confirmed `/api/chat` accepts the DOTTED C-MEM-14 provider-neutral identities (`memory.search` ...) verbatim in `tools[].function.name` and echoes them back unchanged in `message.tool_calls[].function.name` — ollama imposes NO `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$` name grammar, so **there is no wire-name map on this path**. The "coupled to the OpenAI wire-name fix" framing above is therefore superseded: adding an ollama wire-name map would encode a **false capability claim** about the provider, and would additionally require an inbound re-resolve for names ollama never mangles. Direction (2) — narrowing `reflect_memory_provider_capabilities` — was REJECTED on the same grounding: ollama genuinely supports tool calling, so declaring otherwise would amputate the WRITE half of C-MEM-14 (`memory.write_note` / `memory.propose_promotion` / `memory.request_redaction` are unreachable through a prompt-extension packet) for the entire local-open-weight family — a C-MEM-13 selection-semantics regression, not a fix. Because grounding settled direction (1) unambiguously, the row's own "YES if grounding shows option (2)" council condition was not met.
- **What shipped (PR #1140).** `_dispatch_ollama_with_standard_memory_tools` + 6 sibling helpers in `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`, gated by a branch guard byte-mirroring the OpenAI arm's predicate (`standard_memory_tool_executor is not None and memory_context is not None and memory_context.access_mode is STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS`). The loop mirrors the OpenAI arm's SHAPE (same `max_iterations=16` bound, same `_standard_memory_tool_context` scope_ref/policy_ref binding, same deepcopy-before-mutate schema discipline guarding the shared module-level `MEMORY_TOOL_CONTRACTS` against concurrent-dispatch aliasing, same `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` fail-loud convention) against ollama's DIFFERENT wire shapes: **no `choices[]` envelope** (the assistant turn is top-level `ChatResponse.message`, `ollama/_types.py:418`); **`arguments` arrives ALREADY DECODED** as a `Mapping[str, Any]` (`_types.py:346`), so the happy path does not `json.loads` (a JSON string is still tolerated defensively for hand-rolled stubs; junk and non-object payloads fail loud); and the typed client carries **no `tool_call_id` at all** — `Message`'s fields are `role`/`content`/`thinking`/`images`/`tool_name`/`tool_calls` (`_types.py:304-355`), and the daemon's tool-call id is dropped before it reaches Python — so the tool-result turn correlates BY NAME as `{"role": "tool", "tool_name": "<dotted identity>", "content": "<json>"}`; an extra `tool_call_id` key would be silently dropped by the pydantic model (default `extra='ignore'`), so it is deliberately not emitted. **Malformed-call semantics deliberately MIRROR OpenAI: fail-loud** — `_standard_memory_tool_context` raises `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` on a scope_ref mismatch and it propagates exactly as on the OpenAI path; a feed-the-error-back-as-a-tool-turn recovery mechanism was considered and rejected as a per-provider semantic divergence, i.e. a design extension. One adjacent rename: `_openai_function_tool_name` → `_function_tool_name` (the `{"type":"function","function":{"name"}}` envelope reader is genuinely provider-neutral; both arms now use it). **Witnesses:** 6 new deterministic tests in `harness-runtime/tests/test_lifecycle_llm_dispatch.py` — a serialization witness asserting all five DOTTED names plus a caller-supplied dotted duplicate deduped under a `len()` check (a set comparison alone cannot see a surviving duplicate) and the per-dispatch scope_ref/policy_ref binding leaving the shared contract schema unmutated; a loop witness asserting the executor receives the provider-neutral `MemoryToolName`, the tool-result turn's exact ollama shape, and usage read off the FINAL turn's `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count` with no `gen_ai.response.id`; an unknown-name raise (the OpenAI wire spelling `memory_search` is NOT tolerated here — it is a name this path never advertises); a malformed-arguments raise; a scope_ref-mismatch fail-loud; and a bare-path over-fire guard proving a `PROMPT_EXTENSION_PACKET` context injects no tools. Both mutation probes confirmed: reverting the branch guard fails 3 of them, dropping the tool-result-turn append fails the loop witness. The Class 3 doc-clarity observation above stands and is now sharper: the wire encoding is adapter-owned **per adapter** — the OpenAI boundary re-spells, the ollama boundary does not.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 1 — two durable-double-write defects, BOTH pre-existing in the OpenAI sibling, fixed symmetrically in the same PR.** The mandatory sibling check found the OpenAI loop has shared both shapes since it shipped, so fixing only the new ollama arm would have left the higher-traffic provider defective *and* introduced asymmetric semantics between two loops that are meant to mirror. **[P1] batch pre-validation.** Both loops resolved-and-executed each tool call lazily inside a `messages.extend(generator)`, so with a multi-call response an earlier — possibly `memory.write_note` — call committed *before* a later call was validated (unknown name / malformed arguments / `scope_ref` mismatch). Both loops now resolve and fully validate the COMPLETE batch first, via `_openai_prepared_memory_tool_calls` / `_ollama_prepared_memory_tool_calls` returning a `tuple[_PreparedMemoryToolCall, ...]`, and only then execute in order through `_openai_memory_tool_result_messages` / `_ollama_memory_tool_result_messages`. Fail-loud semantics are unchanged — any invalid call still fails the dispatch, just before side effects instead of mid-batch. **[P2] iteration bound.** Both loops let the 16th iteration execute its batch and only *then* raised loop-exhausted, committing a terminal write for a dispatch that reports failure. Both now check the bound BEFORE executing: if a response carries tool calls and no iteration budget remains to send their results back, the exhaustion error raises with nothing executed. **Why these were P1/P2 rather than cosmetic:** both aborts classify `TRANSIENT_RETRY` — `_classify_provider_exception` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:299-304`) fail-fasts only `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError` / `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` / HTTP 401-403 and maps everything else, including bare `RuntimeError` and `MemoryToolExecutionInputError`, to the transient staircase — so `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher` re-ran the whole dispatch from the top and the already-committed call executed a second time. **The exhaustion error type is deliberately unchanged** (the same generic `RuntimeError` both loops always raised, now built by the shared `_memory_tool_loop_exhausted` helper so the two messages cannot drift): re-typing it would change how retry routes loop exhaustion, which is a separate decision from the execute-before-raise defect and was explicitly out of scope. **4 further witnesses, one pair per provider** (a two-call batch whose second call is invalid → the executor receives ZERO calls; an all-tool-calls script driven to the bound → exactly 15 executions, 16 provider calls, exhaustion raised). Both new mutation probes confirmed: making the prepare functions lazy generators again fails both batch witnesses (the failure diff shows the leaked `MemoryToolName.WRITE_NOTE` request — the double-write class, made visible), and moving the bound check back after execution fails both iteration-bound witnesses.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 2 — two more [P1]s, again BOTH pre-existing on the OpenAI sibling, again fixed symmetrically.** **[P1-a] three of the five advertised tools were unreachable.** The dispatch-side `_standard_memory_tool_context` required `arguments["scope_ref"]` for every call, but only `memory.search` and `memory.write_note` declare `scope_ref`; `memory.read` / `memory.propose_promotion` / `memory.request_redaction` declare none **and** set `additionalProperties: false` (`harness-as/src/harness_as/memory_tool_contracts.py` — READ at `:181-217`, PROPOSE_PROMOTION at `:250-283`, REQUEST_REDACTION at `:284-307`), so a schema-conformant model *cannot* send one. Those three therefore failed at the dispatch boundary before ever reaching the executor. **Grounding verdict on OpenAI history:** latently broken there since the memory loop shipped — pre-round-1 `_openai_memory_tool_result_message` called `_standard_memory_tool_context(arguments, ...)` unconditionally with no per-tool branch, and the existing tests only ever exercised `memory.search`, which is one of the two tools that *does* declare the field. The check is now scoped to the declaring tools via `_MEMORY_TOOLS_DECLARING_SCOPE_REF`, derived from the contracts at import — mirroring **both** `_bind_schema_fixed_value`'s properties-presence authority **and** the executor's own partition, since `StandardMemoryToolExecutor._require_scope_ref` is reached only from `_search` and `_write_note` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:195` / `:262`). Nothing is weakened: the authoritative `scope_ref` on `MemoryToolExecutionContext` was always `RuntimeMemoryContext.scope_ref`, with the argument serving only as a cross-check — which is exactly why it can be scoped to the tools that carry one. **[P1-b] automatic memory broke ordinary tool workflows.** With standard-memory mode active, a caller's legitimate non-memory tool survives the dedup filter and is advertised — but a model call to it hit the memory resolver and raised `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError`. Both loops now classify the batch before touching it: if **any** call names something outside our advertised memory identities, the whole response is returned to the caller unprocessed with **zero** memory calls executed. **Grounding verdict on hallucinated names:** the bare paths (`_dispatch_openai` / `_dispatch_ollama`) return every `tool_call` to the caller untouched whatever it names — they never inspect names at all — so hallucinated names were always the caller's to handle. Returning them (rather than raising) is therefore bare-path parity, and raising would be a *new* failure mode that appears only once automatic memory is enabled — precisely the regression class this finding names. **Raises are now reserved for memory-named calls with malformed payloads**, i.e. a tool we advertised, called wrong. The choice also preserves round-1's batch atomicity: a mixed batch cannot half-commit memory before control returns. One adjacent simplification: the two round-2 accessors collapsed into the existing provider-neutral `_function_tool_name`, which reads the same `{"type":"function","function":{"name"}}` envelope for both the outbound `tools[]` array and the inbound `tool_calls[]` list. **6 further witnesses** (a `memory.read` executing end-to-end with no `scope_ref` argument; a mixed memory+caller batch returned whole with the executor untouched; a caller-only batch returned — one triple per provider), and one pre-existing witness was re-pointed: its "invalid second call" is now a *memory*-named call with malformed arguments, since a non-memory name is no longer an error. Both fixes mutation-probed — re-requiring `scope_ref` for every tool fails both `memory.read` witnesses, and dropping the caller-owned-batch return fails all four caller-tool witnesses with the exact `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` the finding reported.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 3 — two bounded [P2]s, again symmetric across both loops.** **[P2-a] the retryable exhaustion error masked a fail-fast one.** Round 2 placed the iteration-bound check before batch preparation, so a *malformed* memory call arriving in the **terminal** batch raised the generic exhaustion `RuntimeError` — which classifies `TRANSIENT_RETRY` — instead of `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError`, which is fail-fast. A request that can never succeed would therefore replay up to 16 provider calls per attempt, plus whatever writes the preceding 15 valid turns committed. Both loops now order the three guards correctly: caller-owned return → **validate the whole batch** → bound check → execute. Validation is pure, so moving it earlier costs nothing and cannot itself commit. **[P2-b] four fixtures used the wrong required key.** `memory.write_note` requires `note` (`harness-as/src/harness_as/memory_tool_contracts.py:218-249`), not `text`; all four corrected. **Grounding — where required-key validation actually lives:** the **executor**, not the dispatch layer. `StandardMemoryToolExecutor._write_note` reads it via `_string_arg(args, "note")` at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:266`, and `_string_arg` raises `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` at `:549-553`. The dispatch-side `_standard_memory_tool_context` validates only `scope_ref`/`policy_ref` presence-and-match — so **no** dispatch-side required-key validation was added (that would have been new semantics this arc has no authority for). Instead one witness now runs through a **real** `StandardMemoryToolExecutor` over a `tmp_path` filesystem store, constructed exactly the way `tests/test_memory_tool_executor.py::_executor` constructs it and pinned to the same `policy:u-mem-16` / `scope:u-mem-16` refs the dispatch fixtures already use — the fake executor validates nothing, so only a real one can witness this class at all. **4 further witnesses** (a malformed *terminal* batch failing fast rather than as exhaustion, one per loop; a real-executor `memory.write_note` round trip whose tool-result turn carries a genuine `memory_ref`/`operation_ref`, proving the write committed; the same call with `text` failing loud). Both fixes mutation-probed: reverting the reorder reproduces the masking `RuntimeError: … exceeded 16 continuation turns` verbatim on both loops, and restoring the `text` key fails at `memory_tool_executor.py:552`. A first draft of the terminal-batch witnesses was **found inadequate by its own probe** — they used a repeating canned response, so they raised on turn 1 and never reached the bound; the probe passed, which is what exposed them. Rewritten to script 15 valid turns followed by one malformed turn exactly at the bound (asserting 16 provider calls, 15 executions, and that the message is not the exhaustion text), after which the probe correctly failed.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 4 — one [P2] fixed, one bounded residual registered as `B-84`.** **[P2] usage was bundled from the final response only.** Both loops returned `_provider_response_bundle(final_response)`, whose usage reads that one response — so every continuation turn's tokens vanished from turn capture, `gen_ai.usage.*`, and cost attribution. **Sibling verdict: the OpenAI arm shared the shape verbatim** — `_openai_response_bundle` read `getattr(response, "usage", None)` off whichever single response it was handed, exactly like `_ollama_response_bundle` read that response's `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`. Both now thread a running `_UsageAttrs` accumulator through the loop, folding each turn in immediately after the provider call and *before* any exit path, so the caller-owned-batch return and the no-tool-calls return both carry full totals. `None` is treated as **absent, not zero** (a turn the provider reported nothing for must neither invent a `0` total nor erase counts already accumulated), and `response_id` is deliberately **not** accumulated — it identifies one response, so the bundle keeps the final turn's, unchanged. Witnessed by extending both existing loop tests rather than adding parallel ones: their two calls already carry distinct counts (10/4 then 12/5 on OpenAI; 20/8 then 31/9 on ollama), so the asserted sums are discriminating against *both* a final-turn-only reading and a first-turn-only one. Mutation-probed — collapsing the accumulator back to the per-turn value fails both, with `assert 12 == (10 + 12)` and `assert 31 == (20 + 31)`. **The registered residual (`B-84`):** an executor-level argument failure — e.g. `memory.read` missing the contract-required `memory_ref` — still occurs *mid-batch* during sequential execution, so a valid earlier write commits before the later call raises, and the transient classification then re-runs the dispatch and duplicates the write. Deliberately **not** fixed here: the naive fix (full per-tool contract prevalidation at the dispatch layer) would mirror-copy the executor's required-key and policy semantics into a second location — the drift class this workspace treats as a defect in its own right, and directly against round 3's grounded boundary that required-key enforcement lives at the executor.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 5 — non-tool-template ollama models were regressed by the injection itself.** `reflect_provider_capabilities` returns `supports_tools=True` for **every** ollama model string (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/provider_capabilities.py:127`, pre-existing), so `select_memory_access_mode` picks `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` even for a model with no tool template — e.g. `llava-llama3` — and the new branch then sends `tools=`, which the daemon rejects with a 400. A dispatch that worked as plain text before B-82 started failing. **Fixed narrowly, with the daemon as the authority rather than a capability table** (a per-model table is a real design question and deliberately out of scope): on the **first** chat call of the memory loop only, a tool-unsupported rejection re-dispatches through the bare `_dispatch_ollama` **without** tools, byte-restoring the pre-B-82 path for exactly those models. *(Superseded at B-83 / PR #1142: the retry remains tool-free — the daemon fix is intact — but now carries the C-MEM-12 packet folded into the single system source when the B-83 repair is authorized; the byte-restore property was itself B-83's defect on this path.)* First call only — a mid-loop rejection would mean the model changed identity between continuation turns, which stays fail-loud. **Both SDK facts were probed live rather than assumed:** `ollama.ResponseError` (`ollama/_types.py:632-651`) carries only `.error` (str) and `.status_code`, giving no machine-readable discriminator, and against a local daemon on ollama 0.6.2 the tool rejection is `.error = 'registry.ollama.ai/library/llava-llama3:latest does not support tools'` with `.status_code = 400`, while a model-not-found is the *same type* with `.error = "model 'x' not found"` and `.status_code = 404` — so a blanket `except ResponseError` would have swallowed unrelated faults, and the message substring really is the only available discriminator. **The brittleness is documented at the catch site**: matching an upstream string means an upstream rewording stops the match — but it then fails **closed** (a loud dispatch failure), never silently absorbing a different error. The predicate duck-types on the class name plus the `.error` substring rather than importing `ollama`, keeping this module free of provider-SDK imports like every other dispatch branch; the *tests* use the real `ollama.ResponseError`, so the shape stays faithful. **The OpenAI loop needs no equivalent and none was added** — every OpenAI chat model supports tools, so the failure mode does not exist there and a mirrored catch would be dead code. **3 witnesses, each mutation-probed against a distinct conjunct:** removing the fallback fails the fallback witness; widening the catch to any `ResponseError` fails the model-not-found propagation witness; dropping the first-call restriction fails the mid-loop fail-loud witness. A **fourth** issue Codex raised in the same round — the SDK silently dropping declared schema constraints — was verified, judged an aggravator of an existing registered class rather than a new defect, and **recorded on `B-84`** instead of fixed here. Full harness-runtime non-e2e suite green (**3123 passed / 10 skipped**).

### B-83 · No dispatch-side guard that the selected `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` access mode is actually served by the provider arm reached *(surfaced by the B-82 fix, 2026-07-27; CLOSED 2026-07-28 — PR #1142)*

- **What it is.** B-82 was one instance of a general shape: `select_memory_access_mode` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/memory_access_mode.py:158-245`) picks an access mode from *declared provider capabilities*, and `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.dispatch` then routes to a *provider arm* — but nothing checks that the arm reached actually serves the mode selected. With B-82 closed, both arms that `reflect_memory_provider_capabilities` can select `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` for (openai, ollama) now serve it, so the defect is not currently reachable through the DEFAULT capability reflection. It remains reachable two ways: **(a)** a caller supplying `MemoryAccessModeRequest.provider_capabilities` explicitly (the `request.provider_capabilities or reflect_...` short-circuit at `memory_access_mode.py:163-166`) can declare `supports_standard_memory_tools=True` for anthropic or an external-CLI binding, whose dispatch arms ignore memory tools entirely — the anthropic arm branches only on `step_has_memory_tool(payload.tools)`/`hitl_tool_loop`, never on access mode, and `_payload_to_external_cli_prompt` is text-only by contract; **(b)** more importantly, a **statically injected** `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.memory_context` (the no-`memory_runtime` path at `llm_dispatch.py:1302`) is composed ONCE and is NOT recomposed when `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher` rebinds the provider per attempt (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:188-191` constructs a fresh `StepEffectiveBinding` with a different provider) — so a context composed for openai under `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` can be dispatched against an anthropic or external-CLI fallback and degrade to zero memory access, silently. The `memory_runtime`-bound path is NOT affected (it recomposes per attempt via `compose_for_dispatch`).
- **Grounding note — what this row is NOT.** The B-82 grounding pass also checked whether C-MEM-13's `no_memory_access is a valid policy outcome and must be ledgered when memory was requested` (`Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:463`) lacks a ledgering witness. It does NOT: `MemoryContextComposer.compose_run_start` ledgers the denial via `_write_injection_decision` and emits a `DENIAL` telemetry span with `POLICY_DENIAL` failure class (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_context.py:165-205`), and a direct witness already exists at `harness-runtime/tests/test_memory_context.py:364-388` (`test_no_memory_access_denial_is_explicit_and_ledgered_without_retrieval`). That candidate finding is recorded here as CHECKED-AND-CLOSED rather than registered, so a future reader does not re-open it.
- **Reachability (c) — DEFAULT-reachable, added 2026-07-27 correcting this row's own earlier claim.** This row originally asserted the defect was "not reachable through the default capability reflection". **That is false, and was falsified by the B-82 round-5 fallback filed the same day.** `reflect_provider_capabilities` returns `supports_tools=True` for every ollama model string (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/provider_capabilities.py:127`), so a model with no tool template — `llava-llama3`, say — selects `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` through **plain default reflection**, and the round-5 fallback then deliberately re-dispatches it bare, with no memory access at all and **no ledger trace of the degradation**. That is precisely this row's shape: a selected access mode the reached provider path does not serve, degrading silently. The fallback is still the right call for its own problem (it byte-restores a previously-working text dispatch, and the daemon is the only authority on which models take tools) — it simply makes B-83 reachable on the default path rather than only via the two exotic routes below, which raises this row's priority. Recorded here rather than fixed because the honest fix is the same posture decision (1) already owes.
- **Adjacent, same family — the caller-owned mixed-batch return.** When a response mixes a memory call with a caller-advertised tool call, both loops return the whole response unprocessed (B-82 round 2, for batch atomicity + bare-path parity). The memory call the model asked for is therefore **not served, and nothing records that it wasn't** — the caller cannot execute it either, since it does not own the memory tools. Same fail-silent family as this row, and it is a *consequence of a deliberate tradeoff* rather than an independent defect, so it is recorded here under this row's scope rather than registered separately: whatever posture (1) settles on — fail-loud, or explicit ledgered degradation — should cover this exit path too.
- **Current state.** **CLOSED 2026-07-28 (PR #1142)** — dispatch-time serve-check + repair-to-packet, covering (a), (b) and (c) from one authority.
- **What was built.** `_standard_memory_tools_context` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`) is now the single predicate answering *"will THIS dispatch inject the C-MEM-14 tools?"*, read by both provider arm guards **and** by the serve-check, so the branch taken and the check applied cannot disagree. Its provider-identity conjunct (`selection.selected_provider != provider_name`) **detects** **(b)** — `MemoryAccessModeSelection.selected_provider` is `request.model_binding.provider` verbatim (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/memory_access_mode.py:372`), the same string that reaches the dispatch, and the `memory_runtime`-bound path recomposes per attempt so the conjunct is inert there. When `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` was selected and the arm will not serve it — anthropic, external-CLI, or an openai/ollama dispatch with no bound executor — the already-retrieved, already-policy-checked C-MEM-12 packet is rendered into the effective system prompt through a new `render_packet_for_degraded_dispatch` sibling in `memory_context.py` (identical body to `render_prompt_extension_packet` via a shared `_render_packet`; only the access-mode gate is dropped, so every existing caller is byte-identical) and appended through the shared `append_rendered_memory_packet` seam. Reachability **(c)** repairs at its own site inside the ollama loop and reports the repair back on a third return element, so one emitter covers all three.
- **Two dispositions — repair vs. report-only** *(split at out-of-family Codex round 1, [P1-a])*. **(a)** and **(c)** are **repaired**: the context was composed *for the dispatched provider*, so its packet is provider-matched by construction and discloses nothing the selection had not already cleared. **(b)** is **report-only** — neither the tools *nor the packet* reach the rebound provider. Retrieval and injection enforce **provider-family scope before ranking** (`Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:481`) and the packet was assembled under provider X's `MemoryScope.provider_family`, so forwarding its *text* to a Y-family provider bypasses that scope boundary — a **disclosure** leak, which read-only framing does not fix and which the write-authority argument this row originally gave does not cover. Recomposition is impossible on that path by construction (it is definitionally the `memory_runtime`-**unbound** configuration) and fail-closed would convert a silent degradation into a run failure, so the degradation is made **visible** in telemetry rather than repaired.
- **Telemetry.** Exactly one `memory.operation` span per degraded dispatch, with every attribute reporting what *actually* happened so the two dispositions are distinguishable without parsing a reason string. **Repaired** — `operation_name=injection`, `operation_kind=inject`, `access_mode=prompt_extension_packet`, the *served* `packet_hash` + `record_count`, and **no** `failure_class` (a successful injection through a different seam, not a failure). **Report-only** — `operation_name=denial`, `operation_kind=inject`, `access_mode=no_memory_access`, `record_count=0`, and **no** `packet_hash` (claiming a served hash for a withheld packet would be a lie); this mirrors `compose_run_start`'s own DENIAL+INJECT shape for the no-memory outcome. `failure_class` is deliberately unset on both: no member of the closed `MemoryTelemetryFailureClass` describes a provider-scope mismatch, and reusing `POLICY_DENIAL` would assert a decision no resolver made. The B-83 detail (`memory.degraded_serve` + `.reason` — `arm_unservable` | `provider_scope_mismatch` — + `.selected_access_mode`) lands on the memory tracer's span only, never on the `gen_ai` span, per C-OD-04 §4.3 namespace discipline; the reasons are span-attribute **values**, never new enum members.
- **Posture chosen — repair, not fail-loud.** Close-out step (1) leaned toward the fail-loud raise. Grounding reversed it: a raise turns a currently-silent degradation into a **run failure** for any deployment on the injected-context + fallback shape, while C-MEM-13 (`Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:460` — "Providers without usable tool support may receive prompt-extension packets") already sanctions serving the packet. C-MEM-14 (`:489`) states the exposure as a present-tense obligation, so serving *something* is the contract-faithful reading. Both cites verified byte-exact at the arc.
- **NOT built, deliberately — recorded so nobody silently absorbs it.** The literal *"explicit **ledgered** degradation"* half of close-out step (1) was **not** implemented. Writing a degradation *entry* (as opposed to the span above) is fork-shaped: the load-bearing blocker is the **absent store carrier on the dispatch path** (the memory-operation sink is reachable only via the composer/executor privates; a dispatcher-visible carrier is a new Protocol/field surface), i.e. an X-AL-3 design extension routed through back-flow, not impl discretion. *(Qualified at the merge-gate: an entry reusing the run-start DENIAL+INJECT shape needs no new enum members — `compose_run_start` already ledgers a no-memory outcome with existing members; new members on the three closed enums — `MemoryOperationKind`, `MemoryTelemetryOperationName`, `MemoryTelemetryFailureClass` — would be required only for a dispatch-time-DISTINCT operation kind, if one were wanted.)*
- **Behavior change, flagged.** The B-82 round-5 ollama fallback **no longer byte-restores the pre-B-82 bare dispatch**. The retry still drops the *tools* (which is what the daemon rejected, so the daemon fix is intact) but now carries the packet as read-only prompt text. The R5 comment block states this explicitly, and its witness was updated to the new contract and renamed `test_ollama_tool_unsupported_model_falls_back_to_the_tool_free_path` rather than deleted.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 7 (final fix round before merge-gate) — one [P2] at the intersection of the authorization and observability surfaces.** **[P2-e]** the span always reported `packet_policy_denied` whenever the packet fallback was ineligible, because the carrier was a **boolean**. A run denied by an **empty token budget**, or by an **absent provider capability**, was therefore reported as an operator **policy** decision — a false accusation about a configuration the operator never made, and one that points any investigation at the wrong file. Fixed by replacing `RuntimeMemoryContext.prompt_packet_fallback_eligible: bool` with `prompt_packet_fallback_denial: str | None` — `None` means authorized; otherwise the counterfactual selector's **own** `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason` value, carried verbatim to the span.
- **Grounded correction to the round-7 brief's own hypothesis.** The brief anticipated three distinguishable causes (policy / budget / capability). The selector yields only **two** reachable values: `token_budget_empty` for the budget gate, and `no_supported_mode` for **both** a denying `injection_access` *and* an absent `supports_prompt_extension_packet` — it does not separate those two once past its packet branch. Verified empirically across all five configurations before writing a line. The fix therefore removes the **false** distinction without inventing one the selector cannot observe, and a witness asserts that non-distinction explicitly so a later reader does not mistake it for a gap. The fail-safe default is a `not_derived` sentinel, asserted **disjoint** from every real `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason` value, so an underived context is never mistaken for a gate that actually closed.
- **Recorded residual of the observability surface → B-87.** The `finally` emission introduced at round 6 over-reports a **pre-wire** translation failure as a completed injection — packet_hash present, `operation.name=injection`, and **zero adapter calls made**. Registered rather than fixed: the imprecision **over**-reports (it claims a disclosure that never left the process, so an investigator over-responds rather than misses a leak), and this arc reached its fix-round cap at Codex R7. *(Superseded — B-87 CLOSED 2026-07-29 at PR #1149; see its own row.)*
- **Out-of-family Codex round 6 — one [P2], a fourth defect shape: the *observability* of the decision.** **[P2-d]** the degraded-serve span was emitted from a **post-dispatch** block, so whenever the provider call raised — timeout, adapter error, or the bare ollama retry itself failing — control left before emission and the only B-83-specific signal vanished. By then the packet had already been **sent** (the disclosure happened) or already been **withheld** (the denial happened): precisely the cases where the signal matters most. Fixed by moving emission into a `finally` around the whole arm-dispatch chain, with `memory.degraded_serve.dispatch_outcome` (`completed` | `provider_error` | `cancelled`) plus `memory.degraded_serve.provider_error_type` on failure. Cancellation is labelled separately rather than blamed on the provider. The enclosing `gen_ai` span already records the exception itself through OTel's `record_exception` / `set_status_on_exception` defaults — which this module relies on everywhere rather than calling explicitly — so the short degraded span carries the class as an attribute instead.
- **The round-2 return-bundle choice had to be reversed.** The R5 fallback decides its degradation *inside* the arm call and reported it as a tuple element — which travels **only on success**. An R5 retry that itself failed therefore lost the report entirely, and the arm site's own local was `None` on that path (the serve-check returns `None` for a servable arm). Replaced with a `_DegradedMemoryServeSink` single-slot carrier, written the moment the disposition is settled and **before** the retry it describes. Both halves — the `finally` and the publish-before-retry ordering — are separately load-bearing and separately probed.
- **Residual exit paths, stated plainly.** `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates *through* `finally`, so the span is still emitted — witnessed, not assumed — and the same holds for any `BaseException`. The only remaining losses are process-level: `SIGKILL`, a hard interpreter crash, or an OTel exporter dropping the span downstream. No in-process placement can address those, and all of them lose the enclosing `gen_ai` span too, so the degraded span is no weaker than the dispatch telemetry it accompanies.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 5 — one [P1], a third defect shape: the repair's own *authorization*.** **[P1-e]** the repair rendered the packet **without evaluating the prompt-packet mode's own gates**. `select_memory_access_mode` returns at the *first* mode whose gates pass, so a `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` selection proves **nothing** about `PROMPT_EXTENSION_PACKET` — that branch was never evaluated. A policy allowing `standard_tool_access` while `injection_access` denies prompt packets is legal and expressible (`DENY` is the field default, and the in-repo `test_external_cli_route_metadata_composes_with_standard_tool_context` already builds exactly that shape), and the packet branch additionally requires `token_budget > 0` which the tools branch does not. The degradation could therefore disclose memory **through a mode the operator switched off**, on an unbudgeted run.
- **Authority gap, stated plainly.** The needed inputs — `workflow_policy` / `step_policy` / `token_budget` / `provider_capabilities` — live on the **composition request** and are on *neither* `RuntimeMemoryContext` *nor* `MemoryAccessModeSelection`. The dispatcher genuinely cannot answer the question at dispatch time. Rather than mirror-copying policy predicates into harness-runtime (the drift class this workspace treats as a defect in its own right) or parsing `decision_trace` strings, the answer is settled at **composition**, where the inputs are in scope, by **re-running the real `select_memory_access_mode`** with native + standard-tools capabilities masked off — the exact counterfactual the repair faces — and carried forward on a new additive `RuntimeMemoryContext.prompt_packet_fallback_eligible`. The probe is pure (the selector is documented "without touching credentials") and composes the whole decision tree in canonical order with **zero duplicated logic**. The field **defaults False**: a context assembled anywhere but `compose_run_start` has not proven eligibility, and unproven reads as ineligible. `compose_run_start` is the *only* production producer (the static `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.memory_context` seam has no production wiring — `materialize_llm_dispatcher_stage` defaults it `None`), so production coverage is total while hand-built contexts fail safe.
- **Fixture honesty.** The B-83 dispatch fixtures **were** silently relying on the unchecked path: their implied `policy:u-mem-16` document leaves `injection_access` at its `DENY` default. The flag is now an **explicit** fixture parameter (default `True`, i.e. those witnesses model an `injection_access=PROMPT_PACKET` policy with a non-empty budget) instead of an unstated assumption.
- **The authorization set is exhaustive against the selector's own decision tree.** The repair requires **(1)** provider identity, **(2)** provider-family scope, **(3)** prompt-packet eligibility — and (3) composes *every* gate on the path to `PROMPT_EXTENSION_PACKET`: `policy.enabled`, `retrieval_access` DENY, external-CLI route/auth denial, `supports_prompt_extension_packet`, `injection_access` ≠ `PROMPT_PACKET`, and `token_budget <= 0`. Verified mechanically by driving each of those six gates negative one at a time: three (`enabled`, `retrieval_access`, external-CLI auth) collapse the selection to `NO_MEMORY_ACCESS`, where `_packet_matches_mode` forbids a packet at all and the repair is unreachable **by construction**; the other three leave `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` selected (repair reachable) and the eligibility flag correctly reads `False`. There is no seventh gate on that path.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 4 — one [P2], the anthropic member of the fold-shape family.** **[P2-c]** the fold asked *"is there an existing system source?"* by **truthiness**, while the conflict check asks it by **presence** (`"system" in kwargs`). Two *valid* shapes slipped through the gap — the SDK content-block **array** (the same `[{"type": "text", ...}]` form `_anthropic_system_cache_block` itself emits) and the **empty string** — landing in the `system`-variable branch, where the still-present `params["system"]` then collided and raised `PromptInjectionConflictError`: the repair converting a *valid* dispatch into a failure. Fixed by keying the fold on `"system" in payload.params`, so **the fold predicate and the conflict predicate agree on what "present" means**, and by routing the value through round 3's `_content_with_appended_packet` — whose sequence branch appends a `{"type": "text", ...}` block, a valid Anthropic `TextBlockParam` (`cache_control` is optional) — so no divergent serialization was introduced.
- **Completeness sweep — the fold family is closed.** Run through the *real* translators across **17 arm × shape combinations**. For each of the four arms the **fold predicate now mirrors that arm's own conflict predicate**: anthropic on `"system" in payload.params`; openai/ollama on a leading `role:"system"` in the **post-`params`-merge** `kwargs["messages"]` (so a `params["messages"]` override is covered, matching `_inject_leading_system_message`); external-CLI on a leading `role:"system"` in `payload.messages` (that renderer ignores `params` for messages, so there is no post-merge divergence to cover). Every value shape reaching a fold is handled totally — `_content_with_appended_packet` (str / `None` / sequence / other) for anthropic+openai+ollama, `_external_cli_message_content` (str / other) for the CLI. All 17 combinations kept the original text **and** carried the packet, with no raise and exactly one system source. Ollama's reachable set is narrower by construction: `Message.content` is `Optional[str]`.
- **One residual, characterized rather than fixed.** The "exactly one system source" property is **index-0-scoped** on openai/ollama — a `role:"system"` message at index > 0 is seen by neither the conflict check nor the fold, so the fold prepends a leading one and the wire carries two system messages. That is the **pre-existing** R-PM-1 conflict-check semantics, not a B-83 regression; it raises nothing, replaces nothing, and OpenAI accepts multiple system messages.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 3 — two bounded [P2]s, both inside the fold helpers round 2 introduced.** **[P2-a]** OpenAI accepts a system-message `content` as either a plain string *or* a content-part **array**, and the fold coerced it through `str()` before appending — putting a Python repr (`"[{'type': 'text', ...}]"`, reproduced verbatim at the probe) on the wire and destroying the parts. Fixed with `_content_with_appended_packet`, which folds each shape in its own terms: string/`None` → string append; a parts **sequence** → one **additional** `{"type": "text", "text": ...}` part (the same part shape this module already emits at the Anthropic system block and the external-CLI response) with every original part preserved in order; any other shape → JSON-serialized (`sort_keys` + `default=str`, matching `_inject_upstream_context_message`) then string-appended, so an unexpected shape is neither mangled nor raised on. **Grounded and skipped for ollama:** `ollama._types.Message.content` is `Optional[str]` (`ollama/_types.py:312`) — str-only, so a parts array cannot reach the daemon through the typed client; ollama shares the helper but can only ever take the string branch. **[P2-b]** the external-CLI fold passed `None` to the append helper for any non-string content, **replacing** the step's own system instructions with the packet alone — and since the external-CLI arm is text-only it *always* degrades `standard_memory_tools`, making that the **common** path there rather than an edge case. Fixed by extracting the renderer's own serialization into `_external_cli_message_content` and reusing it at **both** the render loop and the fold, so a repaired dispatch can never represent the same content differently from an unrepaired one.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 2 — the same two defect shapes, one layer deeper.** **[P1-c]** the round-1 scope conjunct was **identity**-level while the disclosure boundary is **family**-level. On the `memory_runtime` path a cross-family fallback *recomposes* the context for the current candidate — so `selection.selected_provider` matches and the identity conjunct passes — while `compose_for_dispatch` keeps deriving `record_scope.provider_family` from `fallback_chain.primary.family` (`automatic_memory.py:191-199`), and `MemoryRetriever._scope_mismatch` (`memory_retrieval.py:371-384`) filters records on exactly that field. A **primary-family** packet therefore reached the ollama R5 retry and was rendered. Fixed with a family conjunct keyed on the packet's *actual* `record_scope.provider_family` versus `provider_family_for_provider(provider)` (`cross_family_cost_tag.py:82` — the workspace's existing provider→family authority; a second mapping here would be the mirror-copy drift class), reason `provider_family_scope_mismatch`, with both conjuncts now living in one shared `_degraded_serve_disposition` read by the arm-selection check *and* the R5 site. An absent scope or absent family counts as **not** matching: `_scope_mismatch` treats a `None` request family as "no constraint", so the packet may hold records of any family — unverifiable is not safe. This also exposed a **fixture lie**: the test helper hardcoded `provider_family=OPENAI` for every context regardless of provider, so the anthropic/ollama witnesses were asserting a scope their provider did not have; the fixture now derives family from provider through the same authority. **[P1-d]** the *arm-selection* repair still appended the packet as a **second** system source — the exact class fixed at the R5 site in round 2 — so a payload carrying its own system prompt raised `PromptInjectionConflictError` across all four translators. Fixed by threading the packet as a `memory_packet` parameter so **each translator folds it into its own single effective system source** (Anthropic's `params["system"]`-or-kwarg, folded *before* the cache-breakpoint decision so the block covers the merged text; OpenAI/Ollama's leading `role:"system"` message post-`params`-merge; the external CLI's system section) rather than duplicating each translator's rule at the call site. A genuine **two-base** collision (active prompt *and* payload system) still fails loud — witnessed.
- **Grounding finding, registered not absorbed → B-86.** The *servable* tools path crosses the same family boundary with strictly greater reach: the injected schemas bind `scope_ref`/`policy_ref` as fixed values, so a cross-family candidate can `memory.search` across **and** `memory.write_note` into the primary family's scope — read disclosure *and* write attribution, where the packet leak was read-only. Pre-existing since U-MEM-16/B-82 and gated on a C-MEM-11/13 scope-semantics decision, so it is registered rather than absorbed here.
- **Out-of-family Codex round 1 — two real [P1]s, both fixed on this branch, both reproduced empirically before fixing.** **[P1-a]** the (b) repair forwarded provider X's packet to a Y-family provider — the scope leak above; (b) became report-only. **[P1-b]** the R5 retry supplied the packet as a **second** system source, so `_inject_leading_system_message` raised `PromptInjectionConflictError` for any payload already leading with a `{"role":"system"}` message — i.e. the previously-working tool-free fallback hard-failed for the idiomatic self-system-prompt step shape. Closed by folding the packet into the **one** effective system source (`_fold_memory_packet_into_system`, plus a defaulted `memory_packet` kwarg on `_dispatch_ollama` so every other caller stays byte-identical), operating on the **finished kwargs** post-`params`-merge for exactly the reason `_inject_leading_system_message` does — a `params["messages"]` override can hide the real leading system message, so a payload-level merge would reintroduce the collision.
- **Witnesses.** 27 deterministic tests (anthropic override; external-CLI arm; provider-rebound context report-only on a tool-capable openai arm; cross-family recomposed context report-only through the R5 path; ollama tools-unsupported retry; the R5 retry against a payload-carried system message; the arm-selection repair against a payload-carried system message; the arm-selection repair against Anthropic's `params["system"]`; a two-base collision still failing loud; a servable-path over-fire guard; an OpenAI content-part-array system message; an external-CLI mapping-content system message; an anthropic `params["system"]` block array; an empty-string `params["system"]`; a packet-policy-denied context at the arm site; the same at the R5 site; two composer-level eligibility-derivation tests against the real selector; a repair-carrying dispatch whose provider call raises; a report-only dispatch whose provider call raises; an R5 retry that itself fails; a cancelled dispatch; a success-path outcome assertion; an underived-eligibility context reporting `not_derived`; a sentinel-disjointness check; active-prompt composition ordering) and 16 mutation probes: disabling the serve-check fails 4; reverting the R5 packet injection fails only (c); dropping the provider-identity conjunct fails only (b); *repairing* the provider mismatch fails only the (b) report-only witness; reverting to the two-source retry shape reproduces `PromptInjectionConflictError` at the P1-b witness; dropping the family conjunct fails only the cross-family witness; reverting the arm-selection repair to append-as-second-source reproduces `PromptInjectionConflictError` at both P1-d witnesses; reverting the OpenAI content fold to `str()` fails the parts-array witness on a Python repr; reverting the external-CLI fold to the `None`-pass fails the mapping-content witness with the step's directive entirely absent from the prompt; reverting the anthropic fold to the truthiness key reproduces `PromptInjectionConflictError` at **both** the block-array and empty-string witnesses; dropping the eligibility conjunct fails both packet-policy-denied witnesses (arm site *and* R5 site); stubbing the composition-time derivation to always-eligible fails both composer-level derivation witnesses; moving the emission back post-dispatch fails all four exception-path witnesses; publishing the R5 sink *after* its retry instead of before fails the R5-retry-failure witness alone; collapsing the composer derivation back to one label fails both composer-level precise-reason witnesses; collapsing the span reason at the disposition fails all three dispatch-level precise-reason witnesses.
- **Scope split.** The mixed memory+caller batch case, previously recorded under this row's "adjacent, same family" note, is genuinely unrepairable at its site and moved to **B-85**.
- **Close-out steps.** (1) Decide the failure posture: a fail-loud typed error at the dispatch boundary when `memory_context.access_mode is STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` and the resolved provider arm has no standard-memory-tools sibling, versus an explicit, ledgered degradation to `PROMPT_EXTENSION_PACKET`/`NO_MEMORY_ACCESS` (which C-MEM-13:463 would then require be ledgered — the check-and-closed note above confirms the ledgering mechanism already exists, only the dispatch-side re-composition trigger would be new). Fail-loud is the cheaper and more consistent reading given the surrounding `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError`/`MemoryToolExecutionInputError` conventions. (2) Separately decide whether a statically injected `memory_context` should be re-composed (or invalidated) on a fallback provider rebinding, or whether that configuration should simply be refused at bind time when a `fallback_chain` is also bound — the latter is a much smaller surface. (3) Witness with two deterministic tests: an explicit-capability-override dispatch against the anthropic arm, and a rebinding test where a `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` context composed for openai is dispatched through a cross-family fallback to anthropic.
- **Council: likely for step (1), no for step (3).** Choosing fail-loud versus explicit-ledgered-degradation is a C-MEM-13 selection-semantics decision with a blast-radius dimension (a fail-loud raise turns a currently-silent degradation into a run failure for any deployment relying on the injected-context + fallback configuration) — C10 (blast radius) paired with whichever voice owns the memory access-mode selection semantics. Step (2)'s bind-time refusal is mechanical once (1) is settled.

- **What it is.** The B-82 arc's round-1 fix made both memory tool loops validate the COMPLETE batch before executing any of it, which closed the *dispatch-side* half of the partial-batch problem. A second half remains, one layer down: validation the DISPATCH layer legitimately does not perform still happens mid-execution, at the executor. Concretely — a batch of `[memory.write_note (valid), memory.read (missing the contract-required `memory_ref`)]` passes every dispatch-side check, so `_openai_memory_tool_result_messages` / `_ollama_memory_tool_result_messages` execute the calls in order: the write COMMITS a durable record, then the read raises `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` from `_string_arg` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:549-553` — *`_string_arg` is at `:678` at 2026-08-05; the whole helper inventory drifted, refreshed in the 2026-08-05 bullet below*). That error **was** retry-classified TRANSIENT — `_classify_provider_exception` fail-fasted only `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError` / `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` / HTTP 401-403 and mapped everything else to the staircase — so `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher` re-ran the whole dispatch from the top and the already-committed write executed a second time. Same double-write class as the round-1 [P1], reached through a different door. **PARTIAL MITIGATION LANDED (2026-07-28)** — `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` now joins the fail-fast branch of `_classify_provider_exception` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:326-334`), so the retry staircase no longer re-runs the dispatch for this class: on the default single-candidate chain a mid-batch executor input failure now consumes exactly ONE dispatch instead of `max_attempts`. **The row stays `registered_finding`** — the retry-duplication half is closed, the partial-commit half is not: the earlier write still commits before the later call raises, and a MULTI-candidate fallback chain CAN duplicate the committed prefix — contingent, not guaranteed (codex 2026-08-05): the failed inner dispatch's `prepared` batch is local and not forwarded; the next candidate re-samples its own tool calls, which may repeat, differ, or be absent — up to one extra copy per candidate when re-sampled alike, versus `max_attempts` × candidates before.
- **What IS already prevalidated (so the residual is genuinely narrow).** The batch pre-pass built at B-82 rounds 1/3 resolves and checks, for EVERY call, before anything executes: the tool_call wire shape (`function` is a mapping; OpenAI's `id` present and non-empty); the name resolving to a `MemoryToolName` (via the wire map on the OpenAI arm, dotted-only on the ollama arm); the `arguments` payload normalizing to a mapping (already-decoded on ollama, JSON-decoded on OpenAI, fail-loud otherwise); and the `RuntimeMemoryContext` checks — `record_scope`/`scope_ref` present, and the `scope_ref` argument matching the context for the two tools whose contracts declare it. What it does NOT check is per-tool required-argument keys (`note` for `write_note`, `memory_ref` for `read`/`propose_promotion`/`request_redaction`, `query` for `search`, …) or per-tool policy gates — because those are the EXECUTOR's semantics, not the dispatch layer's.

Round 3 established the grounded boundary empirically — required-key enforcement lives at `memory_tool_executor.py:266` -> `:549-553`, and the dispatch layer validates only `scope_ref`/`policy_ref` — so widening the dispatch layer here would be inventing new dispatch semantics, not honoring existing ones. Registered rather than fixed unilaterally.
- **AGGRAVATOR — the ollama SDK silently drops the schema constraints the contracts declare** *(out-of-family Codex round 5; verified empirically at registration time against the locked `ollama==0.6.2`)*. The client **revalidates** caller-supplied tool mappings as its own `ollama.Tool` model before posting to `/api/chat` — `ChatRequest.tools: Optional[Sequence[Tool]]` (`ollama/_types.py:400`) — and that model is a **closed field subset** layered over a plain pydantic `BaseModel`: `SubscriptableBaseModel` (`_types.py:19`) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default `extra='ignore'` applies; `Tool.Function.Parameters` (`_types.py:365-371`) declares only `type` / `$defs` / `items` / `required` / `properties`, and `Parameters.Property` (`_types.py:372-379`) declares only `type` / `items` / `description` / `enum`. Every other JSON-Schema keyword is therefore discarded en route to the daemon, with no error and no warning. Measured directly against the real C-MEM-14 contracts by round-tripping them through `Tool.model_validate`: `memory.search` loses top-level `additionalProperties: false`, `limit.minimum: 1`, and `query.minLength: 1`; `memory.write_note` loses `note.minLength: 1`. The model consequently never sees the constraints the contracts declare, which **raises the odds it emits an argument payload the executor then rejects** — feeding precisely this row's mid-batch / transient-retry class. This is an aggravator only: it changes the likelihood, not the mechanism, and the mitigation menu below is unchanged. (Orthogonal to the separate, already-fixed B-82 round-5 issue of non-tool-template models 400-ing on `tools=` at all.)

- **Close-out steps.** Two candidate directions, both real, neither obviously dominant: **(1) an executor-exposed pure `validate()` pre-pass** — the executor grows a side-effect-free method that runs exactly the argument/policy checks `_execute_authorized` would run, and the dispatch batch pre-pass calls it for every call before executing any. Strictly stronger (it also covers a mid-batch failure that no pre-pass could predict, e.g. a policy resolver flipping or an I/O error) but a materially larger change touching durable-write ordering, and it needs a decision about what "rollback" means for an append-only canonical store — likely compensating ledger entries rather than deletion. **The third, cheaper mitigation is LANDED (2026-07-28) and does not close this row:** executor-level input errors are now fail-FAST rather than transient. **Grounding verdict before building — IMPL-DISCRETION, not spec-enumerated.** Runtime spec §14.6 D2 (`design-substrate/Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md:3796`) states the predicate as *"Retry-eligible iff the provider exception matches CP §21.2 transient staircase (`REFLEXION` / `RETRY_WITH_BACKOFF` stages); fail-fast otherwise (AUTH, payload-shape, shutdown)"* — fail-fast is the RESIDUAL class and the parenthetical is illustrative, not a closed set. A contract-invalid C-MEM-14 memory tool call matches nothing in §21.2 (network / rate-limit / 5xx) and is the same permanent malformed-input class as `RT-FAIL-PAYLOAD-SHAPE` raised one layer deeper, so the reclassification moves the impl TOWARD the spec predicate rather than extending it (no X-AL-3 surface). **One correction to this row's own earlier rationale:** "the same arguments will fail identically" is imprecise — a retry re-dispatches to the provider and re-samples the tool-call arguments, so a retry *could* emit valid ones. The defensible rationale is the spec predicate + the `RT-FAIL-PAYLOAD-SHAPE` parity, and what fail-fast removes is the duplicate durable commit, not merely wasted attempts. **Scope — `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError` deliberately EXCLUDED:** `_read_record_by_ref` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:446-449`) wraps ANY store exception, including genuinely transient I/O, into the denied class, and `_allowed_index_entry` (`:424-435`) raises it off mutable index/store state — fail-fasting the `MemoryToolExecutionError` base would kill retries for real flakes; and whether a policy DENIAL is permanently terminal is a C-MEM policy-semantics decision this narrow change does not take. Both probes confirmed: reverting the `isinstance` addition fails the first two (the second reports `assert 3 == 1` — the three-copy duplication made visible), and widening it to the `MemoryToolExecutionError` base fails the third. **Out-of-family Codex round 1 on this arc — one real [P1], fixed here.** `_allowed_kinds` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:574-598`; the bare conversion sat at pre-fix `:584`) raised a **bare** `ValueError` from `MemoryRecordKind(item)` on an unknown `allowed_kinds` string — and since `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` *subclasses* `ValueError` rather than the reverse, a bare `ValueError` misses the fail-fast isinstance check entirely, so a `memory.search` with a bad kind following a committed `memory.write_note` still replayed transient. ### B-85 · A mixed memory+caller tool batch returns the advertised memory call unserved and un-ledgered *(surfaced at the B-83 fix, 2026-07-28)*

- **What it is.** Both standard-memory-tool continuation loops, on seeing a response whose `tool_calls[]` mixes a C-MEM-14 memory call with a caller-advertised tool call, hand the **whole response back unprocessed** and execute nothing from it. That is a deliberate B-82 round-2 choice, for batch atomicity + bare-path parity: a mixed batch must not half-commit memory before control returns to the caller. The consequence is this row: the memory call the model explicitly asked for is **never served, and nothing records that it wasn't** — no span, no ledger entry, no error. The caller cannot serve it either, since it does not own the memory tools.
- **Reachability.** `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py:3389-3401` (openai arm) and `:3979-3987` (ollama arm) — line numbers at the B-83 arc's final HEAD (they drifted across the arc's later rounds; corrected at the merge-gate) — the two `if not _all_calls_are_memory_tools(...)` early returns. Both sites carry an inline `B-85` marker, which is the durable anchor if lines drift again.
- **Why it was not fixed at the B-83 arc.** B-83's repair is *prompt composition*, applied **before** the provider call. This exit happens **after** a response is already composed, and a prompt packet cannot retroactively answer a tool call the model has already emitted. There is no mechanical repair to apply — only a posture to choose. Note this is **not** a defect in the atomicity choice, which remains correct.
- **Current state — CLOSED 2026-07-28 (Round 37); posture (3) RECORD landed.** Split out of B-83 rather than absorbed by it, precisely because the B-83 repair provably cannot reach it.
- **Close-out steps.** Choose the posture; the mechanics follow trivially. **(1) FAIL** — raise at the mixed-batch detection so the unserved memory call is loud rather than silent; consistent with the surrounding `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` conventions, but it turns a currently-working caller-tool dispatch into a failure. **(2) SPLIT** — execute the memory calls and return the caller's calls unprocessed; restores service but reopens exactly the half-commit window B-82 round 2 closed (the memory writes commit, the caller's handling can then fail, and the whole dispatch retries under the TRANSIENT classification). **(3) REPAIR/RECORD** — keep the return-whole semantics and emit a degraded/unserved telemetry span at the exit; cheapest, preserves atomicity, but leaves the model's request genuinely unanswered. (3)'s span is emittable with the existing closed enums; a **ledgered** entry is not, under the same X-AL-3 constraint recorded at B-83's close-out.
- **Council: likely.** This is the same C-MEM-13/14 serve-semantics decision B-83 answered for the pre-call case, now for the post-response case, and each option trades a different harm: (1) blast radius on working dispatches, (2) reopens a durable double-write window, (3) accepts a silent-to-the-model outcome. C10 (blast radius) paired with whichever voice owns the memory access-mode selection semantics.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-28 (Round 37).** Landed in the same PR as the B-86 Class 1 fork filing.
  - **Posture (3) RECORD chosen, and grounding is what chose it — the spec is genuinely silent.** C-MEM-14 (`design-substrate/Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:489`) obliges tool **exposure**, not service. C-MEM-13's must-ledger clause (`:463`) binds only `no_memory_access` transitions, which this exit is not. And C-MEM-08's **closed** 12-kind operation enum (`:247` / `:251`) has no way to express *requested-but-unserved* — which is precisely what makes the **ledger** half X-AL-3-blocked and the **span** half emittable, exactly as this row's own close-out predicted.
  - **Emission shape — a SEPARATE single-slot sink + emitter, deliberately not the degraded-serve one.** The degraded-serve emitter's `rendered=None` shape hardcodes `DENIAL` / `no_memory_access` / `degraded_serve=True`; all three are **false** at iteration k>0, where the loop has already served k rounds of memory calls. The new span carries `operation_name=standard_tool_call`, `access_mode=standard_memory_tools`, `record_count=0`, **no** packet_hash, **no** failure_class, `reason=mixed_batch_caller_owned`, plus a quantitative `memory.unserved_tool_call.count` — every one of them an attribute **value** per the B-83 precedent, never a new member of a closed enum. Return-whole semantics are byte-identical, and a zero-memory-call caller-only batch deliberately emits **nothing** (negative-asserted, so the row cannot drift into emitting on every mixed batch).
  - **Postures (1) and (2) rejected as Class-2-shaped, not as unworkable.** **(1) FAIL** inverts the witnessed bare-path-parity invariant — enabling memory must never turn a working caller-tool dispatch into a failure — and pays fail-fast candidate abandonment for what is an *observability* gap. **(2) SPLIT** reopens exactly the duplicate-durable-write window B-82 round 2 and B-84 / PR #1143 closed, on a path where the harness cannot serve the caller half anyway.
  - **A fourth option was enumerated and rejected.** Withhold the memory tools whenever the step advertises caller tools, making the mixed batch *unrepresentable*. Genuinely preventive rather than observational — but it disables memory on every tool-declaring step and changes **which** memory a run reaches, which is B-86's territory, not this row's.
  - **Stated honestly.** The span may fire 0..N times across retry attempts, because model-emitted batches are nondeterministic; that is the same property the B-83 span has, and the witnesses do not assert exactly-once.
  - **Not foreclosing.** Advisor and grounding both record that choosing (3) leaves (1) and (2) available later as a Class 2 fork, and that (3) is the option which preserves the committed B-82-round-2 atomicity decision.


### B-86 · Cross-family fallback serves the chain primary's memory scope to a different-family provider on the SERVABLE tools path *(surfaced while grounding B-83 [P1-c], 2026-07-28; CLOSED 2026-07-28 — U-MEM-26 impl leg)*

- **What it is.** The B-83 fix stops the degraded-serve *packet* from crossing a provider-family boundary. The **servable tools path** crosses the same boundary and was deliberately left untouched. On the `memory_runtime` path a cross-family fallback *recomposes* the context for the current candidate, so `select_memory_access_mode` re-picks `STANDARD_MEMORY_TOOLS` from the **candidate's** capabilities and the tools are injected — but `compose_for_dispatch` derives `record_scope.provider_family` from `fallback_chain.primary.family` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/automatic_memory.py:191-199`), **not** from the candidate. The injected schemas bind `scope_ref` (a hash of that primary-family scope) and `policy_ref` as fixed enum values (`_openai_standard_memory_tools` / `_ollama_standard_memory_tools`), so the candidate can `memory.search` **across**, and `memory.write_note` **into**, a scope belonging to a different provider family — read disclosure *and* write attribution, where B-83's packet leak was read-only.
- **The field is a real boundary, not decoration.** `MemoryRetriever._scope_mismatch` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_retrieval.py:371-384`) filters candidate records on `provider_family`, which is what makes the primary-derived scope load-bearing in the first place.
- **Residual, same family.** `provider_family_for_provider` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/cross_family_cost_tag.py:82`) falls back to `LOCAL_OPEN_WEIGHT` for an **unknown** provider key, so an unregistered provider compares equal to an ollama-scoped packet at B-83's new family conjunct — conservative for its original cost-attribution use, wrong for a scope-boundary check.
- **Current state — `closed` (2026-07-28, at the U-MEM-26 impl leg; `registered_finding` → `design_substrate_gated` at the fork filing, → `open` at the spec leg, → `closed` here — all three transits on the same day).** The **C-MEM-13 withhold guard landed** as the **sixth conjunct** of `_standard_memory_tools_context` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`), sharing `_packet_scope_matches_dispatch_family` **verbatim** with the predicate `_degraded_serve_disposition` already reads — deliberately *one* predicate, not a second cross-family test: a divergent test would let a cross-family dispatch fail the arm guard, fall through to `_degraded_serve_for_unservable_arm`, pass disposition conjunct 2, and land on the `arm_unservable` **repair** branch, serving the same cross-family packet as prompt text. Downstream is by construction — the guard returns `None`, the disposition reports `provider_family_scope_mismatch` with `rendered=None`, the plain arm dispatches with no schemas / no `scope_ref` / no packet, and the degraded span carries DENIAL / `no_memory_access` / `record_count=0` / no `packet_hash`. The dispatch still completes. **Two defect-pinning tests were inverted** with contract cites rather than deleted: the B-83-era R5 witness (which required the tools to be *armed* cross-family so the daemon could refuse them) is now `test_u_mem_26_cross_family_ollama_dispatch_withholds_tools_and_packet`, and the r300 `api.run` integration test — which asserted the five C-MEM-14 wire names **do** reach the cross-family openai leg — now asserts the opposite at `test_r300_deterministic_cross_family_fallback_through_production_path`, so the withholding is proven on the **canonical production path**, not only at the unit boundary. Net posture is the report-only **denial**, with **harness-authored capture unaffected** (C3's condition of concurrence), witnessed with the run's composed scope. **Pre-existing** — the tools path had behaved this way since U-MEM-16 / B-82. The close-out steps below are **history (pre-ratification)**.

Ground it first: does a per-candidate scope *fragment* memory across a fallback chain — each family reading a disjoint record set, so a fallback silently loses the run's accumulated memory — and is that preferable to the current cross-family reach? This is the load-bearing question and it is not mechanical. **(2)** If the scope stays primary-derived, decide the dispatch-side posture for a cross-family *servable* dispatch: withhold the tools (memory off for the fallback leg, consistent with B-83's packet posture), or keep them and accept documented cross-family reach. **(3)** Independently and cheaply: make the unknown-provider fallback explicit at B-83's call site — an unknown key should not silently compare equal to `LOCAL_OPEN_WEIGHT` for a scope-boundary decision; a `None`/unknown sentinel forcing report-only is the conservative shape and does not disturb the cost-attribution caller.

(3) is mechanical once (1) is settled and could land ahead of it.
- **GROUNDED + COUNCIL-CONVENED 2026-07-28 (Round 37); flipped `registered_finding` → `design_substrate_gated`.** Filed as `.harness/class_1_fork_b86_memory_scope_provider_family_keying.md` per the **B-70 discriminator**: a real gap that needs spec-level CONTRACT text before code. Neither voice conceded its axis; the mechanism was the conflation.
