### B-87 · Degraded-serve span over-reports pre-wire failures as completed injections *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex round 8 on the B-83 arc, 2026-07-28; CLOSED 2026-07-29 — PR #1149)*

- **What it is.** B-83 round 6 moved the degraded-serve span emission into a `finally` around the whole arm-dispatch chain, so a repair that was *sent* and then failed still reports. That correctly covers **post-wire** failures. It over-covers **pre-wire** ones: when the repair is authorized, `_DegradedMemoryServe.rendered` is populated at the serve-check — *before* any translation runs — and the per-arm translators can raise before the provider adapter is ever called. The `finally` then emits `operation_name=injection` + `access_mode=prompt_extension_packet` + the packet_hash + a non-zero record_count: the span asserts the packet **was injected**, when nothing left the process.
- **Verified empirically at registration time, not hypothesised.** Driving the residual two-base case — an `active_system_prompt` bound *and* a payload-owned `params["system"]`, which B-83 round 4 deliberately leaves as a fail-loud `PromptInjectionConflictError` — through the real dispatcher on a repair-eligible context produced **zero adapter calls** and yet a span carrying `memory.operation.name=injection`, `memory.access_mode=prompt_extension_packet`, `memory.packet_hash=cccc…`, `memory.record_count=1`, `dispatch_outcome=provider_error`, `provider_error_type=PromptInjectionConflictError`.
- **Reachability.** Any translation-layer raise on a **repaired** dispatch: the two-base `PromptInjectionConflictError` residual (reachable on all four arms), `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError` from the external-CLI text-only tools rejection, and any future pre-adapter validation. **Not** reachable for report-only dispositions (`rendered is None` already emits `denial` / `no_memory_access` / no packet_hash), nor when the repair is unauthorized. Note that `test_b83_two_base_system_sources_still_fail_loud_through_the_repair` already exercises this exact path but asserts only the raise, not the span — the suite passes *over* the defect rather than covering it.
- **Candidate fix.** A reached-the-wire marker set at the provider-call boundary — the one place per arm where the adapter is actually invoked — with the `finally` emitting a **distinct** classification when the marker is unset: pre-wire failures reported as e.g. `denial` plus a `dispatch_outcome="translation_error"` value and **no** packet_hash, since no packet reached a provider. Mechanically small; the care is in threading the marker to every arm's true adapter-call site (including the ollama R5 bare retry) without reintroducing the round-6 loss on genuine post-wire failures.
- **Current state.** **CLOSED 2026-07-29 at PR #1149** (branch `b87-reached-the-wire-prewire-marker`) — all three close-out steps land.
  - **Mechanism.** A frame-local `_ProviderWireReachedSink` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`) is constructed once per dispatch and threaded to every arm; `_emit_degraded_memory_serve_span` gained a `reached_wire` parameter and branches on it. Marker **set** → today's post-wire shape **verbatim** (`injection` + packet_hash + record_count, `completed` or `provider_error`). Marker **unset** → `dispatch_outcome="pre_wire_failure"` plus a new `memory.degraded_serve.pre_wire_error_type` attribute, with **no** packet_hash and no `injection` operation name (the existing closed-enum member `packet_assembly` is emitted instead).
  - **The candidate name `translation_error` above was rejected**, at out-of-family Codex R1 [P2], as over-claiming: *any* pre-wire phase can fail — payload-shape rejection, adapter selection, a repair-authorization raise — not only translation. The shipped value is phase-neutral by construction and names the **boundary**, not the phase.
  - **Placement, per arm.** Direct-SDK arms construct the awaitable, mark, *then* await — so a call-time **synchronous** `TypeError` from the SDK is correctly pre-wire (R7). The external-CLI arm fires **inside** the subprocess runner after `create_subprocess_exec` returns — the semantic anchor is that a child process now exists that can observe the payload, so a spawn failure stays pre-wire (R2/R3). The anthropic-memory arm fires once inside `execute_with_memory_callbacks` before its first SDK call (R5), since that helper owns a tool loop the dispatcher cannot see into.
  - **Two declines, on the record.** (a) **In-coroutine vendor-side validation** that raises after the awaitable is entered is **post-wire by design** — resolving it would need SDK-internal hooks that do not exist. (b) Consequently the SDK arms' boundary is **our last observable point**, deliberately; this row does not claim byte-on-the-wire fidelity.
  - **Compatibility tiers.** An adapter or runner that does not **declare** an explicit `on_wire` parameter (a bare `**kwargs` deliberately does *not* count, R4) keeps the pre-B-87 marker placement, discriminated by the single shared `accepts_explicit_on_wire` predicate; the public runner seam statically admits **both** shapes (R6).
  - **Robustness.** An `on_wire` callback that raises after spawn kills and reaps the child, and the orphaned coroutine is closed rather than leaked (R7).
  - **Witnesses.** Step (2) landed as specified — `test_b83_two_base_system_sources_still_fail_loud_through_the_repair` now asserts the **span** as well as the raise. Step (3) resolved as `dispatch_outcome`, an attribute **value**; no member added to any closed C-MEM-19 enum. 8 out-of-family Codex rounds (9 real findings), ~25 mutation-probed witnesses across 4 test files, `just check` 7014 passed.
- **Why registered rather than fixed now — direction rationale.** Two reasons, both deliberate. **(1) The imprecision over-reports, not under-reports.** It claims a disclosure that never occurred; it never hides one that did. An investigator reading this span over-responds — checks a provider that was never called — rather than missing a real leak. That is the fail-safe direction for a telemetry defect on a disclosure-adjacent surface, and it is what makes deferral tolerable at all. **(2) This arc reached its fix-round cap at Codex R7** per the workspace's non-convergent-adversarial-hardening discipline: eight review rounds on a single repair, each finding a narrower instance of an already-characterized surface, is the point at which continued in-arc fixing costs more than it returns. Registering keeps the finding live and specified rather than absorbed.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Add the reached-the-wire marker and branch the `finally` emission on it — marker set → today's behavior verbatim; marker unset → the pre-wire classification with no packet_hash and no `injection` operation name, since claiming a packet_hash for a packet no provider ever saw *is* the defect. Ground the exact adapter-call sites first (there is more than one per arm: anthropic has three variants, ollama has the standard-tools loop *and* its R5 bare retry), and mind that the marker must be set **before** the awaited call, not after — otherwise a post-wire failure regresses to being reported as pre-wire, the mirror image of this row and the exact ordering trap B-83 round 6 [P2-d] already hit once with the R5 sink. **(2)** Extend the existing two-base witness to assert the **span** as well as the raise; the path is already covered, only the assertion is missing. **(3)** Decide whether `dispatch_outcome` gains a `translation_error` value or whether pre-wire failures ride the `reason` axis — either is an attribute **value**, never a new member of the closed C-MEM-19 enums.
- **Council: no.** A telemetry-accuracy fix inside an already-settled span contract, with the classification axis (attribute values, not enum members) established by B-83 rounds 5–7. No cross-domain tension to surface: nothing about *which* memory is served or *who* may see it changes — only whether the span truthfully reports that a disclosure occurred. The one judgement call (`dispatch_outcome` vs `reason`) is impl discretion once the marker exists.

### B-88 · Memory failure telemetry: substring-keyed `classify_memory_failure` collapses the typed input-error family — and two real policy denials — to `io_failure` *(surfaced by the merge-gate lens-2 sweep on the B-84 arc, 2026-07-28)* *(**RATIFIED 2026-08-05 as READING A, sub-decision A-ii = RE-TYPE**; SPEC LEG LANDED 2026-08-06 at PR #1245; IMPL LEG (U-MEM-28) LANDED 2026-08-07 -- CLOSED, with ONE known non-conformant type-boundary site carried at `B-114`)*

- **RATIFIED 2026-08-05 as READING A, with sub-decision A-ii = RE-TYPE.** Operator `AskUserQuestion` on the fork's §8 (`.harness/class_2_fork_b88_memory_failure_input_validation_class.md`). `C-MEM-19` gains **`input_validation_failure`** as a **seventh** failure class (the stated fallback name `input_error` is **not** taken), plus the **boundary invariant** separating it from provider-adapter and serialization failure. **A-ii is ratified in its RE-TYPE form:** the `llm_dispatch.py` sites raising `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` for **internal** `MEMORY_TOOL_CONTRACTS` schema faults contradict that invariant and are **re-typed** — not recorded as mis-typed-at-birth and left in place. **Scoped to SIX sites, not eight** *(out-of-family review round 4 [P2], after direct read)*: the internal set is `llm_dispatch.py:4334`/`:4338` (the harness's own `RuntimeMemoryContext` left unset) and `:4450`/`:4458`/`:4947`/`:4958` (`MEMORY_TOOL_CONTRACTS` schema-injection faults). **`:4344` and `:4346` are NOT re-typed** — they validate the **model-supplied** `scope_ref` argument (missing/non-string, then context-mismatched), which is exactly what the ratified `input_validation_failure` class exists for. **Coverage narrowed honestly** *(out-of-family review round 6 [P2], after direct grounding)*: `classify_memory_failure` has **four** production call sites (`memory_redaction.py:273`, `memory_capture.py:778`, `memory_tool_executor.py:255`, `native_memory_adapter.py:556`) and **zero in `llm_dispatch.py`**. The two retained raises sit in `_standard_memory_tool_context`, called from the **dispatch prepare path** (`:4213` / `:4845`) which runs **before** `StandardMemoryToolExecutor.execute()` opens its span — so they emit **no** `memory.failure_class` today, and the re-type does not change that. **A-ii establishes reachability for the classify-routed population, not for the prepare path**, and the spec leg must say so rather than promise emission it does not wire. **Cross-fork note, in TWO parts** *(separated at out-of-family review round 7 [P2]; an earlier revision called the whole residue pre-existing, which over-claimed)*: **(i) pre-existing** — the `:4344`/`:4346` raises already sit on the unclassified prepare path at HEAD; **(ii) newly introduced by `B-84`'s ratified pre-pass** — checks that today raise *inside* `_execute_authorized()` (`limit=0` among them) **are** classified today via `execute()`'s catch (`memory_tool_executor.py:255`), and relocating them to the prepare path **removes** that emission, which none of `B-84`'s ratified witnesses asserts. **PRESERVATION IS MANDATORY** — the *"or ratify the loss"* arm carried at round 7 is **withdrawn at round 9 [P2]**, because it would authorize a contract weakening with no design-substrate change. **Grounded:** C-MEM-19 (`Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:835`–`:870`) lists **"Standard memory tool call"** among the covered operations and **`memory.failure_class`** among the **required** attributes; Reading A opened **no spec leg** and this row is `open` with no blocker, so an impl leg cannot drop that attribute on its own authority — that is the X-AL-3 silent-absorption failure mode. **The build leg MUST preserve classification for every relocated check and witness the preserved emission end-to-end. If preservation proves infeasible, that is a CLASS 1 back-flow against C-MEM-19, filed and ratified BEFORE the code lands** — not an impl-discretion call, and not closable by witnessing the absence. This constrains *how* Reading A is built, not *whether*. **Retry-exit-class consequence of the re-type** *(round 7 [P2], grounded by direct read + probe)*: `_classify_provider_exception` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:269`) returns `None` (fail-fast) only for an isinstance match including `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` (`:325`–`:333`); everything else falls through to `TRANSIENT_RETRY` (`:337`). **Re-typing the six sites away from that class flips them fail-fast → retry unless the new type is admitted to the tuple**, so internal wiring/schema faults would begin retrying and advancing candidates. The **spec leg must record the intended exit classification** and the **impl leg owes an end-to-end dispatch/retry witness** — this is about RETRY behaviour and is *not* covered by the telemetry-coverage narrowing. **Leg ownership, made explicit** *(out-of-family review round 1 [P2])*: the **spec leg** records the boundary invariant and the re-type **decision** in contract text and establishes the dispatch population's classification **reachability**; the **impl leg** performs the **source** re-typing at the `llm_dispatch.py` sites and carries its reachability **witness** (the fork's *impl rider*). **Readings B and C were not selected and are not partially adopted** — in particular **C's docstring-rewrite-at-ratification obligation does NOT fire**: under A the `memory_tool_executor.py:149`–`:171` stopgap docstring is rewritten **at the impl leg** (fork §9), and no `harness-*/src` edit rides a doc-only ratification. **Status → `design_substrate_gated`** at the ratification, → **`open` at the 2026-08-06 SPEC LEG** *(the enum at `.harness/forward-register.yaml`'s head is explicit: only ratified + applied spec deltas plus their Phase-6 plan deltas open the row for code — both landed there)*. **Spec leg LANDED 2026-08-06 (PR #1245):** `Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` v1.2 → v1.3 **and** `Implementation_Plan_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` v1.2 → v1.3, **both** clearance markers filed. Two departures from the text above are recorded there rather than absorbed, neither changing a disposition: **(i)** the plan delta extended U-MEM-22 `:829` to seven values *as prescribed* but **did** add a new unit — **U-MEM-28 at G8** — because the fork's *"no new unit"* line predates A-ii's ratified scope and the six-site re-typing + retry witness had no owning unit (flagged overturnable); **and (i-b) a SEVENTH re-typing was proposed and WITHDRAWN** — `_prepare`'s executor-side exhaustiveness fall-through (`memory_tool_executor.py:373`) is a harness-internal fault that spec v1.3's type-boundary rule forbids raising as the input-error type, at a site the fork never surveyed because it surveyed `llm_dispatch.py` only. The spec leg initially required it; **out-of-family round 8 objected that a spec leg APPLIES ratified fixes and may not widen a ratified six-site enumeration on its own reading, and the objection was accepted** — the obligation is removed and the finding carried, with the consequence stated: **at U-MEM-28's close, C-MEM-19's type-boundary invariant has ONE known non-conformant site, recorded and unrepaired**, **that finding is now owned by its own row, `B-114`**, so it survives this row's close at U-MEM-28 rather than disappearing with it *(out-of-family round 9 [P1])*. Everything in U-MEM-28 therefore stays within the ratification's own enumerated impl-leg list; **(ii)** the classify-routed population is **five** call sites at HEAD `3a1300eb`, not four — PR #1243's `B-84` validate pre-pass added `memory_tool_executor.py:355` and thereby **satisfies the mandatory C-MEM-19 preservation clause as built** — and every `llm_dispatch.py` offset in the six/two enumeration has shifted (internal: `:4359`/`:4363`/`:4475`/`:4483`/`:4977`/`:4988`; **retained** model-argument: `:4369`/`:4371`), re-resolved by content with the split itself unchanged. **What remains is the impl leg** (1 enum member + 1 declaration flip + 1 docstring rewrite + 1 fixture re-key; 8 witness rows flip + 2 added negative rows + the mutation probes; **plus the A-ii source re-typing** at the `llm_dispatch.py` internal-fault sites and its reachability witness). **Zero hash / CXA / contract-number impact. No council owed** (the convening was conditional on Reading B).
- **What it is.** `classify_memory_failure` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_observability.py:150-163` *(the classifier sits at `:166`–`:200` at 2026-08-05; filing §10)*) classifies into the C-MEM-19 failure vocabulary by matching **substrings** of the exception message and of the lowercased type name. Its third rule is `isinstance(exc, (OSError, IOError)) or "io" in exc_name` — and `"io"` is a substring of **"execut·io·n"**. Every member of the `MemoryToolExecutionError` family therefore matches: `memorytoolexecutioninputerror`, `memorytoolexecutiondeniederror`, and the base `memorytoolexecutionerror` all contain `"io"`. The rules are ordered, so a member escapes only if an EARLIER message rule happens to fire first. That is the whole of what keeps policy denials out of the IO bucket today — an accident of wording, not a type distinction.
- **Empirical evidence (probed at registration time, not inferred).** Fed real exception instances:

  | exception | message | emitted `memory.failure_class` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` | `unsupported allowed_kinds entry …` | `io_failure` |
  | `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` | `memory tool argument 'note' must be a string` | `io_failure` |
  | `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` | `memory tool argument 'limit' must be >= 1` | `io_failure` |
  | `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` | `unsupported promotion target_kind …` | `io_failure` |
  | `MemoryToolExecutionError` (base) | `write_note capture failed` | `io_failure` |
  | **`MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError`** | `memory ref mem:x is **superseded**` (`memory_tool_executor.py:433`) | **`io_failure`** |
  | **`MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError`** | `memory ref mem:x is **not retrievable**` (`:435`) | **`io_failure`** |
  | `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError` | `memory ref mem:x denied by policy` | `policy_denial` (correct) |
  | bare `ValueError` (the pre-B-84 `_allowed_kinds` shape) | `'x' is not a valid MemoryRecordKind` | `provider_adapter_failure` |

  Note the last row: the SAME logical failure changed telemetry class as a side effect of B-84 typing it (`provider_adapter_failure` → `io_failure`). Neither value is right — which is the point.
- **Why it is a defect and not a nit.** `Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:641` *(at `:870` at 2026-08-05; filing §10)* (C-MEM-19 Invariants) requires: *"Failure telemetry must distinguish policy denial, path violation, IO failure, serialization failure, provider adapter failure, and retrieval empty-result."* Two genuine policy denials emitting `io_failure` violates that invariant **on an axis the vocabulary already has** — an operator triaging memory IO failures sees records that were merely superseded or unretrievable. **A second, spec-side half:** the six-value vocabulary has **no input-validation class**, so even a correct classifier has nowhere truthful to put a malformed-argument failure. Whether to add one is a C-MEM-19 amendment — design-substrate, not impl — and must route as back-flow, not be absorbed here.
- **Reachability.** Every standard-memory-tool failure path. `StandardMemoryToolExecutor.execute` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:167-175`) calls `classify_memory_failure(exc)` in its blanket `except`, so the attribute is emitted on every raise, including the now-fail-fast B-84 class. Pre-existing and latent — it predates B-84 and is orthogonal to it, but B-84 is what made it visible (and shifted one class).
- **Adjacent, same family — the fail-fast breaker-cause emission is unwitnessed for this class** *(merge-gate lens 3)*. On the fail-fast exit, `retry_breaker_fallback.py` calls `breaker.record_failure(cause=_classify_breaker_cause(exc))`, which returns `None` for an exception with no `.status_code` — correct, but nothing pins it: a mutation hardcoding `BreakerCause.AUTH_FAILURE` there **survives** the B-84 witnesses. Same telemetry-precision family (a failure emitting a confidently wrong classification), same fix shape (assert the emitted classification, not just the control flow), so it is recorded here rather than as a separate row.

### B-89 · Memory-scope producer asymmetry: capture stamps raw provider KEYS while retrieval requests carry family VALUES *(surfaced by the B-86 grounding pass, 2026-07-28; CLOSED 2026-07-28 — U-MEM-26 impl leg)*

- **What it is.** The two producers of a `MemoryScope` disagree about the *vocabulary* of `provider_family`. The capture path constructs its **own** scope with `provider_family=provider` — the raw per-turn dispatched provider **KEY** (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_capture.py:585-591`; key vocabulary `claude_code` / `codex` / `gemini` / `antigravity` / `ollama` / `anthropic` / `openai` / `google` at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/cross_family_cost_tag.py:60-69`) — while retrieval requests carry the composed `record_scope`'s `ProviderFamily` **VALUE** (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/automatic_memory.py:197`). All three enforcement sites compare raw strings with **no normalization**: `MemoryRetriever._scope_mismatch` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_retrieval.py:371-384`), the index `_scope_matches` (`memory_retrieval_index.py:379-396`), and `memory_policy._scope_not_broader` (`memory_policy.py:336-359`).
- **Empirically confirmed at registration, not inferred.** An `ollama`-written note is invisible even to a `local_open_weight`-scoped request **of its own family**. Tool-written notes are therefore **write-only for 5 of the 8 registered provider keys**; only `anthropic` / `openai` / `google` coincide with a family value, and they do so by accident. The practical consequence: "memory continuity" under primary-derived keying is largely **notional** today — the continuity side of B-86's Q1 tension only becomes real once this row lands.
- **Existence is independent of B-86's Q1; direction is not.** Both Q1 readings leave the `ollama` note invisible — Q1 asks *primary-or-candidate*, this row asks *key-or-value*; orthogonal axes. But the **direction** is determined by the B-86 council record (fork doc §5-Q1): the **writer adopts the reader's key** — the capture path stops constructing an independent `MemoryScope` and consumes the run's composed `record_scope`. That is the larger of the two candidate repairs, correct on one-source-of-truth grounds, and it will incidentally close **B-90** when it lands.
- **Intrinsic evidence for the family reading.** The field is literally named `provider_family` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_record_envelope.py:120`) while C-MEM-03 declares **no value domain** at all. That is evidence for the fork to weigh — **not** an impl licence to normalize ahead of the contract text.
- **Hash-inert; blast radius low.** `MemoryScope` is not folded into `memory_id` (content-hash + run_id only, `memory_capture.py:574-575`), so a writer-side normalization moves **no identities**.
- **Migration residual — forward-only and permanent.** Records already written with raw provider keys stay invisible under family-value requests. That is **not a regression** (they are invisible today), but the spec-leg must **state** it rather than leave it implied, alongside the C-MEM-03 value domain it belongs to.
- **Current state.** `closed` 2026-07-28 at the U-MEM-26 impl leg (`design_substrate_gated` → `open` at the B-86 spec leg → `closed` here). `EpisodicMemoryCapture` gained a **`record_scope` parameter** and writes records under the run's composed scope verbatim; **both construction sites pass it**. The `provider` argument is unchanged and still feeds the C-MEM-08 payload and the C-MEM-19 span **as the raw key it is** — only the *record* scope stops deriving from it; the residual self-construction remains for callers with no composed scope and is bound by the C-MEM-03 value domain instead. The **ollama divergence is the discriminating witness** throughout (its provider *key* is not value-equal to its `ProviderFamily`, so a test that passes under `anthropic` or `openai` proves nothing about canonicalization), and **round-trip retrievability is witnessed directly** — `test_captured_scope_round_trips_where_the_pre_repair_scope_does_not` in `harness-runtime/tests/test_u_mem_26_write_boundary.py`, carrying an explicit precondition anchor because *both sides of its comparison are derived from the writer* and it would otherwise stay green against a writer that repaired nothing (caught by the mutation probe, not by review). Mutation-probed: ignoring the composed `record_scope` reddens all four capture witnesses. The forward-only residual stands as **stated** at C-MEM-03 — pre-repair raw-key records are not rewritten and stay unreachable under family-scoped requests. Close-out steps below are history (pre-ratification).
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Do **not** land ahead of the B-86 spec-leg; the direction is the B-86 council record's, not this row's. **(2)** Once ratified, the repair is mechanical at `memory_capture.py:585-591` and its callers, witnessed by asserting that an `ollama`-written note **is** retrievable under a `local_open_weight`-scoped request of its own family (the currently-failing case), and mutation-probed by restoring the raw-key construction. **(3)** State the forward-only migration residual in the spec-leg.
- **Council: no.** The keying decision is the B-86 council record's; once the spec-leg ratifies, the repair is mechanical (the writer consumes the composed `record_scope`).
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced by the B-86 grounding pass; direction fixed by the B-86 council record; **did** incidentally close **B-90** when the repair landed (both rows closed 2026-07-28). Arc record at `.harness/u-mem-26-impl-leg-close-2026-07-28.md`.


### B-90 · Capture-path `MemoryScope` omits `tenant` and `workload_class` — tool-captured records are tenant-unpartitioned *(surfaced at the B-86 council convening, 2026-07-28; CLOSED 2026-07-28 — U-MEM-26 impl leg)*

- **What it is.** `memory_capture.py:585-591` constructs its `MemoryScope` with only `project` / `workflow` / `provider_family` / `cli_profile` / `visibility`. `tenant` and `workload_class` are **omitted entirely**, while the composed **request** scope populates them (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/automatic_memory.py:194-199`).
- **Why the omission is not benign — wildcard-on-`None`.** A `None` **record** value passes all three enforcement sites: `MemoryRetriever._scope_mismatch` skips a `None` on either side (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_retrieval.py:377-383`); the index `_scope_matches` carries the same field list (`memory_retrieval_index.py:379-396`); and `memory_policy._scope_not_broader` guards only **non-`None`** record values (`if record_value is not None and requested_value != record_value`, `memory_policy.py:336-359`), so a `None` record tenant passes there too. **Net:** every tool-captured / episodic record is **tenant-unpartitioned** and reachable by **any** tenant's family-matching request — against the cleared threat-model mandate at `design-substrate/Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:481`: *"Retrieval and injection enforce project, workflow, tenant, provider-family, CLI-profile, and visibility scope before ranking."*
- **Honest caveats.** Single-tenant local deployment is the current default posture, so **live exposure is bounded today**. And the wildcard-on-`None` semantics were, **at registration time**, load-bearing but undocumented — they are **documented as of spec v1.1** (C-MEM-03) — the B-86 spec-leg's C-MEM-03 null-semantics sentence is what documents them.
- **Current state.** `closed` 2026-07-28 at the U-MEM-26 impl leg (`registered_finding` → `open` at the B-86 spec leg → `closed` here), **incidentally by the B-89 writer repair exactly as route (1) predicted**: the run's composed `record_scope` carries `tenant` and `workload_class`, so tool-captured records are no longer tenant-unpartitioned. Witnessed per step (3) below by **three separate per-predicate assertions** in `harness-is/tests/test_memory_scope_value_domain.py` — `test_b90_tenant_denial_at_the_retriever_predicate` (`_scope_mismatch`), `test_b90_tenant_denial_at_the_index_predicate` (`_scope_matches`), and `test_b90_tenant_denial_at_the_policy_predicate` (`_scope_not_broader`) — **never one composite retrieval test**, which is precisely how the omission survived; a fourth witness, `test_b90_null_tenant_request_is_denied_at_every_predicate`, pins the wildcard-on-`None` arm. Each is mutation-probed. The cleared threat-model mandate at `design-substrate/Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:481` is now conformant for the capture path. Close-out steps below are history (pre-ratification).
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Preferred — fold into the B-89 writer-side repair:** consuming the run's composed `record_scope` brings `tenant` + `workload_class` along, so the B-89 repair will incidentally close this row when it lands. **(2)** An **independent narrow fix** (stamp the two fields into the constructed scope at `memory_capture.py:585-591`) is landable **without** the spec-leg, since it needs no contract decision — but it would be superseded by (1). Prefer (1) unless a multi-tenant deployment lands first, in which case take (2) immediately and let B-89 subsume it. **(3)** Witness either shape by asserting a tenant-A request does **not** retrieve a tenant-B tool-captured record at **all three** enforcement sites; a single-site witness passes over the other two, which is how this survived.
- **Council: no.** Conformance repair to a cleared threat-model invariant (`:481`); no cross-domain tension. Fold into the B-89 writer repair at the B-86 spec-leg's impl leg.
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced at the B-86 council convening (Probe C's adjacent half); **incidentally closed by B-89's repair**, which landed at the U-MEM-26 impl leg 2026-07-28. Arc record at `.harness/u-mem-26-impl-leg-close-2026-07-28.md`.


### B-91 · Report-only degraded-serve `failure_class` / `policy.decision` semantics for the scope-mismatch and `not_derived` reason families *(surfaced by the merge-gate spec-conformance lens on the C-MEM-19 emitter-attrs arc, 2026-07-29; CLOSED 2026-07-29 — Q1 policy_denial applied (R2-converged: class follows the family relation, not the conjunct), Q2 keep-as-is)*

- **What it is.** The B-83 degraded-serve emitter's **report-only** branch (`degraded.rendered is None`, `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`) fires on **three** reason families, not one, and they do not share a telemetry class: **(1)** the scope-mismatch conjuncts (`provider_scope_mismatch` / `provider_family_scope_mismatch`); **(2)** genuine `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason` values carried verbatim from `prompt_packet_fallback_denial` — `no_supported_mode` / `token_budget_empty` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_context.py:134-138`); **(3)** the `not_derived` / `prompt_packet_denial_undetermined` sentinels (`memory_context.py:48-52`). A single rationale covering all three was written into the emitter docstring at PR #1151 and was **false for family (2)**, which is what the merge-gate spec-conformance lens caught.
- **Family (2) is CLOSED at PR #1151.** It now carries `failure_class=POLICY_DENIAL`, mirroring the **primary** DENIAL span, which sets exactly that class for exactly those values (`memory_context.py:210-216`) off a real `select_memory_access_mode` run (`memory_context.py:545-549`). One decision reported by two emitters must not carry two classes. The discrimination is carried as **data** on the `_DegradedMemoryServe` carrier (`policy_denial`, set from membership in the closed `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason` value domain at the site that knows the reason's provenance), never re-derived by string-matching in the emitter.
- **Q1 — should family (1) carry `POLICY_DENIAL` too? DECIDED 2026-07-29: YES.** The deciding text is the C-MEM-13 **recording-surface** paragraph at `design-substrate/Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md:511` — the withholding is recorded on the C-MEM-19 surface *"whose declared coverage already includes standard memory tool calls and policy denial"*. That sentence earns its "no new coverage item needed" by pointing at the **existing** list (`:674-683`), and of its two candidate items a withheld exposure is definitionally **not a tool CALL** — the schemas never reach the model — so *"Policy denial"* (`:683`) is the item being invoked. `memory.failure_class` is the only required attribute (`:687-698`) whose value domain carries that classification, and the failure-class invariant at `:703` uses the **identical phrase**; reading the coverage item and the vocabulary as unrelated would leave the coverage item with no carrier at all. That vocabulary is scoped by **outcome kind** (policy denial / path violation / IO failure / serialization failure / provider adapter failure / retrieval empty-result), never by *which component decided* — which settles the genuinely-open part: a **contract-mandated** withhold and a **resolver's** denial are one telemetry class. Corroborating: the withhold is a `MUST NOT` at `:509`, an invariant at `:523`, a C-MEM-14 exposure qualification at `:559`, and `no_memory_access` — what both branches report — is itself *"a valid policy outcome"* at `:522`.
- **Q1 SCOPE REFINED 2026-07-29 by out-of-family Codex R1 (two [P2]s, both upheld).** The first application set the class on **both** scope conjuncts unconditionally, which over-claimed on two counts — and the arc's own truthfulness principle (never report a determination that was not made) is what condemns it. **[P2-1] the IDENTITY conjunct carries no class at all *(SUPERSEDED by the R2 convergence below — at HEAD the relation IS resolved before the identity return and a confirmed cross-family rebind DOES carry the class)*.** It fires whenever the provider **key** moved, including an `openai`-composed context rebound to `codex` — one family, two keys — where C-MEM-13, which withholds only across **families**, mandates nothing whatsoever; the branch never resolves a family, so it cannot have confirmed the condition the `POLICY_DENIAL` claim rests on. It is a **stale-context safety guard**, and `memory.policy.decision` still names it verbatim. **[P2-2] the FAMILY conjunct carries the class only on a CONFIRMED mismatch.** `_packet_scope_matches_dispatch_family` returned `False` for an absent `record_scope`, an out-of-domain scope family, or an unregistered provider key — states where the relationship is **UNKNOWN**, not known-unequal — so the unconditional flag reported **fail-closed validation** as an operator policy decision. The Q1 reading above is unchanged and still governs the case it actually addressed: a **confirmed** cross-family withhold, both families resolved and unequal. **Discrimination mechanism:** `_packet_scope_family_relation` (new) returns a tri-state `_ScopeFamilyRelation` — `MATCH` / `CONFIRMED_MISMATCH` / `UNVERIFIABLE` — over the **same** existing `provider_family_for_scope_check` + `canonical_scope_family` authorities, no second policy path; `_packet_scope_matches_dispatch_family` is now a pure projection of it (`is MATCH`), so both withholding callers behave **identically** to before and only the telemetry class changed.
- **Q2 — does `not_derived` belong on `memory.policy.decision` at all? DECIDED 2026-07-29: KEEP AS IS** (verbatim; **no code change**). `memory.policy.decision` is a **required** attribute on every memory span (`:694`), so *omitting* it on the one branch where no gate closed would drop a required attribute exactly where a reader most needs to know the decision axis was empty. Mapping to the primary DENIAL span's generic `denied` fallback is the worse option: it asserts a denial **nobody issued** — the same false accusation the per-reason [P2-e] split exists to prevent. Verbatim is truthful on **both** halves of the B-87/B-91 principle: the sentinel names **no gate** (defined distinct from every `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason`, `memory_context.py:48-52`, so it can never be misread as one), while the span still reports `denial` / `no_memory_access` / `record_count=0`, so the degradation is never hidden.
- **No contract defect either way.** C-MEM-19 requires `memory.policy.decision` on every memory span and does **not** enumerate which spans owe a `failure_class`; every answer on the table was conformant, before and after the flip. This row was about telemetry **truthfulness**, not conformance — which is why it registered rather than halted, and why closing it needed a spec **reading** rather than a spec **amendment**.
- **Applied 2026-07-29 (close), as refined by Codex R1 and converged by Codex R2 the same day.** `_degraded_serve_disposition` sets `_DegradedMemoryServe.policy_denial` on exactly the report-only outcomes where a policy determination was **actually reached**: a selector-returned `MemoryAccessModeDenialReason`, and a **confirmed** cross-family withhold (`_ScopeFamilyRelation.CONFIRMED_MISMATCH`) — under **either** scope conjunct. R1 had corrected the first application's unconditional flag to an unconditional `False` on the **identity** branch; R2 found that under-reports by the mirror amount, since an `anthropic`-composed context rebound to `openai` resolves both families, finds them **unequal**, and is a confirmed C-MEM-13 withhold that the identity return exited before ever evaluating — unclassified purely by **test order**. **Converged rule:** `policy_denial` ⟺ `CONFIRMED_MISMATCH`, a function of the family **relation** alone, never of which conjunct fired; the relation is now resolved **once, before** the identity test (it reads only `record_scope` + `provider_name`, neither touched by that test, so no ordering hazard — two dict lookups on an already-degraded path). It stays **unset** on a **same-family** identity rebind, on every `UNVERIFIABLE` family state under either conjunct, and on the sentinels — three shapes of *nobody determined this*. The emitter itself is unchanged, since it already reads the carrier flag. Q2 changed no code. The `#1151`-era emitter docstring, which held the question open, now cites the decisions and the R1 refinement. **Witnesses stay discriminating** per close-out step (3), all four cells pinned: `test_u_mem_26_cross_family_ollama_dispatch_withholds_tools_and_packet` (the confirmed case — scope family `openai`, dispatch `ollama` → `local_open_weight`, **both resolve** and are unequal) asserts `failure_class` **present**; `test_b83_provider_rebound_context_is_reported_but_never_served` (`anthropic`-composed → `openai` — **cross**-family) asserts it **present** on the **identity** guard, while `test_b91_same_family_provider_rebind_is_not_a_policy_denial` (`codex`-composed → `openai`, **one** family) asserts it **absent** on that same guard — the R2 pair pinning the class to the relation rather than to the branch; `test_b83_absent_record_scope_fails_closed_to_report_only` and `test_b86_unregistered_provider_key_fails_closed_against_local_scope` assert it **absent** on the two `UNVERIFIABLE` shapes; `test_b83_undervied_eligibility_reports_not_derived_not_a_gate_denial` asserts it **absent** on the sentinel and additionally pins the Q2 verbatim value. **Mutation probes, all killing** (two re-run at the R2 convergence, on top of three at the R1 refinement and four at the first application): reverting the family construction to an unconditional `True` reddens **both** `UNVERIFIABLE` witnesses; dropping the `CONFIRMED_MISMATCH` `True` reddens the U-MEM-26 cross-family witness; R2 (a) forcing the identity construction back to a relation-blind `False` reddens the **cross-family** rebound witness (`KeyError: 'memory.failure_class'`); R2 (b) forcing it unconditionally `True` reddens the **same-family** rebind witness. **No spec amendment**: a telemetry-truthfulness reading of already-cleared text, decided inside the C-MEM-19 closed enum (attribute **values** only, no new members).
- **Council: no.** A bounded telemetry-semantics decision inside an already-cleared contract, with no cross-domain tension to surface. It does require a careful spec **reading** (C-MEM-13 `:511` / `:523` + C-MEM-14 `:559` against C-MEM-19), so it is not mechanical — but one grounded pass settles both questions.
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced by the merge-gate spec-conformance lens on PR #1151 (the C-MEM-19 `cli_profile` + `policy.decision` emitter-attrs arc); family (2) closed in that same PR. Adjacent registered telemetry-vocabulary row: **B-88** (the closed C-MEM-19 `MemoryTelemetryFailureClass` enum has no input-validation member).
### B-92 · C-MEM-10 promotion eligibility of records captured during a cross-family fallback leg *(named open question carried forward at Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md v1.1 change-note "Named open question carried forward, not discharged." and U-MEM-26's "Out of scope for this unit:" list; Class 1 fork FILED 2026-07-29; CLOSED 2026-07-29 — U-MEM-27 impl leg)*

- **What it is.** The memory spec's **own** named-but-undischarged open question, now filed as a Class 1 fork at `.harness/class_1_fork_c_mem_10_cross_family_promotion_eligibility.md`. Since U-MEM-26 (PR #1148) capture writes under the run's **composed** scope, so a cross-family fallback leg lands an `anthropic`-family record while the dispatch that produced its content ran on `openai`. Whether such a record may be **promoted** — and thereafter injected back into future runs under the primary's family — is the C-MEM-10 question the change-note paragraph **"Named open question carried forward, not discharged."** of `design-substrate/Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` explicitly carries forward: *"whether records captured during a cross-family fallback leg are promotion-eligible under C-MEM-10 … v1.1 neither resolves nor forecloses it"*. `design-substrate/Implementation_Plan_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` lists it out-of-scope for U-MEM-26 with the same carry, at that unit's **"Out of scope for this unit:"** subsection. *(Cite convention, Codex R3 [P2-2]: this row cites the memory spec by contract ID + section name + byte-verified quoted fragment, never by line, per that spec's own v1.1 instruction — "Cite this spec by contract ID and section name, not by line, in any text authored after v1.1." Code cites keep `file:line` and were verified at HEAD `6ab41d7f`, against which no code file differs from the `dd2a8c1a` grounding HEAD.)*
- **Witnessed, not inferred.** A shipped test asserts the behaviour: `test_u_mem_26_capture_is_unaffected_by_the_cross_family_withholding` (`harness-runtime/tests/test_automatic_memory_runtime.py:515`) drives an `anthropic`-primary / `openai`-candidate dispatch and asserts at `:579` that `captured.envelope.scope.provider_family == ProviderFamily.ANTHROPIC.value`.
- **Current behaviour: silent at both entry points — but ZERO live auto-promotion exposure at HEAD.** *(The first draft's exposure claims were corrected by an out-of-family Codex R1 pass, 2026-07-29 — one [P1] and one [P2], both upheld on direct re-read.)* **(1) The hint path — the candidate-side family is producer-defined, hence undefined today.** `_candidate_from_hint` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_promotion.py:296`) builds risk flags from the *hint* with `source_scope=record.envelope.scope` (`:626-629`), but the **candidate** side that `_family_escapes_source` (`:715-743`) compares is `hint.suggested_scope` (`:682`) — a **required, caller-supplied** field (`:191`) with no default and no derivation from the record. A producer mirroring the composed run scope supplies `anthropic` (no flag); a producer supplying the **dispatched** family already trips `CROSS_SCOPE` (`:683`). *Which* convention a producer must supply is itself part of what C-MEM-10 owes, and cannot be read off code that has no producer. `_auto_promote_allowed` (`:776-790`) carries no family term and no risk-flag term. **(2) The model-facing tool path — not a live auto-promotion exposure, for two independent reasons.** `MemoryToolExecutor._propose_promotion` (`memory_tool_executor.py:399-435`) serves the C-MEM-14 `memory.propose_promotion` tool (C-MEM-14 Contract, tool table), hardcodes `confidence=HIGH` (`:423`), and computes `risk_flags=_promotion_risk_flags(source)` (`:425`), which inspects **only** `redaction_state` (`:882-885`) — that no-scope-comparison point stands. What does **not** stand is reachability for a *captured* record. **(a)** The record kind is denied before a candidate is constructed: `_read_retrievable_record_by_ref` (`:554-567`) routes the source through `resolve_retrieval`, and `_record_kind_allowed` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_policy.py:327-333`) denies any kind outside `eligible_record_kinds`; the **sole** production policy `_policy_from_config` (`automatic_memory.py:532-557`) — the only *enabled* `MemoryPolicyDocument` built anywhere under `src/` — pins that set to `_retrievable_kinds()` (`:560-569`), the seven promoted/derived kinds, **excluding every kind capture writes** (`EPISODIC_RUN`/`EPISODIC_TURN`/`TOOL_EVENT`/`COMPACTION_EVENT`, `memory_tool_executor.py:769-775`) — covering both the witness's `EPISODIC_TURN` and `memory.write_note`'s own `TOOL_EVENT` output (`memory_capture.py:471-473`) — so the call raises `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError` (`:565-566`) *before* candidate construction at `:417`. **(b)** An eligible record could not auto-promote either: `_policy_from_config:542` pins `promotion_decision=PROPOSE_SEMANTIC` while `_promotion_auto_allowed` (`:897-903`) returns True only for `PROMOTE_SEMANTIC`/`PROMOTE_PROCEDURAL`, so every candidate on this path takes the `propose_for_review` branch (`:456`) with `review_required=True` — **a branch that is durable but inactive, not ephemeral** *(the R2 correction of the first draft's "review, not durability")*: `propose_for_review` (`memory_promotion.py:328-352`) calls `_persist_decision` with `status=PROPOSED`, and `_persist_decision` (`:451-506`) writes **both** the semantic/procedural record (`write_record`, `:498`) **and** a durable C-MEM-08 operation entry (`append_memory_operation`, `:499-506`). What review withholds is **activation**, not persistence — a `PROPOSED` record is excluded from retrieval by construction (`_INACTIVE_STATUS_REASONS["proposed"]` → `RetrievalExclusionReason.PROPOSED`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_retrieval.py:65` / `:71-77`) — and only `approve` / `edit_and_approve` (`:354-390` / `:416-449`) flip it to `ACTIVE`, neither consulting any family term.
- **What the question actually is, stated exactly.** Not "a live tool auto-promotes cross-family content today", but: **(i)** *future retrievable-kind records* — `eligible_record_kinds` is a C-MEM-09 **policy** field, and a **second-order** case needs no policy change at all, since a semantic/procedural record already promoted out of a cross-family leg is an eligible kind by construction and carries the same unrecorded provenance forward; **(ii)** *future policy configs* setting `PROMOTE_SEMANTIC`/`PROMOTE_PROCEDURAL` with `ReviewMode.AUTOMATIC`, which C-MEM-09 explicitly permits; **(iii)** the *first caller* to populate `promotion_candidates`. **None of the three is individually sufficient, and the row states the combinations rather than letting "a single policy field" imply otherwise** *(Codex R6 [P2-2], upheld by direct read at `1c99e208`; the earlier framing was true of candidate-**reachability**, not of active **promotion**)*: the gate functions are conjunctions and one conjunct is **already satisfied in production**. **(a)** admitting a capture-written kind into `eligible_record_kinds` alone buys **candidate-reachability only** — `_policy_from_config` still pins `PROPOSE_SEMANTIC` (`automatic_memory.py:542`), so `_promotion_auto_allowed` (`memory_tool_executor.py:897-903`) is False and the record lands as a durable, retrieval-excluded `PROPOSED`. **(b)** switching the decision to `PROMOTE_SEMANTIC`/`PROMOTE_PROCEDURAL` alone buys **active auto-promotion of already-eligible kinds only** — exactly the second-order case — since capture-written kinds are still denied before a candidate exists. **(c)** `ReviewMode.AUTOMATIC` buys **nothing: it is already set** (`automatic_memory.py:555`), so only the decision conjunct of `_promotion_auto_allowed` is unmet at HEAD (and the other two modes are live foreclosures a deployment could re-assert — `OPERATOR_REQUIRED` forces review at `:889-890`, `FORBIDDEN` denies the tool at `:406-407`). So on the **tool path** live auto-promotion of a *captured* record requires **(a) ∧ (b)**, both hard-coded side by side at `_policy_from_config` (`:542` and `:556`) and drawn from no `config.memory` field — today a code change, though C-MEM-09 **policy** fields by contract, which is why the gap is real regardless. On the **hint path** it requires **(iii) ∧ (b) ∧ non-`LOW` confidence** (`memory_promotion.py:786-787`; `PROMOTE_PROCEDURAL` specifically for a `PROCEDURAL_UPDATE` kind, `:788-790`) **∧ an actuator that does not exist**: the only `PromotionDecisionService.approve` call site anywhere under `src/` is the tool path's (`memory_tool_executor.py:449`), `extract_from_records` is reached solely from `CompactionSafetyHook.extract_candidates` (`memory_compaction_safety.py:153-159`) whose sibling `complete_compaction` (`:161-209`) persists **dispositions** and never promotes, and `CompactionSafetyHook` itself has no production caller at all (only its definition and its `harness_runtime/__init__.py` export). On that path `auto_promote_allowed=True` is computed, persisted, and **actuated by nothing**. The **contract** gap is unconditioned by all of it — C-MEM-10 has no provenance term at any policy setting. The §1 witness stands regardless: it pins the **capture-side** fact, which is what makes the question well-posed at all.
- **Prerequisite finding — on the composed-scope path (the U-MEM-26 production path), the pipeline cannot discriminate even if policy said to.** *(Scoped by Codex R2; the first draft asserted an exhaustive `provider` data-flow that holds only on that path.)* `EpisodicMemoryCapture` takes `record_scope: MemoryScope | None = None` (`memory_capture.py:253`) and `_scope_for_record` (`:1048-1086`) branches on it. **Composed path (scope supplied):** the envelope is the run's composed scope (`:1074`) through canonicalize-or-deny (`:1083-1086`), and the per-dispatch `provider` never reaches the envelope — this is **production**, since the automatic-memory runtime always supplies a composed scope keyed to `fallback_chain.primary.family.value` (`automatic_memory.py:211-221`, family at `:217`, threaded at `:504-512` / `:511`), and it is the path the witness exercises. **Residual path (no scope):** `_scope_for_record` builds the scope itself with `provider_family=provider` (`:1075-1082`, field at `:1079`), so such a record **does** retain its producing family and the exhaustive claim does not hold for it — but it retains that family by **partitioning the record under it**, the very per-turn re-derivation B-89 named as a defect and B-90 / U-MEM-26 repaired, so the cross-family question **does not arise there at all** (a record written under the producing family is not a foreign-family record inside a primary's partition) and there is nothing for C-MEM-10 to discriminate. **Force undiminished:** the path where the question is well-posed is exactly the path that cannot answer it, and it is the production path. On that path, `capture_turn_completion` writes `content` with **no** provider and **no** dispatched-model field (`:407-422`); `provider` / `model` reach only the **C-MEM-08 ledger row** (`:694-707`; `MemoryOperationPayload.provider` at `:1006`, `memory_refs=(memory_id,)` at `:1010`) and the **C-MEM-19 span** attributes (`:686-688`, `:714-716`) — and promotion reads neither (`_hints_from_record` reads `record.content` alone, `:545-560`). So readings B and C below are not merely unbuilt for composed-scope records (every record the production path writes), they are **unrepresentable**, and surfacing the discriminator is itself contract-altitude work, X-AL-3-blocked at Phase 7.
- **Second grounded correction — `risk_flags` gates nothing today.** A repo-wide grep finds it only at its definition, its two construction sites, and its persistence; `_review_required` (`memory_promotion.py:762-773`) never consults it and `_auto_promote_allowed` reads `review_required`, not flags. Any flag-based reading must therefore state the **gate** as well as the flag or it lands inert.
- **Net, corrected.** The permissiveness is **structural, not yet exercised**: live auto-promotion exposure at HEAD is **nil** on the composed-scope production path — the tool path is closed twice over (by record kind and by policy decision), and the hint path is **unfed** (the sole production caller passes `promotion_candidates=()`, `automatic_memory.py:273`; the extractor is otherwise reached only from compaction safety, `memory_compaction_safety.py:159`) with its candidate convention undefined. What is real *now* is the contract gap — which **no single named change converts into a live exposure** (Codex R6 [P2-2]; the combinations are **(a) ∧ (b)** on the tool path, with **(c)** `ReviewMode.AUTOMATIC` already satisfied in production, or the hint producer **∧ (b) ∧ an actuator that does not exist**). What a single change *does* buy is the **transition below it** — (a) makes captured records candidate-reachable and durably `PROPOSED`; (b) makes the second-order case actively auto-promoting — and each such transition happens **with no further review**, because no gate on any of these paths has a family term to consult. That is why this is a Class 1 **spec** question and not a Phase 7 bug, and why the **urgency** is low while the **necessity** is not: nothing is leaking today, the last step to leaking is a two-field policy change nothing forbids, and the contract has no position to fall back on when it happens.
- **Three readings (fork §4).** **(A)** promotion-eligible unchanged, status quo made **explicit** — cheapest (one C-MEM-10 paragraph, zero code, zero discriminator); grounded in C-MEM-03 §"`MemoryScope.provider_family` value domain and derivation" (the run's partition is a run-level identity the fallback chain preserves), the B-86/B-89 capture ratification (C-MEM-13 §"Cross-family withholding of standard memory tools", "a different authorship class"), and the fact that the content passed the same capture pipeline as any other record. **Codex R4 [P1] correction to that second bullet, upheld by direct read and stated rather than quietly repaired:** a first draft added *"promotion confers durability on content the harness holds, and grants the foreign candidate no new reach"*, and **both halves were wrong — promotion is a reach transition, not a durability one.** The captured record is **already durable**: `_capture` writes it to the canonical store (`self._store.write_record(record)`, `memory_capture.py:730`) *before* its C-MEM-08 row, deliberately (`:721-729`). What promotion adds is **injectability** — every capture-written kind sits outside the sole production policy's `eligible_record_kinds` (`_policy_from_config` pins it to `_retrievable_kinds()`, `automatic_memory.py:556`, defined `:560-569`), and a `PROPOSED` promotion output is retrieval-excluded by construction (`memory_retrieval.py:71-77`), so **only** an `ACTIVE` semantic/procedural record is retrievable and therefore injectable into a future run. Foreign-produced content **does** gain new reach at promotion — content that could not enter a future run's context becomes content that can, under the primary's family attribution — which is exactly the Memory threat model §Threats channel *"Cross-run prompt-injection persistence through promoted semantic/procedural memory."* and exactly the §Invariants transition *"Model-authored notes are episodic by default and cannot become injectable semantic memory without policy and evidence."* What gains nothing is the foreign **provider** (no capability, no tool, no boundary crossing it did not already have) — that, and only that, is the true residue of the C-MEM-13 carve-out. **A's honest form is therefore "the reach transition is *acceptable* because the composed scope is the run's declared identity", not "there is no reach transition"**: A loses the only rationale that claimed the question was *benign* rather than merely *acceptable*, and B's contract argument is correspondingly **strengthened**. **(B)** flag cross-family-produced candidates with a `CROSS_SCOPE`-equivalent risk flag **plus a stated gate** (review-required, never auto-promotable) — preserves eligibility, removes silent auto-promotion, requires the discriminator; grounded in the threat model's own provenance axis (its §Threats opener and its cross-run-prompt-injection-persistence bullet, and its model-authored-notes §Invariant). **(C)** refuse promotion outright — strongest isolation, still requires the discriminator, and forecloses the continuity value the B-86 council explicitly preserved.
- **Discriminator options (fork §5; needed by B and C).** **(i) A new content/envelope field at C-MEM-03 altitude** — **two variants with materially different blast radii, split at Codex R6 [P2-1] (upheld by direct read at `1c99e208`) because the R4 accounting charged the identity-movement consequence to the whole of (i) when it belongs to the content variant alone.** *Both* variants pay a closed-schema amendment (`MemoryRecordEnvelope` is `ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_record_envelope.py:129`; and at contract altitude either reverses v1.1's own *"zero new field"* posture, change-note **"Sections preserved verbatim at v1.1."**, one delta later), *both* are derived at **one central site** (R9 below), and *both* are **forward-only** absent a back-fill (which would be option (ii) run offline, inheriting its whole unresolvable set). **Codex R9 [P2-1] correction, upheld by direct read at `26720e8e` and stated rather than quietly repaired:** the pre-R9 text charged both variants with *"touching every capture writer"* (fork §5: *"Six `capture_*` methods plus `_capture` / `_record` thread the new value"*) — **false on two counts.** There are **seven** `capture_*` methods on `EpisodicMemoryCapture` (`memory_capture.py:294`/`:337`/`:382`/`:439`/`:487`/`:534`/`:585`; class at `:241`), not six, and **none needs to thread anything**: each already takes `provider: str | None` and passes it to `_capture` (`:321`/`:366`/`:423`/`:471`/`:518`/`:569`/`:615`), which threads it into `_record` (`:649-658`). `_record` (`:1015-1046`) already holds **both** inputs the predicate needs — the call's raw `provider` (`:1025`) and the record's **resolved** scope from `_scope_for_record` (`:1038-1042`, defined `:1048-1086`) — so the derivation is a **single hoist inside `_record`**, with zero per-method threading and zero public signature change; What makes the join well-defined is that the capture writer derives the key **deterministically** from the id (`idempotency_key=Identifier(f"idempotent:{action_id}")`, `memory_capture.py:999`, the sole construction site for every `capture_*` method), so the key **is reconstructible at promotion time from the stored record alone**, and once reconstructed the ledger guarantees **at most one** occupying entry. Two consequences the contract must carry: **(1) state the join on the key, not on the id**; and **(2) qualify on `operation_kind == CAPTURE`** — writer namespacing (`capture:...` here vs promotion's `promotion:...` at `memory_promotion.py:523-528`, which shares the *identical* `idempotent:{action_id}` spelling) is a convention across producers, not a ledger invariant, so the matched row must be **confirmed** to be a capture row, never assumed to be one. **Codex R7 [P1] correction, upheld by direct read at `d8df7647` and stated rather than quietly repaired — a matched row is not, by itself, a row about *this version of* the record, so (ii-a) owes a third consequence: a MANDATORY record/ledger coherence check whose detection bound must be stated.** Exhibited by a **shipped test**, not hypothesized: `test_a_divergent_second_run_start_capture_is_not_read_as_completion` (`harness-runtime/tests/test_u_mem_26_write_boundary.py:1602-1662`) — a divergent second `capture_run_start` for one `run_id`, reachable because `EpisodicMemoryCapture` is a **public API** and `LocalAutomaticMemoryRuntime`'s presence guard is not in it, **overwrites `run.json`** (`memory_capture.py:730`) and only *then* meets the first call's row (`:732`). The capture correctly returns `FAILED`, but the durable residue is a record holding **call two's** content beside a single ledger row holding **call one's** `provider`; reconstructing the (ii-a) key against that record still resolves to exactly **one** `CAPTURE` row with a non-`None` provider, so every qualification above passes and the join returns **stale provenance as if determined**. None of cases (1)-(5) catches it. **What is checkable, exactly:** no field on the capture row binds it to a stored-content *version* — `MemoryOperationEntry` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_operation_ledger.py:136-154`) carries no content hash; the `response_hash` inherited from `StateLedgerEntry` (`state_ledger_entry_schema.py:164-169`) is computed over **the ledger entry's own** canonical payload (`compute_memory_operation_response_hash`, `:335-338`, over `canonicalize_memory_operation`, `:324-332`); and `memory_refs` carries a `run_id`-derived, content-independent `memory_id`. So *"bind the row to the stored content hash"* **is not available at HEAD** — the field does not exist. What *is* available is the set of values `_capture` threads from **one call** into **both** surfaces: `entry.timestamp` ↔ `record.envelope.created_at` (to `_record` at `:649-658` and `_operation_payload` at `:694-707`), `entry.cli_profile` ↔ `content["cli_profile"]`, `entry.engine_class` ↔ `content["engine_class"]` (`_engine_class_value`, `:1122-1125`), `entry.step_id` ↔ `content["step_id"]` on the kinds that carry one, and `entry.run_id` ↔ `content["run_id"]` (vacuous — the key already derives from it). The `created_at` comparison must be scoped to **dispatch** rows (`repair_capture_operation` takes the repairer's own `datetime.now(UTC)`, `automatic_memory.py:442`), which costs nothing since a repair row is case (5) already. **Codex R8 [P2-1] correction, upheld by direct read at `d9907c24` and stated rather than quietly repaired — that comparable-field set is PER-KIND and the check is owed on `EPISODIC_RUN` ALONE.** Only `capture_run_start` (`memory_capture.py:309-320`) and `capture_run_close` (`:354-365`) write `cli_profile` and `engine_class` into **content**; `capture_turn_completion` (`:407-422`), `capture_tool_event` (`:459-470`), `capture_provider_route` (`:504-517`), `capture_failure_observation` (`:553-568`) and `capture_compaction_event` (`:604-614`) write neither — for those kinds both values reach the **ledger row only** (`_operation_payload`, `:1008-1009`) — while `step_id` is content-side on the turn / tool kinds and `None` on **both** surfaces for the run kinds (`:328` / `:377`) and compaction (`:622`). Stated kind-blind, the check false-`UNVERIFIABLE`s the entire non-run corpus against content fields those writers never store. **And the window it exists to close is `EPISODIC_RUN`-only anyway:** `_memory_id_for` (`:1100-1109`) derives every non-run kind's id from `content_hash` and `capture_operation_action_id(event_kind, memory_id)` (`:68-77`) composes the join key from that id — so there **the key IS the content binding**, precisely what R7 found missing for `EPISODIC_RUN`; a divergent re-capture is a *different* `memory_id` with its own row, and row and stored version cannot come apart. Every content-side comparator is therefore vacuous by construction there, leaving `created_at` — which **false-positives**: `timestamp` is not in the ledger's equivalence payload (`_equivalence_payload_from_payload`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_operation_ledger.py:499-519`; eighteen keys, `provider` at `:511`, no `timestamp`), so a benign identical-content re-capture at a later instant returns `IDEMPOTENT_NOOP` while re-writing the record with a new `created_at`, and the three JSONL-backed episodic kinds read **last-match-wins** (`_read_jsonl_record`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_store.py:445-463`; `_JSONL_BY_KIND` at `:143-147`). The genuinely divergent case never gets there — the equivalence payload *does* carry `provider`, so a same-content re-capture on a different provider raises `MemoryOperationIdempotencyConflictError` and, not being `RUN_START_EVENT_KIND`, re-raises into `FAILED` (`memory_capture.py:796-802`). **So the contract text is:** mandatory on `EPISODIC_RUN`, comprising `envelope.created_at` ↔ `entry.timestamp` (dispatch rows only), `content["cli_profile"]` ↔ `entry.cli_profile` and `content["engine_class"]` ↔ `entry.engine_class` (on the enum's `.value`, `_engine_class_value`, `:1122-1125`); **not owed on any other kind**. The residual disposition (α/β/γ) is likewise `EPISODIC_RUN`-scoped, which *sharpens* β — it is visibly the whole affected corpus, not a subset. **And the honest bound: this check does not close the case that produced it.** The witness's two calls differ in `workflow_id` / `provider` / `model` / `policy_ref` and agree on `cli_profile`, `engine_class` and `timestamp`; `provider` / `model` / `policy_ref` / `procedural_snapshot_ref` are **ledger-only** and `workflow_id` / `thread_id` / `provider_route` / `started_at` / `close_status` are **content-only**, so a divergence confined to either set is invisible to any comparison the two surfaces support. **The spec leg therefore owes an explicit disposition of the residual**, in one of three forms, none free: **(α)** add the record's `content_hash` (or an envelope-version stamp) to the capture row — a **C-MEM-08 closed-schema field addition**, i.e. exactly the schema cost (ii) was preferred for avoiding, and it repairs no already-written row; **(β)** classify every `EPISODIC_RUN` record `UNVERIFIABLE` by rule, which is (ii-b) applied to that kind and carries its stated foreclosure; or **(γ)** state the residual as **accepted**. **(i-envelope) has no counterpart residual** — its field ships *inside* the version it describes. **(ii-b) fail closed on ambiguity** — define no event-qualified key and map any multi-row resolution to `UNVERIFIABLE`. It invents no join semantics, but it is **not** the conservative default it looks like: it makes **every** `EPISODIC_RUN` record permanently unverifiable the moment `capture_run_close` acquires a production caller, i.e. it silently becomes reading **C** for run records while presenting itself as reading B, and must be taken as a stated foreclosure. The two are **not exclusive**: (ii-a) is the join, (ii-b) is its residue. Its real costs are therefore a **new cross-contract dependency** (C-MEM-10 on C-MEM-08 availability, plus an unindexed scan of `durable/memory_ops.jsonl` — no index over `memory_refs` *or* `action_id`) and an **unresolvable set each round makes larger — R3 took it from one case to three, R4 to five, R7 to six**: (1) no reachable capture row (promotion-, compaction-, native-adapter-authored, or unreadable ledger); (2) `stored_capture_event_type` returning `None` — deliberately strict, *"an unrecognizable record, never a guess at one"* — so the record cannot name its own writer; (3) the composed **key** matching no row (a torn capture whose repair never ran, `memory_capture.py:721-732`); **(4) [R4]** the matched row is **not** a `CAPTURE` row (`operation_kind != MemoryOperationKind.CAPTURE`) — the cross-producer `action_id` namespacing convention did not hold, and the ledger never guaranteed it would; **(5) [R4]** the matched row **is** a capture row but carries `provider = None`, which is the torn-capture **repair** row's shape *by construction* (`repair_capture_operation` passes `provider=None` / `model=None`, `memory_capture.py:938-939`, deliberately — *"a repair row attests that this capture is durable, not which dispatch performed it"*, `:916-921`), so a **repaired** capture yields *unknown* provenance and must not read as *same-family* merely because a row was found; **(6) [R7, scoped at R8]** the matched row **fails the record/ledger coherence check** (above) — row and stored record disagree on a value only one call could have written. **`EPISODIC_RUN` only** (`envelope.created_at` ↔ `entry.timestamp` on dispatch rows, `content["cli_profile"]`, `content["engine_class"]`; **not** `step_id`, `None` on both surfaces there — and the other kinds' join key is itself the content binding, so the failure mode cannot arise) — so the row is about a *different version* of this record and its `provider` is not this content's provenance; **detection-bounded, not exhaustive**, per the residual disposition above. Plus the ambiguity arm: **any** resolution returning more than one row is `UNVERIFIABLE` — **mandatory in the contract regardless**, vacuous only for the exact key-shaped (ii-a) join, since any join keyed on `action_id` or on `memory_refs` carries no single-row guarantee at all. All of them must be specified rather than defaulted — reuse the B-91 tri-state idiom verbatim (`MATCH` / `CONFIRMED_MISMATCH` / `UNVERIFIABLE`; `UNVERIFIABLE` → review-required, never auto-promote).
- **Recommendation: reading B [MODERATE] on Q1. On Q2 the recommendation is WITHDRAWN at R7 — the comparison has LEVELED and is presented as a two-option decision, not a pick, with a payload sub-choice under (i) added at R8.** *(R8 tested the leveling and left it standing: its two findings refine one column each — (ii)'s coherence check narrowed to `EPISODIC_RUN`, (i)'s boolean payload de-priced — and cancel on the balance. **R9 tested it again and it held again:** [P2-1] struck (i)'s write-side reach, but on the one axis (ii) had already won at zero, leaving the three axes that carry (ii)'s side untouched.)* Through R6 the pick was **(ii)** with the **(ii-a)** event-qualified join, held in place by **one** asymmetry: that (i-envelope) resolved the multi-writer kind by silent last-writer-wins accident where (ii-a) resolved it deliberately. **R7 [P2] found that asymmetry false** (envelope and content are co-written from one call, so the field describes the version it ships inside — (ii-a)'s semantics reached *directly*), and **R7 [P1] found the reverse asymmetry real** (nothing on a capture row binds it to a stored-content version, so a divergent second writer leaves (ii-a) reading stale provenance from a correctly-qualified single row — a case (i-envelope) cannot have). Having said at R6 that a struck-out cost *would* move the balance and that this row would say so, it says so. **The leveled ledger.** **(i-envelope)**: same-call provenance semantics that cannot go stale relative to the version they describe; no identity movement; no cross-contract dependency; a one-field read side — *costs* a closed-schema amendment at C-MEM-03 reversing v1.1's own zero-new-field posture one delta later, a second family-valued field beside `MemoryScope.provider_family`, and it is **forward-only** (no help for already-written records absent a back-fill, which is option (ii) offline) — the *"every capture writer touched"* cost previously listed here is **struck at R9 [P2-1]** as false. **(ii)/(ii-a)**: read-side only *as specified*, works on already-written records, and is the **only** option that can answer **aggregate-run** provenance (every capture row for the run is retained with its own `provider`; an envelope carries one writer's value only) — *costs* a new cross-contract read dependency plus an unindexed scan, **five** owed contract sentences (up from four), a mandatory coherence check whose detection bound must be stated, and an explicit disposition of the residual it cannot reach, of which **(α)** is itself a C-MEM-08 closed-schema addition — so "read-side only" is true of (ii-a) *as specified*, not of every honest closure of it. **What would decide it, and what this filing declines to invent:** the two columns answer *different questions* and the requirement has never been stated. **Stored-version provenance** ("which dispatch produced the content I am promoting") leaves them semantically equivalent on the coherent path with (i-envelope) strictly more reliable on the incoherent one; **aggregate-run provenance** ("did any leg of this run run cross-family") *requires* (ii), and adopting that reading is itself a decision this filing has not argued for. Q2 confidence stays **[MODERATE]** and is now confidence in the *framing* rather than in a pick: this comparison has been corrected at R3 (wrong field family), R4 (wrong uniqueness guarantee), R6 (variant-blind cost) and twice at R7, once on each side. What the filing carries forward is the mechanics **both** options must respect — state the key exactly and what enforces its uniqueness; state the coherence check and its detection bound; state the residual's disposition; and under (i) state hash-inertness and the forward-only consequence. The B-86 council record decides it in two directions at once. It **forecloses C**: C3's continuity argument (candidate-side partitioning *"makes the moment accumulated context matters most (the fallback leg) the moment it disappears — silent, permanent, inverted-in-timing data loss"*) and C6's *"a fallback chain is a **continuity** abstraction, not a substitution abstraction"* refinement apply *a fortiori* to a promotion refusal. It does **not license A's silence**: C10 classified `memory.write_note` `write-bounded-irreversible` precisely because it is *"durable, primary-attributed, promotion-eligible"* — naming promotion-eligibility itself as part of the danger — and declined to re-key the scope only because the *mechanism* was wrong (*"the defect is in the absent gate at the dispatch boundary, not in the scope's key"*).
