### B-93 · Whole-root memory-write serialization has no deadline — an unbounded guarded precondition stalls every memory writer on the host *(surfaced by the merge-gate concurrency lens on the U-MEM-27 impl leg, PR #1159, 2026-07-29; classified REGISTER at the post-#1159 gate-log grounding pass, 2026-07-30)* *(**RATIFIED 2026-08-05 as READING B** — deadline YES, Windows NO, vehicle HAND-ROLLED; **CLOSED 2026-08-06 — #1241**, the build leg)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-06 — #1241 (the build leg).** Reading B built as ratified, **hand-rolled, no dependency added**. All **nine** acquisition sites bounded by a non-blocking probe + bounded retry against one typed **`CrossProcessLockTimeoutError` homed at `harness-core`** (`harness_core.cross_process_lock_deadline`, which also hosts the mechanism — `CrossProcessLockDeadline` + `flock_until_deadline`; zero workspace deps, and `fcntl` is imported lazily *inside* the helper so `import harness_core` stays Windows-safe). **Two design choices beyond the ratification, both flagged overturnable.** *First*, the deadline is **end-to-end per entry surface**, not per acquisition — trap 1 says one entry surface blocks at up to three sites in sequence *and* retries the whole acquisition on an inode swap, so a per-acquisition bound is exactly the partial-guarantee-that-reads-as-total variant **F** was dominated on; each of the seven entry surfaces mints one **absolute** deadline and threads it down, witnessed by *elapsed time across two sequential waits* rather than by a docstring. *Second*, the default budget is **300 s** — conservative because the registered harm is entirely prospective while a short bound would convert working systems into failing ones; every entry surface takes a per-call `deadline_seconds` override. **ABBA release-before-blocking preserved** at all three probe arms and separately witnessed (a sibling ledger in the same directory stays writable while a caller waits on the file lock). **Hold-time contract** documented at `write_record_guarded`. **§3(ii) reconciler import repair** landed — see `B-45`, whose no-op-surface enumeration this changes from six to seven. **58 new witnesses** (22 `harness-core` unit + 17 `harness-is` per-site + 19 across the `harness-runtime` suites), every per-site one driven by a **genuine second OS process** and each pinning *which* lock timed out via `lock_target`, so one bounded early acquisition cannot make the other eight pass. **The unwitnessed `_workflow_lock` carrier (codex R9) is now witnessed by execution** — a second OS process runs the *real* `_workflow_lock` and this process provably cannot enter until it leaves; deliberately **not** a deadline test, so exclusion and liveness stay separate claims. **43 PD-8 mutation probes, all RED:** reverting each of the nine sites to a bare blocking `flock` **hangs** its witness (the pre-B-93 harm reproduced); restoring the module-scope `import fcntl` fails the import-repair witness; deleting `_workflow_lock`'s flock fails the exclusion witness; re-minting the deadline at the second site fails the end-to-end witness *on elapsed time*; giving up after the first probe fails the acquire-on-release witness.
- **One behavioural consequence the filing did not anticipate — recorded, not absorbed.** Polling does **not** preserve the kernel's **handoff fairness**. A blocking `flock` parks the waiter in the kernel, which grants the lock on release before the ex-holder can realistically re-acquire it; a *polling* waiter is asleep at that instant, so a hot re-acquiring holder wins the next round. This changes **ordering, never exclusion** — mutual exclusion is the same kernel `flock` it always was — and starvation is bounded at both ends (the poll ceiling, and the deadline itself). It is **intrinsic to the ratified shape**, not to this implementation: `filelock` — the vehicle the fork evaluated and declined — polls at ten times this interval, and `msvcrt.LK_LOCK` retries at 1 s; no portable primitive offers a kernel-parked wait *with* a timeout. It surfaced as a real regression in **one shipped witness**, `test_rollback_cross_process_lock_prevents_lost_concurrent_append`, whose fixed child timestamp silently **pinned the old ordering** under a **zero** clock-skew tolerance — repaired **order-INDEPENDENTLY** — an order-pinned formulation proved flaky in *both* directions (`flock` specifies no acquisition ordering, so an early stamp needs the child to win and a late one needs the parent to), so the child stamps the pre-existing entry's own timestamp and, if the parent landed first, retries with C-IS-07 §7.6's `WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP`. The position assertion an interim round added was **removed** — it asserted a property `flock` does not provide. The load-bearing survival assertion is unchanged, still discriminates under mutation, and the witness is 20/20 clean on repetition. A **second** shipped witness, `test_ac9d_never_holds_two_journal_locks_at_once`, keyed its flock spy on `op == LOCK_EX` and silently reported a peak of **zero** once the probe became `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` — a **pass-on-absence**, fixed by matching the *bit* and by counting only **successful** acquisitions.
- **RATIFIED 2026-08-05 as READING B** — decision 2 (liveness deadline) **YES**, decision 1 (Windows serialization backend) **NO**, decision 3 (vehicle) **HAND-ROLLED EXTENSION of the existing primitive, NOT `filelock`**. Operator `AskUserQuestion` on the fork's §8 (`.harness/class_2_fork_b93_b45_lock_deadline_windows_backend.md`). **The build leg owes:** a deadline at **all nine** acquisition sites; one typed **`CrossProcessLockTimeoutError` homed at `harness-core`** (settled by the `ValidatorEscalationGateTimeoutError` precedent — defining it in `harness-runtime` is **illegal**, inverting the IS 0-outbound invariant); the ABBA release-before-blocking handoff **preserved** at all three probe arms; the hold-time contract documented at `write_record_guarded`; the §3(ii) **reconciler import repair**; and ≥1 process-based deadline witness per site-class **including the `_workflow_lock` carrier, UNWITNESSED at HEAD** (codex R9 — the reconciler CAS test proves `os.link`, not `_workflow_lock`), each with a PD-8 mutation probe. **Vehicle rationale as ratified:** seven of the nine sites are exclusive-only and need no shared face; `filelock` is revisited only if decision 1 later goes YES. **Zero spec and plan delta under every reading** — so **no spec leg** and no X-AL-3 exposure. **Status → `open`** (fork §9: status flips for a YES half; `open` is the enum's actionable-now-no-blocker value and this half has no design-substrate gate); the row closes when the build leg merges. Variants **E** and **F** stay recorded as **dominated** so they are not re-proposed.
- **What it is.** Every `CanonicalMemoryStore` write takes `cross_process_scope_lock` over the whole memory **root** (`_write_scope`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_store.py`) — deliberately, because the section `write_record_guarded` wraps re-reads a caller-chosen set of *other* records before writing this one, and a per-file lock cannot exclude a writer of a file the section has not named yet. That lock is a plain **blocking** `flock(LOCK_EX)` with no timeout (`_DirLock.acquire`, `harness-is/src/harness_is/cross_process_ledger_lock.py`). `write_record_guarded` additionally holds it **across a caller-supplied precondition callable**, so the hold time of a root-wide exclusive lock is set by code the store does not control and cannot bound.
- **No live hazard at HEAD.** The only precondition in the tree is `_provenance_unchanged` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_promotion.py`), bounded at one `read_record` per cited source memory ref — a small N of local file reads, no network, no operator wait, no unbounded loop. This row is registered against a **future** precondition, not a present stall.
- **Why it is worth registering anyway.** The seam is **generic by design** — it "knows nothing about what the precondition tests" — which is exactly what makes the next precondition author unaware that they are holding a host-wide lock. An operator confirmation, a provider round-trip, or a retrieval sweep inside a precondition blocks **every same-host memory writer**: a `harness run` alongside a `harness daemon` is the shared-root case the seam's own SCOPE paragraph documents, and it would block with no deadline and no diagnostic.
- **No convention to copy — which is why this is a scoped arc, not a one-liner.** Counted by direct read at HEAD — **recounted 2026-07-31 at the `B-103` arc: nine, not eight, across four modules, not three** (`journal_workflow_pause_store.cross_process_journal_lock` was created at the `B-97`(a) leg, PR #1171, *after* this row's original count) — this codebase has **nine blocking-`flock` acquisition sites** across **four** modules, reachable through **seven** entry surfaces — and *not one of them* takes a timeout. In `harness-is/src/harness_is/cross_process_ledger_lock.py` (**six** sites): `_DirLock.acquire` `:133` (`LOCK_EX`), the shared engine behind **all four** of that module's entry surfaces (`_dir_lock_for` callers at `:213` scope / `:365` write / `:484` replace / `:572` read); `cross_process_write_lock` `:406` (`LOCK_EX`); `cross_process_replace_lock` `:507` (`LOCK_EX`); `cross_process_read_lock` `:605` (**`LOCK_SH`** — so "they are all `LOCK_EX`" is false); `_acquire_legacy_sidecar_for_writer` `:274` (`LOCK_EX`); `_acquire_legacy_sidecar_if_present` `:330` (`LOCK_EX`/`LOCK_SH`). In `harness-runtime` (**three** sites): `reconciler_pause_resume_substrate._workflow_lock` `:294` (`LOCK_EX`), `protected_result_store._cross_process_lock` `:371` **[superseded — see the post-edit anchor note on this row: `:371` was the pre-#1237 value]** (`LOCK_EX`) *(cite corrected from `:347` at the 2026-08-05 re-check)*, and — **new at the 2026-07-31 recount** — `journal_workflow_pause_store.cross_process_journal_lock` `:489` (`LOCK_EX`), the per-workflow pause-journal append lock promoted to module scope at `B-97`(a); it is a **leaf** (nothing inside its hold takes another cross-process lock), so it adds a site but no ordering hazard. **The `B-45` co-rider text now agrees** — B-45's own 2026-07-31 refresh names this same module as its fourth Windows no-op surface, so both rows enumerate the same four-module primitive set. A deadline means `LOCK_NB` + retry + a new typed exception at each, so putting one on a single site would itself be the inconsistent surface.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Pick the deadline shape — `LOCK_NB` + bounded retry with backoff (portable, and composes with B-45's Windows backend) or a watchdog around the blocking call. **(2)** Choose the timeout's semantics and its exception: a **new** typed error distinct from `MemoryStoreGuardedWriteConflictError`, because a refused commit is a *precondition* outcome and a timeout is a *liveness* one — collapsing them would let a caller retry-loop against a stuck host. **(3)** Apply it consistently across **all nine acquisition sites** above — the acquisition site, not the entry surface, is where a deadline goes. **Two traps** a naive impl falls into. *First*, one entry surface can block at up to **three** distinct sites in sequence (dir lock → legacy sidecar → file lock), so a deadline bolted onto `cross_process_write_lock`'s own `flock` leaves the other two unbounded and the entry surface still has no end-to-end bound. *Second*, the three `LOCK_NB` calls (`:402`, `:498`, `:599`) are contention **probes**, not deadlines, and must not be counted as coverage — on contention each arm releases the directory lock and THEN blocks at `:406`/`:507`/`:605` (release-before-blocking, the ABBA-avoidance handoff to preserve). **(4)** Document the hold-time contract at `write_record_guarded` so a precondition author meets the constraint at the seam rather than in production.
- **Natural co-rider on B-45.** Both arcs traverse the same set of lock primitives — B-45 to give them a Windows backend, this row to give them a deadline — so doing them together costs one traversal instead of two.
- **Council: no.** An implementation-level liveness bound on an already-cleared lock mechanism (C-IS-09 §9.4 defers the mechanism to implementation discretion), with no cross-domain tension to name. Step (2) does carry a real design choice, so it is not mechanical — `advisor()` + out-of-family review at build time is the right weight. Council-eligible only if taken **with** B-45 and the Windows tradeoff makes the deadline semantics non-obvious. ***CONDITION MET AND ADJUDICATED 2026-08-05*** at the B-93+B-45 combined fork filing — the antecedent holds (the rows ARE taken together) and the consequent is **FALSE, probe-resolved**: `msvcrt.LK_NBLCK` gives Windows the same non-blocking-probe shape close-out step (1) prescribes and `LK_LOCK` already carries a fixed ~10 s bound, so the backend decides *exclusion granularity* while the deadline decides *liveness* and neither constrains the other. **No dyad convenes.** The one convening that IS owed: a **Reading-A** selection (Windows backend before a Windows CI witness) owes a dyadic **C3 ⊥ C11** convening — see `B-45`.

### B-94 · Derived-index auto-refresh rebuild overlap race — two concurrent rebuilds can leave the OLDER snapshot last and reading fresh *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex R5 on the B-93 gate-log arc, 2026-07-30; classified PRE-EXISTING by git-show verification against fc40fb2b)*

- **What it is.** `DerivedRetrievalIndexStore.rebuild` computes its entry set from the filesystem and *then* appends it, holding **no lock across the two** (`_append_jsonl` is a bare `open("ab")` + write). Two overlapping rebuilds interleave as: X reads the record set → a commit lands → Y reads the **newer** set and appends it → X appends its **older** set **last**. `read_current` resolves an untokenized ledger by **position** (last rebuild wins), so it returns X's stale snapshot with `stale=False`: a committed record missing from an index reported as current.
- **Pre-existing, and NOT widened by the B-93 arc — verified by `git show fc40fb2b`.** Pre-branch `rebuild` (`memory_retrieval_index.py:177-200`) computed entries at `:180` and appended at `:199` with no lock; `_append_jsonl` (`:571-574`) took none either; `read_current` (`:210-227`) was purely positional last-wins; and `AutoRefreshingDerivedRetrievalIndexStore.read_current` (`automatic_memory.py:110-114`) rebuilt on missing/stale with no coordination. The same interleaving produces the same wrong outcome on the pre-branch code. An all-untokenized ledger takes the identical positional path before and after the arc.
- **What the B-93 arc covered, and why this sits outside it.** That arc added a commit-ordering protocol — `commit_seq` stamped inside the memory store's write hold, plus a `rebuilt_coverage` event binding a rebuild to the commit it answers — which orders **tokenized** rebuilds: the hook path, where the caller has an invalidation event to quote. The **production auto-refresh path is untokenized by design**: it rebuilds because a read found the index missing or stale, not in response to a specific write, so it has no token to pass and correctly falls to the legacy positional rule. The protocol does not reach this race.
- **Candidate fix shape** *(Codex R5's direction, recorded not built)*. Derive a coverage token on the auto-refresh path from **the ledger length captured at the read that decided to rebuild**. That read already walks the whole ledger, so its byte length at that moment is free — and it is exactly the monotonic quantity `_next_commit_seq` uses. It names *"the state I found stale"*, which is the honest under-claiming attribution the rebuild contract already requires. The subclass would capture it in its `except` branch and pass it to `rebuild(commit_seq=...)`; the existing ordering rules then reject the older overlapping snapshot with no change to `read_current`.
- **Open questions for build time.** **(1)** The capture must happen *inside* the failed read or it re-races — `read_current` returns nothing on the raise, so the token needs a carrier on the exception or a private read variant. **(2)** Whether the fix belongs at the `harness-runtime` subclass (where auto-refresh policy lives) or the IS-axis base (where token semantics live) — the IS axis has **zero outbound cross-axis edges**, so a base-class change must not import runtime concerns. **(3)** Whether a losing rebuild should be **pruned** rather than merely ignored, since the ledger still grows by a full snapshot per overlap.
- **Not urgent.** The outcome is a **stale-but-valid** index — a retrieval base that under-serves, never a wrong record — the path self-corrects at the next canonical write's stale marker, and single-process local development (the default posture) does not overlap rebuilds at all.
- **Council: no.** A bounded concurrency fix inside an already-cleared mechanism, with the ordering protocol it would extend already built and witnessed. No cross-domain tension: the question is *where the token is captured*, not whether the index should be ordered. Open question (2) is a real placement decision, so `advisor()` + out-of-family review at build time is the right weight.
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced by Codex R5 on the B-93 gate-log arc. Sibling: **B-93** (no deadline on the same substrate's blocking locks) — both re-check on the same trigger, a second concurrent memory consumer becoming routine.
- **2026-08-05 grounding re-check at HEAD `43d4dda5` — premise INTACT and now documented in code; disposition FORK-SHAPED (low urgency).** The `memory_retrieval_index.py` module docstring names **both** B-95 and B-94 explicitly at `:19-23` (*"Rebuilds that pass no `commit_seq` — which includes the production auto-refresh path, untokenized by design — remain positional last-wins … See register row B-94."*). `_append_jsonl` still takes no lock; `read_current` still resolves untokenized ledgers positionally; and the production auto-refresh path is confirmed untokenized — `AutoRefreshingDerivedRetrievalIndexStore.read_current` calls `self.rebuild(indexed_at=datetime.now(UTC))` with **no `commit_seq`** (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/automatic_memory.py:110-114`). All three build-time decisions stand: where the token is captured, whether the fix lands at the `harness-runtime` subclass or the IS-axis base (a real axis-placement call under IS's zero-outbound-edge invariant), and prune-vs-ignore for losing rebuilds.

### B-95 · Mixed-version ordering bound — a live PRE-B-93 **writer**'s untokenized stale markers cannot be ordered against a covered rebuild *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex R6 on the B-93 gate-log arc, 2026-07-30; REGISTER-AND-HOLD under the arc's own stop rule)* *(**CLOSED 2026-08-05** — a ratified accepted bound; the re-open trigger is preserved verbatim)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-05 by operator ratification, as a RATIFIED ACCEPTED BOUND** — not built, not foreclosed by supersession, but **accepted with its limit documented in shipped source**. This resolves the row's own **flagged-not-flipped** close candidacy: disposition **(3)** (accept and document) is **fully executed at HEAD** — the bound is stated in the `memory_retrieval_index` module docstring at `:19`–`:20` and on `commit_seq` itself at `memory_store.py:154`–`:163`, both citing this row — and all three preconditions were re-verified **counterfactual** by direct read at the 2026-08-05 grounding pass. **The re-open trigger is preserved VERBATIM and survives the close:** *"Re-open when a genuine mixed-version deployment is planned, or when the first production `derived_index_hook` consumer is wired — whichever comes first, since either alone makes a precondition true."* Closure does **not** retire that trigger; it records that no work is owed while both preconditions stay counterfactual. **Trigger-carrier note** *(out-of-family review round 3 [P2], recorded rather than used to reverse the operator)*: the reviewer is right that `--open` no longer surfaces this row, and that the status enum names only two closure senses while this is a **third — a ratified accepted bound**. The operator's answer stands; the trigger is kept monitorable by naming its carriers: **(1) shipped source** — the bound and this row are cited at `memory_retrieval_index.py:19`–`:20` and `memory_store.py:154`–`:163`, so any arc on that surface meets the bound where it lives; **(2) two live sibling rows** over the same mixed-version surface stay in the open inventory and cross-reference this one — **`B-94`** (the untokenized auto-refresh rebuild path) and **`B-45`** (the Windows same-value `commit_seq` bound); **(3)** reopening is a one-field edit, and the information required has been kept deliberately intact. Dispositions **(1)** and **(2)** stay rejected on their recorded grounds, and the **hold rationale stands** — this was the third consecutive self-inflicted `read_current` finding and the arc's pre-declared arms-race stop rule fired exactly as written.
- **What it is.** During a mixed-version window a **new** hook captures snapshot A; a **pre-B-93 writer** commits B and appends an **untokenized** stale marker; the hook then appends A's rebuild pair last. In `read_current` the untokenized marker has no `commit_seq`, so it is excluded from `max_stale_seq`, and accepting the covered rebuild resets the positional `stale_after_current` flag — the A-only index reads **fresh** with B missing. Codex reproduced it deterministically.
- **Precondition triple — each verified by direct read at HEAD, each false today.** **(a)** A live pre-B-93 **writer**, not merely an old *reader* (whose parse compatibility the R3 fix already covers): at HEAD `commit_seq` is a **required** field on `DerivedIndexInvalidation`, so every B-93+ writer stamps every marker, and an untokenized marker can only originate from an older writer process. **(b)** A **wired** `derived_index_hook` — re-confirmed **zero production consumers** at HEAD; the only wirings are `harness-is/tests/test_memory_store.py` and `harness-is/tests/test_memory_redaction.py`. **(c)** An overlapping write + hook-rebuild interleaving.
- **Sharpening found while verifying.** Historical untokenized lines written *before* an upgrade are **benign** — a later rebuild reads the whole filesystem and genuinely covers them. Only a **concurrent** untokenized write, interleaved with an in-flight rebuild, is harmful. The bound is about the live window, not about legacy ledger content.
- **The information-theoretic limit, precisely.** A legacy stale marker carries **no commit token by definition**, so no read-side rule can retroactively order it against a covered rebuild — the information the comparison needs was never written. This is not a missing check; it is **absent data**. Hence only three choices exist:
  - **(1) Serialize notifications during a detected mixed window.** Reintroduces exactly the callback-deadlock surface the arc's first commit removed (a hook holding the notify turn while its inner thread's write waits behind it) — trading a latent ordering gap for a latent hang. Rejected unless the window can be *detected* and the serialization *scoped* to it.
  - **(2) Version-fence the ledger.** Have B-93+ writers refuse to share a ledger they can detect an older writer is also appending to (a writer-version marker line, or a fence file beside the ledger), converting a silent misorder into a **loud refusal** during the upgrade window. Costs a new failure mode operators must understand, plus a decision about what a fenced writer should *do*.
  - **(3) Accept the bound and document it.** **Taken here** — all three preconditions are counterfactual at HEAD.
- **HOLD rationale.** This is the **third consecutive self-inflicted `read_current` finding** (R4 caused by R3's carrier; R5's [P2] by R3/R4's two-pass read; this by R2's ordering protocol). That is the arms-race stop rule the arc pre-declared at round 4, firing exactly as written. **No further carrier change is made.**
- **Documented in code, not witnessed.** The bound is stated in the `memory_retrieval_index` module docstring and on `DerivedIndexInvalidation.commit_seq`, both citing this row. The R3 mixed-version witness was **re-scoped** to say it proves reader *parse* compatibility only and explicitly disclaims any ordering guarantee — deliberately no witness for the gap itself, since it is registered rather than fixed.
- **Re-open when** a genuine mixed-version deployment is planned, **or** the first production `derived_index_hook` consumer is wired — whichever comes first, since either alone makes a precondition true.
- **Council: not for the bound itself** — accepting a documented limit needs no deliberation. **If** direction (2) is ever taken it becomes council-eligible: refusing to write during an upgrade window is an operator-visible availability tradeoff (C11 operator-loop / local-deployment against C3 state-and-persistence integrity), which *is* a nameable cross-domain tension.
- **Cross-ref.** Sibling ordering-scope row **B-94** (the untokenized auto-refresh path, pre-existing); substrate sibling **B-93**. All three re-check on overlapping triggers around concurrent memory consumers.
- **2026-08-05 grounding re-check at HEAD `43d4dda5` — premise INTACT, all three preconditions re-verified COUNTERFACTUAL; disposition VERIFIED-DORMANT.** **(a)** `commit_seq: int` is a **required** field (no default) on `DerivedIndexInvalidation` at `harness-is/src/harness_is/memory_store.py:138`, so every B-93+ writer stamps every marker. **(b)** **Zero production `derived_index_hook` consumers** — the only wirings repo-wide are `harness-is/tests/test_memory_store.py:611` and `harness-is/tests/test_memory_redaction.py:68`; the production surface is only the ctor param (`memory_store.py:215`) and the notify site (`:284-285`). **(c)** A concurrent overlap is still required and absent.
- **📌 Reclassification NOTE (2026-08-05) — flagged, NOT flipped — `[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-05]`, the candidacy it flagged was ANSWERED the same day and this row is now `closed`; kept only as the record of the pass that deferred the call.** The chosen disposition **(3) accept and document** is **fully executed at HEAD**: the bound is stated in the `memory_retrieval_index` module docstring (`:19-20`) and on `commit_seq` itself (`memory_store.py:154-163`), both citing this row. This row is therefore not open work but a **ratified accepted bound with a documented re-open trigger**, and is a **CLOSE candidate at the next operator ratification batch**. The status is deliberately left unchanged here — the accepted bound plus its re-open trigger make closure an operator call, not a sweep's.

- **What it is.** `gc_sweep`'s B-77 first-observation grace refuses to reclaim an entry the store has not already seen past TTL at a PRIOR sweep of the same root. That closes B-77's named defect — a crash-recovered entry carrying only the pre-commit mtime stamp is never reclaimed by the sweep that FIRST sees it, i.e. never by the recovering process's bootstrap sweep. The residue is the grace's **practical duration**: every `run()`/`resume()` sweeps **at least** twice by construction — once at `bootstrap/stage_4_od.py:123` and once, unconditionally, at `shutdown.py` step 5b — plus a **third trigger the original count missed** *(corrected 2026-07-31)*: `_maybe_opportunistic_gc_sweep` (`protected_result_store.py:882`) fires from inside `write_once` at most once per `_OPPORTUNISTIC_GC_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (300s, `:72`), so a long-lived process also sweeps on **write cadence**. "Twice by construction" was a **floor**, not the count — which *sharpens* the finding (a third trigger can only shorten the interval) rather than weakening it. So the gap between first and second observation is the run's own duration, milliseconds for a short or immediately-failing run. A genuinely-live, crash-recovered entry therefore survives only to that same run's shutdown, not for any wall-clock interval a repair flow can rely on.
- **Current state — SUPERSEDED 2026-08-05; the block below is the pre-ratification record.** *(Current state is the two bullets at the top of this block: **Reading C, ceiling C-2**, `status: open` (was `design_substrate_gated`), **spec leg LANDED 2026-08-05 (Runtime v1.111 §14.8.11.1 + plan v2.58 U-RT-150); IMPL leg owed**. What follows described the row while `B-96` was unanswered, and is kept as history.)* Registered, not built. The sweep-COUNT reading is exactly what `B-77`'s ratified close_out specifies (verbatim: "should not reclaim an entry it has not observed in a PRIOR sweep (a grace period) — bounded to one sweep interval"), and it landed as ratified. It was deliberately NOT redesigned mid-arc: `B-77`'s own row records three prior wrong mechanism claims on this same file, and a fourth unratified attempt is precisely the non-convergent-adversarial-hardening pattern this workspace stops on. The practical bound is stated honestly in `gc_sweep`'s docstring rather than overclaimed. Reachability is the same narrow floor `B-74`/`B-77` share: a deployment `ttl_seconds` short enough that the crash window alone tips a live entry past it (the factory default is 86400s, ~7 orders of magnitude above), AND a crash landing strictly between `os.link` and the post-commit refresh, AND a recovering run short enough that its shutdown sweep fires before any repair read.
- **Close-out steps** *(the pre-ratification recipe — RESOLVED 2026-08-05 as Reading C with ceiling C-2; the impl leg builds exactly this, under the ratified form tabled at the fork's §11.3)*. Replace the sweep-COUNT grace with an elapsed-TIME one, using the first observation's wall-clock as the age authority `B-77`'s close_out actually names ("an age authority that cannot predate publication by construction") — record `first_observed_at` alongside the filename in `_root_observed_expired` and reclaim only when BOTH the mtime-derived age AND `now - first_observed_at` exceed `ttl_seconds`. The tradeoff that makes this ratification-owned rather than mechanical: the conservative rule lengthens worst-case retention of a genuine crash orphan by up to one full TTL (a day at the factory default), against the spec's own bounded-retention term (Runtime v1.108 §14.8.11 — *version label refreshed 2026-07-31; bullet text unchanged across v1.106→v1.108* — "a signing outage must not grow an unbounded store of sensitive payloads"). Do not narrow `ttl_seconds` itself (`B-74`'s declined option). Witness by driving a full bootstrap-then-shutdown pair against a crash-window entry.
- **Council: ⚖️ conditional** — the mechanism is mechanical, but the retention bound it picks is a nameable cross-domain tension (C3 state-and-persistence integrity wanting the conservative age authority ⊥ C7/C8 wanting the bounded-retention floor on sensitive payloads); convene if the elapsed-time variant is taken.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-77` (closed — the grace itself); `B-74` (open — the filesystem-granularity dimension of the same mtime-as-age-authority question). All three re-check together.

### B-97 · The durable pause journal carries no tenant binding *(surfaced at the B-69 council convening as residual R-3, routed OUT of that arc, 2026-07-30; half (b), cross-process append serialization, CLOSED 2026-07-31; half (a), the tenant binding, RATIFIED + SPEC-APPLIED 2026-07-31 as Reading A — per-tenant path segregation — with the impl leg owed)*

- **Half (b) — CLOSED 2026-07-31 (the `B-97`(b) arc).** `JournalWorkflowPauseStore._append` now runs its **entire** body — the `is_new_file` / `needs_leading_newline` / append TOCTOU triple, the write, the `fsync`, and the torn-append self-heal — under `_cross_process_append_lock`: a hand-rolled `fcntl.flock` on a dedicated **per-workflow** `<journal>.lock` file, mirroring the primitive already shipped at `protected_result_store._cross_process_lock`. The **read path deliberately takes no lock**, which is what keeps Runtime spec v1.107 §30's `empty-journal` INDETERMINATE clause exact **as written** — and is why the arc owed **zero spec text**.
- **Granularity is the grounded part.** The house `harness_is.cross_process_ledger_lock.cross_process_scope_lock` (one lock per directory TREE) was implemented **first** and **rejected at out-of-family review round 2 [P2]**: a directory-wide lock makes one workflow's append wait behind **another** workflow's, which contradicts this store's own isolation property (per-workflow files exist so one workflow cannot block another) and — because reads are unlocked — widens the window in which a read of the *queued* workflow reports the `absent` cause that §30 attributes as **PERMANENT**. The per-workflow lock leaves that pre-existing capture-not-yet-landed race exactly the size it already was.
- **Two pre-existing crash windows closed on the way past.** Out-of-family review round 1 **[P1]**: a process that creates the journal directory and dies before writing leaves the dirent **present but not durable**, and a parent-fsync keyed on `dir_is_new` alone then skips it **forever** — a capture returns successfully while the whole `pause-journal` directory stays losable. Round 1 re-keyed it on `is_new_file or dir_is_new`; the **pre-merge 3-lens gate found that form narrows but does not close** the window — a writer whose `path.open("a")` creates the journal file and then dies before the fsync leaves **both** flags False for every successor, so *"a journal file exists ⇒ some earlier writer already fsynced"* is false for that interleaving.
- **Shipped form: both directory fsyncs are UNCONDITIONAL.** The parent (`STATE_LEDGER`) fsync runs after `mkdir` and **before the lock**, so it precedes any statement that could create a journal file; the journal-dir fsync runs after **every** append. True by construction, no interleaving exception — and it **deletes both flags** rather than adding a third. The journal-dir level carried the identical defect one level down (create file, write, die before fsync, every successor reads `is_new_file=False`); that one is **purely pre-existing**, byte-identical to the pre-`B-97` code, and is closed here rather than left as a known twin of the defect being fixed beside it. Cost: two best-effort directory fsyncs on a path that already `fsync`s the record, for a human-latency event.
- **Spec refresh owed at the half-(a) leg.** Two Runtime spec v1.107 §30 sentences go **stale-as-described** once half (b) lands: `:3313` term 5 (*"makes no claim about cross-process write-write serialization of the journal, which remains unguarded"*) and `:3319` (*"cross-process append serialization is explicitly unresolved (registered at `B-97`)"*). **Neither is a Class-1 halt** — both sentences' asserted *properties* still hold (term 5's supersession-window claim is untouched; `:3319`'s `empty-journal` indeterminacy never depended on append serialization); only their parenthetical descriptions of the store are now wrong. The half-(a) leg touches §30 anyway for the sixth cause member, so it carries this refresh.
- **Forward note — blocking `flock` on the event loop** *(out-of-family [P2], pre-merge gate)*. `capture()` is called synchronously from the async `capture_pause_snapshot`, so the `flock` blocks the loop. Precedented — the sibling protected result store grew `resolve_result_ref_off_loop` for exactly this — **deliberately not built in this arc**. **SPLIT to its own row `B-103` at the half-(a) spec leg, 2026-07-31**, per this row's own leg-2 obligation: parking it here would have lost it from `--open` the moment this row closes.
- **Sharpening recorded honestly.** The original finding framed (b) as *interleaved / torn records*. An empirical probe at the arc found that half **not reachable at the shipped record shape**: `_append` emits each record in exactly **one** `write()` syscall (measured on the real `FileIO` → `BufferedWriter` → `TextIOWrapper` stack at 60 KB, at 4 MB, and on the leading-newline self-heal path, whose 1-byte newline is coalesced into the same flush), and `O_APPEND` makes a single write atomic on a local POSIX filesystem — a 2×12 concurrent-append run at 12 KB / 60 KB / 500 KB / 4 MB produced **zero** malformed records with the lock **removed**. What the lock genuinely buys: cross-process mutual exclusion **at all**; independence from an **unspecified** platform guarantee (`O_APPEND` atomicity does not hold on NFS/SMB, and the resolved `STATE_LEDGER` dir is operator-configured); and **soundness** for the self-heal's documented single-writer-only reasoning.
- **Half (a) — CLOSED 2026-07-31 (PR #1171): RATIFIED, SPEC-APPLIED at Runtime v1.108, IMPL LANDED at U-RT-149.** *(The bullets below preserve the finding as filed; this bullet records how it was answered. The row's status moved `registered_finding` → `open` → `closed`; the conjunctive closure criterion was met in full, not in part.)* **Gate 1 (operator, 2026-07-31): READING A — per-tenant PATH SEGREGATION**, with a contractually injective **CONSTANT** encoding, the **record shape UNCHANGED**, the five-member `PauseJournalReadCause` vocabulary **staying at five**, a **MANDATORY quiesced cutover**, and the `(workflow_id, run_id)` rider **NOT bundled**. **Gate 2 (operator, 2026-07-31), after the C3 ⊥ C11 dyadic:** **(3a) abandon-by-default CONFIRMED**, and **§5.3.1 = (i)+(iii) with (iii) a PRECONDITION of (3a)** — both as the council recommended. **The four decisions enumerated below are answered as:** (1) the **filename**, under a TOTAL injective encoding closing **all three** hazards (branch / delimiter / field-boundary), realized on the in-house length-prefixed canonical-segment shape as a module constant with **no configuration surface**, delegating to the **Runtime-local** `normalize_tenant_scope` and explicitly **not** to OD's; (2) **DISSOLVED, not discharged** — a wrong-tenant read resolves the caller's **own** path and returns the ordinary `absent`, which under segregation is the *truth*, so **no sixth cause member is minted** and decision (2) as posed below is superseded; (3) **(3a) abandon by default** with the failure-mode asymmetry stated as spec text, plus **(3b)** operator-declared relocation under four mechanical terms; (4) **answered NO explicitly.** **Applied at** `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` **v1.108** (§14.14.8 keying + encoding + migration contract + orphan statement + named silence; §14.14.9.1 parallel keying; §30's `absent` row tenant-scoped across three states; §13.4 rows; **NEW §13.7** enumeration surface) and `Implementation_Plan_Harness_Runtime_v2_56.md` **NEW U-RT-149**. **CP / OD / IS / AS and CXA UNCHANGED**, each determined at the leg rather than assumed — the arc is wholly intra-`harness-runtime`.
- **Half (a) — the finding as filed.** `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` §14.8.11 (`:4804` heading, `:4809` tenant-composite key, `:4812` tenant-bound lookup — **cites refreshed at this arc**; the prior `:4636`/`:4639` pair was stale by ~168 lines after v1.107) commits a **full-strength tenant-composite key + a typed cross-tenant refusal** for comparable durable state. `JournalWorkflowPauseStore` (§14.14.8) is **`workflow_id`-keyed, one file per workflow** — and now carries recovered branch outputs. **PRE-EXISTING and explicitly NOT `B-69`'s**: `api.resume()` reads the same key today, and the `B-69` accessor adds **zero** tenant exposure.
- **Why (a) is fork-shaped, not an impl task.** It changes the store's **keying** — capture-side and hash-adjacent (the `B-73`/`B-80` split-out discipline that kept it out of `B-69` in the first place). The chain mirrors `B-65`'s: **Class 2 fork doc → operator ratification → spec leg → impl leg.** Four decisions the fork must put to the operator, none of which an impl leg may settle silently:
  1. **Key composition** — does the tenant scope enter the sha256 **filename** (opaque, but makes an existing journal unaddressable) or ride **in-record** alongside `workflow_id` (readable, but leaves the path tenant-blind)?
  2. **Refusal semantics** — a cross-tenant read must be **REFUSED TYPED** per §14.8.11 `:4812`, which needs a **sixth** cause in the deliberately **closed** five-member `PauseJournalReadCause` vocabulary (Runtime spec §30). Widening a closed vocabulary *is* the spec question.
  3. **Migration** — an existing untenanted journal must be readable or deliberately abandoned, against §14.14.8's **append-only / never-truncated** substrate invariant, which forbids rewriting in place.
  4. **The `(workflow_id, run_id)` rider** — whether the same arc should carry run-instance distinctness, since both are keying changes and a second keying arc would pay the migration cost twice.
- **Discriminator worth preserving.** The two failure modes are **distinct**, and only (b) was a concurrency question. *Sequential interleaving* — one writer at a time, both records well-formed — is the **supersession** problem `B-69`'s staleness precondition already fences, and it needs no concurrency at all: *"it is not writing at the same time; it is writing in between."*
- **Council: ⚖️ conditional** — (a) is C3's surface (state/persistence keying) with a nameable C3 ⊥ C11 tension if a tenant key adds local-deployment config burden. (b) was mechanical and is closed, so the prior *"convene only if (a) is taken without (b)"* condition is now **unconditionally met**: opening (a) means convening.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-69` (closed — the arc that surfaced it and deliberately excluded it); Runtime spec §14.8.11 (the shape to mirror); §14.14.8 (the store); **`B-102`** — (b)'s lock **shrinks but does not close** the window that row names.

### B-99 · The B-69 projection's `summary_text` exclusion must be re-adjudicated when the `pause_context_reader` deferral is discharged *(named reopening condition registered at the B-69 spec leg, 2026-07-30)*

- **What it is.** A **named reopening condition** — not a defect, not a gate — filed so the `B-69` projection's own justification cannot go stale silently. `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` v1.107 §14.14.9.2 excludes `StateSummary.summary_text` from the caller-facing projection. That exclusion originally rested on **two** legs, and the convening's own adversarial pass **falsified one**.

- **The surviving leg, now carrying the argument alone.** The field is an **unbounded forward channel** — a placeholder *for real ledger content*, with no redaction contract anywhere. An exclusion decided while the field is empty is free; the same exclusion after it carries ledger content is a **removal from a shipped caller-facing contract**, which nobody makes. Decided now, and stated as forward-load-bearing.
- **Honest counter, left unsmoothed.** When a real reader is composed, the **ergonomics case for inclusion genuinely reopens.**

Also re-examine `Implementation_Plan_Harness_Runtime_v2_55.md` U-RT-148 **AC #5** (the W4 characterization witness), which asserts a **placeholder property** and will fail *for a good reason* once a real reader lands — its correct disposition is then **DELETION or INVERSION, never repair**.

### B-101 · Accessor-derived provenance is lost through base-typed Pydantic serialization *(surfaced at the `B-69` impl leg, out-of-family review round 3, reported not absorbed, 2026-07-31; CLOSED 2026-08-01 — disposition (b)-PLUS applied at CP spec v1.114, with a normative PROMOTION TRIGGER to disposition (a) and the pin test retained as the boundary marker)*

- **STATUS 2026-08-01 — `registered_finding` → `closed`. SPEC LEG APPLIED, DISPOSITION (b)-PLUS.** CP spec v1.113→**v1.114**, **ONE amendment site**: §1.2 constraint 3's stated residual is **APPENDED TO** with ONE paragraph — **NO text retracted or reworded** (but see the counter-reading bullet below). The paragraph (i) declares the **ordinary-serialization boundary formally OUT of the staleness fence's scope**, (ii) **NAMES** `StepExecutionContext.resume_context` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/workflow_driver_types.py:460`) as the ONE live base-typed carrier, (iii) **records the three grounded facts** that keep it unreachable at HEAD, and (iv) states the normative **PROMOTION TRIGGER**. **ZERO contract numbers, ZERO carriers retyped, ZERO fields added, ZERO hash impact, ZERO impl units owed, ZERO plan deltas owed, ZERO test changes owed.** Clearance marker `.harness/clearance/spec-control-plane-v1-114-cleared-2026-08-01.md`; `pr: '#1175'` — reconciled 2026-08-01 at this register touch.
- **Why (b)-PLUS rather than plain (b).** Plain (b) would have been satisfied by one sentence of general prose. **This row's own NEAREST-APPROACH VECTOR note forecloses that reading** — the hazard is *one `model_dump` away on an existing carrier*, and *disposition (b) alone would NOT close that vector*. A residual saying *"serialization is out of scope"* without naming the live carrier would be **true and useless**: a later arc adding one `model_dump` to a debug path would land it without ever reading a sentence that applies to it. Naming the carrier is what makes the trigger checkable **at the site**.
- **The grounded facts, re-verified at the spec leg rather than carried from this row's 2026-07-31 note.** **ZERO** `model_dump` / `model_dump_json` / `TypeAdapter` of that field **or of its enclosing `StepExecutionContext`** across `src/` **AND** `tests/` of all seven packages — and `StepExecutionContext` is **never a field of another model**, so it is never transitively serialized either; `compose_branch_child_context`'s `model_copy` (`workflow_driver_types.py:638`) is **shallow and non-revalidating**; `revalidate_instances` is **unset repository-wide**, so Pydantic's `'never'` default holds. Of the **nineteen** `ResumeContext`-typed annotations in `src/**`, exactly **one** is a model field — the rest are sixteen function parameters and two local bindings, none of which is ever serialized.
- **PROMOTION TRIGGER (normative, binding on future arcs; keyed on MECHANISM, not on the named carrier).** Any arc that introduces **ANY base-schema serialization boundary over a `ResumeContext` value on a resume path** — a `ResumeContext`-typed model field (today only `StepExecutionContext.resume_context`), a base `TypeAdapter`/`RootModel` over `ResumeContext` (the route the pin test demonstrates directly, `:960`), a base-annotated parameter or return crossing a schema-generating boundary, or any equivalent — MUST promote this row to **disposition (a)** (the closed variant discriminator on `ResumeContext`) and land that amendment **BEFORE or SIMULTANEOUSLY WITH** the arc. **Never after.** The trigger fires on *introducing the serialization*, not on observing a failure — by then the fence has already silently not fired.
- **Honest limit, stated in the spec rather than papered over.** Trigger enforcement is a **pre-merge review obligation, not a validator rule**. The pin test breaks on a **behavior** change but does **NOT** fire on the bare addition of a `model_dump` call, so an arc could add one on a non-resume path, break nothing, and leave the carrier one step closer to reachable.
- **THE PIN TEST STAYS — do NOT delete it at this close.** `test_provenance_is_lost_through_base_typed_serialization_registered_b101` (`harness-runtime/tests/test_paused_workflow_state_accessor_b69.py:924`) is the **executable half** of the trigger: it asserts the CURRENT lossy behavior deliberately, so any future change to that behavior is reviewed rather than silent.
- **Why this row CLOSES where `B-100` / `B-97`(a) / `B-102` NARROWED.** Those close-outs left **unbuilt impl remainders**, so closing them would have presented unshipped work as done. Disposition (b) is **documentary by construction** — it declares a boundary rather than moving one — so its close-out is fully discharged by the delta. **Verified, not assumed:** `B-101` is cited at exactly ONE place in `design-substrate/**` (`Spec_Control_Plane_v1_113.md` §0.4 finding (vi), as the obstacle `B-107`'s disposition (d) would hit) and at **no implementation plan**.
- **The strongest counter-reading, recorded rather than answered away** *(out-of-family review round 2 `[P1]` at the spec leg)*. `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_112.md` §1.3(c) requires *"no construction path produces a legacy variant from an accessor-derived one"*. **Read at its broadest, a base-schema round-trip IS such a path**, so on that reading the shipped subclass realization does not satisfy (c) and declaring the boundary out of scope is a **NARROWING**, not a clarification. The delta applies the **narrower** reading on three grounds checked at HEAD: constraint 3's own enumeration is of **CP-owned affordances** (*"No downgrade, no `.without_token()`, no field mutation — frozen carriers"*); the detect-then-refuse witness §1.3 REQUIRES for (c) exercises exactly those three and no fourth (`harness-cp/tests/test_pause_state_projection_b69.py:149`, AC #A2), and the base-schema route slips past its third guard for a stated reason — the base schema never emits the provenance field for `extra="forbid"` to see; and constraint 3's own scoping sentence bounds the harm it claims to foreclose. **Escalation is ONE step, not a re-litigation:** a reviewer holding the broad reading routes this to **disposition (a)** — which is exactly what the promotion trigger already binds a future arc to do. If the operator holds the broad reading TODAY, apply (a) now; nothing in the delta obstructs that, and its trigger text becomes redundant rather than wrong. Recorded at `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_114.md` §0.5 finding (vi).
- **Disposition (a) is NOT applied, on this row's own ground.** It breaks the field-set-preserved-verbatim guarantee `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_112.md` §0.4 makes and would owe a byte-compatibility argument for every existing construction site; this row conditions it on *"a serialization boundary ever appearing on a real resume path"*, which **does not exist at HEAD**. `B-107`'s disposition (d) hits the **same** obstacle — the adjacency is recorded at `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_114.md` §0.5 finding (v); the rows are **NOT** merged.
- **What it is.** `AccessorDerivedResumeContext` is a **subclass** of the CP-owned `ResumeContext`, and Pydantic v2 serializes a subclass through a base-typed field or `TypeAdapter` using the **base's** schema. A round-trip through any `ResumeContext`-typed boundary therefore emits only the four legacy fields and silently **drops `pause_state`** — after which `api.resume()`'s variant check sees a legacy context and the §30 staleness fence does not fire.
- **Severity, stated honestly.** **Not reachable on any shipped path today**: `api.resume` takes the object directly, and the in-process MCP handoff stores it without serializing. A latent hazard, not a live defect.
- **Why it is filed rather than fixed.** It **cannot be closed from the subclass** — the behavior is controlled by the base type's schema, and CP spec v1.112 requires `ResumeContext`'s field set be **PRESERVED VERBATIM**, so adding a variant discriminator to it is a **spec change an impl leg must not make**.
- **Relation to the cleared residual.** CP spec v1.112 §1.2 already states *"a caller who takes an accessor read and then, independently, constructs a legacy `ResumeContext` is unfenced … the type system cannot track a side effect that happened before construction."* This is an instance of that — but it arrives through **ordinary serialization** rather than a deliberate act, which is the sharper form and the reason it is registered.
- **Pinned, not just described.** `test_provenance_is_lost_through_base_typed_serialization_registered_b101` asserts the **current** behavior, so the boundary is visible and any future change to it is deliberate and reviewed.
- **Nearest-approach vector** *(scoped re-gate at the `B-97`(b) arc, 2026-07-31)*. `ResumeContext` is **already** a base-typed field of `StepExecutionContext` (`workflow_driver_types.py:460`). It is **not dumped today** — only `HandoffContext` is `model_dump_json`'d, `model_copy` preserves object references rather than revalidating, and `revalidate_instances` defaults to `never` — so the not-reachable-today claim **stands**. But the hazard is **one `model_dump` away on an existing carrier**, not a hypothetical future boundary, and disposition **(b)** (documenting the boundary as out of scope) would **not** close that vector.
- **Close-out.** Both dispositions are spec-side: **(a)** amend CP spec §1 so `ResumeContext` carries a closed variant discriminator and the two variants become an explicit discriminated union — strictly stronger, but it breaks the field-set-preserved-verbatim guarantee §0.4 makes; **(b)** declare the serialization boundary formally out of the fence's scope, extending §1.2's stated residual to name it. **(b)** is the cheaper and more honest default; **(a)** is warranted only if a serialization boundary ever appears on a real resume path.
- **Council.** No — a scoping question about an already-adjudicated residual.

### B-102 · `corrupt-latest` is presented as decisive, but a torn in-flight append tail is cross-process reachable exactly as `empty-journal` is *(surfaced at the `B-97`(b) arc, lens-1 F1, 2026-07-31; spec half DISCHARGED at Runtime spec v1.108, 2026-07-31 — the read-side attribution flip rides the `B-97`(a) impl leg)*

- **SPEC HALF DISCHARGED at the `B-97`(a) spec leg, 2026-07-31.** Runtime spec **v1.108** amends §30's cause table so **`absent` (`:3318`) and `corrupt-latest` (`:3321`) each carry the SAME reachability qualification `empty-journal` (`:3319`) already carried** — permanent for the single-process deployment where it is decisive, **INDETERMINATE across processes**, and *an implementation MUST NOT present either as decisive loss where a second writer is reachable*. **All three permanent-absence causes are now qualified rather than one of three**, and the `RT-FAIL-RESUME-HANDLE-UNKNOWN` taxonomy row plus §14.14.9.4's routing clause were refreshed in the same edit so **no surface flattens the table**. This is the row's own disposition **(a)**, and it needed **no new cause member** — which is why it composed cleanly with `B-97` half (a) rather than competing with it. *(The bullets below preserve the finding as filed.)*
- **IMPL HALF OUTSTANDING — the whole remainder, and it is NOT independently scheduled.** Flip the **shipped** read-side attribution to the indeterminate disposition for `absent` and `corrupt-latest` where a second writer is reachable, matching what `empty-journal` already reports (`journal_workflow_pause_store.py` hard-codes `retryable=False, indeterminate=False` for both today). That flip **rides `Implementation_Plan_Harness_Runtime_v2_56.md` U-RT-149 AC #4(c)** at the `B-97`(a) impl leg — both touch the same attribution site, and two arcs editing one function is the duplication this register exists to prevent.
- **Why NARROWED rather than CLOSED.** Closing while half the row's own close-out is unshipped would present unshipped work as done, and would leave the contract and the code disagreeing with nothing tracking the gap. The stale cross-reference in `B-97`'s own text — that half (a) *"needs a sixth cause member"* — is corrected at that row: **Reading A mints none.**

- **What it is.** `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` v1.107 §30's cause table scopes its MUST-NOT-present-as-decisive clause to **one row of three**. `empty-journal` (`:3319`) carries *"INDETERMINATE across processes — a concurrent `capture()` may complete immediately after this read"* plus *"an implementation MUST NOT present it as decisive loss where a second writer is reachable."* The `corrupt-latest` row (`:3321`) says only **"permanent"**, and the shipped read hard-codes `retryable=False, indeterminate=False` for it (`journal_workflow_pause_store.py`, the non-empty branch of `read_latest_attributed`).
- **Why the same argument applies.** A torn trailing line is **exactly what an in-flight append looks like from a reader**. A read that lands mid-append attributes `corrupt-latest` to a record that is about to become well-formed — and where a second writer is reachable, that outcome is **indeterminate, not decisive loss**. The two rows differ only in *where* the concurrent writer is caught (before its first byte vs. between its bytes), which is not a difference the operator-repair column can act on.
- **The same omission reaches `absent`** *(found independently by out-of-family review round 2 at this arc)*. `absent` (`:3318`) is likewise flat **"permanent"**, yet a read of a workflow whose capture has been dispatched but has not yet created its journal file reports it with `indeterminate=False` — and that capture may complete moments later. So §30 qualifies **one** of the three permanent-absence causes and leaves the other two unqualified on the same reachability.
- **`B-97`(b) shrinks the window; it does not close it.** Concurrent **appends** are now serialized, so a torn tail can no longer be produced by two live writers racing. But a writer **killed mid-append** still leaves one, and a reader racing a **single** live writer is unaffected by a lock the reader deliberately does not take.
- **Severity, stated honestly.** Not a live defect on the shipped single-process deployment. Filed as a **soundness gap in the attribution contract**, exactly as `B-100` was.
- **Close-out — spec-touch owed.** An impl leg must not widen a cleared cause table on its own authority (X-AL-3). **(a)** Amend §30's cause table so `corrupt-latest` **and** `absent` carry the same reachability qualification `empty-journal` already carries, then flip the read-side attribution to `indeterminate=True` for those causes where a second writer is reachable. **(b)** The narrower alternative: leave the table alone and document why they *are* decisive despite the symmetry — viable only if someone can produce the asymmetry, which this row could not. **Prefer (a).** The fix is **attribution-only**: the fail-closed disposition is unchanged either way, and **no new cause member is needed** — which keeps it independent of `B-97` half (a), whose refusal semantics *do* need a sixth member.
- **Council.** No — this asks whether an already-adjudicated qualification reaches one more row of the same table; a scoping question for a spec-writer apply pass, not a fresh cross-domain tension.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-97` (half (a) touches the same closed vocabulary; half (b) is the reachability amplifier that motivated this row); `B-69` (closed — the arc that shipped the five-cause attribution).

### B-103 · The `B-97`(b) cross-process append `flock` is a BLOCKING syscall taken on the event loop *(surfaced at the `B-97`(b) pre-merge gate as an out-of-family [P2], 2026-07-31; split to its own row at the `B-97`(a) spec leg, 2026-07-31)*

- **What it is.** `JournalWorkflowPauseStore.capture()` is called **synchronously** from the async `capture_pause_snapshot`, so the per-workflow `fcntl.flock` `B-97`(b) introduced is a **blocking syscall taken on the event loop**. A contended acquisition stalls the whole loop — every other workflow, every pending timer — for the duration of another process's append.
- **Precedented, which is why it is registered rather than argued.** The sibling protected result store grew an off-loop resolution path (`resolve_result_ref_off_loop`) for exactly this shape.
- **Why it was split rather than folded into the keying arc.** It is a **mechanism / latency** question with **no keying content and no spec text**; folding it into `B-97` half (a) would have mixed two unrelated review surfaces. Parking it in `B-97`'s prose would have lost it from `--open` the moment that row closes — or, if the row were held open for it, would have falsely implied half (a) was unfinished. `[[spine-ledger-forward-arc-registration]]`.
- **Severity, stated honestly.** A durable pause is a **human-latency** event and the lock is held for one append, so the contention window is small and **no live stall has been observed**. This is a soundness / latency gap, **not a live defect**.
- **Close-out** *(as registered — SUPERSEDED, never delivered; see the CLOSED bullet below)*. Move the blocking acquisition off the event loop on the sibling's own precedent (an `asyncio.to_thread`-shaped offload of the locked append, or an equivalent off-loop resolution path), and **witness it by execution**: an unrelated concurrent workflow **and** a pending loop timer demonstrably advance while a second process holds the journal lock — with the **mutation probe** being the direct synchronous call, under which that witness must fail.
- **Two things this row MUST NOT do.** It must **not** change the lock's **granularity** — per-workflow was grounded and defended at the `B-97`(b) arc against a directory-tree alternative, and reopening it here relitigates a settled decision. It must **not** change the **read** path, which deliberately takes no lock — that no-lock property is what keeps Runtime spec §30's `empty-journal` **INDETERMINATE** clause exact as written.
- **Spec expectation.** **No spec text is expected to be owed** — the offload is an execution-venue mechanism and §14.8.1's wrap-asymmetry lineage already covers the class. **Confirm that before building, and file a fork if it turns out otherwise rather than absorbing it.**
- **Council: ❌ no** — a single-axis execution-venue question with no nameable cross-domain tension. The granularity decision that *would* have carried one is settled and explicitly out of scope; route to **C9** (reliability / recovery) directly, plus `advisor()` if the offload shape interacts with drain or shutdown ordering.
- **CLOSED 2026-07-31 at PR `#1172` — FALSE PREMISE, established at source at the merge gate (lens 1), not a delivered fix.** *(PR number stamped on the row 2026-08-05. Re-verified 2026-08-05 by direct read: `capture_pause_snapshot` still calls `self._store.capture(snapshot)` **inline** at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/durable_pause_resume_protocol.py:124`, and the pause-capture path carries **zero** `run_audit_off_loop` references — that helper exists at `lifecycle/audit_offload.py:256`; the PAUSE-CAPTURE path has ZERO references to it — live consumers on OTHER paths at 2026-08-05: `hitl_gate_composer.py:1363`, `llm_dispatch.py:5107`, `cost_attribution_validator_dispatch.py:419`, `webhook_delivery_composer.py:390`, `runtime_tool_dispatcher.py:590`.)* **There is no event loop to starve at any shipped call site.** All **eleven** production `capture_pause_snapshot` invocations reach the protocol through `workflow_driver._run_protocol_method_sync` (`:2583-2603`), which runs the coroutine via **`asyncio.run` on a private, single-task loop** inside the driver's own `asyncio.to_thread` worker. That helper's own docstring states it verbatim: *"no current event loop is bound on the worker thread. `asyncio.run` constructs a new loop for this single coroutine."* The blocking `flock` therefore blocks a thread **already blocked awaiting that very coroutine**, with no co-resident coroutine or pending timer to starve.

Both state that the store is **append-only, never truncated, and writes NO pause-resolved marker**, so a resolved journal is **byte-indistinguishable** from an outstanding one and the read reports the **latest durable record**, which is **not a liveness claim** — and that the limit holds **in steady state for a current-format journal**, not merely for the pre-v1.108 legacy set (the fork's §3(vii) scope correction). The **mandatory docstring companions** land on both public surfaces (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/api.py` — `read_paused_workflow_state` `:925`, and `resume()` at **`:1190` post-edit** on **both** its durable-handle prose and its separately-consulted `resume_handle` parameter entry at **`:1260` post-edit**), **zero logic changed**. *Anchors are stated **post-edit** deliberately — this leg's own docstrings shift `api.py`'s lower half, so the fork's pre-leg `:1170` / `:1197` / `:1223` / `:1321` cites do not resolve in the landed tree.* **The limit is DECLARED, not FIXED**: it closes the **disclosure** half of §3(vii); it does **not** close the blindness. **ZERO** contract numbers minted (a doc-only leg cannot), **ZERO** carriers retyped, **ZERO** fields added, **ZERO** `snapshot_hash` impact, the five-member `PauseJournalReadCause` vocabulary stays **CLOSED at five**, **ZERO** plan units owed at the Runtime / OD / CP plans, and **ZERO** CXA rows (aggregate frozen at 111 — no cross-package consumption at all). *Verified, not assumed:* `B-104` is cited at **no** implementation plan and at **no** acceptance criterion.
