- **COMPONENT 2 — the discriminator is DEFERRED; the reopening triggers are a FALSIFIABLE four-disjunct demand test, any one disjunct fires.** **D-0 (DOMINANT) — a retention / pruning-policy arc opens.** §14.14.8 declares a retention policy a **follow-on arc explicitly not owed** there (`pause_journal_disposal.py:14`–`:17`). **A pruner is UNBUILDABLE without this discriminator**: it cannot be permitted to reclaim an outstanding pause, and format-keying gives it nothing — post-cutover every journal is `CURRENT_FORMAT`. This is the one condition that turns the ceiling into a **hard blocker**, which is why it dominates. **D-1 — any surface BRANCHES on liveness, or a stale re-resume is OBSERVED** (round-2 re-scoped form; the first form — *"a second flow acts on the distinction for a current-format journal"* — was **already satisfied at HEAD** by §3(vii) and would have been vacuous the day it was written). Two disjuncts: **(a)** any code path makes a **control-flow** decision conditioned on whether a durable pause is outstanding — as opposed to merely reading the latest record and being blind to it, which is HEAD's shipped behaviour and is what Component 1 declares; **or (b)** an operator-loop report of a `resume(resume_handle=...)` re-entering an **already-resolved** snapshot in a fresh process. *The harm class, not the asymmetry — the asymmetry is discharged by Component 1.* **D-2 — a second KEYING change is opened.** §14.14.8 contemplates one (*"A future encoding change is a KEYING change and MUST take this arc's fork path"*); it re-runs the whole (3a)/(3b) cutover over an accumulated directory holding one journal per workflow that ever paused, where the upper bound approaches vacuity. **D-3 — the resumer ceases to be the party performing the cutover.** The workspace advances past `solo-developer` on the committed bridging arc (root `CLAUDE.md` §10.2), so the operator confirming a drain is not the party who ran the `resume()` calls. *Same shape as `B-98`'s D-1(b), and the same premise.* **Explicitly NOT a trigger on its own:** the §13.7 listing merely being loose — that is this row's already-disclosed, already-contract-stated condition (term 3-bis) and is what the `UPPER_BOUND_DISCLAIMER` exists to communicate.
- **Grounding carried by the ratification** (fork §3, absorbed into the `close_out`): the hypothesized **derive-from-existing** option is **FALSIFIED** (no resume-specific record carries a re-derivable identity; no identity-bearing record is tenant-qualified; the near-miss is Reading C); sub-decision **(a)-1 is FORCED, not open** — a `PauseSnapshot` sentinel is **resumable**, so only a **wrapper-level** record is non-defective; sub-decision **(a)-2 is confirmed genuine and its default is worse than unspecified** — `corrupt-latest` + `indeterminate=True`, empirically probed, and a **sixth** cause member is mandatory under A; the **second-authority objection to (b) does not hold as written**; the ambiguous set is **frozen, one-time and drainable**; the **NOT-IN-THE-ROW cross-axis cost** — the sixth cause member **forces an OD spec + plan leg**, because `harness-od` re-declares the vocabulary independently (`pause_resume_namespace.py:482`–`:498`) and `api.py:1183` converts **by value** (post-edit anchor); the **NOT-IN-THE-ROW occurrence-key requirement** common to all three build readings, pinned to the shipped §30 staleness token's `(record_count, latest_record_digest)`; and that any build reading **may** re-key disposal's acknowledgement gate — **an explicit decision each owes, not an automatic consequence and not an argument for deferral**.
- **PR #1170's scope, recorded correctly.** It was a **strings-only** self-description refresh (78/16, zero logic) that removed a *phantom* blocker on the drain recourse and left this one untouched — this row must **not** be read as having been narrowed by it.
- **Ordering recorded, NOT acted on.** The cheapest actionable operator-loop improvement is in **none** of the four readings: the drain recourse has **no `resume` ADMIN-CLI command** (the admin surface ships seven commands, none of them resume), so an operator driving pauses to resolution must call the **public package-root Python API `harness_runtime.resume()`** from their own code. **Precision, corrected at out-of-family review round 4 [P2]:** `resume()` **IS a SUPPORTED surface** — it is one of the **three** package-root async functions `B-106`'s own ruling enumerates as the operator-facing API (`run` / `resume` / `read_paused_workflow_state`). What `B-106` ruled **NOT SUPPORTED** is the distinct **embedder** path — direct `run_bootstrap()` / `ctx.pause_resume_protocol` access. The gap here is therefore an **absent CLI affordance, not an absent capability**, and an earlier draft of this bullet conflated the two. This ratification does **not** open that CLI surface.
- **What it is.** The pause journal is **append-only and never truncated** (Runtime spec §14.14.8's v1.107 substrate invariant), and **nothing is written when a resume succeeds** — no resolved-marker, no status field, no removal path anywhere in the store. A journal whose pause was successfully resumed is therefore **byte-indistinguishable** from one whose pause is still outstanding.
- **Why it surfaced now.** Runtime spec **v1.108 §13.7** declares the operator enumeration surface that makes **(3a) abandon-by-default** ratifiable, and council condition `K-10(c)` asks that surface to report *"how much would be LOST"*. **It cannot.** It can only bound the at-risk set **from above**.
- **How the spec leg handled it, and why that is the right disposition.** `K-10`'s **mechanism** was applied unchanged; only its **claim** was scoped, at §13.7 term **3-bis** — the enumeration is an **upper bound**, it cannot discriminate outstanding from resolved, and §13.7 **MUST NOT be cited as proof a cutover is safe**. That is the same discipline `K-1` established for quiescence (state the negative fact rather than a precondition you cannot discharge), applied one condition over.
- **Severity, stated honestly.** **Not a live defect** — nothing miscomputes, and nothing is lost that would otherwise survive. It is a **ceiling on what the operator recourse can tell a human**, and it makes *"drain pauses before upgrading"* a procedure the operator must verify by their own means rather than read off the harness.
- **Close-out — capture-side, therefore fork-shaped.** Any resolved-marker is a write the store does not make today, on a record shape whose hash disposition is load-bearing — the `B-73`/`B-80` split-out discipline that kept the tenant binding itself out of the read-only `B-69` arc. **Two candidate shapes, neither chosen:** **(a)** a **resolved sentinel record** appended at successful resume — cheapest against the append-only invariant, since an append rewrites and truncates nothing and the latest-record read would then report the journal as resolved; it needs a decision on whether that sentinel is a `PauseSnapshot` at all, and on what the **closed five-member cause vocabulary** reports for a resolved journal, which an impl leg must not settle. **(b)** an out-of-band per-journal **marker file** — avoids the record shape entirely but adds a **second authority** over one journal's state, the exact defect the no-fallback-read rule exists to prevent. **Prefer (a) if taken** — but ground it first: check whether an operator holding §13.7's upper bound **plus** their own drain procedure actually needs the discrimination, because a marker bought for a need nobody has is a capture-side change against a hash-adjacent record for nothing.
- **Do NOT bundle into the `B-97`(a) impl leg.** That leg is read-side and keying-side; this is capture-side.
- **Council: ⚖️ NARROWED at the 2026-08-01 Reading D ratification** — from the pre-ratification *"convene only if shape (a) is taken"* to the fork's §7 **per-reading** form, on a probe rather than a preference. **Under the selected D: NONE is owed now** (the record-shape half of C3's position is decided by shipped code — a `PauseSnapshot` sentinel is resumable — and at HEAD no post-cutover flow consumes the distinction), **and ONE IS OWED AT D-0**: a retention policy makes the tension live by turning the absence into a blocker. **If a build reading is later opened:** **A** → a dyadic **C3 ⊥ C11** convening **before the spec leg**, scoped to the sixth-cause-member question (name, semantics, `retryable` / `indeterminate` dispositions) **and to its cross-axis OD leg**, which raises rather than lowers C3's stake; **B** → **no** convening on the record shape (B touches neither it nor OD's mirror), but the §3(v) disposal-brake question still needs an answer at the spec leg — route to **C11** directly plus `advisor()`; **C** → a convening **with C7 or C8 added**, since C introduces an OD-owned schema surface plus a disclosure / tenant question the C3 ⊥ C11 pair does not cover. The tension itself is unchanged and nameable: state/persistence integrity wanting the record shape and the append-only invariant left alone, against operator-loop wanting an answerable *"is anything actually outstanding"* — the same pair the `B-97`(a) dyadic convened.
- **O-3 (lens-1, `B-97`(b) arc, 2026-07-31) — a second, arithmetic bound on the same enumeration.** **Line-count semantics differ across surfaces**: `str.splitlines()` splits on `\x0b`, `\x85` and `\u2028`; `bytes.splitlines()` does not — so two surfaces counting "records" over one journal can disagree. **Unreachable for store-written records** — and the load-bearing property is **`ensure_ascii=True`**, not "`json.dumps` escapes control characters": `_append` calls `json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)`, leaving `ensure_ascii` at its default **True**, so every non-ASCII char (including `\x85` / `\u2028`) is emitted as an escaped `\uXXXX` sequence. Named precisely because it is an **editable default, not a law** — **seventeen** other modules in this tree pass `ensure_ascii=False` explicitly (counted programmatically across all seven axis packages at this arc — the merge-gate lens said "seven"; the empirical count at HEAD is 17), so the vaguer claim would silently falsify the moment someone added that argument here. Recorded as a bound on the enumeration's arithmetic under **hand-edited or foreign-written** journals, not as a live defect.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-97` half (a) (the arc whose §13.7 surface this bounds); `B-98` (the sibling capture-side pause-carrier gap — gate description absence — same class, same reason it is not absorbed).

### B-106 · Embedder-path event-loop exposure for `capture_pause_snapshot` *(surfaced by the out-of-family confirming round on the `B-103` rework, PR #1172 codex [P2], delivered post-merge, 2026-07-31)*

- **Structural-option preference RESOLVED 2026-08-05 by operator ratification: `run_bootstrap` STAYS EXPORTED in `harness_runtime.__all__`** (`__init__.py:266`, re-exported at `:44`–`:49`). The default stands — the operator-decidable follow-on this row **named but did not absorb** (dropping the package-root export to make the not-supported ruling **structural** at zero call-site cost) is **declined**, on the ground this row already recorded against it: it is a **public-surface narrowing**, major-bump-shaped by the corpus's own version-evolution grammar. The exclusion-defined ruling therefore remains **documentary**, which is what it already was and what the four grounding legs support. This resolves the standing preference; it does **not** reopen the shared `B-103`/`B-106` trigger, which is unchanged.
- **What codex found, after the merge.** The `B-103` premise-falsification is scoped to the SHIPPED call path (`workflow_driver._run_protocol_method_sync` → `asyncio.run` on a private single-task loop in the driver's `to_thread` worker). Codex's confirming round — whose output flushed only after the rework had merged — identified the one path outside that set: `run_bootstrap()` is a public export, `ctx.pause_resume_protocol` is a context field, and an **embedding application** that directly awaits `capture_pause_snapshot(...)` on its own live loop has no private-loop helper in between. Codex measured a 300 ms loop sleep delayed to ~2 s while a second process held the journal lock.
- **Why this is its own row rather than a B-103 reopen.** The `B-103` close_out's claim ("no event loop to starve at any shipped call site") stays literally true; what is genuinely open is whether the embedder surface is *supported* — a scope question, not a mechanism question. The mechanism sits on the shelf: the offload was built, witnessed, and gated at PR #1172's pre-rework commits and applies as-is if grounding rules the surface in. This row carries the decorrelated-reviewer disagreement (lens-1/orchestrator vs codex) on the record instead of silently adjudicating it — per the §13.1 disagreement-is-the-strongest-signal discipline.
- **Close-out.** Ground the embedding contract first; SUPPORTED → the preserved offload + a re-priced cancellation window (the withdrawn `B-105` analysis) against a now-real benefit; NOT SUPPORTED → one documentation sentence and close.
- **CLOSED 2026-08-01 — NOT SUPPORTED. The embedding contract is defined by EXCLUSION, not by silence** — so this is a ruling, not an absence of evidence. Four legs, each re-verified by direct read at head: **(1)** Runtime spec **§4 (`:3093`)** says it verbatim — *"`HarnessContext` is an internal type (consumers reach into specific fields, not the whole context) … The type is not part of any operator-facing surface in Track A."* `ctx.pause_resume_protocol` **is** one of those fields. **(2)** The operator-facing API **enumerates itself** and is exactly three package-root async functions — **§8 (`:3264`)** `run()`, **§30 (`:3363`)** `resume()`, **§14.14.9.1 (`:3456`)** `read_paused_workflow_state()`, introduced as *"exactly one"* / *"a second"* / *"a third async function exposed at the `harness_runtime` package root"*. `run_bootstrap` is not among them; a closed self-counting enumeration is the strongest exclusion this corpus has. **(3)** The contracted external-caller pause route is **designated, and it is not the protocol**: `pause_requested_flag` (**§4 `:3085`** — *"Caller-side pause-signaling primitive. Set by external caller (operator API, MCP tool, etc.)"*; **§14.14.7 `:5897`** leaves that flag-setting surface to implementation discretion). The caller **signals**; the **driver** captures. **Grounded sharpening (out-of-family round 1, [P2], accepted on the source rather than argued down):** no external setter is *exposed* today — the sole in-repo production setter is the internal HITL gate composer (`lifecycle/hitl_gate_composer.py:1329`); every other setter is a test reaching through `ctx`. That is not a hole in the ruling, it is the ruling's own evidence: the designated external route is *deliberately still at discretion*, which is exactly what "the embedding surface has not been minted yet" looks like from the inside. The embedder path is therefore a *second, uncontracted* route to something the contract routes elsewhere **and has not yet opened**. **(4)** No embedding surface exists to be in scope: a full scan of `design-substrate/**.md` finds **zero** library-embedding text (every `embed*` hit is the unrelated CP **EMBEDDING routing layer** or *"embedded credentials"*), and the committed deployment surfaces are the **ADR-D2 v1.2 three-tier** set — local-development / self-hosted-server / managed-cloud (`CLAUDE.md` §10.2) — with no library-embedding tier. **Precedent: `B-69`** is the controlling *how-surfaces-get-minted* rule — a surface is **minted by a ratified spec leg**, never inherited by an internal field that happens to be reachable. Minting one here would be an X-AL-3 silent design extension.
- **The mechanism half is real and is not explained away.** `DurablePauseResumeProtocol.capture_pause_snapshot` calls `self._store.capture(snapshot)` **synchronously** inside the async method (`lifecycle/durable_pause_resume_protocol.py:124`), and the `flock` inside would block a live loop — codex's 300 ms → ~2 s measurement stands. It is a measurement of a path **outside the contract**. The **daemon was checked** rather than assumed: its captures also route through `workflow_driver._run_protocol_method_sync`'s private single-task loop, so `B-103`'s falsification survives it and the embedder path is the **sole** live-loop route — which is why ruling it out-of-contract closes the whole question.
- **What shipped: documentation only, zero logic** (impl-discretion — it restates the cleared §4 invariant and mints nothing). An **AUDIENCE** paragraph on `run_bootstrap`'s docstring (`bootstrap/__init__.py`) naming the internal-type ruling, the three contracted functions, the caller's own-loop obligation and the `pause_requested_flag` route; and the concrete blocking-`flock` fact on the `pause_resume_protocol` field comment (`types.py`). **No spec text owed** — confirmed by `B-103`'s own recorded confirmation for the mechanism half (§14.8.1's *"The wrap chain above pins composition, not execution venue"*), and because this row adds no contract, config scalar, failure class or observable surface.
- **The `B-103` offload STAYS SHELVED** (preserved at PR #1172's pre-rework commits, `3636762c`-era head of `b103-off-loop-journal-lock`). `B-103`'s **reopening trigger is unchanged** — a future arc replacing `_run_protocol_method_sync`'s `asyncio.run` with a **captured-loop bridge** (`:2598-2601`). **Added here: re-check `B-106` alongside `B-103` at any change to that helper** — if the bridge lands, the **shipped** path joins the embedder path in being loop-co-resident, the harness acquires an **in-house** benefit from the offload, and the SUPPORTED branch reopens on *that* benefit rather than the embedder's. One trigger, two rows, evaluated together.
- **Named, not absorbed — the structural option, an OPERATOR-DECIDABLE follow-up.** `run_bootstrap` sits in `harness_runtime.__all__` (`__init__.py:266`, re-exported at `:44-49`) with **zero in-repo package-root consumers**: 215 occurrences across 40 files, and **every** import site is `from harness_runtime.bootstrap import run_bootstrap` (28 import lines; the two non-test callers, `api.py` and `cli/app.py`, are intra-package). Dropping the package-root export would make this ruling **structural at zero call-site cost** — an embedder would have to reach into a private submodule to obtain the context at all. It is **not absorbed here** because it is a **public-surface NARROWING**, major-bump-shaped by the corpus's own version-evolution grammar (**§9 `:3343`** — *"Removing a field is always a major bump"*; **§4 `:3093`** — *"field-removals or type-changes are major (consumers break)"*), and because the spec itself references `harness_runtime.run_bootstrap(...)` illustratively at `:6262` (inside an implementation-discretion note — not a contract, but not nothing). A major-bump-shaped narrowing of a public surface is an **operator** call, not an impl-discretion one. **Default = leave the export**; the docstrings carry the ruling without it.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-103` (shares the one reopening trigger; its offload is the shelved mechanism); `B-105` (withdrawn with that offload); `B-69` (the how-surfaces-get-minted precedent); `B-97`(b) (introduced the lock).

### B-107 · No channel REFUSES an operator resolution addressed to an EMPTY effect-fence key — the response map and the scalar uniform fallback DROP it on all three carriers, and the level-local abort scans MIS-APPLY it to a keyed sibling *(surfaced at the `B-100` spec leg, out-of-family review rounds 3 + 8, reported not absorbed, 2026-07-31; the over-application half established at the 2026-08-01 grounding pass)*

ZERO capture-side change, ZERO `snapshot_hash` impact, ZERO contract numbers, ZERO Runtime/CXA delta; `PauseTreeWalkEntry.effect_fence_key` still surfaces `""`; `B-101` untouched.

- **What it is.** An **empty captured `idempotency_key`** is reachable on the durable effect-fence carriers, and **no channel REFUSES an operator resolution addressed to it**. **TWO failure modes, not one** — the second **established at the 2026-08-01 grounding pass** (below): most routes **DROP** it silently, and the level-local `_any_fence_abort` scans **MIS-APPLY** it, since a `{"": ABORT}` suppresses a **keyed sibling's** valid directive at `:8238` / `:12576` — the cross-location misattribution `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_107.md` §1.1(a) forbids. **Two channels, and `B-100` closes neither by type.**

At the **fan-out per-branch** and **orchestrator** consults the truthiness guard means it is never consulted at all. **Different mechanism, identical outcome — a silent INERT re-pause with no diagnostic.**

  - **(a) Resolver-side — closes the SCALAR channel only.** Filter empty keys out of `compute_effect_fence_uniform_fallback_eligible_key`'s candidate set, exactly as its sibling already does at `:3054`, making an empty-key location *unaddressed by construction*. It changes a **CP classification rule**, so it needs a §1.1(a) spec amendment. **Liveness, grounded rather than assumed** *(an earlier draft claimed a liveness COST; round 4 [P2] falsified it)*: **neutral** in the lone case — the run already re-pauses INERT today — and **strictly more live** in the mixed case (one empty + one keyed), where today the 2-member unaddressed set blocks *both* while filtering leaves the keyed location solely eligible. **But it removes a false acceptance without producing a refusal, and does not touch the map channel.**

  - **(c) Refuse-at-the-seam.** Raise rather than silently skip or thread when a resolution is addressed to an empty key. **The only option that converts DROP into REFUSE.** **But its seam is not one function** *(corrected at round 11 [P2]; **CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-01** — the round-11 sentence was itself FALSE for the BRANCH carrier)*: placing the refusal inside `_resolve_effect_fence_gated` alone **misses the orchestrator's own carrier entirely** (site 6, `:12118`, its only consult, truthiness-guarded) but **DOES reach the branch/worker carrier**, whose level-local `_any_fence_abort` scans at `:7839` / `:11708` call the resolver with `""` **UNGUARDED** — per the corrected seven-site map above. Full coverage needs **either** an earlier validation seam that sees the location before any consult is skipped — resume-context admission, or the collector — **or** a per-consult refusal at each of the three sites. The cheapest sound placement is an **admission-time** check, which also subsumes (d)'s map channel. It changes a resume path's failure mode either way. **RE-OPENED 2026-08-01:** that placement was chosen against the **false** map *and* against an `api.py` admission point that the public `harness_cp.workflow_driver.execute_workflow` export bypasses — see fork decision 3 above.

- **Closure criterion — WIDENED 2026-08-01 across TWO review rounds.** *(Round 1 [P1] required the widening be applied here rather than deferred, since the prior wording was literally satisfied by the defect; round 5 [P2] found the first widening **still permitted an empty key to be HONOURED as an address locally** — which contradicts the **adjudicated rule** settled at the `B-69` / `B-100` records and published at `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_113.md` §1.2, that an empty fence key is **position-only** and the resume path **cannot address it**.)* `B-107` closes iff, **on every channel and every carrier**, an empty-key location is either **(i) removed BY CONSTRUCTION from the addressable/eligible set**, or **(ii) REFUSED** — and **never (a)** silently **dropped**, **nor (b) HONOURED as an address** (a resolution keyed to `""`, or a scalar uniform value threaded at an empty-key location, is a forbidden outcome *even when it affects nothing else*, since the directive it produces carries `idempotency_key=""` and no runtime fence can ever match it), **nor (c)** permitted to **alter another location's decision** (the `{"": ABORT}` over-application at `:8238` / `:12576`) — witnessed **per channel** (map, scalar) and **per carrier-SITE** (see the witness shape above). **Honouring an empty key locally, and mis-application at a different location, are both non-closure, exactly as silent drop is. Partial is non-closure. Ground (a)+(d) against (c) before opening any of them.**

### B-108 · §14.8.11's typed report-log term has NO sink the HARNESS configures — absent host/operator logging configuration every report-log line reaches stderr and dies with the process *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex round 2 on the `B-96` council record, independently re-verified and CONCEDED by C7; scoped at round 3, 2026-08-01)*

- **What it is.** `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md` §14.8.11 (`:4909`) requires that TTL expiry *"surfaces as a TYPED report-log line"*, and the protected result store ships four such emissions (`protected_result_store.py:830`, `:839`, `:849`, `:855`). **The harness configures no logging sink of its own — and that, precisely, is the claim; it is NOT that no sink can exist.** *(Scoped at round 3, out-of-family [P2]: the grep below proves only that the **harness** installs no handler. `harness.*` loggers set no `propagate = False` anywhere — verified: zero occurrences in production source, so the stdlib default `True` holds — which means a HOST embedding the harness, or an operator configuring logging around the CLI, CAN attach a handler to the root or to `harness.*` and capture these lines durably. The finding is therefore about the STOCK, unconfigured deployment, and it is exactly consistent with the `B-96` record's condition #12 term that carrier durability is deployment-configured. The original "any deployment shape" framing over-claimed and is withdrawn.)* A whole-tree scan of **all seven** production `src` trees (`harness-{runtime,core,is,as,cp,od,cxa}/src`) for `basicConfig` / `dictConfig` / `fileConfig` / `addHandler` / `logging.config` / `StreamHandler` / `FileHandler` / `configure_logging` / `setup_logging` / `handlers[` / `lastResort` returns **ZERO matches** — re-run programmatically at this filing, not carried from the reviewer. All **30** emission sites live in `harness-runtime/src` and sit on the `harness.*` logger hierarchy, so with no handler attached anywhere on that hierarchy or on root, every line falls through to Python's `logging.lastResort` handler: **WARNING+ to process stderr, and nowhere else.**
- **How it surfaced.** Out-of-family Codex round 2 [P1] against the `B-96` council record (`.harness/council-b96-grace-ceiling-2026-08-01.md` §11.2b, finding **C2-2**) falsified C7's `[MODERATE]`-tagged premise that *"the report log survives process exit"* — the step that made a **trend** diagnostic (compare successive grace-reset emissions) viable. **C7 conceded without reservation** in its round-2 response, re-verifying the grep independently and noting that the inference had been available to it in round 1 (it had already established there is no OTel log bridge) and was not drawn.
- **Scope — workspace-wide, not `B-96`-specific.** It is a property of **every** `logger.*` call in the harness. It applies **identically at HEAD, under `B-96`'s C-1 and under its C-2** — which is exactly the orthogonality discriminator that council used to route the write-driven-cadence gap out of its filing, applied consistently here.
- **Severity, stated honestly.** **Not a live data-loss defect** — nothing miscomputes, no payload is lost, and the store's own durability is untouched. What is absent is the **forensic surface the spec term names**: the report log is a **timely notification on stderr**, not a durable measurement. In the one-shot process shape nothing accumulates across runs, so any diagnostic requiring comparison of successive emissions is unavailable in the stock deployment.
- **What `B-96` already absorbed, so this row is not double-counted.** The **claim** half is closed by that council record: condition **#12** now states that carrier durability is **deployment-configured and MUST NOT be assumed**, condition **#6** demotes its own emission to timely notification, and condition **#8(b)** relocates the *authoritative* diagnostic onto an on-demand `harness-inspect` pull surface with **no configuration dependency** (C7's principle: *measure the fault on the substrate the fault preserves*). **This row carries only the GAP half — whether the harness owes a default sink at all.** That question is untouched by any `B-96` leg.
- **Close-out — ground first; three candidate shapes, none chosen.** **(1) Default handler at the CLI entry** — configure the `harness.*` hierarchy once at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/cli/app.py`, level + destination operator-overridable. Cheapest, and it closes the one-shot case; but it is an **operator-facing behaviour change** (where lines go by default, at what level, with what rotation), and it does **not** cover the `api.py` library path, where configuring logging from inside a library is the anti-pattern. **(2) OTel log bridge** — route `harness.*` into the OTel pipeline that already exists for spans (`LoggerProvider` + `LoggingHandler`), making the report log a first-class signal alongside the 15-namespace OD schema. This **mints a new signal family** and is therefore **X-AL-3 spec-gated**: a Class 1 back-flow plus an OD/Runtime spec leg is owed **before** any code. Two independently verified absences it would close together: **no metrics pipeline** (no `get_meter` / `MeterProvider` anywhere) and **no log bridge** (no `LoggerProvider` / `LoggingHandler` anywhere). **(3) Document and close** — state normatively that carrier durability is deployment-configured and that no condition may depend on emission durability for its correctness; **half-taken already** by `B-96`'s conditions #12 and #6 (spec text owed at the `B-96` spec leg), which is precisely why (3) alone does not close this row.
- **Witness — DIFFERENT PER SHAPE, because one witness cannot cover all three** *(scoped at round 3, out-of-family [P2])*. **Shapes (1) and (2), which ADD a sink:** an **end-to-end run** (not a unit test) that drives a real TTL-expiry sweep and asserts the typed report line is retrievable from the configured sink **after the emitting process has exited**. A `caplog` assertion proves nothing for these — `caplog` installs the very handler whose absence **is** the finding. **Shape (3), which adds NO sink:** a post-exit witness is **impossible by construction** and demanding one would make the shape unclosable; the correct witness is instead **documentary and negative** — the spec text states the deployment-configured limit, and no condition anywhere in §14.8.11 depends on emission durability for its correctness (checkable by inspection against the twelve conditions, which the `B-96` record already satisfies at #6/#7(c)/#8(b)/#12).
- **Council: ⚖️ conditional.** Shape (3) alone needs no convening (stating a true negative is not a design decision). Shapes (1) and (2) carry a nameable **C7 ⊥ C11** tension — observability owns the signal, its carrier and its namespace and wants the store's sole forensic artifact to actually persist; operator-loop/local-first bears the configuration burden and the stderr noise on a local-development CLI and pays for whatever default the harness picks on the operator's behalf. Convene **dyadic only if (1) or (2) is taken**.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-96` (the arc that surfaced it; its conditions #6/#8(b)/#12 absorb the claim half and its council record cross-references this row); `B-74` / `B-77` (the same store's retention lineage).

### B-110 · The GC observation record cannot distinguish generations of a REUSED temporary candidate name *(surfaced at the B-96 spec leg, out-of-family Codex rounds 3-4, 2026-08-05)*

- **What it is.** Runtime spec **v1.111 §14.8.11.1 term 5** keys the durable GC grace record on the **candidate filename** over both sweep classes, with a content set **RATIFIED CLOSED at two members** `{candidate filename, first_observed_at}`. The authorizing council record's condition #5 asserts a name is *"stable and never reused for a different file"* for **both** classes, grounding it on the absence of any rename/replace in the store. **That ground establishes the LIFETIME half only.** A temporary name is drawn by a mechanism that avoids only names **currently present**, so once an orphan is removed its name is redrawable and a surviving record row can match a **different** later file. The published-entry class is **not** exposed — those names are non-invertible digests of a `uuid4`-bearing composite key.
- **Why it could not be closed at the B-96 spec leg.** That leg's first response **mandated** that a stale row never be honoured. Out-of-family round 4 **[P1]** showed this is **unsatisfiable inside the ratified two-member set** — there is no field to carry a generation identity, and adding one would widen a **ratified closed set**, which is an operator decision rather than a spec-leg act. The guarantee was therefore **narrowed to what the ratified carrier can actually deliver**, and the remainder registered here.
- **What it costs, exactly.** **For the RECORD-MEDIATED reclaim decision the conjunctive rule still gates the recreated file by its own TIMESTAMP — which is the TIMESTAMP-DERIVED bound, NOT term 2, whose publication bound does not extend to a name that was never published and whose timestamp can predate its own creation:** term 1's conjunct (a) is keyed on the **new** file's own filesystem timestamp, so the *decision* to reclaim cannot precede that file's own timestamp + TTL. **This claim is scoped to the DECISION, and deliberately so — a second, DISTINCT and PRE-EXISTING mechanism can still reach a replacement file, and it is recorded below rather than folded into this bound.** What degrades is the **additional** grace: for a reused temporary name alone, the reclaim bound falls back to the pre-existing timestamp-derived one, reintroducing the under-report-width window **for that single candidate**. Reachability is remote — the name is drawn from a large random space and must be redrawn within the interval between two sweeps — and is confined to **crash orphans**, never to a paid effect's stored entry.
- **A SECOND, DISTINCT mechanism — PRE-EXISTING at HEAD, recorded not absorbed** *(surfaced at out-of-family review round 6 [P2]; verified by direct read)*. The sweep **selects** candidates under `_publish_lock` + the cross-process lock (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/protected_result_store.py:781`–`:800`) but performs the **removals OUTSIDE** it (`:821`–`:822` for entries, `:845`–`:847` for temporary orphans). Two concurrent sweeps can therefore both select the same expired orphan; if the first removes it and a publisher is then handed the same freed name, the second sweep's **stale path** can unlink that **active replacement** — a **premature deletion**, not merely a lost grace. **This is a property of the shipped sweep's phase split, NOT of the observation record**: it is present at HEAD today under the sweep-COUNT grace, is reachable without any record at all, and is **not introduced by the `B-96` amendment**. **Disposition (c) — LOCK-BOUND IDENTITY REVALIDATION BEFORE REMOVAL**, i.e. re-verify under the lock that the path still names the same file the selection decided on. Cheap, and **`B-96`'s U-RT-150 is already working at that exact site, so that unit MAY take it** — but it is **NOT owed** by the `B-96` legs, whose ratified scope is the reclaim *rule*, and mandating it there would be scope creep on a pre-existing hazard. **Reachability is the same remote name-redraw window as the primary item, further narrowed by requiring two overlapping sweeps.**
- **Close-out — two grounded dispositions, neither owed by the `B-96` impl leg.** **(a) ACCEPT AND DOCUMENT** — the residual is already stated at §14.8.11.1 term 5 with its exact cost, and `B-96`'s **U-RT-150 AC #5** witnesses the **timestamp-derived bound** — explicitly **not** term 2, whose publication bound does not extend to a reused temporary name — rather than an unbuildable freshness guarantee; on this disposition the row closes as documented-and-accepted. **(b) WIDEN THE RATIFIED CONTENT SET** — a generation-stable identity as a third member, or a key that is not the bare basename. **That is a Class 2 operator decision**: the two-member closure is ratified at the `B-96` fork §11.3 table and at council condition #5, whose stated ground is that widening the candidate *classes* adds no field, no carrier and no namespace. **A fork filing is owed before (b) may be built.**
- **NOT owed by any leg.** Reopening the `B-96` ceiling question; any change to the **candidate-filename key over BOTH sweep classes**, which condition #5 requires for an independent reason (crash orphans would otherwise be permanently unreclaimable).
- **Council: not owed at registration.** Whether a ratified CLOSED content set should grow one member to close a remote, bounded, crash-orphan-only residual is a scoping question for an operator ratification, not a nameable cross-domain tension. **If disposition (b) opens, re-evaluate** — a third member touches the same C3 (state/persistence integrity) ⊥ C10/C7 (content restriction on a sensitive-payload store) axis condition #5 was authored on.
- **2026-08-07 — RE-SCOPED at a grounding pass; the row now carries mechanism (c) ALONE.**
  - **(i) The primary half is DISCHARGED IN SUBSTANCE.** Disposition **(a) accept-and-document** is **satisfied at HEAD**: the landed **U-RT-150** witness `test_reused_temporary_name_stays_bounded_by_its_own_filesystem_timestamp` (`harness-runtime/tests/test_lifecycle_protected_result_store.py:2731-2795`) asserts exactly the **timestamp-derived** bound this row says survives a name reuse — the recreated file is **not** reclaimed before its own filesystem timestamp + TTL, and **is** reclaimed after (`:2794-2795`). The degradation is therefore witnessed at the strength the ratified two-member carrier can actually deliver, and no unbuildable freshness guarantee is claimed anywhere. **Disposition (b)** remains a **Class 2 operator decision** and is **not** opened by this pass; the row does not carry it as owed work.
  - **(ii) What the row retains: mechanism (c) alone.** **Offsets re-stamped at HEAD by content** — the bullet above cites `:781`–`:800` / `:821`–`:822` / `:845`–`:847` from the B-96-era file and those are **superseded**. At HEAD, selection of **both** candidate classes happens under `self._publish_lock` + `self._cross_process_lock()` at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/protected_result_store.py:1111-1135`; the **entry** unlink is **off-lock** at `:1173`; the **tmp-orphan** unlink is **off-lock** at `:1201`.
  - **(iii) Severity sharpened — (c) is a HOLE IN `B-68`'s OWN whole-lifetime-lock fix**, not merely an adjacent race. `_publish_atomic` holds **both** locks across the temporary's **entire lifetime** (`:810-858` — `mkstemp` at `:811` inside the `with` opened at `:810`, `os.unlink(tmp_name)` in the `finally` at `:857-858`) **precisely so that no sweep can unlink an in-flight temporary**. A **second** concurrent sweep's off-lock unlink at `:1201` walks a path captured **before** that hold began and therefore **bypasses** it. If it fires, the publisher's subsequent `os.link` raises `FileNotFoundError` — **a lost recovery record for a completed paid effect**, the exact loss this store exists to prevent.
  - **(iv) Reachability, quantified** *(why it stays registered rather than opening)*. Firing requires an **exact** `tempfile._RandomNameSequence` redraw of the just-freed name inside the window: 8 characters over a 37-symbol alphabet = **3.51e12** distinct names, so **~2.8e-13 per redraw** (ground-truthed against Python 3.12.13's `tempfile` on the dev machine), narrowed further by requiring two overlapping sweeps with a publish landing between them.
  - **(v) Trigger replaced.** The *"`B-96`'s U-RT-150 is already working at that exact site, so that unit MAY take it"* trigger is **expired** — U-RT-150 landed and did **not** take it. The standing trigger is now **opportunistic: the next arc that touches `gc_sweep`'s phase split takes it.** Nothing else opens the row. *(SCHEDULED 2026-08-07 at the B-111 plan leg's round-4 absorb: the U-RT-151 impl arc touches the phase split, so the trigger FIRES there — that arc takes the priced fix as a companion; see the B-111 row's APPLIED bullet.)*
  - **(vi) The fix is priced** so that arc need not re-derive it: move the `tmp_candidates` unlink loop (`:1199-1201`) back **under** the lock — `B-75`'s off-lock rationale does **not** bind it, since that loop performs no decrypt and no unbounded work — and add identity revalidation against the `(st_dev, st_ino, st_mtime)` triple captured at **selection** time, because a bare re-`stat()` is **insufficient** (POSIX offers no compare-inode-and-unlink primitive, so the comparison must be made under the same lock the unlink takes). **~25 lines plus one injected witness**: monkeypatch `tempfile.mkstemp` to hand the publisher the just-freed name, and assert the second sweep **refuses** to unlink it.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-96` (the arc that surfaced it — spec leg PR #1235); Runtime spec §14.8.11.1 terms 1/2/4/5/9; `B-108` (the sibling gap the same council record registered).
- **CLOSED at the same arc as `B-111` (the U-RT-151 impl leg, PR #1260) — the trigger fired as SCHEDULED.** U-RT-151 extends `gc_sweep`'s UNLOCKED enumeration phase and threads the collected list into the locked publication, which is exactly the phase-split condition bullet (v)'s re-armed opportunistic trigger names, so that arc TOOK the priced fix of bullet (vi): the `tmp_candidates` unlink loop is relocated back UNDER the lock hold that SELECTED the candidates (`B-75`'s off-lock rationale does not bind it — no decrypt, no unbounded work), and each unlink is now preceded by an identity revalidation against the `(st_dev, st_ino, st_mtime)` triple captured at SELECTION time, under that same hold; a mismatch REFUSES the unlink and reports it. The ENTRY unlink stays off-lock and is NOT in scope. **Witness:** `test_a_recycled_temporary_name_is_refused_by_lock_bound_identity_revalidation` — phase 1 asserts the removal runs with the selecting lock HELD; phase 2 INJECTS the collision deterministically (the other sweep's unlink, then a monkeypatched `tempfile.mkstemp` handing the publisher the just-freed name) and asserts the replacement SURVIVES. Both halves mutation-probed (relocating the loop off-lock kills phase 1; dropping the revalidation kills phase 2).

### B-111 · The GC observation record's publication temporary is unreclaimable after a mid-publication kill, because both sweep globs exclude it by construction *(surfaced at the B-96 impl leg, out-of-family Codex round 2 [P2], 2026-08-05)*

- **What it is.** Surfaced at the B-96 IMPL leg (U-RT-150) by out-of-family Codex round 2 [P2], against that leg's own code -- reported, not absorbed. `_publish_observation_record` publishes the durable grace record by `tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="gc-observations.publishing-")` -> write -> fsync -> `os.replace`, with an `except BaseException: unlink(tmp); raise` cleanup. A process KILLED strictly between `mkstemp` and `os.replace` runs NO Python cleanup, so the temporary survives. That prefix is deliberately disjoint from BOTH sweep globs (U-RT-150 AC #15's second half REQUIRES the disjointness: reusing the `.tmp-` payload prefix would make the next sweep classify the artifact as crash-orphaned ciphertext and unlink it as though it were a payload), and nothing else in the store enumerates it -- so no path ever removes it, and it is invisible to the term-8 gauge and to the `harness-inspect` counts as well. A repeated crash loop landing in that window could therefore accumulate files on the store volume with no bound and no operator-visible signal. Reachability is REMOTE and of the same order as B-110: the window is the sub-millisecond gap between `mkstemp` and `os.replace`, once per sweep, and it needs a KILL (not an exception -- an exception takes the cleanup path, which is witnessed by `test_record_publication_is_crash_atomic_and_never_no_replace_or_unlink_recreate`).

- **Current state (superseded — see RATIFICATION below).** DECLINED at the `B-96` impl leg with a grounded pin, registered rather than absorbed; the residual is stated in `_publish_observation_record`'s own docstring.

- **RATIFICATION — operator, 2026-08-07: DISPOSITION (a).** `status: registered_finding → open`. Narrow U-RT-150 **AC #15**'s no-removal clause to the **SWEEP's PAYLOAD-orphan accounting path**, then build the prefix-scoped cleanup. **The deciding argument is PLAN-TEXT CORRECTNESS, not severity:** AC #15's text encodes a constraint **stronger than its own stated reason** — the reason it gives is entirely about the artifact being *classified and handled as a PAYLOAD* (*"count and age accounting, being reported as a candidate, and being unlinked as though it were ciphertext"*), and nothing in it is about the artifact **surviving**. Read literally the clause also forbids the store's **own** publication path from reclaiming its **own** leftovers, which — combined with the disjointness AC #15's **first half requires** — is what leaves a killed publication's temporary reclaimable by **no path at all**. AC #15 as written is therefore **the sole reason this row is open**. Disposition **(b)** (accept and document) is **NOT** selected; the two dispositions recorded as *not owed by any leg* (re-prefixing toward `.tmp-`; widening a sweep glob) remain **not owed and are not taken**.

- **APPLIED — plan leg, `Implementation_Plan_Harness_Runtime_v2_59.md` (cleared 2026-08-07).** **ONE amendment site plus ONE new unit.** U-RT-150 **AC #15** gains an **APPENDED** qualifier (its existing body **PRESERVED VERBATIM** — no word retracted, reworded or reordered): the **SWEEP half is PRESERVED UNQUALIFIED** — the `_ENTRY_GLOB` / `_ORPHAN_GLOB` enumeration and everything downstream (count/age accounting, the AC #8 gauge at **both** surfaces, candidate reporting, reclaim-as-ciphertext) still must never enumerate, report, classify or remove the record or any intermediate file of its publication, **no glob widens**, and the **`.tmp-*` PAYLOAD-orphan semantics are BYTE-UNCHANGED** — while the record's **OWN publication path MAY** remove stale leftovers of its **OWN** `_GC_OBSERVATION_RECORD_TEMP_PREFIX`, **prefix-scoped by construction** and **under the locks the publication already holds** (§14.8.11.1's *"Published under the same locks the sweep already holds"* — no new lock, no new lock scope). **THE RUNTIME SPEC IS UNTOUCHED — v1.111 stands and NO spec delta is owed**, determined by direct read: §14.8.11.1 *"The observation record's carrier"* commits the publication mechanism and the lock scope and **explicitly acknowledges the orphan** (*"a failed write leaves only an orphan temporary file"*) while stating **no disposition** for it, and leaves the record's file name to implementation discretion — so the prohibition this row runs into exists **only in the plan**. **The qualifier is a PERMISSION, not an obligation — deliberately:** U-RT-150 is **LANDED and CLOSED** (PR #1237), and a **MUST** written into AC #15 would make its conjunctive closure criterion **retroactively false**, the exact defect the Runtime plan v2.58 §0.3 names;
