### B-112 · Deadline'd lock polling drops kernel handoff fairness, so a caller-sampled ledger timestamp can be overtaken and refused *(surfaced by out-of-family review round 1 on the B-93 build leg, 2026-08-06; reproduced 12/20 by the reviewer's own contention probe)*

- **What it is.** The `B-93` deadline replaces a bare blocking `fcntl.flock` with the ratified **non-blocking probe + bounded retry** shape. A blocking `flock` **parks** the waiter in the kernel, which grants the lock on release before the ex-holder can realistically re-acquire it; a **polling** waiter is asleep at that instant, so an ex-holder that releases and immediately re-acquires **wins the next round**. This changes **ordering, never exclusion** — mutual exclusion is the same kernel `flock` it always was.
- **Where it reaches a production contract — exactly one place.** `append_ledger_entry` (`harness-is/src/harness_is/state_ledger_write.py`) validates a **caller-sampled** timestamp against **physical append order** under a `_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE` of **zero**. A waiter whose timestamp was sampled *before* it queued can now be overtaken by a later-arriving writer and refused with `NonMonotonicTimestampError`. Out-of-family review reproduced the dropped waiter in **12 of 20** runs of a focused two-process contention probe.
- **Not newly possible, newly likely — stated against interest.** The same refusal was always reachable whenever the later writer genuinely acquired first, and POSIX `flock` specifies **no** acquisition ordering at all — so the pre-`B-93` code was relying on an **unspecified** kernel behaviour. `B-93` raises the probability; it does not create the class.
- **The lock layer cannot fix this and should not try.** No acquisition ordering makes a timestamp sampled arbitrarily long *before* acquisition correct, and **no portable primitive offers a kernel-parked wait *with* a timeout** — `F_SETLKW` has none, and a watchdog thread would orphan an acquisition in exactly the wedged-holder case the deadline targets, accumulating one stuck thread per attempt. Polling is intrinsic to the **ratified shape**, not to the implementation: `filelock` — the vehicle the fork evaluated and **declined** — polls ten times coarser (`poll_interval=0.05`), and `msvcrt.LK_LOCK` retries at 1 s.
- **The mechanism exists in the cleared spec, but §7.6 scopes it AWAY from this row's surface** *(corrected at the merge-gate — the first filing got this wrong in the row's own favour)*. C-IS-07 §7.6 added **`WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP`**, which samples **inside** the write critical section so the C-IS-05 §5 constraint (verbatim) *"holds **by construction** on this surface — concurrent sibling drains cannot invert"*. **That surface is the buffered/branch-drain path only.** §7.6's *"Surfaces that do NOT change"* paragraph keeps every **direct** append on caller-supplied semantics verbatim, and its **registered residual** says extending writer-owned authority to direct surfaces *"would change caller-supplied semantics for every existing direct producer and **requires its own back-flow**"* — naming **`B-57`** as the owner of the remaining direct writers. The deferred-to-discretion footer likewise constrains the carrier to *"preserve the direct-path caller-supplied contract byte-verbatim"*.
- **The zero-delta claim is RETRACTED, and the adoption question defers to `B-57`.** Adopting the sentinel on direct producers **is** the extension §7.6 routes to back-flow. `B-57` already owns that residual and already prescribes the route — *a narrow IS spec delta extending §7.6's writer-owned sampling to an opt-in direct-append mode (or per-writer serialization guidance) + U-IS-11 widening*. **Why this stays a separate row rather than folding into `B-57`:** `B-57` registers the direct-writer inversion as a **latent** possibility whose close-out is conditioned on it *"materializ[ing] in practice"*; this row is the **evidence that its probability changed** — a specific, reproduced (12/20) mechanism, introduced by a specific arc, on a specific lock. Folding it in would bury a falsifiable trigger inside a dormancy note. The rows are **cross-linked**: `B-112` is the cause-and-evidence record, `B-57` is the remedy owner, and `B-57`'s materialization condition should be read as **partially met** by this evidence.
- **Test-side adjudication** *(by direct read of §7.6's scope, as the gate asked)*. `test_shadow_git_rollback.py`'s concurrent-append worker retries with `WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP` on a **direct** append surface. §7.6's constraint is about changing the **contract** — *"caller-supplied semantics for every existing direct producer"* — and the sentinel is the ratified opt-in **carrier**, explicitly left to implementation discretion. A single test explicitly opting in changes no producer's semantics and sets no default, so the constraint does **not** forbid it and **the test is unchanged**. Recorded here as evidence: it is the first direct-surface use of the sentinel in the tree, and a data point `B-57` should weigh when it prices the opt-in mode.
- **Why registered rather than applied at the `B-93` leg.** Selecting writer-owned sampling changes **whose clock** an entry records — a semantic decision *per call site*, not a mechanical substitution (some entries deliberately carry an event time that is not the append time). Converting callers wholesale inside a lock-deadline arc is exactly the opportunistic scope creep the surgical-change discipline forbids. One **shipped witness** was repaired in place at the `B-93` leg for this reason (`test_rollback_cross_process_lock_prevents_lost_concurrent_append`, whose fixed child timestamp had silently **pinned** the old ordering). It is now **order-INDEPENDENT** rather than re-pinned — an order-pinned formulation proved flaky in *both* directions, so the child stamps the pre-existing entry's timestamp and retries with §7.6's `WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP` if the parent landed first; its load-bearing survival assertion is unchanged and still discriminates under mutation.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Sweep the production callers of `append_ledger_entry` and classify each: does it pass a caller-sampled timestamp, *and* can its ledger be appended to by a second OS process concurrently? Only the **intersection** is exposed — the `harness run` alongside `harness daemon` shared-root topology named in `write_record_guarded`'s own SCOPE paragraph is the reference shape. **(2)** For each exposed caller, decide between `WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP` (correct wherever the timestamp means *"when this was appended"*) and keeping caller-supplied semantics (correct wherever it means *"when the event happened"*, where an out-of-order refusal is the honest outcome the caller should handle). **This is the actual decision, and it is per-caller.** **(3)** Only if some exposed caller must keep caller-supplied semantics: decide separately whether `_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE` — documented as *"configuration-supplied"* but hard-coded to `timedelta(0)` — should become genuinely configurable. Widening it weakens the C-IS-05 §5 monotonicity guarantee **for everyone**, so it is a contract question, not a tuning knob. **(4)** Witness with a two-OS-process probe: a waiter whose timestamp is sampled first must not be refused after a later writer overtakes it. **Do not attempt a fairness fix in the lock layer** — the substrate reasons above are why.
- **Council: no** (conditionally yes at step 3). Step (2) is a per-caller semantic classification against an already-cleared contract, with no cross-domain tension to name. Step (3) **would** be council-eligible if reached — widening the skew tolerance trades information-substrate integrity (**C3**) against operator-loop robustness (**C11**) across every ledger writer at once — but it is reached only if step (2) leaves an exposed caller that cannot adopt writer-owned sampling.
- **Adjacent infra gap, registered not built** *(merge-gate lens 3, G3)*. This arc hit a **silent test-loss** defect: two new test files shared a basename, and because every `tests/` directory is a package literally named `tests`, the module path **collided** — pytest imported one module for both paths and silently dropped **12 witnesses** (34 collected where 35 were written). Caught only by recounting programmatically; the suite was **green** throughout. **Nothing guards against a recurrence:** `__init__.py` is present in every tests dir and does **not** prevent this, so the invariant the tree actually relies on is **unique test basenames repo-wide** — currently true, currently unenforced, and violated *silently* rather than loudly. A CI guard (basename-uniqueness across `harness-*/tests/**`, or per-package rootdir isolation, or `--import-mode=importlib` with unique package names) is its own mini-arc with its own tradeoffs and is **not** built here. Recorded on this row because the same arc surfaced it; a future infra arc may lift it to its own row.

- **In-process widening** *(2026-08-07 grounding pass; **code-grounded, explicitly not reproduced**)*. The overtaking is **not** confined to two OS processes. `flock` contends between separate **file descriptors even within one process** — stated in the lock module's own text at `harness-is/src/harness_is/cross_process_ledger_lock.py:120` (*"`flock` contends between separate fds even within one process"*), which is precisely why the module carries a refcounted **in-process `_rlock` face** at all. A sibling **thread** in the **same** process that loses the in-process probe therefore enters the **same polling wait** (`:173-184`: `self._rlock.acquire(blocking=False)` fails → `resolved.note_contention()` → a `timeout`-bounded `acquire`), and the cross-process arm beneath it polls the same way (`:524`). The exposed population is therefore **broader** than the `harness run` alongside `harness daemon` two-process topology close-out step (1) names: it is **any two concurrent direct appenders on one ledger root, threads included**. Recorded as a code-grounded **widening of scope only** — the 12/20 figure remains a **two-process** measurement and **no in-process probe was run** at this pass.

- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced by out-of-family review round 1 on the **`B-93`** build leg. The fairness property itself is documented at `harness_core.cross_process_lock_deadline._MAX_POLL_SECONDS`, which names this row.
- **2026-08-07 — CLASS 2 FORK FILED** at `.harness/class_2_fork_b57_direct_append_writer_owned_opt_in.md` *(doc-only; this row's status is **UNCHANGED** at `registered_finding`)*. This row is the **cause-and-evidence record**, and the adoption question it defers to `B-57` is what that filing decides. **This row's `council` condition is resolved NEGATIVE by probe:** step (3) — `_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE` configurability, the C3 ⊥ C11 dyad — is reached *"only if step (2) leaves an exposed caller that cannot adopt writer-owned sampling"*, and the filing's twelve-site classification leaves exactly **one** site retaining caller-supplied semantics (`as_is_wiring.py:129`, `timestamp=composed.timestamp` — genuine **event time**, single-producer, for which an out-of-order refusal is the honest outcome by design). That is not a stranded exposed caller, so **step (3) is never reached and no convening is owed**. **Close-out step (1) is DISCHARGED** by the filing's §3(ii)/(iii): the production callers of `append_ledger_entry` are swept and classified **by content** at HEAD `73b0e87b`, and one of them (`sibling_ledger_entry_composition.py:163`) proved **production-unreachable** — its `cp_is_wiring.emit_sibling_ledger_entry` entry point has **zero non-test callers** — so the exposed surface is **11 sites, not 12**. Re-commissioning the sweep at a later leg is not owed; re-grounding it at the spec leg is. **The in-process widening** recorded on this row was **re-verified by direct read** at the filing's HEAD (`cross_process_ledger_lock.py:120` module text; `:173-184` in-process probe then bounded acquire; `:524` cross-process probe) and remains **code-grounded, not reproduced** — the 12/20 figure is still a two-process measurement only.

- **2026-08-07 — the deferred adoption question is ANSWERED; this row's status does NOT move.** This row deferred the adoption question to `B-57`; the `B-57` Class 2 fork was **operator-ratified 2026-08-07 as Reading A** (per-call-site opt-in to `WRITER_OWNED_TIMESTAMP` on DIRECT append surfaces, default unchanged for every non-electing producer) and applied at **IS spec v1.13** (NEW C-IS-07 **§7.6.1**, extending the EXISTING §7.6 — no contract number minted) + **IS plan v2.9** (U-IS-11 ACs #14–#20 + #14-bis + the per-site classification table). **This row stays `registered_finding`:** it is the **cause-and-evidence record**, not the remedy owner, and what it records — the polling wait dropping kernel handoff fairness — is unchanged and unrepaired by the ratification. What changed is that its named consequence now has an authorized remedy at the exposed call sites. **Its own remaining disposition resolves at the `B-57` impl leg, on evidence:** the two-process contention witness that leg owes is the direct analogue of this row's own 12/20 repro, and a green witness under a PD-8 mutation probe is what would let this row close. **Step (3) — widening `_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE`, this row's stated council-eligible trigger — is still NOT reached**, re-determined (not inherited) at the spec leg: the classification leaves exactly ONE site retaining caller-supplied semantics (`as_is_wiring.py:129`, genuine **event** time), for which an out-of-order refusal is honest **by design**. **LIVE TRIGGER:** if the `B-57` impl leg judges **either** injection-caveat site (`audit_writer`, `cost_attribution_f2_write`) **RETAIN**, step (3) IS reached and the C3 ⊥ C11 dyad is owed **before** any tolerance change is authored.

### B-113 · The three ABBA contention probes classify contention by EXCEPTION CLASS, so an emulated-`flock` platform would leave three of the nine acquisition sites unbounded *(surfaced by out-of-family review rounds 8 and 10 on the B-93 build leg, 2026-08-06; DECLINED AT THE LEG, registered)*

- **What it is.** The three ABBA arms in `cross_process_ledger_lock` run a non-blocking probe under the directory hold and key their contention arm on **`except BlockingIOError`** — on the exception **class**, which CPython raises for `EWOULDBLOCK`/`EAGAIN` only. `fcntl.flock`'s own docstring records that it is *"emulated using fcntl() on some systems"*, and the `lockf` docs spell out that a non-blocking failure arrives as **`EACCES` or `EAGAIN`**, with an explicit instruction to *"check for either value"*. On an emulated platform those probes raise `PermissionError` immediately instead of entering their release-and-wait arm — so `flock_until_deadline` is never reached and **three of the nine `B-93` sites would not be deadline-bounded there**, while the leg's own documentation says all nine are.
- **What `B-93` did fix.** The shared helper classifies contention by **errno** (`EWOULDBLOCK`/`EAGAIN`/`EACCES`), witnessed by an injected-`EACCES` test. Every acquisition the helper performs is correct on an emulated platform; only the three **pre-existing** probes that gate entry to it are not.
- **Why declined at the `B-93` leg** *(raised by out-of-family review at rounds 8 and 10; accepted as a finding, declined as a change)*. **(1)** The narrow catch is **shipped `B-46` behaviour**, not introduced by `B-93` — the helper mirrored it deliberately. **(2)** Widening it means **merging** each arm's `except BlockingIOError` with the `except OSError` beneath it that classifies `ENOTSUP` and yields **unguarded** — restructuring three hardened arms whose ABBA release-before-blocking invariant the fork forbids breaking. **(3)** `EACCES` from a **native** `flock` is not contention at all but a genuine permission failure, so the widening is unambiguously correct only on the emulated platform. **(4)** The exposure is **dormant on every platform this workspace can observe** — Linux and macOS both provide native `flock`; CI is `ubuntu-latest` only; the operator's machine is an x86 Mac.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Establish **which** targets CPython emulates `flock` on (`HAVE_FLOCK` is a build-time `configure` probe, so this is a fact about the target, not a runtime condition). If no supported target lacks native `flock`, this row closes **unreachable**, not fixed. **(2)** If one does: merge each arm's `except BlockingIOError` into a single `except OSError` dispatching on errno — contention errnos take the release-and-wait path, `ENOTSUP` keeps its yield-unguarded arm, everything else re-raises. **(3)** Witness by **injection**, as the `B-93` helper's own `EACCES` witness does; a real emulated-`flock` platform is not available and pretending otherwise is the unwitnessable-claim failure `B-45` exists to avoid. **(4)** **Coupled to `B-45`:** if a Windows backend is ever built the same errno-vs-class question recurs there (`msvcrt.LK_NBLCK` raises `OSError`, not `BlockingIOError`), so read the two rows together at that point.
- **Council: no.** Implementation-level errno classification inside an already-cleared mechanism (C-IS-09 §9.4 defers it), no cross-domain tension to name; the only judgement is the platform-reachability fact at step (1).
- **✅ CLOSED 2026-08-07 — UNREACHABLE, NOT FIXED** *(the disposition this row's **own** step (1) provides for)*. **The finding is correct by inspection and is declined on REACHABILITY, not on correctness:** the three arms do key their contention path on the exception **class**, and on a platform where CPython emulates `flock` via `fcntl()` they would raise `PermissionError` and skip the ABBA release-and-wait arm exactly as described.
  - **What step (1) established.** **(i)** The discriminator is the **build-time `configure` probe `HAVE_FLOCK`**, not a runtime condition — a CPython built with `HAVE_FLOCK` defined calls native `flock(2)`, and only a build **without** it takes the `fcntl()` emulation whose non-blocking failure can arrive as `EACCES`. **(ii) Empirical positive control** on the operator's dev machine (Python **3.12.13**, `darwin`, x86_64): `sysconfig.get_config_var('HAVE_FLOCK')` is `1`, and a **real two-fd contention probe** (`LOCK_EX` held on one fd, `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` attempted on a second fd over the same file) raised **`BlockingIOError`** with **`errno 35` (`EAGAIN`)** — native, not emulated, so the shipped `except BlockingIOError` arm is correct there. **(iii) The committed deployment surface contains no emulated target.** The ADR-D2 decision matrix (`design-substrate/ADR-D2.md:96-98`) commits exactly three deployment surfaces — local-development, self-hosted-server, managed-cloud — and every one is a Linux/macOS/BSD-family target whose CPython builds provide native `flock`; CI is `ubuntu-latest` only; the RC runbook's Docker / Lima path is a Linux VM. The platform families where CPython actually emulates `flock` via `fcntl()` (the Solaris / HP-UX / z-OS class) appear **nowhere** in the committed surface — not in ADR-D2, not in CI, not in the RC runbook. Step (1)'s condition — *if no target the workspace supports lacks native `flock`, this row closes as UNREACHABLE rather than fixed* — is therefore **met**, and steps (2)–(3) are **not owed**.
  - **Two reopen triggers, both PRESERVED rather than discharged by this close.** **(A) `B-45`:** if a Windows serialization backend is ever built, the same errno-vs-class question recurs there — `msvcrt.LK_NBLCK` raises `OSError`, **not** `BlockingIOError` — so the two rows must be read **together** at that point, exactly as step (4) says. **(B) NEW, and independent of `B-45`:** **any new supported deployment target whose CPython build lacks `HAVE_FLOCK`** reopens this row directly, because the close rests on the composition of the committed deployment surface and on nothing else. Neither trigger is a defect in the finding; both are the conditions under which its dormancy ends.
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced on the **`B-93`** build leg (PR #1241). Sibling: **`B-45`** (the Windows backend, deferred on witnessability) — same "correct by inspection, unwitnessable here" posture, same platform gate.

### B-114 · `_prepare`'s executor-side exhaustiveness fall-through raises the memory-tool INPUT-error type for a harness-internal fault, violating the C-MEM-19 type-boundary invariant v1.3 introduced *(surfaced at the B-88 spec leg, out-of-family Codex rounds 3/7/8, 2026-08-06; the re-typing was PROPOSED and WITHDRAWN there on authority grounds, registered)*

- **What it is.** `StandardMemoryToolExecutor._prepare` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/memory_tool_executor.py:359-373`) dispatches over `MemoryToolName` to one `_prepare_<tool>` per member and ends with `raise MemoryToolExecutionInputError(f"unsupported memory tool {tool_name!s}")` at `:373`. `MemoryToolExecutionRequest.tool_name` is typed `MemoryToolName` (`:205-212`, the field at `:210`) on an `extra="forbid"` model, so a request that reaches `_prepare` **always** carries a valid enum member — the branch therefore fires only when the executor lacks a `_prepare_*` for one. That is a **harness-internal exhaustiveness fault**, not a caller- or model-supplied argument.
- **Why it is a defect once `U-MEM-28` lands.** `Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` **v1.3** C-MEM-19 gained a `### Input validation failure` subsection and a type-boundary invariant: where an implementation determines the failure class from the raised exception type, the type carrying `input_validation_failure` is raised **only** for argument refusals at the memory tool boundary, and **a harness-internal fault is not raised as that type**. Today the site is conformant, because `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` still declares `provider_adapter_failure`. The moment U-MEM-28 flips that declaration, this site becomes a **known non-conformance with a cleared contract**.
- **Harm, stated against interest.** Latent, not active. The branch is defensive and unreachable while every `MemoryToolName` member has a `_prepare_*`; the cost is one triage entry under `input_validation_failure` that is really an internal wiring fault, and a contract invariant with one named exception.
- **Why this is a separate row rather than U-MEM-28 work — authority, not merit.** The `B-88` spec leg (PR #1245) initially **required** this seventh re-typing alongside the ratified six in `lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py`. Out-of-family review round 8 objected that the operator ratified an A-ii list of **exactly six**, that a spec leg *applies* operator-decided fixes rather than deciding them, and that **recording** a contradiction does not authorize it. The objection was **accepted** and the obligation removed (fork `§11.6` item 4; plan v1.3 change-note; U-MEM-28's Out-of-scope list). Round 9 then observed that a finding carried only on `B-88`'s close-out would **vanish from open work** when that row closes at U-MEM-28 — hence this row, which owns the question and outlives `B-88`.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Ground first** at the then-current HEAD: re-read `_prepare` and `MemoryToolExecutionRequest.tool_name`. If either has changed such that the branch is reachable from caller-supplied input, the site is **conformant as it stands**, and this row closes with that finding recorded and no code change owed. **(2) Decide the disposition**, and the discriminator is whether an operator gate is needed at all: **(a) plain conformance repair against a cleared contract** — the type-boundary rule is already ratified spec text and the executor site was **never before the operator** (the `B-88` fork surveyed `lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py` only), so nothing the operator decided is being extended and this is impl work under the cleared floor; or **(b) a genuine extension of the ratified A-ii enumeration**, needing a Class 2 fork and operator ratification. **Reading (a) is the stronger one** on the grounding above and is where a grounding pass should start — but the `B-88` leg deliberately did not take it on its own authority, and this row does not pre-decide it. **(3) If repaired:** re-type `:373` to a type outside the input-error family declaring the residual, under the **same receiving-type constraints** U-MEM-28 fixes for the six dispatch sites — **not** a subclass of `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` (the declaration is read through the MRO), and **not** the family base itself (`isinstance` is subclass-inclusive, so admitting the base to `_classify_provider_exception`'s fail-fast tuple would silently fail-fast the **denied** and **store** subtypes that deliberately stay retryable). Witness **both halves**: the emitted `memory.failure_class` **and** `_classify_provider_exception(exc) is None`, since telemetry alone cannot see a base-raise regression. The `test_memory_failure_classification.py` row carrying the *"unsupported memory tool"* message re-keys with it. **(4) Not actionable before U-MEM-28 lands** — until the declaration flips, this site is conformant.
- **CLOSED 2026-08-07 — step (2) resolved to READING (a), plain conformance repair, and the repair landed.** **The adjudication, on the invariant's own words.** C-MEM-19 v1.3 `### Invariants`: *"Where the failure class is determined from the raised exception type, the type carrying input validation failure is raised only for those argument refusals, and **a harness-internal fault is not raised as that type**; separating such a fault out does not change its retry disposition."* The prose paragraph it summarizes has the same scope, and closes *"The rule constrains the type-to-class relation only; it fixes neither the number nor the naming of an implementation's exception types."* That is **kind-of-fault** language quantified over the TYPE — not an enumerated-sites list; the em-dash clause (*"an unset runtime memory context, or a missing or malformed entry in the harness's own memory tool schema table"*) glosses what *harness-internal* means and is introduced as a definition, not as the exhaustive set of covered sites. The ratified "exactly six" enumerates what the **`B-88` arc undertook**; the invariant states what the **codebase must satisfy**. Reading (b) would require the cleared invariant not to bind this site — which the design substrate itself denies: fork `§11.6` item 4 and plan v1.3 U-MEM-28 Out-of-scope both call it a *"REAL non-conformance"* / *"ONE known non-conformant site"* against the cleared contract. Design-phase authority had therefore already adjudicated that the invariant **binds** here; what round 8 withheld was only the **spec leg's** authority to perform the repair in that leg. Treating six as a ceiling on conformance would make cleared spec text unenforceable wherever a filing did not happen to survey, inverting the `CLAUDE.md` §1.3 authority chain. This arc is an **impl leg**: zero `design-substrate/**` edits, no contract number minted, no re-clearance owed.
- **Premise check at HEAD — step (1)'s falsifier NOT met.** Offsets moved (`_prepare` at `:407-421`, the raise at `:421`; the `tool_name` field at `:258`), substance unchanged: still typed `MemoryToolName` on an `extra="forbid"` model, all five members still armed, so the branch is still reachable only from a harness-internal fault. Step (4)'s precondition is met — U-MEM-28 landed at `#1247`.
- **What landed** (offsets resolved **by content** — the docstring edits above the site shift every offset in this file, so the raise sits at `:421` pre-change and `:441` at the landed commit)**.** The fall-through raise re-typed to `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError` (which already satisfies the three receiving-type constraints and is already admitted BY NAME to `_classify_provider_exception`'s fail-fast tuple as of U-MEM-28, so the retry disposition is preserved by construction); the receiving type's and the fail-fast tuple's docstrings amended to name the seventh raise site; the `test_memory_failure_classification.py` row **re-keyed** onto the internal type expecting the inherited residual `provider_adapter_failure` (eight input rows → seven + one internal), exactly as U-MEM-28's own comment there said it would; and NEW `harness-runtime/tests/test_b114_prepare_fall_through_conformance.py` carrying the **both-halves** witnesses — raised type + *not* a subclass of the input type; emitted `memory.failure_class` on **both** classify-routed paths (`execute()`'s catch and the B-84 `validate()` pre-pass); and `_classify_provider_exception(exc) is None` — plus the reachability positive control (every shipped `MemoryToolName` member reaches its own arm), which doubles as the tripwire if a later arc adds a member without one. Unlike the six dispatch sites, this one **is** on a classify-routed path, so the repair **moves** the emission to the residual rather than withdrawing one: conforming per C-MEM-19 v1.3's residual paragraph (*"a report … is the ABSENCE of a claim"*) and consistent with its coverage paragraph, which forbids withdrawal.
- **PD-8 probes, both restored.** (a) Revert the fall-through raise to the input type → the three real-site witnesses go RED (the population-table row stays green, correctly — it pins a type's declaration, not a raise site). (b) Drop the internal type from the fail-fast tuple → **only** the retry-exit assertion goes RED while all three telemetry witnesses stay green, which is the discriminating shape the two independent obligations require. Zero existing witnesses weakened (full `harness-runtime` suite: 3692 passed / 39 skipped); ruff + pyright clean. `.harness/u-mem-25-memory-closeout-evidence.md`'s C-MEM-19 row and recorded-residual paragraph refreshed in place so the U-MEM-28 certification no longer carries a stale open residual.
- **Council: no** (assessed at registration, and the assessment held). No nameable cross-domain tension: the contract rule was already ratified, the blast radius is one defensive branch plus one witness row, and the only open judgement was the conformance-repair-vs-ratified-extension discriminator at step (2) — a governance reading resolved by grounding rather than a design fork between substantive alternatives. It would have escalated to a Class 2 fork only under reading (b), which did not obtain.
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced on the **`B-88`** spec leg (PR #1245), rounds 3 / 7 / 8; registered at round 9. Sibling finding carried on `B-88`'s own close-out (not here, because it is inert until a dispatch-side emission is wired): the cross-entry-path `scope_ref`-mismatch divergence between `_require_scope_ref` (`memory_tool_executor.py:794-800`, a **denial**) and `lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py:4371` (an **input error**).

### B-115 · Memory capture same-text / same-model-NAME / different-PROVIDER re-entry: a duplicate record JSONL line, then a `TRANSIENT_RETRY` staircase via `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError` *(MEASURED at the `B-84` build leg, PR #1243, W-5 cell (3); ratified by the operator 2026-08-07; **CLOSED at the (b′) split — Runtime v1.113 §14.6.3 row 6 discharged + plan v2.61 U-RT-153, waiver tuple 4 → 5**)*

- **What it is — MEASURED, not inferred.** Executed at the **`B-84`** build leg (PR #1243) as **cell (3)** of that leg's W-5 four-cell matrix, and recorded there on the now-**closed** `B-84` row's `close_out`. A memory capture whose **text** and **model NAME** are unchanged but whose **PROVIDER** differs re-derives the **same `memory_id`** (`summary_model` is hashed into the id; the provider is not), so the record JSONL line **is appended a second time**, and the operation ledger then **raises** on its 18-field equivalence payload (because `provider` differs) — surfacing as `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError`.
- **Why that is the LIVE half.** `_classify_provider_exception` admits `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` and `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError` to its fail-fast branch **by name**, and deliberately **not** the family base, precisely so the *denied* and *store* subtypes are not swept in. The store error therefore is **not** fail-fast, classifies `TRANSIENT_RETRY`, and **re-enters the retry staircase**. **This answers `B-84`'s filing D-2 falsifier affirmatively:** the landed fail-fast half **is** re-enterable through the store-error class.
- **Stated against interest.** This is a **pre-existing** residual that `B-84`'s ratified Reading A explicitly priced as **out of scope** (A never claimed to close store errors) — **not** a regression the build leg introduced, and **not** a new defect. `B-84` left it **open and measured**.
- **Why this row exists.** `B-84` is **CLOSED**, so the residual currently lives only inside a closed row's `close_out` and is **not open-row-queryable**. This row makes the live residual queryable at its own id. **No disposition is committed here.** *Ratified by the operator 2026-08-07 on recommendation.*
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Ground first** at the then-current HEAD, by content: the `memory_id` derivation (which dimensions are hashed, and specifically whether `provider` is among them), the record-append path, the ledger's 18-field equivalence payload, and that `_classify_provider_exception` still admits only the two memory types by name. If any has changed, the mechanism may no longer hold and this row closes with that finding. **(2) Decide the disposition** — candidate readings, none pre-selected: **(a)** make `provider` part of the capture identity (collapses cell (3) into cell (1) — an extra *distinct* note — but is an **identity-dimension change to a content-addressed id**, carrying the full new-surface hash audit and an already-persisted-address-space question); **(b)** leave identity alone and make the store-error class non-re-enterable (addresses the **staircase** half, not the duplicate line); **(c)** accept and document. **(3) Note the interaction** with `B-84`'s other two open residuals (policy-flip TOCTOU, intra-call window). **(4) Witness** with the same *executed*-matrix discipline plus a PD-8 mutation probe — a code-read inference is **not** sufficient here, since this row's whole value is that cell (3) was **executed**.
- **Council: no at registration; conditionally yes at step (2).** Framing a measured residual commits to no design. Reading **(a)** *would* be council-eligible — an identity-dimension change to a content-addressed `memory_id` trades capture fidelity against the stability of an already-persisted address space (C3 ⊥ whichever voice owns memory-capture semantics). Convene **only** if step (2) leans (a), and only after step (1)'s grounding. Readings (b)/(c) sit within a cleared contract and owe no convening.
- **Cross-ref.** Successor to **`B-84`** (closed; `pr:` #1228 + #1233 + #1243) — specifically its `close_out` W-5 cell (3) record and the filing's **D-2** falsifier.

- **CLOSED — 2026-08-08, disposition (b′) BUILT. All four registered steps executed.** **(1) Grounding** was done by content at HEAD `1bce5d15`, **not** from this row's own snapshot — which had drifted: the row says `_classify_provider_exception` admits only the input and internal memory types, but at HEAD it admits **five** named types plus the 401/403 duck-typed arm, `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeInternalError` having been added by the `B-116` impl leg (PR #1271) *after* this row was written. The store subtype was nonetheless re-confirmed **absent** from that tuple, so the mechanism held — and was re-confirmed **by execution**, the landed W-5 cell-(3) witness running green at HEAD. The `memory_id` derivation, the record-append path (`_JSONL_BY_KIND` includes `TOOL_EVENT`; `_append_jsonl` is unconditional) and the ledger's single conflict raise site with its two 18-field projections (`provider` is field 11 of 18; `timestamp` is **excluded**) were all re-read directly. **(2) Disposition (b′)**, per the #1265 grounding which falsified (b)-as-registered. Reading **(a)** is **not** built and remains the registered residual. **No council was owed** — the council row made convening conditional on step (2) leaning (a); it leans (b′), which sits within a cleared contract. **(3) `B-84`'s other two residuals are neither re-opened nor contradicted, structurally rather than by assertion:** the policy-flip TOCTOU window lives at the **policy resolver**, which this leg does not touch; the intra-call window is the record-before-ledger ordering, which this leg **preserves byte-for-byte** — AC #6 pins it, and W-5 cell (3)'s `== 2` duplicate-line assertion is **PRESERVED VERBATIM** so the leg cannot claim a closure it did not deliver. What (b′) closes is the **retry amplification** (one duplicate instead of `max_attempts` duplicates), not the duplicate line. **(4) Witnessed** with the executed-matrix discipline plus five PD-8 probes, all confirmed RED then restored. **Determinism — which §14.6.3 row 6 required but which neither the spec nor the council DELIVERABLE ever defined (`REVIEW-e2.md` F-05 flagged exactly that circularity)** — is discharged against a four-part definition this leg supplies and states at contract altitude: repeat-invariance (8/8), candidate-independence, state-driven-not-stochastic (the origin candidate's payload resolves as `IDEMPOTENT_NOOP` — the positive control that stops repeat-invariance passing vacuously), and structural clock-exclusion. - **GROUNDED — 2026-08-07 (grounding leg at main `35afeda1`): classification (a) BUILDABLE as reading (b′), SEQUENCED AFTER the B-116 ratification.** All six row cites verified EXACT at HEAD (zero drift since `73b0e87b`). Probes AMPLIFY the harm: the duplicate is not singular — the record JSONL grows **N+1 lines for N staircase re-entries** (measured 4 lines after 3 retries) while the operation ledger stays flat, the same harm-class B-84 Reading A closed for the argument-shape class. Reading (b) as registered is **FALSIFIED**: `_capture`'s broad catch (`memory_capture.py:892`) wraps genuine transient I/O too, so a blanket fail-fast for `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError` would kill retries for real flakes — the identical objection the code records for the denied class at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:343-349`. **Buildable shape (b′)**: split the DETERMINISTIC ledger idempotency-conflict out as a distinct non-retryable type keyed on a closed discriminator (`MemoryCaptureResult` closed-schema extension ~15 lines; a `MemoryToolExecutionConflictError` raise ~8; BY-NAME fail-fast admission ~6; ~90 witness lines incl. line-count-caps-at-2 and a transient-I/O-still-retries positive control), justified under Runtime §14.6 D2's iff-rule — no spec amendment needed. **COUPLED to `B-116`**: the (b′) fix routes a new deterministic class onto the exact fail-fast branch B-116 re-scopes — its breaker disposition is row (6) of the B-116 filing's table; build only after that ratification. Reading (a) (`provider` into capture identity) stays registered as the residual — (b′) caps the duplication at 2 lines, it does not eliminate it.

### B-116 · Should DETERMINISTIC harness-internal faults count toward a PROVIDER's circuit-breaker state? *(pre-existing; spans C-CP-03 §3.4+§3.5 + Runtime §14.6; RATIFIED Reading (II) 2026-08-07 — spec v1.112 + plan v2.60 landed; U-RT-152 impl leg merged #1271; **CLOSED at the `B-116-t3` OD leg — OD v1.37 §9.2 18 → 19 + plan v2.32 U-OD-58**)*

- **The question, which this row frames rather than answers.** When the retry/breaker/fallback dispatcher **fail-fasts** a candidate, it records **one breaker failure against that candidate's PROVIDER** before exiting. Should a **deterministic, harness-internal** fault do that?
- **Grounded by content at HEAD `73b0e87b`** *(the inbound note's `~:1025` is **corrected** — `:1025` is the `"retry.fail_class"` attribute-set line)*. `retry_breaker_fallback.py` computes `breaker_cause = _classify_breaker_cause(exc)` at **`:1006`**, and on the `cause is None` (fail-fast) branch calls `transition = breaker.record_failure(cause=breaker_cause)` at **`:1028`**. The **fail-fast set** (`_classify_provider_exception`, from `:272`) has **five** members: `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError`; `LLMDispatchPayloadShapeError`; a raw SDK exception with `.status_code in (401, 403)`; `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError`; `MemoryToolExecutionInputError`.
- **The sharpened framing — finer than "internal faults get tagged as provider faults".** `_classify_breaker_cause` is duck-typed on `.status_code` and returns `None` for anything lacking one (`:404-406`), so a `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError` yields `cause=None` — it is **not mis-tagged**. But `record_failure` (`retry_breaker.py:219`) **increments `fail_count` regardless of `cause`** — `cause` is telemetry-only (`:228-233`) — so the failure **still counts toward `fail_threshold`** and still moves the provider toward `OPEN`.
- **The tension.** `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError` is **by construction** a harness-internal wiring fault (an unset `RuntimeMemoryContext.record_scope`/`.scope_ref`; a `MEMORY_TOOL_CONTRACTS` entry whose input schema has no `properties` mapping) and is admitted to fail-fast on the express grounds that it is *"deterministic and candidate-independent"*. Such a fault is **not evidence about the provider's health** — yet it consumes provider breaker budget, and a repeated internal misconfiguration could **open a healthy provider's breaker**.
- **Pre-existing, not introduced by any recent arc.** Spans **C-CP-21** and **Runtime §14.6** (Runtime + CP). **No commitment to a change is made here.** *Ratified by the operator 2026-08-07.*
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Ground first** by content: `_classify_provider_exception`'s membership, `_classify_breaker_cause`'s `None` return, the `record_failure` call on the cause-`None` branch, and `record_failure`'s counting semantics — **the whole framing rests on `record_failure` counting independently of `cause`, and that is the first thing to falsify.** **(2) Establish the contract position BEFORE deciding anything:** read **C-CP-21** and **Runtime §14.6** for what a breaker failure is *defined* to mean. If the contract already says, this is a **conformance** question, not a design fork; if it does not, that silence is itself the finding. **(3) Only then decide.** **(4) Note the scope asymmetry** when pricing: the question applies with **different force to each of the five members** — 401/403 is genuinely a provider-credential fact and unreachable is genuinely a provider fact, while payload-shape and the two memory types are harness-side. Any fix must be **per-member, not wholesale**, or it will silently stop counting real provider auth failures.
- **The discriminator.** Does the breaker count *"this **CANDIDATE** failed to produce a result"* or *"this **PROVIDER** is unhealthy"*? Under the first, an internal fault legitimately counts — the candidate did fail, and the chain is right to move on. Under the second it must **not** count, and the fix is to skip `record_failure` (or record on a non-provider scope) for the deterministic harness-internal members.
- **Council: no at registration; conditionally yes at step (3).** The tension is nameable in advance — changing what counts toward a breaker trades control-plane reliability semantics (C1/C9: a breaker that **under**-counts fails to protect a genuinely failing chain) against operator-loop robustness (C11: a breaker that **over**-counts opens a healthy provider on the operator's own misconfiguration). Convene **only** if step (2) finds the contract silent **and** step (3) leans toward changing the counting rule.
- **Cross-ref.** The `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError` fail-fast membership was established at the **`B-88`** spec leg (U-MEM-28) and extended to a seventh raise site by **`B-114`**; the `MemoryToolExecutionInputError` membership at **`B-84`**. ### B-117 · Duplicate pytest test-file BASENAMES across workspace packages silently drop witnesses from collection, and nothing guards against it *(lifted to its own row 2026-08-07 from the `B-112` close-out's registered ADJACENT INFRA GAP, per that row's own "a future infra arc may lift it to its own row")*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-11 (#1315)** — the cheapest close-out shape built: `tools/module_path_guard.py` + root `conftest.py` raising `pytest.UsageError` at session start when ≥2 `harness-*/tests` files claim the same **relative module path** (the collision unit sharpened from bare basename during the build: `tests/test_x.py` vs `tests/integration/test_x.py` are distinct modules — the relpath rule reports exactly the drop shape with zero false positives; nested `integration/` subpackages exist at HEAD). Failure venue: collection-time hard failure everywhere (local + every CI axis job) — a CI-only step would leave local runs green while witnesses drop, the defect's own signature. Re-measure at HEAD (step 1): zero collisions across 517 files (both pytest discovery patterns, nested dirs included; recounted after codex r1/r2 broadened the scan). 15 witnesses — incl. a real-entry-point SUBPROCESS witness for the conftest half (a synthetic colliding workspace aborts an actual pytest session with the guard report) and probe-derived cases for both codex catches (*_test.py drop; outermost-contiguous-package anchoring with the broken-chain collision + non-package legality; r4 norecursedirs exclusion; r6 non-identifier package-boundary anchoring) — plus a LIVE e2e probe (a real duplicate aborted an unrelated package's run; removal restored green). The heavier candidates (per-package rootdir isolation; renaming the seven `tests` packages) priced and not taken — the hook covers the class. ONE residual class recorded, held with grounds (codex r8 vs its own r4, the opposite-direction pair): collisions under norecursedirs dirs reachable only via EXPLICIT pytest args are outside the guarded set — the gate protects recursive suite runs; including them re-opens r4's realistic false-positive block. CI roster: `test_module_path_guard.py` joins the tools pytest step.

- **What it is.** Every `harness-*/tests/` directory is a package literally named `tests` (all seven carry an `__init__.py`), so two test files that share a **basename** across two packages resolve to the SAME module path. pytest imports ONE module for BOTH paths and **silently drops** the loser's tests. This is not hypothetical: at the `B-93` build leg (PR #1241) `test_b93_cross_process_lock_deadline.py` existed in both `harness-is/tests/` and `harness-runtime/tests/`, and **12 written witnesses never ran** — 34 collected where 35 were written. The suite was **GREEN throughout**; it was caught only by recounting programmatically.
- **Why it is registered rather than absorbed.** The defect is silent in the worst direction — it removes coverage while every signal (exit code, pass count, CI green) says nothing is wrong. It is invisible to the `[[count-claims-drift-every-review-round]]` discipline unless someone happens to compare *written* against *collected* for that specific pair of files.
- **`--import-mode=importlib` is ALREADY SET and does NOT fix it — reproduced at HEAD `e711a857`, stated against the `B-112` close-out's own candidate list.** Root `pyproject.toml:380` carries `addopts = "--import-mode=importlib"` (with an explanatory comment at `:377-379` naming exactly this collision). A positive-control probe — one `test_zz_collision_probe.py` in `harness-is/tests/` (1 test) and another in `harness-runtime/tests/` (2 tests) — collected **2 of 3**, and the run reported `harness-runtime/tests/test_zz_collision_probe.py::test_is_side_probe`: the runtime path was resolved to the **IS** module's contents. The `__init__.py`-bearing `tests` packages defeat the import-mode fix. Probe files were removed after the measurement; nothing was left in the tree.
- **The invariant the tree actually relies on.** UNIQUE TEST BASENAMES REPO-WIDE — **currently true** (511 `harness-*/tests/**/test_*.py` files, zero duplicate basenames, measured at HEAD `e711a857`), **currently unenforced**, and violated **silently rather than loudly**.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-measure first** — re-run the basename-uniqueness count and the positive-control collision probe at the then-current HEAD; if a duplicate already exists, the guard's first run is also a repair. **(2) Price the guard against the three candidate shapes** the `B-112` close-out named, now that one of them is falsified: a **basename-uniqueness check** across `harness-*/tests/**` (the cheapest — a ~15-line `conftest.py` collection hook or a standalone CI step; the only shape the probe above leaves standing); **per-package pytest rootdir isolation** (heavier — changes how the whole suite is invoked); `--import-mode=importlib` **with unique package names** (the import-mode half is already in place, so this reduces to *renaming the seven `tests` packages* — a tree-wide rename, priced accordingly). **(3) Decide the failure venue** — a collection-time hard failure (loud, blocks the developer immediately, but fires inside every `pytest` invocation) versus a dedicated CI step (cheaper at inner-loop time, later feedback). **(4) Witness it under PD-8** — the guard must be shown to FAIL on a deliberately introduced duplicate basename and pass once it is removed; a guard that has never been seen red is not a guard.
- **Council: no.** A test-infrastructure hygiene guard with no cross-domain tension to name — the only tradeoff is inner-loop cost versus feedback latency (step 3), which is a single-domain judgment, not a nameable dyad. Route to a single voice plus `advisor()` if it is contested at all.
- **Trigger.** The next test-infrastructure arc, **or** any recurrence (a duplicate basename appearing, or a written-versus-collected count mismatch surfacing at any leg).
- **Cross-ref.** Surfaced on `B-112`'s close-out via merge-gate lens 3 (G3) at the `B-93` build leg; `B-112` itself is `closed` and its own subject matter (deadline'd lock polling and kernel handoff fairness) is unrelated to this row.

### B-118 · The half-open latch is dead code, so `OPEN` is an absorbing breaker state for the process lifetime *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C9), 2026-08-07)*

- **What it is.** `BreakerStateMachine.attempt_half_open()` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker.py:289`) has **ZERO production call sites** — the only three occurrences across every `harness-*/src` tree are two docstrings (`:51`, `:201`) and the definition itself (`:289`), re-verified at HEAD this session. `should_attempt()` (`:309-311`) is a pure state read that holds no clock, and `RuntimeRetryBreaker.get_breaker` (`:379-400`) caches breakers identity-stable for the process. Therefore **`OPEN` is an ABSORBING state for the process lifetime at HEAD** — the shipped breaker is a one-way latch. The contract already writes text for the transition the runtime never performs: OD spec v1.32 §7.1 names the *"caller-driven `open → half_open` cooldown-elapsed transition"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:46`), and `record_failure`'s own `half_open → open` arm (`retry_breaker.py:239-251`) is unreachable for the same reason.
- **PRIORITY RAISED, and why.** This was C9's A1 recommendation 3 (register separately, do not fold into `B-116`). At the E2b reconcile it was **raised to the highest-priority forward row by finding F-06**: `B-116`'s ratified **normative test** is stated over exactly this path — *"a fault charges the provider-model breaker only if a half-open trial call could return a different result than the trip did, for a reason attributable to the `{provider, model}` the breaker is keyed to."* The test is not void (OD §7.1 contracts the transition, so it stands as design intent), but `B-116` now depends on a recovery path with no production caller. C9 stated the dependency direction plainly at cross-read: **ratifying a reading whose cost is a function of the latch ratifies the latch's consequences without ratifying the latch.**
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** zero production call sites and that `get_breaker` still returns identity-stable machines. **(2) Decide who holds the clock** — the state machine deliberately holds none (`retry_breaker.py:290-296` assigns it to the L8 orchestrator), so the caller must thread one; C9's Pillar-4 requirement is *half-open after the cooldown, one trial call, close on success, re-open on failure*, which `attempt_half_open` / `record_success` / `record_failure` already implement. **(3) Wire it** at or beside the breaker pre-check (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:674`). **(4) Witness both directions** — a real `open → half_open → closed` recovery AND an `open → half_open → open` re-trip; a green unit test on the state machine alone is not the witness, because the state machine is already green and the gap is reachability. **(5) Re-ground `B-116`'s witnesses** — C9's A1 recommendation 2 forbade asserting a half-open path while it is unreachable, so `B-116` asserts `fail_count == 0` and `state is CLOSED` instead; once this row lands those may be strengthened, and they should be, deliberately.
- **What would falsify it.** A production call site appearing (then the row is already closed), **or** a decision that absorbing-`OPEN` is intentional — in which case OD §7.1's transition text and `B-116`'s normative test both need amending, which is a Class 1 design-substrate route, not an impl fix.
- **Council:** **No at registration.** A single-domain C9 reliability-mechanism gap with no nameable cross-domain tension — the mechanism, the contract text, and the recovery model are all in one voice's lineage. **Conditionally yes** only if step (2) proposes a *durable* cooldown clock: that re-opens the persistence tension `B-116` term **t4** pinned (a durable breaker opened by a fault the operator cannot see survives the restart the operator reaches for first), which is a genuine C9 ⊥ C11 dyad.
- **CLOSED 2026-08-08 — PR #1275 (Runtime spec **v1.114** + plan **v2.62** U-RT-154 + impl, ONE bundled leg).** All five close-out steps executed. **(1)** Re-verified at HEAD `fb3dda44`: zero production call sites, `should_attempt()` clock-free, `get_breaker` identity-stable. **(2) The clock is SPLIT** — the **composer** holds the source (an injectable `monotonic` field defaulting to `time.monotonic`, mirroring the existing `sleep_fn` posture); the **state machine** holds only the caller-recorded `opened_at` deadline, because that state is per-`(scope, identifier)` and the composer has no per-breaker storage (a composer-side map would be a SECOND authority for breaker state). The machine still never reads a clock. NOT a `RuntimeConfig` scalar. The in-tree shape template is `BreakerGuardedSigningBackend` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/config/audit_signing.py`), which has carried an injected-clock + single-probe breaker since ADR-D8. **(3)** Wired at the pre-check, now **three-way**: `closed` proceeds / `open` attempts a conjunctively-gated trial **capped at ONE attempt** / `half_open` means a sibling holds the permit and is skipped with the new `half-open-trial-in-flight` reason. `should_attempt()` narrows to `state is closed`, which **is** the permit — `half_open` exists only while a trial is in flight, so the prior `state is not open` admitted every concurrent branch into a call contracted to be single. **No lock, and the absence is a decision**: all mutators run on one event loop, so the hazard is interleaving at the `await`, not a data race (contrast the signing breaker, which *does* lock, because span-end worker threads sign). **(4)** BOTH directions witnessed **end-to-end through the real composer** with an injected clock — `open → half_open → closed` recovery **and** `open → half_open → open` re-trip — plus a three-branch concurrency witness whose interleaving is **guaranteed** by an `asyncio.Event` rather than hoped for. **(5)** The `B-116` witnesses were strengthened **deliberately**: seven rows gained their now-available assertions (the Probe-C **clock-advance** form, which discriminates *never-opened* from *opened-and-reset*; the 401 and response-parsing **recovery-completion positive controls** that make the CHARGE mean something; the exhaustion-identity admissibility loop), three were left unchanged by name, and `B-115`'s IS-side determinism witnesses were untouched.
- **The one operator gate, and what was NOT derivable.** Grounding surfaced an interaction the ratified **Reading (II)** does *not* answer. With the `B-116` guard, a **waived** fail-fast during a trial charges nothing — so `record_failure` never runs and the machine is **stranded in `half_open`**, where `should_attempt()` refuses everyone and `attempt_half_open` returns `None`: **a NEW absorbing state strictly worse than the absorbing `OPEN` this row removes**, and one the wiring would itself have introduced. Four further cells (audit-signing hard failure, terminal HITL control flow, `DispatchFenceTrippedSignal`, `CancelledError`) strand identically. INCONCLUSIVE → re-arm is derivable from Reading (II)'s attributability clause; the **FRESH-vs-PRESERVED cooldown** choice is not, and was surfaced. **Operator-ratified 2026-08-08 (AskUserQuestion): FRESH cooldown**, `trigger_count = 0`, `fail_count` unchanged. All nine cells are contracted at **NEW Runtime spec v1.114 §14.6.4**. **The council condition did NOT fire** — the design is in-memory monotonic with nothing persisted, so the durable-cooldown-clock trigger for the C9 ⊥ C11 dyad was never reached and no council was convened.

- **Out-of-family review rounds 1 + 2.** Round 1 returned two REAL findings, both fixed: the **stale-outcome race** (the `_epoch` guard the in-tree `BreakerGuardedSigningBackend` template carries and the first build dropped — a stale SUCCESS resolving a trial it does not own closes an unhealthy breaker; fixed by a per-breaker admission epoch on all three `half_open` resolution paths, stale outcomes DROPPED without charging, `closed`-state accounting byte-unchanged) and **cell 4 unreachable** under the ONE-attempt cap (voided BY CONSTRUCTION, cap kept, not renumbered). Round 2 returned one mechanical count reconciliation (**11 ACs / 14 PD-8 probes**) and one **cross-transition** stale-outcome variant — a request admitted while `closed` that survives a trip AND a recovery, then resets `fail_count` on the tokenless `closed` arm. **Adjudicated PRE-EXISTING and REGISTERED, not absorbed**: the `closed`-arm success-reset is shipped consecutive-failure semantics reachable with **zero trips**, and guarding it would mean epoch-capturing every ordinary dispatch and rewriting contracted success-reset semantics — a redesign this leg does not price. Declared at Runtime spec v1.114 §14.6.4's honest-boundary paragraph and minted as forward row **`B-135`**. **Round 3** returned one further REAL finding — the round-1 release obligation guarded the DISPATCH but left the admission's own transition EMISSION outside it, so a raising span exporter stranded the shared breaker in `half_open` with no owner: **the absorbing latch this row removes, recreated by its own fix**, and strictly worse than absorbing `open` since the re-arm refuses a non-owner too. Fixed structurally (the protected region now begins at the **transition**, not the dispatch; the release there is state-only so the broken emitter is not re-entered and the original fault is not masked); the other four transition emissions were **swept** and verified to follow their state mutation. **Round 4** returned the MIRROR of round 3 at the inconclusive EXITS — a failing re-arm emitter raised BEFORE the bare `raise` and **replaced** the propagating `AuditSigningFailedError` / terminal HITL signal / `DispatchFenceTrippedSignal`, trading a contracted terminal mapping for a telemetry fault; fixed by a disposition flip keyed on whether an exception is in flight (suppressed **and attached** via `add_note`, never discarded), with the scope bound kept so exporter breakage still surfaces on the common path. **Round 6** found that §14.6.4's own text **overclaimed**: a `closed`-era dispatch keeps its multi-attempt policy and can resume attempt 2 across a trip, overlapping "the single trial" — but the non-re-consultation is **pre-existing** (the pre-check is per-candidate by contract) and the ratified intent bound THE TRIAL, never stale dispatches. Scoped §14.6.4 to **era-consistent admissions**, pinned the declared behaviour by witness, refused mid-staircase re-consultation as unpriced semantic surgery, and folded the attempt side into **`B-135`**. **The merge gate (#1275)** then MEASURED a witness gap the leg's own PD-8 discipline had missed: dropping `trial_token` from the max-attempts-exhaustion charge left the whole suite green while `fail_count` went 3→2 and `trigger_count` 3→0, because cell 5's witness asserted only `state is OPEN` + a fresh `opened_at` — **both equally true of an inconclusive re-arm**. Closed with the discriminating pair plus probe P17; the escalation site's token threading resolved by determining unreachability from content and pinning it; cells 7/8 given the `opened_at`-FRESH assertion; both `BaseException` asymmetries witnessed. Unit now **15 ACs / 17 probes**, closure criterion stated over the SETS rather than a count.
### B-119 · No per-provider breaker is constructed anywhere, so `BreakerScope.PER_PROVIDER` is a declared-but-unbuilt scope *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C9), 2026-08-07)*

- **What it is.** `BreakerScope` declares **two** values — `PER_MODEL` and `PER_PROVIDER` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/harness_breaker_schema.py:105-112`) — and both are contract-declared: CP §3.5 gives `harness.breaker.scope ∈ {per_model, per_provider}` (`design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:402`, re-tabled at `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_3.md:75`) and OD §7.1 mirrors it (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:38`). The **only** breaker constructed anywhere is `PER_MODEL`, at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:662-665`, keyed `f"{candidate.provider}:{candidate.model}"` (`:662`). C9 records this as his own **FM-O** (single-breaker-scope), live at HEAD.
- **Why it matters, in `B-116`'s own terms.** With no provider-scope aggregation, the **only** provider-wide health signal an operator can get today is *"every per-model breaker in the chain opened"* — which is precisely the signal a candidate-independent fault manufactures. `B-116`'s executed Probe B showed one dispatch burning one failure on **every** chain breaker across **both** providers, and Probe C showed `fail_threshold` repeats opening them all. So the absent scope is not merely unbuilt; its absence is what let a config-shaped fault imitate a provider outage.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** that `PER_MODEL` is still the only constructed scope. **(2) Decide whether `PER_PROVIDER` should exist at all** — either build it (a second `get_breaker(BreakerScope.PER_PROVIDER, provider)` charge alongside the per-model one, with its own threshold and its own trip semantics) or record the enum member as deliberately forward-only in the same shape OD v1.32 used for `capability_shortfall` (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:50`). Do not leave it declared-and-silent. **(3) If built, price the `B-116` interaction explicitly:** the ratified guard is stated on `record_failure` at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:1028`, and a *second* charge site must inherit the same negative predicate — otherwise the four demoted harness-internal members re-enter the breaker through the provider scope and `B-116` is silently undone. **(4) Witness scope discrimination** at the emission, which today can only ever report `per_model`. **(5) Note the coupling to `B-125`** — `emit_breaker_transition_event` defaults `tool_id` to the breaker key **only at `PER_MODEL` scope** (`retry_breaker.py:459-461`), so constructing a second scope changes which trips carry that default.
- **What would falsify it.** A `PER_PROVIDER` construction site appearing anywhere in `harness-*/src`.
- **Cross-note 2026-08-08 (`B-118` closed).** This row is **untouched** and not dependent on `B-118`, but its C11 half is materially changed. The registered council framing weighed detection breadth against *"one provider-scope `OPEN` disables every model of that provider at once, **and with `B-118` unfixed it does so irreversibly**"*. `B-118` is now closed — `OPEN` is escapable, bounded by a real cooldown with a single-trial half-open probe — so the irreversibility clause no longer holds and the C11 objection is **weaker** than when it was registered. The dyad is **not dissolved** (a provider-scope breaker still has a wider blast radius, and a recovery probe still costs one real call), but any future step-(2) deliberation MUST re-ground the C11 position against escapable-`OPEN` rather than quoting the registered text.
- **Council:** **No at registration** — nothing is decided here. **Conditionally yes at step (2):** building a second breaker scope trades detection breadth (C9 — a provider outage should be visible as one fact, not inferred from N per-model facts) against operator recoverability under a materially wider blast radius (C11 — one provider-scope `OPEN` disables every model of that provider at once, and with `B-118` unfixed it does so irreversibly). That is nameable in advance and dyadic.
- **CLOSED — 2026-08-08, PR #1277 (doc/register-only disposition leg). FORWARD-ONLY RECORD, not built** — the `capability_shortfall` shape (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:50`). *This bullet states the CURRENT result; the bullets above are the row's registration text and are superseded where they conflict.* **(1) Re-verified at HEAD `49591934`.** `PER_MODEL` is still the **only** constructed scope: the sole production `get_breaker` call is `retry_breaker_fallback.py:774-776` (`breaker_identifier = f"{candidate.provider}:{candidate.model}"` at `:774`). The registration's `:662-665` is **line-drifted by `B-118`**, not falsified. `PER_PROVIDER` appears in `src` **only** at its enum declaration (`harness_breaker_schema.py:112`) plus one docstring mention (`config/audit_signing.py:81`); the only constructions anywhere are **tests** (`test_lifecycle_retry_breaker.py:187`, `:497`) through the scope-agnostic registry (`retry_breaker.py:546-568`). **The falsifier is not met.** **(3) Priced honestly, and the registration understates it.** The `B-116` waiver predicate is **free** to inherit — `_is_breaker_charge_waived(exc)` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:456-467`) is purely exception-type-based over the tuple at `:420-427` and is **key-agnostic**, so the registration's fear that the demoted members "re-enter through the provider scope" is unfounded (and the tuple is **five**, not four, since `B-115` (b′)). What is **not** free is the `B-118` machinery: the pre-check at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:804-895` is a **single**-breaker state machine (one `half_open_trial` flag, one `trial_token = breaker.trial_epoch`, one one-attempt `effective_policy` cap, one `try/except BaseException → re_arm_half_open_trial` protection boundary). A second scope makes admission a **product of two independent permits** — per-model `CLOSED` × per-provider `HALF_OPEN` has **no defined cell**, and Runtime v1.114 §14.6.4's nine-cell matrix is written for **one** machine, so one dispatch outcome would resolve **two** trial tokens. That is a **Runtime spec delta**, not "a second `get_breaker` charge alongside". **Half-open coherence, answered:** a provider-scope trial *is* semantically coherent and §14.6.3's test is satisfiable at `{provider}` keying — the incoherence is **compositional**, not semantic. **(2)/(4) Demand is absent at HEAD, measured not assumed.** **Zero** consumers branch on `harness.breaker.scope`; the only production **read** of the value is `B-125`'s own default at `retry_breaker.py:627`.
