### B-120 · The breaker-transition emission passes no `permanent_fail_repeats` and no `model_version`, so two declared attributes have no producer *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C9), 2026-08-07)*

- **What it is.** `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher._emit_breaker_transition` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:1130-1136`) calls `emit_breaker_transition_event(transition, parent_span)` positionally and passes **none** of the three optional correlation keywords the registry accepts — `permanent_fail_repeats`, `tool_id`, `model_version` (`retry_breaker.py:430-437`). `BreakerTransition` itself carries no field for any of them (`retry_breaker.py:183-189`). Two of the three are therefore **dead at every shipped trip**: `harness.breaker.permanent_fail_repeats`, the declared C10 gating signal (*"Whether this trip is from repeated C5 permanent-fail-exits — the C10 gating signal"*, `Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:42`; CP §3.5 `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:402`), and `harness.breaker.model_version` (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:44`). C9 names this his own **FM-Q**, live.
- **The one-third correction, carried rather than dropped.** C9's A1 asserted all **three** are vacuous. That is true of the **call**, and false on the **wire** for `tool_id`: `emit_breaker_transition_event` sets `effective_tool_id = transition.identifier` whenever `tool_id is None` at `PER_MODEL` scope (`retry_breaker.py:459-461`), with the default stated as contract in the docstring (`:445-446`). C7 repeated the *"never populated"* claim at A2, C11 falsified it at cross-read, and C7 **formally withdrew** it at E2b. Since `PER_MODEL` is the only constructed scope (`B-119`), **every** shipped trip already emits `harness.breaker.tool_id = "provider:model"`. That half is `B-125`'s row, not this one.
- **Why it matters directionally.** C9's warning, not a slogan: the fail-fast branch maps to `PERMANENT_FAIL_EXIT` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:1024-1027`), so **the moment anyone wires `permanent_fail_repeats`** — the natural follow-on — it begins gating on exactly the branch `B-116` re-scoped. Under the rejected reading (I) that would have driven C10's `gate_combination` to gate a *healthy* model+tool combination off a harness config bug. Reading (II)-as-ratified makes the signal more meaningful, not less, but the sequencing is load-bearing.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** that the call site passes no keywords and that `BreakerTransition` still has no carrier fields. **(2) Decide per attribute whether a real producer exists** — `permanent_fail_repeats` needs per-cause failure history the state machine does not keep (the same gap `FIVE_XX_STREAK` already carries in-code at `harness_breaker_schema.py:145-149`), whereas `model_version` needs a binding-side value the dispatcher demonstrably has. These are not one task. **(3) For any attribute with no producer,** either wire it or record it as a forward-compatible slot in the shape OD v1.32 used for `capability_shortfall` (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:50`) — declared-and-dead-and-undocumented is the state to leave. **(4) Sequence AFTER `B-116`'s guard lands,** per C9's own directional warning above. **(5) Witness** a trip carrying each newly-populated attribute, and a trip that legitimately omits it (the attributes are optional by contract, and `absent` is a meaningful value here).
- **What would falsify it.** A producer already existing for either attribute on some path this search missed.
- **Council:** **No.** Populating declared-but-unset attributes inside a cleared schema is adjudicated by the attribute owner (C7/OD); there is no cross-domain tradeoff to name. Route to a single voice plus `advisor()` if step (2) is contested.

### B-121 · `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError` means **unregistered** at all three raise sites, and the misleading name is a demonstrated defect vector *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C9 E2b reconcile, on adversarial finding F-01), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-12 (#1317) — option (b′) via the U-HK-13 two-reviewer resolver (AGREEMENT: out-of-family codex, pick salvaged from its timed-out run's own loop-state record, + a neutral-brief Claude adjudicator with facts independently re-verified; RESOLVE row at `.harness/loop_status.md`), bundled Runtime spec v1.120 + implementation.** C-RT-14 now separates the genuine stage-3a network class `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-UNREACHABLE` from the per-dispatch registry class `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-UNREGISTERED`; the former row and C-RT-05 escalation remain byte-identical. All three registry-only raise sites now use `LLMDispatchProviderUnregisteredError`, and the C-RT-15/C-RT-16 failure narrative, waiver tuple, B-122 startup diagnostic, and active witnesses follow the accurate name. The v1.2 coherence row is qualified against the post-split C-RT-14 set; no Runtime plan unit, CXA row, cross-axis edge, configuration field, or behavior beyond diagnostic identity was added.
- **What it is.** The type is named *Unreachable*; **all three** of its raise sites are harness-side registry lookups that never contact a provider. Counted at HEAD: exactly **3** `raise LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError` sites in `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/llm_dispatch.py` — `:1525` (`provider_name not in self.providers`, an in-process dict), `:1549` (`_PROVIDER_OPERATIONS.get(...) is None`, whose own comment at `:1546-1548` reads *"Defensive — every key in `self.providers` is one of the three constructed at stage 3a per C-RT-05"*), and `:1865` (the terminal `else` of the `isinstance` adapter-arm chain). The class docstring is explicit: *"Raised when `binding.model_binding.provider` resolves to a provider absent from `ctx.providers`"* (`:184-193`). The semantics are **unregistered**, not **unreachable**.
- **Why it is a defect and not a nit.** The name is the **defect vector**, demonstrably. It misled the `B-116` fork filing's §5 table and **all four** council voices into keeping member #1 counting through A1 and the entire cross-read; the adversarial leg's halt-class finding F-01 demoted it on raise-site evidence, and C9 recorded the correction against himself: *"This is a defect I authored — my A1 row 1 came from the type's NAME, not its raise sites."* Under the ratified recovery-model test a half-open trial re-executes an in-process dict built once at bootstrap and re-fails identically for the process lifetime. Genuine provider-down never travels as this type at all: a real network fault raises the provider SDK's own exception, carries no `.status_code`, falls to the catch-all `TRANSIENT_RETRY` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:371`) and charges the breaker at `:1072`/`:1091`, outside the branch `B-116` touches.
- **This is a Class 2 back-flow, and the row says so rather than walking it.** The type maps to the `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-UNREACHABLE` fail-class token per **C-RT-14** (docstring `:189-190`), and that token is carried in cleared design-substrate — Runtime §C-RT-16's fail-class narrative propagates it through the wrapper (`design-substrate/Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md:4194`). Renaming the **Python type** is code-local; renaming or re-taxonomising the **token** is a `design-substrate/**` change and routes as a **Class 2 fork** per root `CLAUDE.md` §4.3, with the taxonomy value owned by C5/C7/OD — not by an impl leg. **Status stays `registered_finding`;** the fork route is named here, not taken.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** the three raise sites and that none contacts a provider. **(2) Decide the scope:** **(a)** rename the Python type only, keeping `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-UNREACHABLE` — cheapest, but leaves the operator-facing token still misleading, which is most of the harm; **(b)** mint a distinct `RT-FAIL-PROVIDER-UNREGISTERED` token and re-map, which is the design-substrate change. **(3) Route (b) as a Class 2 fork against the C-RT-14 taxonomy BEFORE any code lands** (X-AL-3 — no silent H_T design extension at Phase 7). **(4) Do not re-litigate `B-116`:** member #1's demotion stands on raise-site evidence regardless of what the type is called. **(5) Note the sibling** — `B-122` is the same raise sites' other half (should this fault be discoverable at bootstrap at all).
- **What would falsify it.** A fourth raise site that *does* contact a provider (then the type is genuinely heterogeneous and needs a split, not a rename — the `B-116` member-#2 shape).
- **Council:** **No.** The substantive question — does it count toward the breaker — was settled at `B-116` on evidence. What remains is a naming/taxonomy call inside a contract with a named owner, plus a routing decision this row already names.

### B-122 · Nothing validates at bootstrap that every fallback-chain candidate names a **registered** provider *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C9 E2b reconcile, on adversarial finding F-01), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-12 (#1316)** — built as a stage-3b startup **DIAGNOSTIC**, deliberately not a gate: the close-out's venue counter-argument decided from the code's own commitments (skipped registration is a supported deployment shape per the `LLMDispatchProviderUnregisteredError` docstring's Ollama-degraded path; tool-only bootstraps run provider-free per v1.47 §2.1) — a hard refusal would be wrong, so `_warn_unregistered_chain_providers` logs once on `harness.runtime.fallback_chain` (the stage-5 prewarm best-effort venue precedent) naming the unregistered candidates + the dispatch-time consequence, and bootstrap continues. Partial-coverage limit stated in place (per-dispatch role-augmented chains, `retry_breaker_fallback.py`). Witnesses: partial-registration shape (openai registered / anthropic candidate not → warning + completed inference-bearing bootstrap) + all-registered silence; deletion mutation RED. The B-121 sibling closes in the bundled v1.120 naming/taxonomy split.

- **What it is.** The same three raise sites that ground `B-121` establish the shape: a fallback-chain candidate naming a provider absent from `ctx.providers` is discovered **at dispatch time, per dispatch**, as a runtime exception (`llm_dispatch.py:1525`) — and, after `B-116`, as one that charges no health counter at all. Nothing validates the chain against the registry earlier. The comment at `llm_dispatch.py:1546-1548` records that the provider set is fixed at **stage 3a per C-RT-05**, so the check is in principle decidable before any dispatch runs: both the chain and the registry are known. C9's framing — *"config faults fail at stage 3a, not at a runtime health counter"* — and he assigned the surface to C1/C11 rather than authoring it.
- **Stated honestly: this row is THINNER than its siblings.** C9 registered it in a single line at the E2b reconcile, with **no probe run, no venue chosen, and no shape priced**. Everything above beyond the raise-site facts is this row observing that the check is decidable — not a council finding, and not a designed proposal. It is registered so the observation is queryable, not because it arrived costed. Read it as a question, not a plan.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Ground the bootstrap sequence first** — where the fallback chain is composed relative to where `providers` is constructed, and whether a candidate can enter a chain **after** bootstrap. It can, partially: `_advance_or_exhaust` traverses a per-dispatch *effective* chain that may be role-augmented rather than the stage-bound one (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:878-883`), which bounds how total a bootstrap check can be. Answer this before pricing anything. **(2) Decide the failure venue, and answer the counter-argument first:** the class docstring names *"Ollama-degraded path skipped registration"* as an expected case (`llm_dispatch.py:186-187`) — if skipping registration is a supported deployment shape, a hard bootstrap refusal is **wrong**, and the correct answer is a startup diagnostic, not a gate. **(3) Price whatever survives (2).** **(4) Witness** with a configuration naming an unregistered provider, asserting the chosen venue fires and that a legitimately degraded deployment still boots.
- **What would falsify it.** Step (2) can kill the row outright, and that is a real outcome rather than a formality — the degraded-provider shape is sanctioned by the type's own docstring. Step (1) can also narrow it to near-nothing if augmented chains make the check substantially partial.
- **Council:** **No at registration** — the row is a question with no priced alternatives. **Conditionally yes at step (2)**, and only if step (1) finds the check can be made total: a bootstrap hard-fail trades fail-early configuration hygiene (C1/C9) against the degraded-provider local-deployment shape the docstring already sanctions (C11). Do not convene on the current thin state.

### B-123 · The tail-keep breaker trigger matches a **span name** while the breaker emits a span **event**, so the trigger may be inert *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C7 A2 consultant, registered adjacency 1), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 at the Leg-1 impl (PR #1279) — read this bullet first; everything below it is the REGISTRATION HISTORY, preserved verbatim and superseded where it conflicts.** The settled step-(2) repair is BUILT: `is_classification_trigger` now resolves the two §10.2 trigger names against the span **name** and, when the name does not match, against the names of the span's **events**, via a DERIVED two-member frozenset composed from the existing name constants so the span arm and the event arm cannot drift apart under a rename. The owed doc obligation is discharged — OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 term 3, which explicitly DECLINED to widen and named this row, is **replaced in full** at v1.39; plan leg v2.34 **U-OD-60** (twelve ACs). **§10.2 itself is NOT amended, and that is the point:** its table already specified the event carrier, so this was a conformance repair to cleared contract text, not a contestable spec direction, and nothing routed to the operator. **Admission-bounded** — per `B-137` the sibling tree is preserved only for head-ADMITTED carriers (~10% at base-rate 0.1, ~20% at 0.2); no full-floor claim is made. §10.2 row 1 stays `B-124`'s.
- **⚠ THE CLASS-3 RIDER BELOW IS FALSIFIED — do not carry it.** This row's own Class-3 informational bullet claims §10.2 row 1's cite (*"permanent-fail per ADR-D2 §1.8"*) does not resolve. **It does.** `design-substrate/ADR-D2.md` §1.8 is at line 301 and its table at lines 303–311 carries THREE columns — the second headed *"C5 fail-class"* — whose values include **`permanent-fail`** at `:305` (`escape_attempt`), `:306` (`egress_denied`) and `:309` (`signal`). The original claim was derived from the `sandbox.fail.class` value enum at `ADR-D2.md:285` alone and missed the fail-class column of the very table it cites. The rider was **NOT** carried into v1.39 or v2.34; the falsification is recorded at v1.39 §0.6 and plan §0.5, reached **independently at both legs** by separate direct reads.
- **A PD-8 probe changed the deliverable.** Deleting the event arm's own root-close materialize call left the first real-dispatch witness GREEN — exposing that the shape OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 term 5 says actually ships (*the dispatch carrier IS routinely the root close*) had NO real-dispatch coverage under the widened flag. A **second** witness was ADDED rather than the probe restated, and the re-run turns it RED. A further out-of-family [P2] (a doubled `span.events` read per buffered span, a regression this arc introduced) was taken and is witnessed by AC #11's `== 1` counting double.

- **What it is.** `is_classification_trigger` matches the §10.2 breaker trigger on the **span name**: `if name == BREAKER_TRIPPED_SPAN_NAME` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/tail_keep_classification.py:94-95` — **re-grounded at HEAD**; C7 cited `:92-93`, which at HEAD is the sibling `SANDBOX_VIOLATION_SPAN_NAME` arm). The real breaker emission is a span **event on a parent span**: `parent_span_ref.add_event(name="breaker.tripped", attributes=attributes)` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/harness_breaker_schema.py:282`, with the shape committed in the function docstring at `:236-243`). If no span is ever *named* `breaker.tripped`, the §10.2 trigger is inert on the dispatch path — and every claim about breaker-trip visibility at tail-sampled production surfaces is smaller than either `B-116` primary assumed.
- **C7 filed this as a PROBE, not a finding — preserved verbatim here.** His own words: *"I surface this as a probe, not a finding — it needs a positive-control run before anyone cites it."* That framing is load-bearing and is not upgraded by registration. The row exists so the probe is queued, not so the conclusion can be cited.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) RUN THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST.** Drive a real breaker trip through the tail-keep processor and observe whether the trace is preserved. Grep proves presence; only the run proves behaviour, and this row is entirely about behaviour. **(2) If inert, decide the repair** — match the event name as well as the span name, or emit a span so named. **(3) Widen the probe by one arm:** the identical span-name-only shape governs `sandbox.violation` (`tail_keep_classification.py:92-93`), so cover both rather than assuming the sibling is fine. **(4) Note the `B-116-t3` interaction:** C7's E2b argument for pinning `fallback.exhausted` to the §9.2 floor leaned on `head=1.0` **precisely because** the tail-keep mitigation might be inert. If this probe returns *the trigger fires*, t3's merits argument changes — it does not evaporate (a `head=1.0` guarantee does not depend on a trigger), but the row it rests on becomes weaker and should be re-stated rather than carried.
- **Council:** **No.** A probe with a binary answer and a named positive control. Convene nothing until it has run; if it returns *inert*, the repair is single-domain (C7 owns both the predicate and the emission shape).
- **Probe observation recorded at the `B-133` leg, 2026-08-08 — an OBSERVATION, not a closure; this row stays `registered_finding`.** The `B-133` positive control drove a REAL charging-fault dispatch to exhaustion through the REAL `TailKeepSpanProcessor` and observed the predicate directly on the carrying span: **`is_classification_trigger(span)` returned `False`** on the wrapper span `harness.runtime.retry_breaker_fallback` that carries the `breaker.tripped` **event**, and the trace's buffered siblings were consequently **dropped** at root close. **That answers this row's step (1) in the affirmative for the breaker arm: the §10.2 trigger is inert on the dispatch path.** It does **not** answer step (3) — the `sandbox.violation` sibling arm was not exercised — and it does not decide step (2)'s repair. OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 **term 3 deliberately declined** to widen `is_classification_trigger` to event names while closing the §9.2 half beside it, and U-OD-59's witness **W7 pins the boundary** (an event-carried `breaker.tripped` forwards its own carrier under the §9.2 floor but sets no keep flag), so widening it later is a deliberate, test-visible act rather than silent drift. C7's *"I surface this as a probe, not a finding"* framing is preserved: the probe has now **run for one of its two arms**, and the result is recorded so the conclusion can be cited **for that arm** — with the repair decision still owed.
- **GROUNDED 2026-08-08, PR #1277 (doc/register-only leg) — steps (3) and (4) ANSWERED, step (2) SETTLED. Row stays `registered_finding`; it closes at the Leg-1 impl.** *This bullet states the CURRENT result; the bullets above are superseded where they conflict.* **(3) The `sandbox.violation` arm — RESOLVED NEGATIVE; the sibling IS fine.** It is emitted as a **real span**, not an event: `tracer.start_as_current_span("sandbox.violation")` at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/runtime_tool_dispatcher.py:725` (inside `_emit_sandbox_violation`, `:707-728`). An **exhaustive** `add_event(` sweep over all seven `harness-*/src` trees returns exactly **six** sites — `harness_breaker_schema.py:282`, `alignment_floor_drift_detection.py:242`, `retry_breaker_fallback.py:749`/`:879`/`:1151`, `retry_breaker_tool.py:314` — and **none** is named `sandbox.violation`. So `tail_keep_classification.py:92-93` matches a name that is genuinely produced, and this row **narrows to the breaker arm alone**. **What is still broken after `B-133`, sharpened by direct read.** The landed §9.2.1 arm is `tail_keep_span_processor.py:364-388`: it forwards the carrier, then at `:376-377` calls `is_classification_trigger(span)` — which at `tail_keep_classification.py:91-95` matches **span names only**. The carrier is named `harness.runtime.retry_breaker_fallback`, so the predicate returns `False`, the per-trace keep flag is **never set**, and `:386-387` then calls `_materialize_trace_decision`, which at `:445-452` **drops** the buffer when `keep` is False. **Net effect: the trip's own carrier span survives (`B-133`'s delivery), but its entire sibling TREE is dropped at root close.** `B-133` changed *signal* delivery, not *tree* preservation. The code says so deliberately at `:369-375` and names this row as owner; U-OD-59's **W7** pins the boundary, so the debt is test-visible, not silent.
- **(2) The repair — SETTLED, and NOT an operator gate.** The §10.2 contract table at `design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_2.md:582-584` reads **verbatim** *"Parent + sibling spans of any `sandbox.violation` **event** preserved"* and *"…of any `breaker.tripped` **event** preserved"*. **The contract already says EVENT.** The name-only predicate is therefore **non-conformant to the contract as written**, and widening `is_classification_trigger` to scan `span.events` is a **conformance fix**, not a contestable direction — there is no genuine fork and nothing to route to the operator. Of the registration's two candidates, the **first** ("match the event name as well as the span name") is selected; the second mints a new emission primitive and is the X-AL-3 back-flow route `B-133` already refused as venue (b). **Shape + venue:** single-domain **C7/OD**; ~4 lines in `tail_keep_classification.py` reusing the `_carries_always_sampled_event` pattern (`tail_keep_span_processor.py:190-223`) but matched against the **two §10.2 names** rather than the §9.2 SSOT, plus the AC that the keep flag now sets for an event-carried trip, witnessed **by execution** through the real processor and a real exhausted dispatch. **One doc obligation rides it:** OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 **term 3** explicitly declined to widen and named this row, so the impl leg owes a small OD spec realization delta flipping term 3 plus an OD plan unit in the U-OD-58/U-OD-59 shape. **Realism caveat the leg must state rather than overclaim:** per `B-137`, **non-root** spans are head-starved (~**9%** preservation measured at base-rate 0.1 for a non-root `sandbox.violation` trigger), so the repair delivers the tree only for head-**admitted** carriers. Correct to build; must not be sold as a full floor.
- **(4) The `B-116-t3` restatement — one line, and the direction is the OPPOSITE of the one anticipated.** `B-116` is **closed** (#1271 + #1272). ### B-124 · `validator.fail.permanence` is never set on any span, so its OD §9.2 always-sampled row and its §10.2 tail-keep trigger are both inert *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C7 A2 consultant, registered adjacency 2), 2026-08-07)*

- **What it is.** Two live surfaces read this attribute. OD §9.2's always-sampled floor carries the row *"`validator.fail.*` at `validator.fail.permanence=permanent`"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_2.md:530`), realized in code at `harness-od/src/harness_od/sampling_mode.py:136`. `is_classification_trigger`'s §10.2 row-1 arm reads the same attribute (`tail_keep_classification.py:58` declares the key, `:99` compares it). The value is **derived** by `validator_fail_permanence(fail_class)` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_fail_taxonomy.py:169-176`) and declared in the CP schema at `:149`. But the function has **zero call sites** across `harness-{runtime,cp,od}/src`, and **nothing anywhere sets `"validator.fail.permanence"` as a span attribute** (searched at HEAD). Both rows are therefore inert on the dispatch path.
- **One refinement the council did not carry, added by direct read at HEAD.** There **is** exactly one structured carrier of the value: `ReplaySemanticDivergenceError.validator_fail_permanence: str = "permanent"` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/idempotency_join_dedup.py:361-368`, per §14.5.3). It is a frozen Pydantic record field, **not** an OTel span attribute — so neither the attribute-reading tail-keep predicate nor the always-sampled lookup can see it. The finding stands; its precise statement sharpens from *nothing carries the value* to **nothing carries it on a span**, which is what the two readers require.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** zero span-attribute set sites and that the derivation function still has no callers. **(2) Determine whether a validator-fail span or event is emitted at all on any live path.** If none is, this row is about a whole missing emission rather than one unset attribute, and it must be **re-scoped upward before it is priced** — fixing the attribute on a span that never opens is motion, not progress. **(3) If an emission exists,** wire the derived attribute at it and witness that the §9.2 always-sampled lookup and the §10.2 trigger both fire, by execution rather than by grep. **(4) Carry it as rider (c) of the `B-116-t3` leg**, per C7's own registration — t3 is the arc that opens OD §9.2, and touching the table twice is the waste to avoid.
- **What would falsify it.** An emission site existing on a path this search missed — the search covered `harness-{runtime,cp,od}/src` only.
- **Council:** **No.** Wiring a declared-but-unset attribute inside a cleared schema, with a named owner (C7/OD). The only judgement is step (2)'s scope question, which grounding answers rather than deliberation.
- **GROUNDED 2026-08-08, PR #1277 (doc/register-only leg) — THE ROW SPLITS; it is not one finding. Row stays `registered_finding`.** *This bullet states the CURRENT result; the bullets above are superseded where they conflict.* Rider (c) of `B-116-t3` is **retired as a routing** (step (4)): `B-116` closed at #1271 + #1272 and the t3 leg is gone, so the two halves route independently. **(1) Re-verified at HEAD `49591934` — both halves hold.** `validator_fail_permanence()` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_fail_taxonomy.py:169-176`) has **zero `src` callers** (only the definition, a docstring reference at `tail_keep_classification.py:60`, and three test assertions at `harness-cp/tests/test_validator_fail_taxonomy.py:76-83`); **no** span-attribute set site for `"validator.fail.permanence"` exists anywhere; the sole structured carrier remains `idempotency_join_dedup.py:366`. **(2) ANSWERED — an emission DOES exist, so the row does NOT re-scope upward; but the honest answer is sharper than the registration's binary.** A live `validator.evaluate` span is opened at `harness-cp/src/harness_cp/workflow_driver.py:5600`, attributes applied at `:5620-5622`, built at `harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_framework.py:320-352`, which on non-PASS sets **four** sibling `validator.fail.*` attributes at `:343-349` — `next_action`, `escalation_owed`, `class`, `detail_hash` — but **not** `permanence`. The registration's own falsifier ("an emission site existing on a path this search missed") **is met**: the search covered the derivation function and the attribute *name*, and missed the emission because the emission never names the attribute.
- **(3) The two readers do NOT share a fix — the load-bearing result.** **(A) The §10.2 half is CLOSEABLE.** `is_classification_trigger` reads the attribute off **any** span (`tail_keep_classification.py:96-100`), so setting `validator.fail.permanence` on the `validator.evaluate` span **would** make row 1 fire. **Owed at Leg 1, named — `pr: pending-leg-1`:** ~3 functional lines at `validator_framework.py:_build_span_attributes` deriving from `result.outcome` (`ValidatorOutcome.PERMANENT_FAIL → "permanent"`, else `"transient"`), witnessed **by execution** through the real `TailKeepSpanProcessor`, not by grep. **(B) The §9.2 half is NOT closeable by wiring the attribute and is RE-SCOPED FORWARD.** `is_always_sampled` resolves the `validator.fail.*` row against the span/event **NAME**, never against a carrier's attributes: `_conditional_always_sampled` gates on `event_name.startswith("validator.fail.")` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/sampling_mode.py:239-241`) and the literal / dot-anchored-prefix fallbacks (`:264-269`) also key on name. The live span is named `validator.evaluate`, so setting the attribute changes **nothing** there. Nor does `B-133`'s arm reach it — that arm resolves **event names** and this data is **attributes**. (A span named exactly `"validator.fail"`, the declared `SPAN_SITE_VALIDATOR_FAIL` at `harness-od/src/harness_od/validator_namespace.py:54`, would **also** miss: the derived prefix carries the dot anchor.) **This is a THIRD realization-mismatch shape — attribute-on-a-differently-named-span** — distinct from `B-133`'s (event-on-carrier) and `B-123`'s (event-vs-name at the §10.2 predicate). **The family is four rows, not three.** **Demand trigger for the §9.2 half:** any arc touching §9.2 **realization** (as opposed to membership) — the natural rider is `B-137`'s step-(3) posture decision, since candidates A/B/C all re-open how the floor resolves at the SDK boundary.

That collision is registered separately as **`B-138`**, and **`B-138` MUST be dispositioned BEFORE any arc touches `_build_span_attributes`** — including Leg 1's (A) above — because deriving permanence from `result.outcome` mints a *second* derivation from a *third* taxonomy on a function whose authoritative domain is itself unsettled.

This row now **owns the derivation sub-decision** (materialize the retry-exit classification at the emission site / ratify the narrowing WITH §21.6 re-specified / another carrier) and notes **`B-140`** (the `validator.fail` span-site gap) as ADJACENT, not gating: this row's §10.2 trigger reads the permanence ATTRIBUTE from any span, so the span-site gap gates the §9.2-style NAME-keying family (`B-123`/`B-133`/`B-137`), not this half (codex round-3 venue correction).
- **OPERATOR RATIFICATION 2026-08-16 — Reading A (materialize the retry-exit classification at the emission site).** Selected via `AskUserQuestion`; **discharges** the Class 2 fork filed at PR #1283 and makes the row **buildable**. **The fork recommended Reading D** (defer with a demand trigger) at `[MODERATE]`, resting on its §3(iv) — that the §9.2 half is the more valuable of the two and does not depend on the derivation landing now. **The operator selected A.** Recorded as provenance, not dissent: the recommendation was MODERATE and argued only that the derivation could *wait*, and Reading A is the direct repair that deferral was deferring. **Do not re-litigate it.** **What A commits:** derive the classification **at the emission site**, so `validator.fail.permanence` exists as something the sampling surfaces can read. ### B-125 · `harness.breaker.tool_id` is a homonym-in-waiting: it echoes the breaker **key** at every shipped trip while its contract gloss promises a **tool identity** *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C7 A2 -> C11 cross-read falsification -> C7 E2b withdrawal), 2026-08-07)*

- **What it is.** The attribute is declared at OD §7.1 as *"Specific tool ID the failures correlate with (when scope is per-model and failures correlate with a specific tool)"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:43`) and at CP §3.5 as *"per-model scope correlation"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:402`); it sits in the nine-member `HARNESS_BREAKER_ATTRIBUTES` tuple at `harness-od/src/harness_od/harness_breaker_schema.py:98` (**re-grounded at HEAD** — C7 cited `:101`, which at HEAD is `harness.breaker.cooldown_ms`). What it actually carries is the **breaker key**: `RetryBreakerRegistry.emit_breaker_transition_event` sets `effective_tool_id = transition.identifier` whenever `tool_id is None` at `PER_MODEL` scope (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker.py:459-461`), with the default stated as contract in the docstring (`:445-446`). Since `PER_MODEL` is the only scope constructed (`B-119`), **every** shipped trip emits `harness.breaker.tool_id = "provider:model"`.
- **The correction chain, recorded because it is the row's whole substance.** C7 proposed at A2 populating the attribute with a real tool id to discriminate a memory-tool trip, on the claim it is *"never populated"* and that `BreakerTransition` has no such field. `BreakerTransition` indeed has no field (`retry_breaker.py:183-189`) — but the **registry supplies the default**, so the wire value is populated. C11 falsified the claim at cross-read by direct read of `:459-461`; C7 **formally withdrew** it at E2b: *"My A2 claim that `harness.breaker.tool_id` is 'never populated' is FALSE and I withdraw it."* The consequence C11 drew and C7 adopted **against his own proposal**: populating it with a real tool id makes one attribute carry two domains — tool identity at one call site, breaker-key echo at every other — discriminable only by string shape. That is exactly the cross-namespace homonym C7 had just **refused** for `capability_shortfall` (`harness_breaker_schema.py:141-143`).
- **Why it is registered rather than repaired.** C7 **declined the repair rather than pricing it**, on his own `B-131` standard: *the skip must demote the detail, never delete it* — and suppressing the `:459-461` default would **delete** the only populated meaning the attribute has at every shipped `PER_MODEL` trip. He also recorded the full price had he taken it: the default removal, the `:442-446` contract docstring, every witness asserting the default, and a re-read of CP §3.5's *"per-model scope correlation"* gloss. It is moot for `B-116`'s member #5 (conceded — there is no #5 trip left to discriminate) and **not owed** for the members that still trip, because `harness.breaker.cause` is populated at all three real `record_failure()` sites (`retry_breaker.py:451-453`, B-38), so those trips are already discriminated.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** the default and that `PER_MODEL` is still the only constructed scope — this couples to `B-119`, since building `PER_PROVIDER` changes which trips receive the default at all. **(2) Decide the disposition BEFORE any caller passes a real `tool_id`:** **(a)** keep the breaker-key echo and forbid real tool ids on this attribute — in which case the OD §7.1 and CP §3.5 glosses are wrong as written and owe a correction; or **(b)** suppress the default and mint a separate attribute for the key echo, at C7's enumerated price above. **(3) The trigger is a caller passing a real tool id** — that is the moment the homonym goes live and the attribute becomes uninterpretable without a string-shape heuristic. This row must be dispositioned *before* that, not after.
- **Council:** **No.** An attribute-domain call owned by C7/OD, already argued to a conclusion in venue by two voices including a formal withdrawal. What remains is choosing (a) or (b) and paying for it.
- **CLOSED — 2026-08-08, PR #1277 (doc/register-only leg). DISPOSITION (a): keep the breaker-key echo, FORBID real tool ids, DECLARE the bound** — the `B-101` **(b)-PLUS** declared-bound shape ratified at Runtime v1.114. **No shipped behaviour changes.** *This bullet states the CURRENT result; the bullets above are superseded where they conflict.* **(1) Re-verified at HEAD `49591934`, with a line-drift correction.** `B-118` (#1275) **moved** the default: it is now `retry_breaker.py:626-628` (`effective_tool_id = tool_id` at `:626`; the `PER_MODEL` scope guard at `:627`; `= transition.identifier` at `:628`), and the contract docstring is now `:609-612`. The registration's `:459-461` / `:445-446` are **stale cites, not falsified findings** — the mechanism is byte-identical. The attribute still sits at `harness_breaker_schema.py:98`. `PER_MODEL` is still the only constructed scope (`B-119`, closed at this same leg as a forward-only record), so **every** shipped trip carries `harness.breaker.tool_id = "provider:model"`.
- **Two grounded facts that change the calculus.** **(i) The trigger is architecturally distant, not imminent.** Step (3) names it as *"a caller passing a real tool id"*. At HEAD there is exactly **one** production caller — `_emit_breaker_transition` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:1477-1482`) — and it passes **no** `tool_id`. The composer that would supply one **does not participate at all**: `retry_breaker_tool.py:152-153` states *"per Q1a=(i) ratification, `get_breaker` / breaker transition events are NOT invoked at v1.15"*. A real tool id can arrive only **after** a tool-scope breaker lands — a separate, explicitly-ratified-as-absent surface. **The homonym cannot go live by accident.** **(ii) C7's enumerated price for option (b) is overstated at HEAD, falsified by count.** *"Every witness asserting the default"* is **one** test — `harness-runtime/tests/test_lifecycle_retry_breaker.py:583-604` — and it asserts only `emission.attribute_count == 8`, **never the value**. The only other occurrences in tests are attribute-**name** list assertions (`harness-od/tests/test_harness_breaker_schema.py:33`, `harness-cp/tests/test_retry_fallback_namespace.py:49`). (That witness constructs the breaker with identifier `"search-tool"` — a tool-shaped key at `PER_MODEL` scope, the homonym in miniature.) **The price correction does not flip the disposition:** C7's substantive objection — that suppressing the default **deletes** the only populated meaning the attribute has at every shipped trip, violating his own `B-131` *"demote the detail, never delete it"* standard — stands unchanged and is what decides it.
- **The promotion trigger (falsifiable, one disjunct).** The **first** caller passing a non-`None` `tool_id` to `emit_breaker_transition_event`. That is the instant the attribute carries two domains discriminable only by string shape, and it **re-opens this row to disposition (b)** — suppress the default, mint a separate attribute for the key echo — at the (now measured) price above. A second, weaker trigger is `B-119`'s: constructing `PER_PROVIDER` changes which trips receive the default at all. **`B-119`'s step (5) is therefore discharged here.**
- **The owed gloss corrections — carried as a NAMED RIDER rather than applied** (the #1263 stale-prose-carrier rider precedent). Under (a) the two contract glosses are **wrong as written**; this leg deliberately does **not** correct them because it edits no `design-substrate/` file. **(1)** OD §7.1 *"Specific tool ID the failures correlate with (when scope is per-model and failures correlate with a specific tool)"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:43`) — owed correction: the shipped meaning is the **breaker key** (`"provider:model"`); a real tool id is forbidden until the promotion trigger fires. **(2)** CP §3.5 *"`harness.breaker.tool_id` (string; per-model scope correlation)"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:402`) — same. **Rider owner:** the **next** OD or CP spec delta that opens §7.1 or §3.5 respectively MUST carry these; they are **not** a standalone arc. The code-side docstring at `retry_breaker.py:609-612` already states the default as contract and needs no change.

### B-126 · The `retry.*` namespace has three different cardinalities (manifest 4, code 6, wire 8 after `B-116`) and only the first is verified *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C7 A2 consultant, registered adjacency 3), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 (#1289)** — built, and **this row's own framing was falsified in the process.** The three-cardinality structure holds and the corrected wire count of **TEN** is confirmed by two independent sweep shapes (a broad literal sweep and an AST emission-position sweep, both over `harness-*/src`, both returning exactly 10 distinct `retry.`-prefixed **attribute** keys = 5 declared at `C-CP-03 §3.5` + 5 undeclared). **But the discretion-lane premise is wrong**: of the 5 keys beyond §3.5, only `retry.skipped.candidate` rides pure telemetry-volume discretion — the other four are **mandated by name** at `Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md:4217` (§14.6 step 4), `:4364` (§14.6.3 t1+t2), and `:4227-4230` + `:5684-5687`. So `retry.*` is declared at **two contract venues** and the `C-CP-24 §24.1` manifest counts only one; it is not four declared keys plus a free-for-all. **Step (2) is answered as the re-grounding said** — the lane IS unbounded (`:4279`, `:5729` state no cap) — so what shipped is a **REGISTER, not a cap**: a new key is permitted, but not *invisibly*. Built: `RETRY_WIRE_REGISTER` (7 rows) + `RETRY_SPAN_AND_EVENT_NAMES` (3) at `harness-cp/src/harness_cp/retry_fallback_namespace.py`, count-language corrections at `cp_namespace_export_manifest.py` **and** the cross-axis-facing `cp_cross_axis_composition_manifest.py:118`, and **17 drift-catching tests / 29 assertions** at `harness-cp/tests/test_b126_retry_wire_register.py`, each load-bearing line shown RED under a mutation probe *(recounted programmatically at the arc close — an earlier "10" here and a contradictory "8" in the YAML were round-1/round-3 leftovers, caught by the merge gate)*. **ZERO** cardinality bump / §3.5 amendment / contract number / plan leg / design-substrate edit. **Two new findings registered rather than absorbed:** `B-144` (§24.1.B's count column was never re-tabled after §3.5's two amendments, and the code manifest resolves the divergence *inconsistently per row*) and `B-145` (`retry.backoff_ms` + `retry.cause_class` have zero producers; the mandated `retry.terminal = "escalate"` value is never emitted, collapsed into `max-attempts`). A **third** stale figure fixed in place: the manifest claimed a 63-attribute sum while the derived constant is **65**, misattributed to the wrong sub-table. **The close-out steps below are PRESERVED AS HISTORY and are `[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-09]` — do not action them.**

- **Re-grounded 2026-08-09 (#1285, batch pass) — SHARPENED, and this row's own count is wrong.** The three-cardinalities structure holds, but the wire figure UNDERCOUNTS: an exhaustive literal sweep of `harness-*/src` returns **five** undeclared keys, not four — the missed one is `retry.terminal` (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:1253`), which `git log -S` shows landed at **#1065**, *before* the council that filed this row. Corrected total: **ten** distinct wire keys, not eight. Step (2) is answered by the spec rather than open — Runtime §14.6's discretion bullet (`Spec_Harness_Runtime_v1.md:4279`) states no cap, so the lane is intentionally unbounded and this is manifest-conformance, not a fork. **Shape: BUILD-NOW.**

The **code-side** `RETRY_NAMESPACE_SCHEMA` already carries **six** (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/retry_fallback_namespace.py:168-207`, whose own docstring records *"v2.3 amendment from 4"*; the contract re-table is `design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_3.md:76`, against the four-attribute v1.2 row at `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:403`). On top of that, the shipped `retry.skipped.reason` / `retry.skipped.candidate` pair (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:678-679`) rides the `retry.*` namespace **outside any §3.5 declaration**.

C7's point is that this is **precedent, and precedent accumulates**: `B-116`'s ratified terms **t1+t2** add two more undeclared `retry.*` attributes (`retry.breaker_waived.reason` / `.candidate`), which he required be *"filed alongside"* the existing pair rather than silently added. - **Close-out steps.** **(1) Recount all three at the then-current HEAD** — these drift every arc, so a stale count is worse than none. **(2) Decide whether the discretion lane has a boundary.** If it does not, say so in the contract: an unbounded lane means the pinned `attribute_count=4` is not a cardinality guarantee about the *namespace*, only about the *declared subset*, and the 63-sum acceptance means less than it reads. Reading this row as a veto would invert its author's own position.
- **Council:** **No at registration** — nothing is decided until the recount. **Conditionally yes at step (2)** if it leans toward closing the lane, which trades emission-site observability freedom (C7) against the cardinality and cost guarantees the pinned manifest exists to give (C2/C6). Do not convene before the recount, per the workspace probe-first discipline.

### B-127 · The breaker-open advance passes no `exhaustion_cause`, so an all-breakers-open chain reports **retry** exhaustion when no attempt ran *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C1 A2 consultant, standing observability pre-check), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 (#1287), paired with `B-131`.** The skip branch now passes `exhaustion_cause=skip_reason`, so an all-breakers-open chain reports the actual terminal cause. **Passed through, not hard-coded, and that is load-bearing:** `skip_reason` takes TWO values here — `breaker-open` and `half-open-trial-in-flight` (the second added by `B-118`) — so a hard-coded literal would mislabel every half-open skip. A dedicated witness exists for that exact mutation and probe **P2** turns it RED. Three witnesses (the all-open chain with **zero** inner dispatches; a discriminator keeping ordinary retry exhaustion at its default; and the half-open variant built on a **real** event-gated concurrent trial). `_advance_or_exhaust`'s signature and default are unchanged.

- **Re-grounded 2026-08-09 (#1285) — INTACT, confirmed BY EXECUTION.** A probe tripped both candidates' breakers OPEN with cooldown unexpired: **zero** inner provider calls, skip reasons `[breaker-open, breaker-open]`, and `fallback.exhaustion_cause = per-candidate-retry-exhaustion`. A chain where no attempt ever ran reports retry exhaustion. Step (2) settled empirically: `fallback.exhaustion_cause` is declared in **no** spec (zero hits) — a free `str` with its own hyphenated vocabulary, so the fix is a matching literal, NOT reuse of the underscored CP enum. **Shape: BUILD-NOW** — one keyword argument at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:888-895`. **Land together with `B-131`** (same call site, different attributes; neither fix resolves the other).

- **What it is.** `_advance_or_exhaust` takes `exhaustion_cause: str = "per-candidate-retry-exhaustion"` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:866`) and writes it onto the terminal `fallback.exhausted` event as `fallback.exhaustion_cause` (`:891`, in the attribute dict at `:888-897`). The capability-shortfall pre-check passes `exhaustion_cause="capability-shortfall"` **explicitly** (`:656`), and the method's own docstring states why: *"so an all-candidates-incapable chain is not mis-classified as retry exhaustion (no provider attempt ran in that case)"* (`:874-876`). The breaker-open pre-check, twenty-eight lines below the shortfall one, passes **no** `exhaustion_cause` (`:684-691`) and therefore takes the default. So an all-breakers-open chain exhaustion is reported as **retry** exhaustion — the identical mis-classification the sibling path was written to prevent, on the identical premise (no attempt ran).
- **Scope and ownership as the voice left it.** C1 surfaced this as an adjacency he *"did not see filed"*, one line away from C11's `:683` row (`B-131`), and routed the **value** to C7/OD while keeping only the naming: *"I own naming that the topology emits the wrong-shaped terminal event."* He explicitly registered it rather than folding it into `B-116`'s diff. It fires under **either** `B-116` reading, and after ratification it still fires for the members that keep counting.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** the default, both call sites, and that `fallback.exhaustion_cause` is written **unconditionally** — unlike its sibling `fallback.last_failure_detail`, which is written only `if last_failure_detail is not None` (`:893-894`; that asymmetry is `B-131`). **(2) Select rather than mint, if possible:** `FallThroughCause.BREAKER_OPEN` already exists byte-exact in the closed CP §3.5 `fallback.cause` domain (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/fall_through_procedure.py:67-68`; `design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:401`). But `fallback.cause` and `fallback.exhaustion_cause` are **different attributes**, and the value domains must be checked before reuse — the same homonym discipline C7 applied when refusing `capability_shortfall`. **(3) Pass it** at `:684-691`. **(4) Witness both** — a breaker-open exhaustion carrying the new value, and a per-candidate retry exhaustion still carrying the default, so the fix is discriminating rather than blanket.
- **Price, stated because it is itself the argument.** One keyword argument at one call site, plus a value decision. The sibling path is the shipped precedent for both the fix and its rationale. A defect this cheap to close is one to close rather than carry.
- **Council:** **No.** A one-value fix inside a closed, declared domain with a shipped sibling precedent and a named value owner. Route to C7 plus `advisor()` if step (2)'s reuse question is contested.

### B-128 · The dispatcher borrows the validator-side `PERMANENT_FAIL_EXIT` label while performing none of the escalation that label routes to *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C1 A2 consultant, HITL pre-check), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 (#1285) as a forward-only record — read this first.** The premise is intact, but this row's **own falsifier was run and does not fire**: close-out step (1) demanded an enumeration of `retry.fail_class` readers, and it returns **six** hits — five producers, and one consumer-shaped reference (`per_class_attribute_composition.py:209`) that is a **presence-only** tail-sampling trigger. Nothing branches control flow on the value. The row states its own disposition for exactly this result (*"the row is documentation-shaped, and that is the honest outcome to record rather than a reason to build"*), and is closed on that instruction. **Demand trigger:** any future reader that branches on the VALUE.

- **What it is.** The fail-fast branch tags the inner attempt span `retry.fail_class = ValidatorRetryExitClass.PERMANENT_FAIL_EXIT.value` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:1024-1027`). C-CP-21 §21.1's five-class fail taxonomy routes `permanent-fail-exit` as *"SKIP STAIRCASE; route directly to C11 HITL (validator-escalation placement per §17.1)"* (`design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:1852`, in the §21.1 table at `:1843-1853`). But that taxonomy is **validator**-side: the dispatcher borrows the label for a span attribute while the exception propagates to a plain step failure — `workflow_driver.py:5564-5572` returns `RunStatus.FAILED` with a `terminal_step_index`, and no HITL invocation occurs. C1's statement: **the escalation the attribute names is not the escalation the topology performs.**
- **The operative warning, which is why it is a row and not a footnote.** C1 flagged it [MODERATE], declared it *"not this fork's business"*, and attached the reason it must still be recorded: the label *"must not be quietly used as evidence that an escalation path exists."* That is a stale-carry hazard aimed at future readers of the span attribute, not at `B-116`.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Enumerate producers and consumers first.** Every producer of `retry.fail_class = permanent-fail-exit` and — the load-bearing half — every consumer that reads the class as a **routing** signal rather than as telemetry. The divergence only bites where such a consumer exists. **If there is none, the row is documentation-shaped, and that is the honest outcome to record rather than a reason to build.** **(2) Then decide:** either the dispatcher stops borrowing the validator label (a new dispatch-side value in the `retry.fail_class` enum — a closed-domain extension against a C5/C7-owned vocabulary, expensive), or the contract records that `retry.fail_class` and `validator.fail.class` share a vocabulary but not a routing (cheap, and matches what the code does today). **(3) Do NOT resolve it by wiring the HITL escalation.** No voice proposed that, C1 and C11 concurred independently that no gate belongs on this path, and `B-116` ratified term **t5** (no HITL gate here). A fix that adds one would contradict a ratified term.
- **What would falsify it.** A consumer that **routes** on the dispatcher-set value would upgrade this from a labelling note to a live defect — that is the single check step (1) exists to run.
- **Council:** **No at registration.** **Conditionally yes at step (2)** only if the enum-extension branch is chosen, which touches a closed C5/C7-owned domain and trades vocabulary precision against domain closure — and only after step (1) shows a routing consumer exists.

### B-129 · The memory-tool argument-shape degradation signal has no vocabulary home after `B-116` demoted it off the breaker *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C1 A2 consultant; conceded by C9, conditioned by C11), 2026-08-07)*

- **Re-grounded 2026-08-09 (#1285) — INTACT, and one of its two stated obstacles is already gone.** The row worries (step 5) that its own preferred placement lands on a base-rate-only surface *"dropped nine times in ten"*, leaving C11's condition unmet. **That worry is stale:** the OD-side ingestion gap was closed by the landed `B-116-t3` leg, and `fallback.exhausted` is now row 19 of the §9.2 always-sampled roster (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_38.md:78`) — so C11's condition is already satisfied and the placement is cheaper than the row assumes. **Shape: DEFER-WITH-TRIGGER** — step (2) remains a measurement question a read-only pass cannot answer.

- **What it is.** `B-116` ratified member #5 (`MemoryToolExecutionInputError`) as **don't-count** — but C9's substantive point survived his own concession: a model that repeatedly cannot emit the declared memory-tool argument shape **is information**, and reading (II) orphans it. The signal is real at the raise site: `llm_dispatch.py:4376-4383` validates the **model-supplied** `scope_ref`, and the in-file comment at `:4362-4367` explicitly distinguishes it from the two harness-internal sibling checks immediately above (`:4368-4375`), which the B-88 A-ii re-typing moved to `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError`. What is missing is a **home** for the signal.
- **Where the type system points, per C1.** The only `BreakerCause` that would fit is `capability_shortfall`, whose in-code scope **explicitly disclaims** exactly this use — *"names a separate, out-of-scope cross-family fallback-exhaustion path, not a per-step dispatch failure"* (`harness-od/src/harness_od/harness_breaker_schema.py:141-143`, mirroring OD §7.1's forward-slot note at `design-substrate/Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_32.md:50`). Meanwhile `FallThroughCause.CAPABILITY_SHORTFALL` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/fall_through_procedure.py:64-65`) **is** the per-dispatch chain-advance vocabulary. C1: *"the type system is pointing at the fall-through path, not the counter"* — and he declined to author a value, because `FallThroughCause` is **closed at 4** and its own docstring names extension *"a Workflow §4.1.2 Class-2 D-revision"* (`:52-58`), with the domain CP-declared at `design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md:401`.
- **Stated against interest.** C9 accepted the placement while naming exactly what it costs him: *"be honest about what it gives my domain: a **registered home, not a live signal**. I accept that trade only because the alternative live signal is a corrupted counter."* C11 accepted it **conditional** on the `B-116` t3 sampling term, since a signal relocated from an inviolable §9.2 floor to a base-rate surface is dropped nine times in ten at `team-binding × self-hosted`.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** both enums' scoping text and the closed-at-4 cardinality. **(2) Decide whether a fall-through value is warranted at all — and note this requires a POPULATION question, not a code read.** Does the shape actually recur in practice? That cannot be answered from the source, so the honest first step is **measurement**, not a mint. **(3) If warranted, route the extension as the Class-2 D-revision the enum's own docstring names** (C5/C7/OD own the value) — a spec leg, not an impl leg. **(4) Choose the producer site deliberately:** `B-116`'s guard means #5 no longer reaches `record_failure` at all, so the emission must be placed on the fall-through path itself, not inherited from the old one. **(5) Note the `B-116-t3` coupling** — C11's acceptance is conditioned on the sampling guarantee, so landing a value onto a base-rate-only surface satisfies C1's placement while failing C11's condition.
- **Council:** **No at registration.** **Conditionally yes at step (3):** extending a closed, CP-declared domain to carry a reliability signal is the C9 ⊥ C7 tension (signal fidelity versus vocabulary closure) the deliberation already surfaced once and resolved by refusal. Convene only **after** step (2) produces a measured population — convening on an unmeasured one would repeat the mistake the probe-first discipline exists to prevent.

### B-130 · All-candidates-permanently-ineligible is a reachable terminal state no canonical artifact declares *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C1 A2 consultant), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 (#1285) as a forward-only record — read this first. The row is PARTIALLY FALSIFIED, and its own step (4) anticipated it.** Claim A (a zero-attempt exhaustion is reachable) is **still true** and was reproduced by execution — `inner.calls == 0`, three `retry.skipped`, `chain_length == 3`. Claim B (that this is **permanent/irreversible**) is **FALSE at HEAD**: `B-118` landed, and the same repro extended past the cooldown window **recovered** — `OPEN → half_open → closed` on a successful trial, dispatch returning normally. The state is **bounded and self-healing**, not an irreversible candidate-set deletion — a circuit breaker working as designed for a genuinely-down provider set. The negative claim was still enumerated and holds, but no new terminal-state enum is warranted; the one useful residual (making zero-attempt exhaustion distinguishable in telemetry) is already `B-127`'s. **Demand trigger:** any arc weakening cooldown-based half-open recovery.

- **What it is.** The breaker pre-check at `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:674-683` is not telemetry — it is a **topology gate** that deletes a candidate slot from the chain. Combined with `B-118` (`OPEN` is absorbing for the process lifetime), a trip is an **irreversible candidate-set deletion**. C1's end state: a declared N-candidate fallback chain that has silently become a **null topology** — every subsequent dispatch walks N slots, emits N `retry.skipped` events (`:675-681`), does zero work, and exhausts. What the design **does** declare, both verified at HEAD: candidate exhaustion *within* a dispatch (`RetryBreakerFallbackExhaustedError`, `:899`) and first terminal step failure *within* a run (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/workflow_driver.py:5564-5572`, `RunStatus.FAILED` plus `terminal_step_index`). *"All candidates permanently ineligible"* is neither.
- **The amplifier neither primary named.** `_advance_or_exhaust` is a **multiplier**: one candidate-independent fault is charged N times per dispatch, N = chain length (`B-116`'s executed Probe B: three breakers, one dispatch). So **lengthening the fallback chain to improve resilience makes the harm strictly worse and trips the whole chain sooner** — a topology decision inverting into a reliability regression. Scope after ratification, stated so the row is not read as larger than it is: `B-116`'s guard removes the four harness-internal members from the multiplier, so the shape narrows to the members that still count. It does not disappear.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify** the two declared terminations and that no third exists. **(2) Decide whether the state needs naming at all — and weigh C1's own three-level bound, which argues it may not:** `max_attempts=3` within a candidate (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:130-134`), chain length then `:899` within a dispatch, and first-failed-step termination within a run (`workflow_driver.py:5564-5572`), with the other topologies bounded too (evaluator-optimizer caps at `_DEFAULT_EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER_MAX_ITERATIONS = 3`, `workflow_driver.py:10555`). For a candidate-independent fault the bound is **one step per run**, which is the honest argument for leaving the state undeclared. **(3) If it is declared, do not mint twice** — the natural carrier is the `fallback.exhaustion_cause` value `B-127` is already about. **(4) SEQUENCE `B-118` FIRST:** wiring the half-open latch stops `OPEN` being absorbing, which weakens this row's premise substantially and may retire it.
- **Council:** **No at registration.** A C1-domain termination-criterion question with C9's mechanism underneath (T-perm-3, C1 ⊥ C9, fires literally here — the breaker is a reliability primitive performing an irreversible topology edit, and C1 asked that it be recorded as such on the row). But C1 argued both halves in venue and the probe-first answer — the driver's own terminality — is grounded at HEAD. Re-convene only if step (2) leans toward declaring a new terminal state.

### B-131 · The breaker-open skip **deletes** the prior candidate's failure detail instead of demoting it, so a chain exhaustion reports no cause at all *(surfaced at the B-116 council deliberation (C11 A1 primary (c), reframed by C7 A2, re-grounded by C11 at cross-read), 2026-08-07)*

- **CLOSED 2026-08-09 (#1287), paired with `B-127`** — same call site, different attributes of the same event, neither fix resolving the other. A skip no longer clobbers a real candidate diagnostic: the unconditional overwrite is gated on a new `last_failure_is_real_attempt` flag. **The flag shape was chosen over a `None`-check deliberately:** a chain can take consecutive skips with *different* reasons, which must keep overwriting each other — a `None`-check would have frozen the FIRST skip reason instead of the last, silently breaking pre-existing behaviour. The row's own sub-claim was corrected at grounding: the class never fell through to `"unknown"`; it carried a **real-but-wrong** value, worse because it looks legitimate. Probes **P3** and **P4** turn the two witnesses RED respectively.

- **Re-grounded 2026-08-09 (#1285) — INTACT in mechanism, SHARPENED in one sub-claim, reproduced by execution.** The row's own step-(4) scenario was run: candidate 0 fails with a real diagnostic, candidate 1 is breaker-open-skipped, and `fallback.exhausted` carries `last_failure_class: breaker-open` with `fallback.last_failure_detail` **absent entirely**. **The sharpening:** the row says `last_failure_class` falls through to the literal `"unknown"`. It does not — it is SET to the skip reason, which is truthy, so the `or "unknown"` fallback never fires. The attribute is overwritten with a **real-but-wrong** value that masks the actual failure class, which is worse than `"unknown"` because it looks legitimate. Witness gap confirmed: no existing test exercises the multi-candidate erasure. **Shape: BUILD-NOW** — first-write-wins retention; **land with `B-127`.**

- **What it is.** **Before** the breakers open, the operator's terminal is correct and loud: `_failure_detail` composes `"<Type>: <message>"` bounded (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:178-187`), `RetryBreakerFallbackExhaustedError.__init__` appends it as *"; last failure: ..."* (`:169-175`), `_step_fail_class` interpolates `str(exc)` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/workflow_driver.py:1686-1687`), and the CLI echoes it to stderr (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/cli/app.py:141-143` and `:243-244`). **After** a breaker opens, the pre-check sets `last_failure_class = "breaker-open"` and `last_failure_detail = None` (`:682-683`) — and the exhausted event writes the detail attribute **only** `if last_failure_detail is not None` (`:893-894`). So the overwrite does not set the field to `None`: it makes `fallback.last_failure_detail` **vanish from the event entirely**, while `fallback.last_failure_class` falls through to the literal `"unknown"` (`:890`). Within **one** dispatch, candidate 1's real fail-fast detail (set at `:998`) is destroyed by candidate 2's **skip**.
- **The mechanism, in C7's framing which C11 adopted verbatim.** *"A strictly-information-destroying write by a path that learned nothing"* — a monotonicity violation on a last-write-wins diagnostic slot. **The skip must demote the detail, never delete it.** C11 adopted that as the row's title at cross-read. It fires under **either** `B-116` reading, for the members that still count — i.e. genuine provider outages arrive at the operator as *"chain exhausted, no reason given"*. There is no compensating surface: **zero** `breaker` hits across `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/cli/` (three files, re-verified at HEAD), so no operator-facing breaker readout exists to cite in either direction.
- **The correction carried, not laundered.** C11's A1 additionally called `retry.skipped.reason = "breaker-open"` **false**. C7 refused that half — *"it is a proximate-mechanism statement about why THIS candidate was skipped, and the breaker WAS open; calling a true attribute false weakens the row"* — and C11 **conceded and withdrew the sentence** at cross-read. **This row therefore does not rest on any truth-value claim about `retry.skipped.reason`.** It rests on the erasure mechanism, which C11 then grounded more sharply than either voice had written it.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-verify the erasure chain** — `:682-683`, `:890`, `:893-894`, `:998`. **(2) Implement demotion rather than deletion:** preserve the prior candidate's detail (and class) across a skip instead of overwriting, or carry the skip as an **additional** fact alongside the retained detail. The open choice is the retention shape — first-write-wins, a list, or a two-field split — not whether to retain. **(3) Respect the `B-116` adjacency:** `B-116`'s binding term (C11's (a)) already requires the **non-counted** fault to keep carrying `type(exc).__name__` and the bounded message on `last_failure_detail` at `:1031-1035`. This row and that guard touch adjacent lines and must not fight; land them in a known order. **(4) Witness the multi-candidate case specifically** — candidate 1 fails with a real detail, candidate 2 is skipped breaker-open, and the `fallback.exhausted` event must still carry candidate 1's detail. A single-candidate test cannot see this defect. **(5) Note `B-127`** — the same terminal event's `exhaustion_cause` is mislabelled on the same path; the two are one event apart and should be priced together.
- **What would falsify it.** Nothing found. Two voices grounded the mechanism independently at HEAD, and the one contested claim was withdrawn by its author rather than carried.
- **Council:** **No.** C7 (attribute and schema owner) and C11 (operator surface) converged in venue on both the mechanism and the framing, including one concession in each direction. What remains is choosing the retention shape — a single-domain implementation judgement.

### B-132 · The classifier catch-all routes harness-side memory subtypes to the staircase, where they charge the breaker at escalation/exhaustion *(surfaced at the B-116 spec leg, fresh-context review round, 2026-08-08; **NARROWED — not closed — at the `B-115` (b′) leg, which removed the deterministic ledger-refusal population**)*

- **Re-grounded 2026-08-09 (#1285) — INTACT, corroborated by the shipped code's own comments.** Verified by direct classifier calls, not grep: `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError` and `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError` both → `transient-retry`, **not waived**; `MemoryToolExecutionLedgerConflictError` → waived (the `B-115` split, confirmed live). **What precisely remains after that narrowing: exactly TWO members** — the denied subtype, and the store subtype minus the ledger-conflict slice (now exclusively disk-full / permission / other genuinely-transient I/O). Both still charge the **provider-model** breaker for a candidate-independent harness-local fault. **Shape: FORK-SHAPED** — either a finer split on the wrapped exception's own type (the `B-115` precedent), or a staircase-side waiver that **reopens the `B-116` C1/C9 ⊥ C11 dyad**. The hard part is untouched: discriminating transient store I/O from a persistent local fault without message-sniffing.

- **What it is.** `_classify_provider_exception`'s terminal arm (`retry_breaker_fallback.py:371`) maps EVERY unlisted `Exception` subclass to `TRANSIENT_RETRY` — deliberately, per its own docstring, treating unknown faults as transient until proven otherwise. `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError` and `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError` — siblings of the two WAIVED memory types under the same family base — fall to that catch-all, travel the retry staircase, and charge the provider-model breaker at both staircase `record_failure` charge sites (`:1072`, `:1091` at HEAD). Under the `B-116` ratified normative test, a DETERMINISTIC policy denial or a local durable-store write failure charging the breaker is a residual — the same defect shape `B-116` closed at the fail-fast site, alive on the staircase path.
- **Why a residual, not a miss.** The council's ratified scope binds the fail-fast site only, and the classifier's exclusion of the denied class from fail-fast is itself deliberate and documented (its raise sites read mutable index/store state and it WRAPS genuinely transient store I/O — the docstring's own grounds at `:343-349`; wholesale fail-fasting it would kill retries for real flakes). The residual was stated as a FALSE universal (*"every other path passes the test by construction"*) in the first drafting of spec §14.6.3; the fresh-context review round falsified it by direct read, and the spec now declares the residual and cites this row.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1)** Re-verify the catch-all membership and the two staircase charge sites at the then-current HEAD. **(2)** Decide PER-SUBTYPE whether a finer classification is owed: a class that wraps genuinely transient I/O cannot be wholesale fail-fasted, so any fix is a finer split — discriminating persistent policy denial from wrapped transient I/O (e.g. on the wrapped exception's own type), or a staircase-side waiver at the exhaustion charge for instances that fail the recovery-model test. **(3)** Any change routes through the `B-116` normative test PER-MEMBER, per the §14.6.3 discipline. **What would falsify it:** the catch-all arm gaining member-specific handling for the denied/store subtypes, or an operator decision recording the staircase charge as accepted behaviour.
- **NARROWED at the `B-115` (b′) leg, 2026-08-08 — not closed, and the distinction is load-bearing.** That leg SPLIT the deterministic ledger divergent-replay refusal out of `MemoryToolExecutionStoreError` into a new sibling `MemoryToolExecutionLedgerConflictError`, which is now admitted to fail-fast BY NAME and waived as the **fifth** member of the §14.6.3 tuple. The population still riding the catch-all is therefore strictly smaller: the genuinely transient store I/O the store subtype thereafter exclusively carries, plus `MemoryToolExecutionDeniedError`. The store subtype's disposition is otherwise **UNCHANGED** — it keeps `io_failure`, keeps classifying `TRANSIENT_RETRY`, and still charges at both staircase sites. **What this means for the forward work:** the easiest candidate for a finer split has been taken, so what remains is the harder question the row was really about — whether a class that wraps transient I/O can be discriminated at all without message guessing. The (b′) leg is also the **worked precedent** for step (2)'s finer-split option: it discriminated on the wrapped exception's own TYPE by making that type survive the capture boundary, rather than by reading `failure_reason` wording.
- **Council: no at registration; conditionally yes at step (2)** if a staircase-side waiver is proposed — that re-opens the `B-116` C1/C9 ⊥ C11 dyad on a NEW path with its own retry-visibility tradeoffs.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-116` (the ratified fail-fast-site waiver whose scope boundary this row marks); the §14.6.3 declared-residual paragraph cites this row by id and records the narrowing; `B-115` (the (b′) leg that narrowed it).

### B-133 · The §9.2 always-sampled floor classifies **span names** at both consumers while three of its members are span **events**, so their head=1.0 floor is unrealized on the dispatch path *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex round 1 at the `B-116-t3` leg, 2026-08-08; same family as B-123 / B-124)*

- **CLOSED — 2026-08-08. Steps (1) and (2) EXECUTED; step (3) STILL OPEN**, carried as a named residual on this closed row (the `B-104` precedent) and **MERGED with `B-137`**. *This bullet states the CURRENT result; the bullets above it are the row's registration text and are superseded where they conflict.* **(1) The positive control was run FIRST, end-to-end, and before any repair was written** — a REAL `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher.dispatch` driven to fallback-chain exhaustion through a `TracerProvider` wired with the REAL `HarnessCompositeSampler` **and** the REAL `TailKeepSpanProcessor`, across **seven** configurations covering **all three** event-shaped members by their own real dispatch shapes (chain exhaustion → `fallback.exhausted`; capability-shortfall exhaustion → `fallback.triggered`; charging-fault exhaustion at `fail_threshold=1` → `breaker.tripped`, chosen deliberately because `LLMDispatchProviderUnreachableError` is a §14.6.3 **waived** type and does not trip). **Result — ZERO spans exported at BOTH consumers for ALL THREE members.** The `base_rate=1.0` control exported 3, proving carrier and event exist. **The decisive discriminator:** at `base_rate=0.0` a span **NAMED** `fallback.exhausted` survives while a span **carrying it as an event** is dropped — *event-shaped, not name-shaped* is the **measured** cause. **(2) Repair venue (a) BUILT**, as this row ranked it; venue **(b) REFUSED** as the X-AL-3 extension this row already classified it as. Contract at OD spec **v1.38** NEW **§C-OD-09 §9.2.1** (five terms); unit at OD plan **v2.33 U-OD-59**; **sixteen witnesses W1–W16** (40 cases, homed across the axis boundary — the five real-dispatch witnesses at `harness-runtime/tests/test_b133_event_aware_tail_floor_real_dispatch.py`, the nine processor-contract witnesses at `harness-od/tests/…`, which stays `harness_runtime`-free because the axis-isolation CI leg prunes every sibling of `harness-od`) plus **seven PD-8 probes**, every figure re-measured against the final roster after the decorrelated 3-lens merge gate on PR #1276 returned a **real BLOCK** — a first-event-only scan passed all 65 cases then in the suite while reinstating `B-133` on the production-reachable `retry.skipped`-first ordering, closed by **W15/W16** and pinned by probe (vii) — two changed the deliverable (probe (ii) caught the trigger-flag mirror witness **passing under the mutation it existed to catch**, sharpened membership→export ORDER, re-run 27 failed / 5 passed; probe (iii) returned GREEN as the **correct** result, ordering being a cost property), and probe (vi) **validates** rather than changes, inverting exactly the bound witnesses. **What the arm delivers, as measured scope rather than coverage:** it realizes the floor for carriers the head **ADMITTED**, and for those delivers **100%** (420/420, 837/837) — what bounds it is **admission, not classification**. `tracer_provider.py` binds the §10.3 ratio at the head **unconditionally in both §9.1 modes**, so admission measured **10.4%** (`team-binding × self-hosted-server`), **20.9%** (`multi-tenant-compliance × managed-cloud`), **100%** at the base-rate-1.0 cells. **The head bound therefore reaches FIVE of the EIGHT active cells** — every cell whose head base-rate is below 1.0 — **and it is SHAPE-specific**: at the same cell and rate a §9.2 member realized as a **root span name** is admitted at **100%** (4,000/4,000 for `sandbox.violation`), so only **event-carried** members and **non-root** spans are starved, the latter including non-root §10.2 triggers at ~9% preservation. Pinned by **W5 + W13 + W14**, named as a bound. **History, compressed rather than carried twice:** two successive framings of this bound were wrong and were corrected by **measurement, not argument** — first this row's own step-(2) hypothesis that head-based-dev cells *"sample at 1.0 anyway"*, then the leg's first drafting, which over-corrected to *"exactly one cell"* and claimed every `TAIL_BASED_PROD` cell was covered by terms 1–3. Both are **superseded** by the statement above; the full narrative is at OD spec v1.38 §0.2 and plan v2.33 §0.9. **Two closing routes remain, both outside this row:** the **shape** half is venue (b) (a new emission primitive, back-flow per X-AL-3); the **admission** half is **`B-137`**. **(3) F-08 per-tenant keep-volume — STILL OPEN**, and now **merged with `B-137`**: measure at a `TAIL_BASED_PROD` **multi-tenant** cell (head-based cells engage no tail consumer) and measure it **jointly**, because today's ~20% admission is the **ceiling** on this arm's added keep-volume and `B-137`'s candidate A removes it. **`B-123` NOT closed** — its step-(1) probe is answered as a side effect (an event-carried `breaker.tripped` sets no keep flag); term 3 declines to widen the predicate and **W7** pins the boundary. **`B-136` newly registered** (the pre-existing name-arm root-close buffer leak; this arm must not extend it — term 5 + AC #6c + PD-8 probe (iv)). **`B-137` newly registered** after out-of-family Codex round 1 against commit `ff63c725`, adjudicated empirically at the real production wiring and CONFIRMED: the arm is **real but partial**, and what was defective was the contract **TEXT**, not the arm.
- **What it is.** Both C-OD-09 §9.2 consumers resolve the always-sampled floor against a **span name** and never against an **event name**. **Head:** `HarnessCompositeSampler.should_sample` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/composite_sampler.py:100`) branches on `is_always_sampled(name, attributes)` at `:110`, where `name` is the span name supplied at span creation. **Tail:** `TailKeepSpanProcessor.on_end` (`harness-od/src/harness_od/tail_keep_span_processor.py:207`) branches on `is_always_sampled(span.name, span.attributes)` at `:259` and **never inspects `span.events`** — grounded at HEAD by direct read: the module contains **zero** occurrences of `.events`.
- **Three §9.2 members are span EVENTS on a wrapper span, not spans of their own.** `fallback.triggered` (`outer_span.add_event` at `retry_breaker_fallback.py:688-689`); `fallback.exhausted` (`outer_span.add_event` at `:946-947` — the row the `B-116-t3` leg added); `breaker.tripped` (`parent_span_ref.add_event(name="breaker.tripped", ...)` at `harness-od/src/harness_od/harness_breaker_schema.py:282`, the same emission shape `B-123` grounds). For all three the §9.2 head=1.0 guarantee is carried **only insofar as the WRAPPER span is kept** — at a base-rate-sampled cell the wrapper can be dropped and the always-sampled event goes with it.
- **PRE-EXISTING, not new exposure from the `B-116-t3` leg — and this is the load-bearing scope fact.** `fallback.triggered` and `breaker.tripped` have carried the identical shape since the **original OD ingestion** of §9.2, so the characteristic is a property of the **floor mechanism**, not of the row this leg added.
