- **What is NOT in question.** The §9.2 **membership contract** is correct regardless, and so is the **ingestion-chain direction** that placed the row in OD rather than demoting CP — neither turns on how the floor is realized at the SDK boundary. **`B-116` CLOSED at its ratified gate**, whose stated content was the roster widening plus its sampling fixtures per the council record `C-c7-reconcile.md`'s own pricing; **this row carries the realization debt that pricing never covered.** *Registration is the non-silent disposition* — the finding is neither absorbed into a closed row nor repaired by redesign at a leg with no authority for it.
- **Why it is not fixed here.** The reviewer's two proposed remedies are both **REJECTED at the t3 leg**. Emitting a dedicated span mints a **new emission primitive no cleared spec authorizes** — an X-AL-3 design extension routing through back-flow, not an impl fix. Making the wrapper span always-sampled would always-sample **every dispatch wrapper**, over-sampling far beyond the three rows at issue and silently rewriting the §10.3 per-cell envelope.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Run the positive control first, end-to-end rather than at the predicate** — drive a real **exhausted** dispatch through the composite sampler **and** the tail-keep processor at a cell whose `base_rate` < 1 and observe whether the wrapper span carrying `fallback.exhausted` is dropped; cover the two siblings in the same run, since a repair scoped to one row leaves the family half-fixed. **(2) If dropped (expected), decide the repair venue — the two candidates differ in KIND:** **(a)** an event-aware arm at tail-keep `on_end` scanning `span.events` names against the §9.2 roster before the drop decision — single-domain C7, no new primitive, no spec amendment, and it **composes with `B-123`'s trigger arm** since both want the same event-name lookup; **(b)** an event→span projection at emission — a **new primitive routing through back-flow per X-AL-3**, which also changes the span topology every existing witness asserts against. Prefer (a) unless the control shows the tail arm cannot reach the decision; note (a) repairs the **tail** surface only — a head-based-dev cell samples at 1.0 anyway, so the head arm may need nothing (**confirm, do not assume**). **(3) Post-realization, and only then,** bound the multi-tenant keep-volume against the C-OD-11 §11.1 per-tenant **1,000 spans/sec** budget per C7's F-08 — the **population question the `B-116-t3` leg left explicitly OPEN**, that leg having established only the **structural** result (the budget enforces at COLLECTOR_BOUNDARY / BACKEND_INGESTION independently of any sampling decision, so membership cannot admit throughput past the enforced caps, and the event is once-per-exhausted-dispatch so membership adds no multiplicity). Measuring volume before the floor is actually realized would measure the wrong thing.
- **Council: no** — a probe-then-repair row in the `B-123` family; convene nothing until the positive control runs. **Conditionally yes** only if step (2) selects candidate (b): a new emission primitive re-opens the **C7 observability-floor ⊥ C11 telemetry-volume** tension on a surface wider than these three rows. Candidate (a) is single-domain and owes no convening.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-123` (the §10.2 tail-keep trigger arm of the *same* span-name-vs-span-event mismatch) and `B-124` (the inert attribute-qualified §9.2 row) — **the three are one family and should be dispositioned together**. `B-116` / the `B-116-t3` leg (`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_37.md`, whose change-note carries the matching honest-scope paragraph).
- **Out-of-family Codex round 1 against this leg's commit `ff63c725` — ONE P1, adjudicated EMPIRICALLY at the real production wiring and CONFIRMED, with the leg's own contract TEXT corrected where it overclaimed.** The reviewer held that at `TAIL_BASED_PROD` cells with `base_rate < 1` the head sampler drops the carrier at span **creation**, so no `ReadableSpan` reaches the new tail arm and §9.2.1 term 4's coverage claim is false. **Grounded first, not assumed either way:** `tracer_provider.py` resolves `build_default_sampler(base_rate=PER_CELL_BASE_RATE_ENVELOPE[cell].default_rate)` **unconditionally**, and says in the same function that *"the current default sampler ignores the mode … Future units may wire mode-conditional samplers."* **Then measured** over 4,000 carriers per cell through the real composition: `team-binding × self-hosted-server` (base 0.1) admitted **10.4%**; `multi-tenant-compliance × managed-cloud` (base 0.2) admitted **20.9%**; `solo-developer × self-hosted-server` (base 1.0) admitted **100%**. **The repair this row built is therefore REAL but PARTIAL** — it realizes the floor for head-**admitted** carriers, and of those it delivers **100%** (420/420 and 837/837). **What was defective was the TEXT, not the arm:** term 4's *"every `TAIL_BASED_PROD` cell … is covered by terms 1–3"* is **RETRACTED** and replaced by a per-cell admission table plus the statement that the head bound reaches **five of the eight** ACTIVE cells, not one. **A second framing was ALSO falsified by the same run and is recorded so it is not carried forward:** the starvation is **not uniform**. A §9.2 member realized as a **root span name** is admitted at **100%** even at base-rate 0.1 (measured 4,000/4,000 for `sandbox.violation`), because the head resolves `is_always_sampled` against the span **name**. Only **event-carried** members and **non-root** spans are starved — the latter including non-root §10.2 triggers, measured at **~9%** preservation at base-rate 0.1. That shape-dependence is exactly what this row named. The architecture-level question — an unconditionally admitting head in `TAIL_BASED_PROD` mode with the §10.3 ratio moved into the tail consumer — is **registered as `B-137`**, not absorbed: it spans every class the tail preserves and multiplies admitted volume by `1/base_rate` at every production cell. Witnesses **W13** (parametrized over the two production cells) and **W14** (the root-name-vs-event asymmetry) pin the corrected bound on the **W5 pattern — named as a bound, not hidden** — and **PD-8 probe (vi)** shows they are load-bearing by inverting them under a `B-137` candidate-A sketch. **`B-137` MERGES with this row's F-08 residual** rather than sitting beside it: today's ~20% multi-tenant admission is the **ceiling** on the arm's added keep-volume, and candidate A removes that ceiling, so F-08 must be measured **jointly with `B-137`**.

### B-134 · Should `C-MEM-19` gain a dedicated failure class for deterministic ledger conflicts, rather than routing them to the residual? *(surfaced at the `B-115` (b′) leg, 2026-08-08 — the leg took the residual per the U-MEM-28 precedent and registered the vocabulary question rather than widening a ratified enumeration on its own authority)*

- **What it is, and it is a question the `B-115` leg deliberately did NOT answer on its own authority.** That leg introduced `MemoryToolExecutionLedgerConflictError` for the C-MEM-08 operation ledger's divergent-replay refusal. The type **declares no C-MEM-19 failure class** and inherits the family base's **residual** `provider_adapter_failure`.
- **Three options; none obviously dominant.** **(i) Keep `io_failure`** — REJECTED, the one clearly wrong answer: a ledger refusal is a pure comparison over durable state under a lock, not an I/O fault, so `io_failure` is a positively **wrong** claim. **(ii) Inherit the residual** — TAKEN. Per C-MEM-19 v1.3 a residual report is the **absence** of a claim rather than an assertion of adapter-hood, so this **withdraws a false positive** without inventing a replacement; it follows the **U-MEM-28 precedent**, which moved an emission `input_validation_failure` → residual on exactly these grounds; and it makes the two `classify_memory_failure` consumers **agree**, since `memory_redaction.py` already reports the underlying `MemoryOperationIdempotencyConflictError` as `provider_adapter_failure` under a landed two-row discriminating witness. **(iii) Mint a dedicated `ledger_conflict` class** — NOT taken, and the reason is **jurisdictional rather than technical**: it would widen C-MEM-19's ratified vocabulary, and `Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` v1.3 records at its own change-note (the round-8 finding on the seventh re-typing) that widening a ratified enumeration on a leg's own reading of the rule is the **X-AL-3 shape even when the reading is sound**.
- **The honest cost of (ii), stated so the row is not read as cost-free.** The residual bucket now carries a well-typed, deliberately classified population alongside genuinely untriaged failures — the same triage-blindness C-MEM-19 v1.3's `input_validation_failure` section was written to forbid for a *different* population. The difference in scale is a reason to **defer**, not a reason the concern does not apply.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Re-ground** at the then-current HEAD: C-MEM-19's enumeration and invariants; that the residual is still `provider_adapter_failure`; that the conflict type still declares nothing (the `B-115` witness asserts the declaration-**absence** over `vars()`, so a silent later declaration would already have failed there). **(2) Measure the residual bucket rather than arguing about it** — enumerate every type and raise-site population currently reporting `provider_adapter_failure` and state how much is deliberately-classified-but-unnamed versus genuinely untriaged. **If the deliberate half dominates, the residual has stopped meaning "absence of a claim" and the vocabulary owes a member — that is the falsifiable trigger.** **(3) If a class is warranted**, it is a Class 2 fork against C-MEM-19 with a Memory spec leg (v1.3 → v1.4) plus a Memory plan unit, on the `B-88` / U-MEM-28 precedent — a full spec-leg arc, not an impl-discretion flip. The flip site is **one line** by construction (the type declares a `ClassVar` instead of inheriting), because the `B-115` leg wrote the declaration explicitly as an absence. **(4) Consider scope** — the same question applies to `MemoryToolExecutionInternalError`, which inherits the same residual for the same stated reason at U-MEM-28; a vocabulary arc should decide **both together** rather than minting one member and leaving its sibling in the residual. **What would falsify the deferral:** the bucket measured at step (2) turning out majority-deliberate, or an operator decision recording the residual routing as permanently accepted.
- **Council: no at registration** — the row frames a vocabulary question and commits to nothing. **Conditionally yes at step (3)** if a class is proposed: minting a C-MEM-19 member trades telemetry triage precision (**C3**, which owns record and ledger semantics) against vocabulary stability for every downstream consumer that switches on the enum (**C7**). The tension is nameable in advance, which is the convening discriminator. Convene **only** if step (2)'s measurement supports the widening.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-115` (the (b′) leg that surfaced it); `B-88` / U-MEM-28 (the precedent for both the residual routing and the fork shape a widening would need); `Spec_Memory_Substrate_v1.md` v1.3 C-MEM-19.

### B-135 · Stale-era breaker dispatches act under a superseded era on BOTH sides — outcomes reset the `closed`-arm `fail_count` un-epoch-guarded, and attempts continue a multi-attempt staircase across a trip that can overlap the single half-open trial *(outcome side surfaced by out-of-family codex review round 2 at the `B-118` leg, attempt side by round 6, both 2026-08-08 — each adjudicated PRE-EXISTING, so the leg declared the boundaries rather than absorbing an unpriced redesign)*

- **What it is.** The `B-118` trial-epoch guard (Runtime spec **v1.114 §14.6.4**) binds the **`half_open` resolution arms ONLY** — `record_success` / `record_failure` / `re_arm_half_open_trial` refuse to resolve a `half_open` machine unless the caller presents the current admission epoch. The **`closed` arms stay TOKENLESS by design.** Codex round 2 named a scenario that crosses the boundary: a request admitted while the breaker was `closed` survives, in flight, through a trip **and** a successful half-open recovery, and its stale success then arrives while the breaker is `closed` again. It takes the tokenless `closed` arm, resets `fail_count`, and erases whatever failure accumulation has built up **since** the recovery.
- **Why this is PRE-EXISTING and not a `B-118` regression — verified, not assumed.** `record_success` resetting `fail_count` in `closed` is the shipped **consecutive-failure** breaker semantics on main (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker.py`, the `record_success` CLOSED arm, pre-`B-118`), and the erasure is reachable with **ZERO trips and ZERO recoveries**: siblings fail twice, an older in-flight success lands, the count resets. That is the definition of a consecutive-failure counter and it long predates this leg. `B-118` adds **one more path** into the same arm (a request that outlived a full trip-and-recover cycle) but changes **nothing** about the arm's semantics.
- **Why the `B-118` guard deliberately stops at `half_open`.** The `half_open` race is categorically different — there a stale success does not merely reset a counter, it **resolves a trial it does not own** and closes a breaker the machine had already judged unhealthy, after which the real trial's failure lands under threshold and the provider-model is silently readmitted. Guarding `closed`-arm outcomes instead requires capturing an epoch on **every ordinary dispatch** and changes **contracted** success-reset semantics for every caller — an unpriced redesign, not a bug fix. That is why the leg **declared** the boundary at §14.6.4 rather than absorbing it.
- **The ATTEMPT side, added 2026-08-08 (out-of-family review round 6, same `B-118` leg).** The family has a second half. A dispatch admitted while the breaker was `closed` keeps its **multi-attempt** `RetryPolicy`. If it fails transiently, and siblings then trip the breaker while a later dispatch acquires the `half_open` permit, the `closed`-era dispatch resumes **attempt 2 with no breaker re-consultation** — a concurrent **paid** call overlapping what §14.6.4 calls "the single trial".
- **Why the attempt side is PRE-EXISTING too.** The breaker pre-check is **per-candidate** by contract (§14.6 step 4): it runs once when a candidate is selected and is never re-consulted between that candidate's own retry attempts. The pre-`v1.114` loop behaved identically, so `B-118` neither introduced nor priced this. What round 6 actually caught is that **`B-118`'s own §14.6.4 text overclaimed** — the ratified intent (C9's Pillar-4, the cell-3 operator ratification) binds THE TRIAL to one call and never deliberated stale `closed`-era dispatches. That text is now **scoped** at §14.6.4 to *era-consistent admissions*, with the boundary **declared and witnessed** rather than defended.
- **One family, two sides.** A dispatch admitted under an earlier breaker era continuing to act under that era's policy — whether it is reporting an **outcome** or making another **attempt**.
- **Close-out steps.** **(1) Decide whether `closed`-arm outcome ordering should be epoch-aware at all** — not obviously yes: a consecutive-failure counter that forgives on ANY success is a deliberate, contracted design, and making it order-aware changes what `fail_threshold` means for every caller. Ground against C-CP-03 §3.5 before pricing. **(2) If yes, price BOTH sides honestly** — epoch-awareness on one alone leaves the family half-open. **(2a) The outcome side** — the ordinary-dispatch epoch capture — it touches the **hot path**, not the rare recovery path the `B-118` guard touches, and needs its own witness set plus a decision about what a stale `closed`-arm success does *instead* of resetting (drop it? apply it to the epoch it belongs to? neither is free). **(2b) The attempt side** — mid-staircase re-consultation, the more expensive half and the reason this is registered rather than absorbed: re-checking the breaker *between* a candidate's own retry attempts means **abandoning a candidate partway through its attempt loop**, changing exhaustion accounting and `fallback.last_failure_class` attribution for a path that predates `B-118` entirely. Semantic surgery on the staircase, not a defect repair. Note the two sides can be decided **independently** — guarding outcomes without guarding attempts is coherent (a stale success can no longer close a breaker, even though a stale paid call may still land); the reverse is not, so if only one is built it should be the outcome side. **(3) Note the `B-116` t4 interaction** — any future breaker-persistence arc must replay epochs consistently, or a rehydrated breaker treats every in-flight outcome as stale (or every stale one as current), which is worse than the failure this row describes.
- **What would falsify it.** A demonstration that the `closed`-arm reset is NOT reachable without a trip (which the grounding above already contradicts), **or** a ratified decision that consecutive-failure-with-forgiveness is exactly the intended semantics — in which case this row closes as WORKING-AS-DESIGNED and §14.6.4's boundary paragraph becomes the permanent statement of it.
- **Council:** **No at registration.** A single-domain C9 breaker-semantics question — what `fail_threshold` counts, and whether a counter that forgives on any success is intended — with no nameable cross-domain tension. **Conditionally yes** only if step (2) proposes a **durable or persistent** epoch, which re-opens the persistence tension `B-116` term t4 pinned and is a genuine C9 ⊥ C11 dyad.

### B-136 · The tail-keep **name-matching** always-sampled arm returns before the root-close materialization, so an always-sampled **root** leaves its trace buffered until `force_flush` *(surfaced by direct probe at the `B-133` leg, 2026-08-08 — pre-existing; the `B-133` event arm deliberately does NOT share the shape)*

- **✅ CLOSED 2026-08-13 (PR #1331) — REPAIRED, and it matters more than the row priced.** **(1) Re-ground:** the two-trace probe still read **1 vs 0** at HEAD — the arm had not moved. **(2) Is it a defect — YES**, and the row's own *"nothing is lost, `force_flush` drains keep-all"* premise is **false under pressure**: at `max_buffered_traces=3` over 100 always-sampled-root traces, **97 are evicted** and their children never export. More decisively it contradicts **v1.28 §1.1's own containment model** — *"a new trace whose first observed span is already its root-close materializes + frees its slot … so it does NOT evict"* — an always-sampled-root trace root-closed yet behaved like a never-closing one, displacing live traces. **(3) Repair:** mirror §9.2.1 **term 5** onto the name arm — the same two lines the `B-133` **event** arm already carries, whose comment names B-136 as the case it must not extend. Consistency with the spec-normative arm is the justification. **(4) Both directions witnessed:** slot freed for every root shape; a **triggered** trace exports its siblings *earlier*; a **quiet** always-sampled root (e.g. `hitl.gate.evaluated`) now **drops** them — a real reduction, and exactly what an **ordinary** root already did. **(5) Venue:** not WORKING-AS-DESIGNED — §9.3's implementer discretion is exercised toward the model v1.28 already documents. **No existing witness asserted the stranding** (all 1178 OD tests passed unchanged), so the re-grounding concern was precautionary. **Witness:** `harness-od/tests/test_b136_name_arm_root_close_materialization.py` — 6 tests, mutation-probed (4/6 RED pre-repair).
- **Adjacent finding registered — `B-163`** *(out-of-family Codex round 2 on this PR)*. All three materialization sites — `:478` (original ordinary-root close), `:437` (`B-133` event arm) and `:391` (this repair) — pop the per-trace bucket with **no lock**, while a concurrent child `on_end` can `setdefault` an empty bucket and append to it *after* the pop, losing the span entirely. That window is **pre-existing and module-wide** (no `threading.Lock` anywhere), so it is **not introduced here** — this repair widens the exposed population by making every always-sampled root materialize. Registered **and fixed** as **B-163** in this same PR — one `threading.RLock` guards every buffer/keep/counter mutation, never held across `downstream.on_end`, with a coordinated deterministic witness that loses the span when the lock is neutered.
- **⚠️ COUPLING TO `B-137` STEP (3) — the most consequential part of this closure.** B-137's **candidate C1** was priced *one day earlier* as costing **data loss rather than delay**, because under C1 every workflow trace has an always-sampled root and therefore hit **this** arm (measured 3 buffered / 97 evicted at cap 3). **Post-repair the identical C1 counterfactual reads 0 buffered / 0 evicted**, and with a §10.2 trigger present **100/100** ordinary children export where **0** did before. So **C1's principal cost belonged to B-136, not to C1** — fixing B-136 makes C1 substantially **more attractive**, leaving it at its `1/base_rate` volume multiplier with ordinary trace semantics. **B-137's step-(3) council must be briefed:** the deferral filed earlier today cited C1's eviction cost, and that citation is **superseded**. Both B-137 C1 witnesses were re-priced in the same PR.
- **What it was** *(HISTORY — CLOSED at PR #1331; retained as the pre-repair description, no longer a live statement of behaviour)*.** `TailKeepSpanProcessor.on_end`'s §9.2 **name-matching** arm (`harness-od/src/harness_od/tail_keep_span_processor.py`, the `is_always_sampled(span.name, span.attributes)` branch) forwards the span downstream, optionally sets the §10.2 keep flag, and **returns — unconditionally**, before the `is_root_close → _materialize_trace_decision(trace_id)` step further down the method. When the always-sampled span is itself the trace's **root close**, the trace's buffered siblings are therefore never resolved: they sit in `self._buffer`, holding a `max_buffered_traces` slot, until `force_flush` drains them keep-all at shutdown. **Probed directly at the `B-133` leg, 2026-08-08:** a trace whose root is named `sandbox.violation` with one ordinary buffered child leaves `buffered_trace_count == 1` after the root closes; the control trace with an ordinary root returns `0`.
- **Why it mattered** *(HISTORY — the displacement described here is REMOVED by the repair)*.** The slot is not merely held, it is **charged**: under `max_buffered_traces` pressure `_evict_oldest_trace` sheds the oldest buffered trace FIFO, so a population of never-resolving always-sampled-root traces **displaces live traces** that would otherwise have taken a real keep decision. The module's own *"Eviction fidelity tradeoff"* paragraph reasons about eviction on the assumption that buffered traces resolve at their root close; this arm is the case where they do not.
- **Why it is PRE-EXISTING and not `B-133` exposure.** The name-matching arm and its unconditional return long predate the `B-133` leg; that leg only **asked** the question, because its own new event-aware arm sits beside the same return and the dispatch carrier span **is** routinely the root close, so an unconditional early return there would have put the common case into the leaking shape. **The `B-133` arm does NOT leak** — OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 **term 5** makes the root-close materialization normative for the event arm, U-OD-59 AC #6c witnesses it, and PD-8 probe (iv) goes RED without it. The asymmetry between the two arms is **deliberate and recorded**, not an oversight: repairing the name arm changes shipped behaviour for every name-shaped always-sampled root, which the `B-133` arc had no authority to do.
- **Close-out steps** *(ALL DISCHARGED at PR #1331 — steps (1)–(5) are answered in the CLOSED bullets above; retained as history. DO NOT re-run: this row is closed.)*.** **(1) Re-ground, because the arm may have moved** — re-run the two-trace probe at the then-current HEAD (always-sampled root + one ordinary child, versus an ordinary root + one ordinary child) and confirm `buffered_trace_count` is still 1 versus 0. Grep proves the `return`; only the run proves the trace is still stranded. **(2) Decide whether it is a defect at all**, and this is a real question rather than a formality: `force_flush` drains keep-all, so **nothing is lost** — what is affected is *when* the siblings export (at drain rather than at root close) and how much `max_buffered_traces` headroom a long-running process retains. A deployment whose always-sampled roots are rare pays nothing. Ground against C-OD-09 §9.3's implementer-discretion clause, which is where the buffering algorithm's shape lives. **(3) If it is a defect, the repair is small but NOT free** — mirror OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 term 5 onto the name arm (~2 lines). What is not free is the **behaviour change**: every existing witness asserting on export order or `buffered_trace_count` around an always-sampled root must be re-grounded, and a trace whose siblings previously survived to `force_flush` keep-all would, after the repair, be **DROPPED** at root close if no §10.2 trigger fired. That is a real reduction in exported spans for a real population, and it is why this was registered rather than folded into the `B-133` arm. **(4) Witness BOTH directions if built** — the root-close resolution (`buffered_trace_count → 0`) **and** the drop-when-no-trigger consequence, so the repair is not mistaken for a pure bookkeeping fix. **(5) Decide the venue** — if the answer to (2) is that `force_flush` keep-all is the **contracted** behaviour, this closes as WORKING-AS-DESIGNED and the module docstring's *"Drop semantics (false-but-bounded)"* paragraph should be extended to say so, since it currently describes only the never-root-closing case and not this one.
- **What would have falsified it** *(HISTORY — the re-ground at PR #1331 confirmed 1 vs 0, so neither falsifier held)*.** A re-run showing `buffered_trace_count == 0` for the always-sampled-root trace (the arm having changed since), or a ratified reading that deferring always-sampled-root traces to `force_flush` is intended.
- **Council: no.** A single-domain **C7** question about the tail-keep buffering algorithm's own bookkeeping, sitting squarely inside §9.3's implementer-discretion clause, with a named two-trace probe that answers it. The one thing that would change that is step (3) turning out to reduce exported spans for a population an operator depends on, putting the C7 observability floor against the C11 telemetry-volume posture — but that is a consequence to **measure** at step (4), not a tension nameable in advance, so it does not meet the convening discriminator at registration.
- **Cross-ref.** `B-133` (the leg whose probe surfaced it, and whose own arm deliberately does not share the shape); OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 term 5; OD plan v2.33 U-OD-59 AC #6c + PD-8 probe (iv).

### B-137 · Head sampling starves the tail-keep mechanism for every preserved class that is **not a root span name** — the shipped head sampler applies the §10.3 ratio in **both** §9.1 modes *(surfaced by out-of-family Codex round 1 against the `B-133` leg's commit `ff63c725`, 2026-08-08; premise adjudicated empirically at the real production wiring and CONFIRMED, with the non-uniformity falsifying the first framing)*

- **What it is, measured at the real production composition.** C-OD-09 §9.1 says `TAIL_BASED_PROD` means the sampling decision is taken **at trace completion**. The shipped composition does not deliver that: `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/tracer_provider.py` resolves `build_default_sampler(base_rate=PER_CELL_BASE_RATE_ENVELOPE[cell].default_rate)` **unconditionally, for every cell**, and states in the same function that *"the current default sampler ignores the mode … Future units may wire mode-conditional samplers."* So at a `TAIL_BASED_PROD` cell the §10.3 ratio is applied by `ParentBased(HarnessCompositeSampler(base_rate))` **at span creation**, and `TailKeepSpanProcessor` only ever sees the admitted fraction. **A span the head dropped never reaches `on_end` at all**, so no tail-side preservation rule — not §10.2 tail-keep-on-classification, not the §9.2 always-sampled forward, not the `B-133` event-aware arm — can act on it.
- **Measured** over 4,000 carriers per cell at HEAD: `team-binding × self-hosted-server` (base 0.1) admitted **10.4%**; `multi-tenant-compliance × managed-cloud` (base 0.2) admitted **20.9%**; `solo-developer × self-hosted-server` (base 1.0) admitted **100%**.
- **The starvation is NOT uniform, and the non-uniformity IS the finding** — an earlier framing of it as *"every preserved class is equally starved"* was **falsified by the same run**. A §9.2 member realized as a **root span name** is admitted at **100%** even at base-rate 0.1 (measured 4,000/4,000 for `sandbox.violation`), because the head sampler resolves `is_always_sampled` against the span **name** and returns `RECORD_AND_SAMPLE`. What **is** starved is everything the head cannot classify at creation, and there are exactly two such populations: **(i)** §9.2 members carried as span **events** — the `B-133` family, measured 10.4% at base-rate 0.1 — and **(ii)** **non-root** spans of any class, because `ParentBased` consults the inner sampler **only for roots** and children inherit an unsampled parent's decision. Population (ii) includes the §10.2 classification triggers when they are not roots: a trace with an ordinary root and a `sandbox.violation` **child** was preserved in **182 of 2,000** traces (~9%) at base-rate 0.1.
- **Why this is PRE-EXISTING and not `B-133` exposure.** Population (ii) is the bound `composite_sampler.py`'s own *"Enforcement boundary (honest scope)"* docstring **already declares**, and that the `B-TAIL-CONDITIONAL-SAMPLING` arc was opened for; it long predates `B-133`. Population (i) is `B-133`'s, whose **tail** half `B-133` closed for head-admitted carriers and whose **head** half OD spec v1.38 §9.2.1 term 4 declares as a bound with the per-cell table. **Neither row priced the architecture question this row carries.**
- **What makes it architecture rather than a defect repair.** Closing it means making the head unconditionally admitting in `TAIL_BASED_PROD` mode and moving the §10.3 ratio into the tail consumer — which multiplies admitted span volume by `1/base_rate` at every production cell (**×10** at the team cells, **×5** at multi-tenant), changes what `max_buffered_traces` and the C-OD-11 §11.1 per-cell budgets are sized against, and alters the posture of **every** class the tail preserves, not only the three `B-133` named.
- **RE-MEASURED AT THE REAL VENUE 2026-08-13 — steps (1) and (2) are DONE; step (3) is the only live step.** **(1) Re-grounding:** `tracer_provider.py:236-240` still binds `build_default_sampler(base_rate=PER_CELL_BASE_RATE_ENVELOPE[cell].default_rate)` unconditionally, still discards the mode (`_ = resolve_sampling_mode(...)`), and still carries the *"the current default sampler ignores the mode … Future units may wire mode-conditional samplers"* note. **No mode-conditional sampler has landed; this row is not closed by other work.** **(2) Re-measurement, EXECUTED THROUGH `api.run`** — not a manufactured composition (an earlier draft of this arc was correctly rejected by out-of-family Codex for driving an uncalled helper). Running the B-72 fan-out workflow end to end with a real `TracerProvider` and the production sampler at `base_rate=0.0`, **nothing is exported at all** — including `hitl.gate.evaluated`, which **is** a §9.2 member carrying a declared `head=1.0` floor. With an always-on provider the identical run records exactly `workflow.envelope` (ROOT) and `hitl.gate.evaluated` nested under it. **All three of step (2)'s populations are now EXECUTED, not just the venue one (codex round 6).** The `api.run` witness covers the non-root population only; `test_all_three_starved_populations_at_one_composition` covers **root-name-matched** (survives), **non-root** (dropped) and **event-carried** (dropped) at one composition — the probe shape step (2) actually prescribes. **And a tripwire for the very fix this row awaits:** every other measurement supplies a deterministic sampler override, so a future mode-conditional sampler repairing only `TAIL_BASED_PROD` would leave them all green — `test_a_production_cell_still_binds_the_unconditional_ratio_sampler` composes a real production cell (`team-binding × self-hosted-server`, rate 0.1) through the shipped stage with **no override**, so it reddens the moment that sampler lands and forces re-measurement.
- **Why — the floor is ROOT-ONLY.** `workflow_driver.py:3305` opens `workflow.envelope` as the trace root; `workflow.envelope` is **not** a §9.2 member; and `ParentBased(root=HarnessCompositeSampler)` consults the composite sampler **only for roots**. The root loses its base-rate draw and every child inherits the drop, its own name never consulted. **The tail half is executed too** (the row's step (2) names `TailKeepSpanProcessor` explicitly): driving the REAL processor through the REAL run at `base_rate=0.0`, `on_end` receives **zero** arrivals — a head-dropped span is never recorded, so that processor's own §9.2 bypass-the-buffer arm can never act on it.
- **SCOPE — an earlier draft of this arc overclaimed, and the overclaim is WITHDRAWN.** It asserted that *all 19 §9.2 members, at their real emission sites, are children of the envelope.* **False.** Only **11 of the 19** have a span-open site in `src/` at all (the other 8 are event-carried or unimplemented — population (i)), and at least one span-backed member is a **root**: `skill.activation` is emitted from `workflow_driver.py:3206`, which **precedes** the envelope's open at `:3305`. The starvation is **scoped to the members emitted inside the envelope**, and any repricing of step (3) must be against that set rather than all 19. **Qualified 2026-08-13 (codex round 14).** That root status holds for a **top-level** run only. The emit sits inside `execute_workflow`, which is exactly the function the child runner re-enters under an active `subagent.span` — so under a nested recursive run the same pre-envelope emit is a **child** and is starved like the rest. The counterexample **scopes** the starved population rather than exempting `skill.activation`. **General lesson, now applied to every root/child claim on this row:** source-line ordering relative to the local envelope proves *ordering*, never *trace-root status* — root status depends on the call venue, and there are at least two (top-level `api.run`, nested sub-agent dispatch) for the same code.
- **Witness — `harness-runtime/tests/integration/test_b137_ninety_two_floor_at_the_real_run_venue.py` (18 tests).** Deterministic at `base_rate=0.0`, where the ratio arm never admits and the always-sampled arm always does, so each assertion is a decision rather than a sample; a positive control fails loudly if the membership patch stops reaching `is_always_sampled` (patching the public `ALWAYS_SAMPLED_EVENT_CLASSES` frozenset alone is a silent no-op — the literal/prefix structures are derived once at import at `sampling_mode.py:160-172`; there is no runtime mutation path in `src/`, so this is test mechanics, not a defect). **Mutation-probed** by replacing `ParentBased(root=X)` with the bare `X`: both load-bearing tests go RED.
- **Step (3) — repriced by two measured counterfactuals at the same venue. NOTE the naming: neither counterfactual is the row's original candidate A**, which is *mode-conditional* `ALWAYS_ON` in `TAIL_BASED_PROD` with the §10.3 ratio moved **into the tail consumer** — that mechanism was **not** measured here and its ×10-on-everything cost stands as the close-out states it. What was measured: **(A′) bare-composite head** — drop `ParentBased` so the composite sampler is consulted for *every* span. It admits `hitl.gate.evaluated` but **still drops `workflow.envelope`**, yielding **orphaned floor spans whose parent trace was discarded**, at `1/base_rate` applied to floor-member spans **only**. Cheap, and it breaks trace structure. **(C1) admit the root** — add `workflow.envelope` itself to §9.2. Delivers the floor to every in-workflow member **by inheritance**, in one line. ~~keeps traces whole~~ **CORRECTED 2026-08-13 (codex round 3) — it does NOT keep traces whole, and its real cost is worse than a volume multiplier.** Measured through the shipped `TailKeepSpanProcessor`: C1 forwards the envelope and every §9.2 member (both take the always-sampled bypass arm at `tail_keep_span_processor.py:361`), but an ordinary non-member child stays **buffered at root close** — and **a §10.2 classification trigger does not rescue it**, because making the ROOT always-sampled means the root itself takes the bypass arm and `return`s **before** the root-close flush-or-drop decision runs. So under C1 a workflow trace **that contains at least one ordinary non-member child** becomes a never-resolving buffered trace, drained only by `force_flush` — and **worse than that under production bounds** (measured 2026-08-13, codex round 12): `span_processor.py:373-374` always supplies `max_buffered_traces` / `max_spans_per_trace` from `CollectorConfig` (defaults **4096** each, `types.py:741,752`), and the buffer evicts **drop-oldest** — so beyond the ceiling the ordinary children are **evicted and lost**, and `force_flush` never sees them. Measured at a cap of 3 over 100 traces: 3 buffered, **97 evicted**. Under sustained load that is the steady state, since under C1 every trace with an ordinary child occupies a slot and none is released at root close. **C1's cost is data loss, not delay.** **SCOPED 2026-08-13 (codex round 4)** — an earlier wording said *every* trace, which is wrong: this arc's own B-72 venue emits only `workflow.envelope` + `hitl.gate.evaluated`, both of which bypass the buffer under C1, leaving its buffer at **zero**. The measured stranding used a manufactured `validator.evaluate` child. **How often that child population occurs in real workflows is UNMEASURED and is owed before step (3) chooses C1** — the driver does open ordinary spans (`validator.evaluate` at `workflow_driver.py:5600`, plus `tool.dispatch` / `sandbox.*` / `secret.fetch` in the tool dispatcher), so the population is non-empty, but its frequency is not established here. That is exactly the **B-136** pressure this row's own step (5) predicts, and **C1 maximises it** rather than avoiding it. So the live option set is A (unmeasured, literal reading of §9.1) / A′ (measured, cheap, orphaned spans) / **C1 (measured, full trace admitted at the HEAD but ordinary children stranded in the tail buffer, full cost — *not* “whole traces”, corrected 2026-08-13 codex round 5)** / B (reporting only, not a repair) / C (ratify a root-only floor, which must amend §9.2/§9.3's *head=1.0 across all cells* language). The dyadic **C7 + C11** council's stated precondition — step (2)'s re-measurement first — is now **met**. **A′ is a PARTIAL, name-only remedy (measured 2026-08-13, codex round 15).** It addresses only one of the two starved populations: removing `ParentBased` exposes every span's **name** to `HarnessCompositeSampler`, repairing the non-root **name-backed** members, but does **nothing** for the **event-carried** members (the `B-133` family, which B-137 explicitly includes) — those ride as span EVENTS on an ordinary carrier, and at span creation the head still sees only the carrier's name. Measured at `base_rate=0.0`: A′ exports `hitl.gate.evaluated` and **not** the event-carrying `ordinary.carrier`. **A′ must not be selected at step (3) as a complete repair.** Pinned by `test_candidate_a_prime_is_a_name_only_remedy`.
- **C1 MEASURED ON A′'S OWN FALSIFYING TEST 2026-08-15 — the step-(3) option set now compares on ONE axis, and the comparison moves decisively to C1.** The two measured candidates had never been run against the same question: A′ was demoted to a *partial, name-only remedy* by exactly one test (`test_candidate_a_prime_is_a_name_only_remedy`), and **that test was never run against C1**. It has been now, at the same composition, `base_rate=0.0`, every assertion a decision rather than a sample — `harness-runtime/tests/integration/test_b137_c1_discriminator.py` (8 tests, mutation-probed: neutering the C1 patch reds the positive control, the discriminator and the A-equivalence). **Three results.** **(1) C1 rescues BOTH starved populations where A′ rescues one.** Under C1 the ROOT takes the always-sampled arm, so `ParentBased` hands every child an inherited `RECORD_AND_SAMPLE` and never consults a child's name — which is exactly why the event-carried population (the `B-133` family) survives C1 and dies under A′, whose repair works by exposing the child's *name* and an event-carrier's name is ordinary. **A′'s name-only limitation is therefore not shared by C1.** **(2) C1's coverage bound is exactly the starved population this row names.** A carrier that is its own trace root still takes the base-rate draw under C1 (`test_c1_does_not_rescue_a_carrier_that_is_its_own_root`) — and this row's own scope statement, after it withdrew the *"all 19 members are children of the envelope"* overclaim, is that the starvation is *"scoped to the members emitted inside the envelope."* Coverage and scope coincide; C1 is not claimed to reach further. **(3) C1 and candidate A are NOT export-equivalent, and candidate A cannot be fully measured at all — a first draft of this arc claimed equivalence and it is WITHDRAWN (out-of-family Codex round 1, absorbed 2026-08-15).** Two measurement errors produced the withdrawn claim, and both are now pinned as tests rather than prose. **(i) Head admission is not export:** the draft composed only a `SimpleSpanProcessor`, so it measured what the head ADMITTED and reported it as what the pipeline EXPORTED. Every survival claim now runs through the real `TailKeepSpanProcessor`. **(ii) The event name chosen decides the answer:** the draft used `sandbox.violation`, which is a §9.2 member but ALSO a §10.2 classification trigger (`SANDBOX_VIOLATION_SPAN_NAME`), so it rescues its own whole trace at the tail and makes every candidate look equivalent. The representative `B-133` event-carried names (`fallback.triggered` / `fallback.exhausted`) are members and NOT triggers. **Measured properly** — real tail, `fallback.exhausted` — C1 exports `[workflow.envelope, hitl.gate.evaluated, ordinary.carrier]` and an unconditional head exports `[hitl.gate.evaluated, ordinary.carrier]`: **the envelope is dropped**, because under C1 it is a §9.2 member taking the bypass arm while under an unconditional head it is an ordinary span buffered and dropped at root close, the trace carrying no §10.2 trigger. The contrast is itself pinned at `test_the_trigger_event_hides_the_difference_that_the_representative_event_shows`. **And candidate A is not modellable here at all:** its defining half — the §10.3 ratio moved INTO the tail consumer — does not exist in code, so `ALWAYS_ON` is A's HEAD HALF against today's tail and no claim about A's full cost or behaviour follows from it. **What survives is the COST half only, and it is a head-admission fact asserted as one:** at `base_rate=0.0` an out-of-envelope ordinary root is admitted by an unconditional head and not by C1, so C1's `1/base_rate` multiplier is scoped to envelope-rooted traces while an unconditional head admits every root the process opens. **Net, stated at the strength the measurements support: C1 dominates A′ on coverage (both starved populations vs one, verified end-to-end); C1's head-side volume cost is scoped where an unconditional head's is not; and NO equivalence between C1 and candidate A is claimed in either direction.** **What this does NOT settle — the council's remaining question is narrowed, not answered.** The ×10 in-envelope multiplier at `team-binding × self-hosted-server` (rate grounded live at `test_the_production_cell_this_is_priced_against_still_carries_its_rate`) is **real and unpriced against the C-OD-11 §11.1 per-cell budgets** — that is C11's half of the declared C7 ⊥ C11 tension and no probe here touches it. The dyadic **C7 + C11** convening remains owed, and its agenda is **narrowed but not reduced to one question**. What this arc removes from the agenda: **A′ is out** as a complete repair (measured twice, both drafts agree), and **C1's coverage is settled** — it reaches both starved populations end-to-end. What remains genuinely open: **A vs C1 is NOT resolved**, because A's defining tail half is unbuilt and therefore unmeasurable here, so the council still weighs A, C1, B and C; and the **×10 in-envelope multiplier stays unpriced against the C-OD-11 §11.1 per-cell budgets**, which is C11's half of the tension and which no probe in this arc touches.
- **C11 HALF GROUNDED 2026-08-15 — facts filed at `B-182`; this bullet deliberately does NOT restate them.** Three successive rewrites of this bullet drifted out of sync with the row that owns the evidence (out-of-family Codex caught the contradiction twice, at rounds 4 and 6), so the structural fix is a **pointer, not a copy**: `B-182` is the single owner of the C11 grounding and is where the council reads it. Two things only, because they change what the council should ask. **(i) C11's numeric bound EXISTS — the open question is volume evidence, not a missing cap.** `Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_37.md` Rider (a) states `cell_rate_limit=10_000.0` spans/sec at **every** ACTIVE cell, team × self-hosted included. What §11.1 leaves open at the team cells is the *throughput/population* to assess that cap against (deferred to `Persona_Document_v1.md` §11 open-item 4, still open). So the council must NOT be told there is no committed figure — it must be told the figure is committed and the **evidence to price against it is not**. **(ii) Process placement comes from C-OD-20 §20.1**, the canonical per-cell collector placement matrix — not from the implementation's logical `enforcement_layer` enum. Per §20.1 exactly ONE cell is unambiguously in-process (`solo × local-development`). Earlier drafts of this bullet asserted four, then three; both are **withdrawn**. **Neither `B-182` nor this bullet says whether C1 is affordable** — that call is untouched and still owed. **A discriminating question, registered not asserted:** if the effective cap is a rate limiter, raising head admission RELOCATES the drop rather than breaching the budget, and a rate limiter carries no §9.2 membership knowledge, so C1's floor could be shed one hop later. No artifact currently asks it.
- **C11's VOLUME EVIDENCE — attempted, NOT LANDED, and HELD after three successive wrong compositions (2026-08-16). The requirement is now precisely specified; the measurement is not made.** C11's budget factors as `spans/sec = spans-per-run × runs-per-sec`. `runs/sec` IS Persona §11 open-item 4. **`spans/run` is measurable and still unmeasured** — an arc tried and produced a different answer three times, each correction introducing a new error, so it was **withdrawn entirely rather than shipped at a fourth guess** (`[[reviewer-oscillation-register-and-hold]]`). **The three failures, recorded so the next attempt does not repeat them:** *(1)* reused a helper attaching only a `SimpleSpanProcessor` and reported **head admission as exports** — the exact error the preceding arc documented in a module the attempt cited by name; *(2)* hand-attached a `TailKeepSpanProcessor` to correct it, giving 2 spans/run — but **production omits that processor entirely at `local-development`** (`span_processor.py:368`: the wrap happens only when `deployment_surface != LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT`), so that chain exists at no shipped local run; *(3)* divided the `team-binding × self-hosted-server` cap by a count measured at `solo-developer × local-development`, which is what the B-72 harness actually binds — invalid, since the deployment surface **selects the processor chain** and the persona affects HITL behaviour. **THE REQUIREMENT, stated so it is executable:** build a `RuntimeConfig` bound to a **production surface** (`self-hosted-server` or `managed-cloud`) at the persona whose cap is being priced, drive `api.run`, and let the **stage-4 composer attach the processor chain** — never hand-assemble it, because the chain is cell-selected and that selection is the thing being measured. **AND DEFINE THE DENOMINATOR BEFORE DIVIDING ANYTHING (out-of-family Codex round 3).** Even at the right cell with the right chain, a single `api.run` measures **one workflow shape**; tool-heavy, retrying, or nested-agent workflows differ substantially in spans/run, so dividing the cap by one sample would reproduce this attempt's third failure in a new place. **And the units do not currently meet:** Persona §11 open-item 4 specifies *throughput per DAY*, generically — not workflow **runs/sec** — while the cap is **spans/sec**, so a division needs per-workload counts paired with throughput in matching units, or a representative workload mix. Establish the denominator first; only then divide. **Nothing about C1's affordability is established, and no spans/run figure from this attempt should be quoted.**
- **Cite drift — `workflow_driver.py:3305` → `:3458`.** This row cites the envelope open as `:3305`; at HEAD that line is skill-emitter code and the envelope really opens at **`workflow_driver.py:3458`** (`start_as_current_span("workflow.envelope")`, under the C-OD-25 §25.3 comment block). Mechanism unchanged — only the line moved. *(Kept as its own bullet deliberately: as a trailing sentence on a neighbouring bullet it was destroyed twice by region-rewrites of this row, at rounds 2 and 6, and both times only out-of-family review caught it.)*

With B-136 repaired the identical counterfactual reads **0 buffered / 0 evicted** (was 3 / 97 at cap 3), and with a §10.2 trigger present **100/100** ordinary children export where **0** did. C1 now costs its `1/base_rate` volume multiplier with **ordinary trace semantics** — no stranding, no eviction, no never-resolving population — and the B-136 interaction step (5) predicted is **discharged** rather than aggravated. **A′'s partial, name-only limitation is unchanged**, so the A′-vs-C1 comparison has moved materially toward **C1**.

Retained as history; step (3) onward remain live.)* ~~**(1) Re-ground the wiring first**~~, because it is explicitly marked provisional — confirm `tracer_provider.py` still binds the per-cell ratio in both modes and still carries the *"ignores the mode … future units may wire mode-conditional samplers"* note. If a mode-conditional sampler has since landed, this row may already be closed by that work and should be **re-measured rather than re-argued**. **(2) Re-measure, do not re-reason** — the probe is four lines of composition (`build_default_sampler` at the cell rate + the real `TailKeepSpanProcessor`, counting arrivals at `on_end`) across the three populations above, so the non-uniformity is re-established rather than assumed. **(3) Decide the posture — a genuine architectural fork, not a bug with a fix.** *(AMENDED 2026-08-13 — the option set below is EXTENDED, not replaced, by the measured A′ and C1 in the step-(3) bullet above; candidate A as defined here was NOT measured and its cost statement stands.)* **Candidate A: mode-conditional head** — `ALWAYS_ON` in `TAIL_BASED_PROD` mode with the §10.3 ratio applied inside the tail consumer at the root-close decision. This is what §9.1 literally says and what `tracer_provider.py` already names as an unbuilt surface, but it multiplies in-process span volume by `1/base_rate` and moves the ratio decision to a component with no ratio logic at all. **Candidate B: rejected-carrier recording** — leave the head as is, but record a counter or minimal marker for dropped spans that *would* have carried a preserved class, so the loss is **observable rather than silent**. Cheaper and honest, but it does not deliver the floor. **Candidate C: accept and document** — ratify that the §9.2 floor is a floor over the **admitted stream**, which would require amending §9.2/§9.3's *"head=1.0 across all cells"* language, since that language is what makes A the literal reading. **(4) Price the volume consequence before choosing A — and note it MERGES with `B-133`'s open F-08 residual** rather than sitting beside it: today's ~20% multi-tenant admission is the **ceiling** on the `B-133` arm's added keep-volume; candidate A removes that ceiling, so F-08 measured against today's admission **would not survive this repair**. The two must be measured together. **(5) Note the `B-136` interaction** — candidate A increases the buffered-trace population by `1/base_rate`, making `B-136`'s never-resolving always-sampled-root traces a proportionally larger share of `max_buffered_traces` pressure.

- **Council: YES** — and this is the row in the family that genuinely earns one, unlike `B-133`, whose repair was single-domain. Candidate A trades a real observability floor (**C7**: a preserved class dropped before any preservation rule can act on it is not preserved) against a 5×–10× in-process span-volume increase at every production cell (**C11**: telemetry volume, collector capacity, and the C-OD-11 §11.1 per-cell budgets those caps were sized against). The tension is **nameable in advance between two specific voices**, which is the convening discriminator, and the decision changes a committed per-cell envelope rather than an implementation detail. ### B-139 · `validator.fail.cause_attribution` is declared always-emitted at TWO canonical surfaces (ADR-D5 §1.10.1 + C-CP-21 §21.5) but has ZERO producers *(surfaced at the B-138 codex round, 2026-08-09)*

But **zero producers exist**: the framework producer (`validator_framework.py:_build_span_attributes`, `:320-352`) sets `class`/`detail_hash`/`next_action`/`escalation_owed` and never this key; the runtime escalation composer (`validator_escalation_composer.py:143-153`) likewise; an `rg` over `harness-*/src` finds no write site. Surfaced at the `B-138` spec-leg out-of-family codex round (P2), 2026-08-09 — the `B-138` leg corrected the `class` domain and demoted the permanence derivation clause, and without this row the third §21.5 attribute would be left declared-required with no owner.
- **GROUNDED 2026-08-15 — ROUTED TO BACK-FLOW AS A CLASS 1 FORK** (`.harness/class_1_fork_b139_validator_fail_cause_attribution_has_no_producer.md`, filed at #1359). **Step (1) CONFIRMED, row NOT falsified:** a FIXED-STRING search across **all seven** `harness-*/src` trees (`as`, `core`, `cp`, `cxa`, `is`, `od`, `runtime`) returns five hits and **none is a producer** — the declaration at `harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_fail_taxonomy.py:144`, a cardinality docstring at `:156`, an OD content-structure list entry, two OD comments. **A near-miss was ruled out rather than counted:** `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/api.py:1182` writes a bare `cause_attribution=` keyword but builds a `PauseStateCauseAttribution` on a `PauseStateAuditPayload`, and `retry.cause_attribution` is a different attribute that *does* have producers — so a loose search is the wrong instrument and the fixed-string one is sound. **Step (2)'s probe is decisive and prices (a) higher than this row assumed:** `ValidatorResult` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_framework_types.py:171-188`) carries exactly `outcome` / `fail_class` / `revalidation_payload` / `escalation_brief` / `fail_detail_hash` — **no cause field, none derivable** — and `_build_span_attributes` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_framework.py:237`, `:305`) receives only `step` / `result` / `next_action` / `burden_count`. The declaration and the declared producer's contract shape are **irreconcilable as written**, so this is Class 1, not a Phase-7 absorption. **This row's own claim that the cause values live in the staircase is FALSE at HEAD** (re-grounded at review round 3, after the fork first repeated it): `StaircaseTransition.on_cause` is typed `ValidatorRetryExitClass` (`harness-cp/src/harness_cp/validator_fail_transient_staircase.py:64`, docstring at `:66` — *"not a fail-cause token"*) and `_classify_provider_exception` (`harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/retry_breaker_fallback.py:281`) returns the same class. The staircase carries the **5-class retry-exit taxonomy**, not the 15-value attribution alphabet. **The cause-source inventory churned across rounds 3-5 and is now stated per surface, verified, and NOT asserted as complete:** the 5 F5 `secret_*` refinements have a typed carrier (`SecretFailClass`, `harness-as/src/harness_as/secret_fail_class.py:33-41`) and **partly** live producers (`SecretResolutionError` constructed **11x** by AST count — 8 in `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/config/provider_secrets.py`, 3 in `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/runtime_tool_dispatcher.py`, zero in `types.py`; only 3 of the 5 values are referenced in production, `SECRET_EXPIRED` and `SECRET_REVOKED` have zero constructions and zero emissions, appearing only in the enum declaration and its metadata table); `replay_semantic_divergence` has a typed carrier (`harness-od/src/harness_od/idempotency_join_dedup.py:375-377`) with NO live constructor, and is ADR-D6's addition rather than a base member; the **10 base values have no general mapping from a validator failure at all**; and the staircase carries `ValidatorRetryExitClass`, not causes. So the precise defect is that **no general mapping exists**, which is what an always-emitted declaration requires — narrower than "nothing exists", and it re-prices (B) DOWN from the round-3 wording while leaving the gap real. An **undischarged cross-ADR obligation** also constrains every disposition: `ADR-D6` §1.5.2 says ADR-D5 absorbs `replay_semantic_divergence` at the next D5 revision (`B-141` assigns that sync here), so demoting D5 while D6 stands would mint a fresh contradiction. the C5 sync scope is **every semantic occurrence, swept by SEARCH not by a hand list** (a `grep -c cause_attribution` over that file currently returns **33** lines; this fork's own enumeration grew 2 → 6 → 11+ before being retired).

One DECLARED surface family still binds the OLD retry-exit domain to the wire name: C-OD-14 §14.5.3's replay-semantic-divergence escalation carrier `ReplaySemanticDivergenceError` (`idempotency_join_dedup.py:345-367`) fixes `validator_fail_class = "terminal-fail-exit"` (plus `cause_attribution = "replay_semantic_divergence"`, `permanence = "permanent"`, `always_sampled = True`), enforced by `test_idempotency_join_dedup.py:304-306`; and ADR-D6 v1.2 declares the retry-exit five-value domain at its ingestion rows (`ADR-D6_v1_2.md:120`, `:298`). **Zero production emission sites construct the carrier at HEAD** (declaration + test only), so no live wire value violates the disposition — but the declared surfaces contradict it, and the `B-138` grounding claim (*"no reader asserts a retry-exit value"*) was falsified by this family at codex round 3.
