### B-232 · merge-door lease released after content merge; refresh covers N merges *(trigger-gated by B-230 Task 8, 2026-09-04; HELD until the trigger fires)*

- **What it is.** Releasing the merge-door lease after the content merge and letting one terminating refresh cover N merges would end the per-unit serialization the loop pays today, but it needs three coupled changes: the C-HE-06 invariants (`.harness/spec/Spec_HE_Loop_Lanes_v1.md:317-321` — the lease is never released while the merge SHA's own `main` run or the terminating refresh is unconfirmed), the §12.2.1 one-commit fixed point in root `CLAUDE.md`, and `_owed_lag` in `tools/codex_context_guard.py:443`. Until this arc the data could not justify it in either direction: the only door row on record was the budget-exhausted one (`lease_acquire_budget_exhausted`, after twelve backoffs of up to ten minutes), so "2 rows in 76 arcs" counted hour-long stalls, not contention.
- **Current state.** HELD, trigger-gated — `held` because every other register status is schedulable and the loop would otherwise select this row before its trigger (codex r1 on b-230-task-8); the hold is grounded, not parked: the data cannot justify the change in either direction until the counter moves. Since the b-230-task-8 arc `merge_door.wait_for_door` appends ONE `NOTIFY` row per contention event — at the first `held` observation, cause `merge-door-lease-acquire:lease_held_yield`, detail `holder=<arc id> backoff=0` — to the shared `loop_status.md` (never the tracked gate log, whose mid-wait rows could not reach merged history), and `uv run python tools/loop_cost_baseline.py --loop-status <loop_status.md>` reports `lease_held_yields` (lifetime) and `lease_held_yields_30d_max` (the most rows in any half-open 30-day window), and `tools/roadmap-audit/session-start.sh` evaluates the trigger EVERY session through `tools/lease_yield_trigger.py`, printing `[b-232] lease_held_yields_30d_max=<n>/5` in the banner and `TRIGGER FIRED` past 5 — the mechanical carrier of "re-evaluated at each refresh". Both counts read 0 at registration.
- **Closure shape.** TRIGGER: `lease_held_yields_30d_max > 5`, printed by the SessionStart banner every session. When it fires, flip this row to `design_substrate_gated` and open the spec leg as a Class 2 decision with a proposed text at the next unallocated `Spec_HE_Loop_Lanes` version carrying the three cites above; until then nothing in acquire, release, the C-HE-06 invariants or the §12.2.1 fixed point changes.

### B-233 · the generic `just` verb alternation in the permission guard is not end-anchored — a trailing token is parsed by `just` as a chained second recipe *(surfaced by codex r1 on u-he-37, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** The loop-mode allowlist branch in `tools/hooks/permission-guard.sh` matches `just[[:space:]]+(check|lint|…)([[:space:]]|$)` — with no end anchor. `just` runs every trailing token as a further recipe, so `just lint main-protection-rollback` is auto-approved and executes an otherwise ask-gated outward-facing branch-protection mutation after `lint` finishes. Confirmed empirically rather than argued: `just lanes-pilot-report aaa zzz-nonexistent-recipe` errors with "justfile does not contain recipe", which is only reachable if the trailing token was parsed as a recipe.
- **Current state.** REGISTERED, pre-existing and general. Surfaced by codex r1 on u-he-37 against that arc's two new recipes; those two now carry their own end-anchored, arity-bounded matcher with seven negative guard cases, and `arc-close` was already immune because its variadic `*QUEUE_ARGS` swallows trailing tokens. Neither fix generalizes to the rest of the alternation.
- **Closure shape.** Every recipe in the generic alternation is end-anchored with its own arity bound, variadic, or moved to an exact-shape branch, with per-recipe negative chain cases in `tools/hooks/test_permission_guard.sh`. This needs a per-recipe arity audit of the justfile — a blanket anchor would break the parameterized entries that rely on the loose match — so it is an audit, not a one-line fix.

### B-234 · pilot membership is inferred, and arcless loop-ledger rows cannot be attributed to a pilot *(surfaced by codex r3 on u-he-37, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** Four bounds the C-HE-13 §3 pilot report cannot close from the consumer side — three of which, (a), (c) and (d), block a trustworthy PASS. Codex r3 surfaced the two below; r4 added the two door-completion bounds under *Also carries*, and the closure shape covers all four. Membership is inferred from the reservations that carry `pilot_run_id`, because nothing persists an expected roster — a lane that created its reservation and died before recording the id is invisible, so a four-lane pilot that lost one lane can still present three lanes and satisfy the 3–4 check. And the friction window closes at the pilot's last arc-attributed row, while three `merge_door._notify` details carry no leading arc id (lease acquired, lease released, main-CI queue depth), so the door's own release attestation falls outside every defensible close.
- **Current state.** REGISTERED, and **BLOCKING the Scope-level completeness of U-HE-37**. Until bounds (a), (c) and (d) land, `lanes-pilot-report` does NOT compute the C-HE-13 §3 iff-clause completely: three paths produce a false PASS — a lane that died before recording `pilot_run_id` is invisible and a short run presents as a valid clean one (a); an already externally-MERGED PR receives a `merge_sha` from `merge_door.land()` and satisfies clause (a) of the iff-clause (c); and a malformed live `LEASE` reads as absent so the report can PASS before the door's post-merge checks finish (d). **A PASS from this report must not be relied on for any decision that assumes every intended lane landed through the door and finished.** Bound (b) is reporting-only and does not gate a PASS. Three review rounds on u-he-37 landed on the friction-window heuristic, which is the register-and-hold point: the root cause is producer-side, not another consumer bound. (This disposition is mirrored here deliberately. Since `B-235`, `--detail` prints the canonical `close_out` **above** this prose, so a blocker recorded solely in `close_out` is no longer invisible to the lookup routing uses — the earlier claim here that it would be is superseded. The mirror stays because the drift check still compares headings only, so this body and `close_out` can still disagree; a reader now sees both.) Interim floor landed with the unit — the report prints `arcs`, `lanes` and a `membership: inferred …` field so a PASS cannot be read as "every intended lane landed", and the module docstring states bounds (a) and (b) — the two known when it was written — but not (c) or (d), so the hazard set a reader of the code sees is two of four until the next `lanes_pilot.py` touch adds them (which a doc-only PR cannot do: `tools/` is IMPL and this plan is DESIGN).
- **Also carries, from codex r4 on the same arc.** Two door-completion bounds of the same shape: a non-empty `merge_sha` does not by itself prove a *door* landing, because `merge_door.land` accepts a PR already externally MERGED, reconciles the cycle and still writes that SHA; and `read_lease()` maps a present-but-malformed lease file to None, so a corrupted live lease lets the report proceed while post-merge checks are unfinished. Four review rounds converged on this family rather than on the code, which is the signal that the report sits outside the door and cannot verify door completion from the stores alone.
- **Closure shape.** (a) The pilot runner persists an expected participant roster at start and the report compares it against the reservations that recorded the run id; (b) every `merge_door._notify` detail leads with its arc id, so ledger rows are attributable without a time window at all. (b) alone retires the friction bound and is the smaller change; (a) needs a roster surface C-HE-13 does not define today, so it may route to a spec leg. (c) The door publishes an explicit completion marker the report can read — a released-lease record or a terminal door row — so "landed through the door and finished" stops being inferred from reservation payload; (d) `read_lease()` distinguishes absent from unreadable, as every other store reader in this family already does.

### B-235 · the register keeps one claim on two hand-maintained surfaces and the drift check compares only headings *(surfaced by codex r8 on u-he-37-plan-record, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** One claim, two hand-maintained bodies, and no check that compares them. **As first registered:** `close_out` in `.harness/forward-register.yaml` was the canonical field, but `forward_register.py --detail` rendered the **prose** carrier *alone*, and `check_prose_drift()` compares **headings only** — never bodies, so a safety-critical disposition had to be typed twice and reverting either copy left `--check` green while the canonical field and the surface routing actually reads disagreed about which bounds block a PASS. **The rendering half is now fixed** — `--detail` prints `close_out` above the prose — **and the unchecked-second-body half is not**, which is why this row is still open. See *Current state* for exactly which half is which.
- **Current state.** OPERATOR-FACING HALF REPAIRED; detection half deliberately not built, and this row stays open so that residual is tracked rather than named on a closed one. `forward_register --detail` now prints the **canonical `close_out`**, read from the YAML row, *above* the prose block and separated by `PROSE_DELIMITER` — so the surface operator routing actually reads carries the authority itself, and a drifted prose body is seen *beside* the canonical text instead of standing in for it. `close_out` is **always stated and never rendered as silence** — as its text when present, as MISSING when required at this status and absent, and as an explicit not-required line otherwise (worded differently for a `held` row and a closed one). The *count* of renderings is deliberately not stated: it changed once already — codex r8 found the closed branch emitting nothing at all — and a number in prose drifts while the invariant does not. **Residual:** the two bodies can still diverge with nothing detecting it — materially less dangerous now that the canonical text reaches the reader, so it is registered rather than driven.
- **Why it is registered rather than argued.** It is the root cause of four consecutive review rounds on `u-he-37-plan-record`: r5 found the blocker recorded only in YAML and therefore invisible to `--detail`; r6 found the canonical YAML still saying two paths after the other two surfaces said three; r7 found a fourth carrier — the `tools/lanes_pilot.py` module docstring — asserted to agree while carrying two of four bounds; r8 found the plan's own paragraph saying "two" four lines above a sentence saying "all three". Each was a human re-typing a claim that has one authority.
- **Closure shape — the prescribed one was wrong, and building it proved why.** This row first prescribed extracting the bound letters from both bodies and comparing the sets. That would **not** have caught the r6 defect it was written for: at r6 the YAML asserted `(c)` and `(d)` as the blocking set while *mentioning* `(a)` and `(b)` elsewhere, so letter extraction yields the same four letters on both sides and reports agreement. Phrase-anchored extraction is fragile in the other direction, and a pattern that matches nothing on both sides passes **vacuously** — a gate that cannot tell empty from unlooked, which is the class this register exists to record. Rendering the canonical field removes the need to parse prose for the fact at all. A structured `blocking_bounds` field was considered and **not** built: exactly one row carries bounds today, and a schema field for a generality that does not exist is speculative carrying cost.
- **Consumer note.** `tools/leg_selfcheck.py` parses the prose half of `--detail` and now splits on the imported `PROSE_DELIMITER`. Without that split the canonical header would have become `body[0]` — hard-failing every new row on the lead check and, worse, making its empty-body branch unreachable so the YAML-only-row gate would have stopped firing **silently**. Both directions are witnessed by mutation probe; the probe also caught that the first version of the lead-check test was vacuous.
- **Why not here.** `tools/forward_register.py` matches `codex_context_guard.IMPL_RE` and this plan is a DESIGN surface, so the fix cannot ride the doc-only PR that found it. Interim state, verified by reading each surface at head `27f3066ca`: the three register-side enumerations are currently identical and in the same order.

### B-236 · the dirty-carrier guard checks the tree once, then renders it N times *(surfaced by the merge-gate concurrency lens on b-235, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** A TOCTOU in `check_register_rows`' committed-mode guard. It reads `git status --porcelain` **once**, and if the register carriers are clean it falls through to a loop that spawns one `forward_register.py --detail <rid>` subprocess **per row**. `forward_register` reads the **live working tree** directly — `load()` opens the ledger path, the prose comes from `read_text()`, and it never reads a git blob. So the guard certifies the tree at one instant while the reads it protects happen at N later instants, with no lock and no re-check.
- **Current state.** OPEN and registered, not driven. A concurrent uncommitted edit to `.harness/forward-register.yaml` or `.harness/post-phase-8-forward-register.md` landing inside that window is invisible to the guard: `--detail` renders prose the push will not carry, a heading-only committed row is downgraded from HARD to ADVISORY, and `leg-selfcheck OK` ships. That is the round-11 `[P2]` fail-open reopened from the **timing** side rather than the already-dirty side the guard closes.
- **Why it is registered rather than absorbed into b-235, which found it.** The guard is **pre-existing on main** — `git show main:tools/leg_selfcheck.py` carries it at line 1122 using `_run` — so the window predates that arc. b-235 touched exactly one line of it, swapping `_run` for `_run_checked`, which moves the guard **strictly in the safe direction**: a failed `git status` used to return empty stdout, indistinguishable from a clean tree, and now raises. b-235's review budget was also exhausted at 15/15 rounds when this surfaced, so absorbing a new, unreviewed bound there was the worse trade.
- **Closure shape, for whoever takes this row.** Make the mutation **detectable** rather than preventable: re-run the same dirty check *after* the row loop and fail HARD if the carriers changed during the run. That needs no new locking primitive and converts a silently wrong answer into a loud one. Two remedies proposed at surfacing do **not** hold and should not be retried: reading `git show HEAD:<path>` instead of the live tree would break `--uncommitted` mode, whose entire purpose is rendering the working tree; and re-checking immediately before each `--detail` call narrows the window without closing it, since the write can still land between that re-check and the subprocess's own read.
- **Reachability.** Only with a genuine concurrent writer in the same checkout — which this workspace does have (background lanes, editor autosave), so it is real rather than theoretical, but narrow.

### B-237 · C-HE-28 §2's drift numerator has no emitter, so the correlation is built but unmeasurable *(surfaced by the out-of-family reviewer on u-he-38, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** C-HE-28 §2 requires refresh-collision incidence to be correlated against `concurrent_lanes_at_open`. U-HE-38 built and tested that correlation in `tools/arc_metrics.py` `summary()` — but its numerator source does not exist. `ROADMAP_STATUS_DRIFT` is raised at `tools/codex_context_guard.py:1515` as an **in-memory CI guard** `Finding(severity, code, message)`; nothing appends it to `.harness/merge-gate-log.jsonl`. Zero rows carry the name in `producer` or `finding_type` anywhere in the live log.
- **The second-order problem.** Because the durable row has never existed, its **shape** is unspecified too. The log's own convention puts detection identity in `producer` (`merge-door-post-merge-ci`, `merge-door-lease-acquire`) and a closed severity vocabulary in `finding_type` (`terminal-block`, `clean-approve`, `probe-sample`, `transient-retry`, `HITL-recoverable`, `permanent-fail-exit`, `probe-result`), so `producer` is the likelier carrier — but nothing binds it. Two successive review rounds on u-he-38 each proposed a *different* single field with confidence; both predicates were vacuous against the live log. An interim revision hedged by accepting **either** carrier; that hedge was removed at r6, because `finding_type` is an unconstrained string and the hedge traded a real misclassification risk (an unrelated producer's row counted as a collision) against a speculative miss — and a miss renders `--` rather than a wrong number. **The consumer binds to `producer` alone**, which is obligation (1) below; an emitter written from this row must name the detection there.
- **Current state.** OPEN and registered, not driven. The emitter is producer-side work in `codex_context_guard`, outside U-HE-38's declared files (`tools/arc_metrics.py`, `tools/test_arc_metrics.py`); wiring an unreviewed new durable-write path into the CI guard mid-arc was the worse trade.
- **Not held bare — the same-round fail-closed floor.** Two parts, both landed with the registration. **(i)** The report refuses to launder the gap: while nothing attributable has been seen every cohort renders **`--/<cohort size>`**, never a digit, and its provenance line states that `--` means no attributable row was seen — either none was written, or none could be tied to an arc — while a numeric `0` means the detector ran and recorded no collision. (r3 landed this as a 0-with-caveat; r5/r6 replaced the caveat with the `--` value itself; r8 made the denominator the cohort; r9 moved the gate to attributable rows.) **(ii)** The verification-manifest claim was **split** rather than over-stated — `tools/lanes_verify.py` registers `C-HE-28 §1+§3` and deliberately does *not* claim §2, so no green check stands over a measurement that cannot happen. That over-claim is the shape C-HE-22's "result row required before pilots" P1 had, and it was caught here by the reviewer before it shipped.
- **Closure shape, for whoever takes this row.** Give the guard a durable append at its detection site, then flip the manifest row to cover §2. Two emitter obligations are already load-bearing for the consumer that exists:
  1. **Name the detection in `producer`.** `finding_type` carries the closed lifecycle vocabulary and is an unconstrained string, so a detection name there could be collided into by an unrelated producer. The consumer binds to `producer`; the either-carrier hedge was removed at r6 once that risk was named.
  2. **Set an emitter-activation boundary.** This is the denominator's only open question, and it is now the whole of it. An interim revision of this row required a `no_finding` marker per *checked* arc, so the denominator could be distinct *observed* arcs; that requirement is **withdrawn** (u-he-38 r8). It invented a producer contract no spec states, contradicted the plan's own fixture (which expects `1/6`, not `1/1`), and against the real detector it inverts — `codex_context_guard` runs in CI on every merge, so every arc *is* examined and the exposure is simply the cohort, which is what the consumer now uses. What survives is narrower and real: arcs that ran **before** the emitter existed were genuinely never examined, so once it lands they must *leave* the denominator rather than dilute it. C-HE-28 defines no such boundary, and guessing a date or commit would bake an unreviewed constant into the metric, so it is producer-side work owed with the emitter.
- **Why nothing can be misread meanwhile.** The consumer side is complete and inert: reduced by `finding_id`, `rejected` findings dropped, lane-mismatch rows excluded from the numerator, and — with no drift-class row of any kind in the log — every cell renders `--/<cohort size>` rather than a digit. A `--` numerator means no emitter has written to this log at all; a numeric `0` means one ran and recorded no collision. The report will not merge those two facts.

### B-238 · lever stratification of the joint cohort key, deferred until the ledger can carry a third axis *(raised twice and rejected on u-he-38, 2026-09-04; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** The out-of-family reviewer argued twice (r2, r5) that C-HE-28's joint cohort key must stratify by `levers_active` as well, so a lever's effect cannot be attributed to lane count. The concern is live, not theoretical: 6 of 35 ledger rows carry levers across 3 distinct exact lever sets (`B-211 + B-212` ×3, `defect-class-preflight + register-pr-prose` ×1, that pair plus `review-loop-gate` ×2), and those arcs pool with the 29 baseline arcs inside each `(N, arc_type)` cell.
- **Current state.** OPEN and registered, not driven. The joint cohort key ships as the 2-tuple `(concurrent_lanes_at_open, arc_type)`; no lever axis is applied, and none is owed until the reopening condition below is met.
- **Why it was rejected as a change to U-HE-38.** C-HE-28 §1 names the split explicitly — "the split MUST be joint on (concurrent_lanes_at_open, arc_type)" — a 2-tuple. §3's honest-first-months claim then enumerates the populated cells in that same 2-tuple form, `(N=1, inventing)` n=6 and `(N=1, null)` n=12: the spec's own worked example of what a joint cell *is*. The "exact-lever-set discipline" §1 invokes is scoped by its own parenthetical — "do not collapse every non-empty levers_active into one TREATED cohort" — to the lever cohorts, which `by_levers` honours intact by keying on the exact sorted set.
- **Evidentiary symmetry, stated so the rejection cannot look selective.** That same §3 enumeration was *decisive in accepting* the r5 finding that historical rows belong at N=1 rather than in their own cohort. One reading of one clause, applied to both findings, sending them opposite ways.
- **Why it is registered anyway.** The confound is real and will matter once treated arcs are numerous enough for a cell to be more than a singleton. At 35 rows a third axis shatters the ledger — 4 lever sets × 6 lane values × 3 arc types — and every median becomes a single arc, destroying the descriptive counts the stratification aims to protect.
- **Not held bare.** The standing floor is C-HE-28 §3 itself, which this report prints in its header as the CORRELATIONAL note and which forbids an effect estimate at this sample size. The confound cannot be laundered into a causal claim while that holds.
- **What reopens this row.** Enough treated arcs that a `(lever set, N, arc_type)` cell is non-singleton, or any move to state an effect rather than a count — at which point the stratification is owed *before* the claim, and a spec amendment naming the 3-tuple is owed with it.

### B-239 · the cohort field is named for lanes and stores siblings, and the spec counts both ways *(surfaced on u-he-38 r6, 2026-09-04; consumer resolved, spec text REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** Two scales share one name across the cleared spec. The **sensor stores siblings**: `open_with_sensor` sets `concurrent_lanes_at_open` from `sibling_open_count(arc_id)` (`tools/reservations.py:786`), which excludes the arc's own reservation, and C-HE-03 §7 defines the field as the "count of sibling `open` reservations". A solo arc stores `0`; a stored `1` means two live lanes.
- **Where it collides.** C-HE-28 §1 names that field as the cohort key, while §3 counts in **lanes**: "the only populated joint cells are `(N=1, inventing)` n=6 and `(N=1, null)` n=12" — 18 rows at N=1 at a HEAD where *no* row carried the field — and "every N ≥ 2 cell … starts at 0". Both §3 sentences are true only of lanes: a lone arc is one lane, and AC#10 asks whether two or more lanes help, which is `N ≥ 2` in lanes but `≥ 1` in siblings. Read literally as the raw field, §1 would label a solo arc `N=0` — no arc runs in zero lanes — and would make "N ≥ 2" mean three lanes.
- **Current state.** OPEN against the SPEC TEXT only; the consumer is fixed and shipped. No live report surface is ambiguous today — the ambiguity remaining is in C-HE-28's own wording, which an implementation arc may not amend.
- **Resolved in the consumer.** `tools/arc_metrics.py` `lanes_at_open` converts siblings to lanes (+1), places absent-key rows in the 1-lane baseline alongside stored-0 solo arcs, and renames the report labels to `lanes_at_open` rather than continuing to name a field whose raw value they no longer show. No live surface is ambiguous today.
- **Why the spec text is registered, not edited.** Amending `design-substrate`-class wording from an implementation arc is the silent-absorption failure mode (root `CLAUDE.md` §4.3/§4.4); a cleared contract's prose is amended through back-flow, not by the consumer that noticed.
- **The cost of leaving it, measured.** This ambiguity survived **six review rounds** on this arc. Rounds 4 and 5 both reasoned about the cohort key at length, and r5 shipped a fix that mapped historical rows onto a stored `1` — onto *two lanes* — precisely because the field name asserts lanes while the sensor counts siblings.
- **What closes this row.** A spec amendment that either renames the field to say siblings, or states the conversion at C-HE-28 §1 where the cohort key is defined, so the next consumer does not have to re-derive it from `reservations.py`. Either is a wording change to a cleared artifact and routes through design-phase back-flow.

### B-245 · C-HE-33's outcome measure has no input on the arc-metrics row *(surfaced on u-he-42 grounding, 2026-09-15; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** C-HE-33 §4 names the outcome measure for closing the local/CI gap as two tracked cohorts (C-HE-28): the share of branches burning at least 6 CI runs, and the CANCELLED-run share. Plan U-HE-42 Step 2–3 places it as "two lines in `summary` (`arc_metrics.py`) over `ci_runs` (already on the row) — no new store".
- **Why it cannot be built from the row.** Grounding at `c2fa885c6`: `tools/arc_metrics.py` fills `ci_runs` from `ci_metrics(row.merge_sha)`, which asks `gh run list --commit <merge sha>`. That counts the runs on the landed merge commit, not the runs a branch burned before it landed. The same function keeps only green-run durations in `ci_wall_s` and stores no per-run conclusion, so the CANCELLED share has no input either.
- **Current state.** OPEN, surfaced at `c2fa885c6` and landed on the register after U-HE-42 merged (PR #1527, merge `107e5533`; plan amendment and marker on #1530, merge `100733c4`): neither `summary` line exists, and the arc-metrics row carries no branch-level CI run count and no per-run conclusion to compute them from.
- **What landed instead.** The rest of U-HE-42's C-HE-33 scope: the `codex-context-check-ci` recipe, `tools/test_codex_context_guard.py::test_local_ci_parity`, and the pre-push line in both ship-pr carriers.
- **What closes this row.** An arc that captures a branch-level CI run count and each run's conclusion on the arc-metrics row at queue time (a C-HE-25 row-field extension), then adds the two `summary` lines over those fields; or a C-HE-33 §4 amendment naming a measure the existing row supports.

### B-246 · C-HE-33 parity is false in CI's two-parent merge checkout *(surfaced on u-he-42 codex r10, 2026-09-15; MEASURED; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** C-HE-33 §3's parity claim — CI-shaped and local-shaped guard invocations agree for one committed SHA apart from `PARITY_EXCLUSIONS` — does not hold in the checkout shape CI actually produces. `actions/checkout` leaves a two-parent synthetic merge at HEAD on `pull_request` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:430-436`); the registered witness `test_local_ci_parity` builds a one-parent child instead.
- **Measured, not inferred (2026-09-15, at `32a4f26f4`).** Two fixtures identical except for parentage: **one-parent** → symmetric difference `{ROADMAP_STATUS_DRIFT_ALLOWED, ROADMAP_STATUS_BRANCH_DIVERGED}`, both named, outside-exclusions **empty**; **two-parent** → CI emits `TRACKING_SURFACES_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, local does not, outside-exclusions **`{TRACKING_SURFACES_REVIEW_REQUIRED}`**.
- **Mechanism.** The code is `warn` (`tools/codex_context_guard.py:1594`) and fires on `mode in {closeout, check} and state.changed_files and not _has_tracking_changes(...)` (`:1587-1591`). `changed_files` is the one field honouring `--head-ref`, so the CI shape reads the committed `base..pr_head` range while the local `codex-context-check` shape reads `--include-branch-diff` against live HEAD — on a merge commit those differ.
- **Round 10's stated mechanism was different, and does not reproduce.** It predicted `ROADMAP_STATUS_LAG_EXPECTED` via `_owed_lag`'s first-parent inspection (`:464-465`). Probed: `lag_expected` and `owed_lag` are both False in the merge fixture and that code appears in neither shape. The finding's *conclusion* is correct; its *cause* is this row's.
- **Current state.** OPEN; the arc landed (PR #1527, merge `107e5533`) with the one-parent witness. `TRACKING_SURFACES_REVIEW_REQUIRED` appears nowhere in `tools/test_codex_context_guard.py` and is not in `PARITY_EXCLUSIONS`, so no committed witness can observe this. Codex r12 re-derived the defect and it was adjudicated rejected-as-registered; merge-gate r3's accepted class sibling (undriven `CONTEXT_CHECKPOINT_*` exclusions, absorbed in `fdd47ef38`) left the fixture shape unchanged.
- **What closes this row.** Rebuild the witness over a real `git merge --no-ff` fixture, then either name the code as a CI-only exclusion with its reason, or make the shapes agree. Not by widening the exclusion set without a case that drives the merge shape — that was the r8 defect.

### B-247 · C-HE-27 spans keep only round 1, so N6 overstates multi-round arcs and per-round wall clock is unmeasured *(surfaced by the u-he-42 wall-clock audit, 2026-09-16; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** C-HE-27 §3 accretes each phase's `{start, end}` pair once on the reservation's `phases` map; `record_phase` (`tools/reservations.py`) is first-write-wins and replay-idempotent, and the review wrapper's own comment above `emit_verify` (`justfile`, `review-with-failover-logged`) states that re-review rounds 2..n re-emit as no-ops, so the durable pair stays the round-1 window.
- **Why it matters.** §4 defines N6, "problems prevented per hour", as accepted findings divided by the sum of `phases.verify` + `phases.edit` hours read from that map. Only round 1's window is in the map, so the denominator is under-counted on every arc with more than one round and N6 is over-stated on exactly the arcs it exists to measure.
- **Measured (u-he-42, reservation generation 53 at merge, 2026-09-16 audit).** `phases` holds queue 2.1 min, verify 1.7 min, absorb 0.5 min, edit 5.2 min, all inside the first 31 minutes of a 547-minute arc that ran 12 codex/gemini rounds and 6 merge-gate lens rounds; the gate-log rows span roughly 345 minutes of rounds. The audit had to re-derive per-round wall clock from inter-row gaps in `.harness/merge-gate-log.jsonl`, the one method §2 forbids as a measurement.
- **Current state.** OPEN against the contract shape. Nothing was built on u-he-42; the observation is recorded here so the next arc-metrics consumer does not rediscover it from `reservations.py`.
- **Why registered, not edited.** The one-pair-per-phase shape is C-HE-27 §3's v1 decision on a cleared spec; amending it from the arc that noticed is the silent-absorption failure mode (root `CLAUDE.md` §4.3/§4.4).
- **What closes this row.** A C-HE-27 amendment that keys spans per (phase, round) or accretes per-round durations on the reservation, with §4's denominator summing every round and `REVIEWER_UNAVAILABLE` rounds bucketed as §4 already specifies; then the wrapper emits the round key the gate admission already knows and `tools/arc_metrics.py` folds the map at drain. Until then, N6 on a multi-round arc is an upper bound, and per-round timing is read from the gate log with §2's caveat stated next to the number.

### B-248 · B-162's AST site counter sees 3 of 11 capture sites *(surfaced by E2b reviewers, 2026-09-16; VERIFIED; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** test_the_driver_emits_at_every_capture_site (harness-runtime/tests/integration/test_b162_pause_resume_span_emission_is_wired.py:155-185) counts capture sites with `isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) and node.func.value.id == "protocol"`. workflow_driver.py at 2c9094c62 has 11 `capture_pause_snapshot(` call sites: 3 bare (5276, 5482, 5556) and 8 wrapped as `cast(PauseResumeProtocol, <name>).capture_pause_snapshot(` (10504, 11322, 11490, 12531, 13360, 14860, 15714, 15780), whose `func.value` is a Call node. The filter yields 3; emit_sites is 11; `len(emit_sites) >= len(capture_sites)` is 11 >= 3 and cannot fail when an `_emit_pause_captured` after a cast-wrapped site is removed, contradicting the docstring's "asserted structurally by AST" for all six topology executors.
- **Current state.** REGISTERED 2026-09-16 from the E2b evaluation (docs/research/context-stack-evals/E2b-results.md), NOT absorbed: E2b is a doc-only research arc and the fix belongs to a code arc under the normal gates. Found independently by the pack and the no-pack Sonnet reviewer (the pack run cited the exact file; the no-pack run cited the neighbouring B-137 test file).
- **What closes this row.** make the matcher receiver-agnostic (match `node.func.attr == "capture_pause_snapshot"` regardless of `node.func.value`), assert the count equals the known site total rather than `>=`, and add a mutation witness that removing one cast-wrapped site's `_emit_pause_captured` turns the test red.
- **Council.** NO -- a verified test-adequacy defect with a named fix; nothing to convene over.

### B-249 · B-71 token population wider than the spec's wording; resolvability stamp rides it *(surfaced by the E2b pack reviewer, 2026-09-16; carriers VERIFIED; REGISTERED)*

- **What it is.** `pre_dispatch_escalation_basis` is derived UNCONDITIONALLY at both fan-out branch-composition sites (workflow_driver.py:8560-8572, per the §0.4.1 correction note) and carried to every later step of the branch (workflow_driver_types.py:585-601, "a branch child never re-derives it"). `resolve_escalation_instance_id` arm 2 mints whenever the basis is non-None, and `_escalation_operator_surface` (hitl_gate_composer.py) stamps `resolvability: PauseLocationVariant.UNIFORM_FALLBACK_ONLY` plus `branch_context` whenever a token exists. CP v1.119 states the token's absence as "every population that has no pre-dispatch gate-owning branch/escalation" (§25.20 value/absence rows, §0.4 arm 3, §26.9). A gate in a fan-out branch that escalates AFTER its child was dispatched -- a pause the operator can address directly by child_run_id -- would therefore carry the token and be told to use the uniform fallback. The audit-key widening itself is spec-directed (Runtime spec v1.121 site 2 names `_compose_and_persist_audit`), so the question is the population, not the fold.
- **Current state.** REGISTERED 2026-09-16 from the E2b evaluation (docs/research/context-stack-evals/E2b-results.md), NOT absorbed: this is a spec-versus-implementation question on a cleared CP spec (v1.119) and routes as a fork, not a patch (root CLAUDE.md §4.3). The E2b no-pack reviewer independently found the audit-key widening for non-escalating fan-out-branch gates; that part is spec-directed and its residue is a test gap (no test in #1341 exercises a non-escalating fan-out-branch gate's key).
- **What closes this row.** (1) re-trace whether a post-dispatch escalation in a fan-out branch reaches `_escalate_to_secondary_channel` with the branch's step_context (the reviewer named the dispatch loop and the durable-async branch in hitl_gate_composer.py); if it does, (2) either amend CP v1.119 to state the wider population and make the stamp conditional on the channel actually being fallback-only, or narrow the basis carry so only pre-dispatch gates mint -- an architect call, then spec-writer, then impl; (3) add the two population witnesses (non-escalating fan-out gate: byte-identical key; post-dispatch escalating fan-out gate: correct resolvability).
- **Council.** YES if step (1) confirms the path -- population semantics of a cleared contract across CP and Runtime (C1 ⊥ C10); dyadic council before the AskUserQuestion, per CLAUDE.md §13.4.
